title: 18.1.20 Mixed volumes
text:
We first extend the notion of volume in definition 16.6.13 to the mixed case. Let $	heta _1,\ldots ,	heta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing pseudo-effective classes. Definition 18.1.21 . EDCDF35668C4 Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. We define the mixed volume $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ as follows: 65AD0F03CD20 18.1.22  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight). \end{equation} When $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, the definition ( 18.1.22 ) does not depend on how we represent $T_ i$ as $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$, this is a consequence of theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 16.6.9 . Lemma 18.1.23 . 20316D4886CF 4642B46CE130 The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. 2AE20B98C203 For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have 7F052390F186 18.1.24  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ night)=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega ight). \end{equation} D321C1B261ED Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$ with positive volumes, then 7.10  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} 7787D4E19E46 Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ with positive volumes and $\lambda > 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] DAD3C89C5ACC Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.11  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} The notation $\operatorname{Reg}$ is defined in ( 5.19.13 ). Proof. 1 This follows from the symmetry of the mixed non-pluripolar product in ( 18.1.22 ), cf. proposition 13.11.4 2 . 2 For each $i$ and each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{	heta _ i+\epsilon \omega }\left[P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}ight]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{	heta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] as a consequence of example 18.1.11 . Hence using proposition 16.8.22 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 6 , \[   egin{aligned} & \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega )\  =& \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ X \left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 3 We write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ as before for each $i$ and $T_1'=	heta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1'$. The potentials $P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal I}$ and $P_{	heta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal I}$ are $\mathcal I$-model with positive masses, hence $\mathcal I$-good. By proposition 18.1.17 , their sum is $\mathcal I$-good. Moreover, it is $\mathcal I$-equivalent to $\varphi _1+\varphi _1'$. Then thanks to proposition 18.1.17 , \[  P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{	heta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{	heta _1+	heta _1'}\left[P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{	heta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} ight]_{\mathcal{I}} = P_{	heta _1+	heta _1'}\left[\varphi _1+\varphi _1'ight]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] Thus by proposition 16.8.22 , we have \[   egin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\  =& \int _ X \left( 	heta _1+	heta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1+	heta _1'}[\varphi _1+\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} ight)\wedge \left( 	heta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =& \int _ X \left( 	heta _1+	heta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} ight)\wedge \left( 	heta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 4 This follows from ( 18.1.22 ), proposition 16.6.27 1 and proposition 13.11.4 6 . 5 Our assertion follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$ In view of 18.1.23 2 , we may extend the definition of mixed volumes to the more general setting as follows: Definition 18.1.25 . 7731FA7D8BFD Let $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We define the mixed volume $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ as 0141EC0ADB1E 18.1.26  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ night)=\lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega ight). \end{equation} Note that $\operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega )$ is decreasing as $\epsilon 	o 0+$ due to 18.1.23 3 , so the limit exists. Furthermore, $\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)$ does not depend on the choice of $\omega $, as a consequence of 18.1.23 3 . Proposition 18.1.27 . DF8A923E8F3E 74EAB3B1411B The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. AEBD6B8A6D3F Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$, then 7.22  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} 439CA74101C3 Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] CB1FF7FB0BEC Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.23  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} 5BDABA896DC6 Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then 7.24  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\operatorname{Reg}T_1,\ldots ,\operatorname{Reg}T_ n ight). \end{equation} EF34C0318EDD For any closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$, we have 1BAF68507D97 18.1.28  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T,\ldots ,T)=\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} Proof. 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 are immediate consequences of the corresponding properties proved in 18.1.23 . 5 Using 3 and 4 , it suffices to establish the following: Suppose that 5EAAF326E66A 18.1.29  egin{equation}  T=\sum _ i c_ i[E_ i] \end{equation} is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$, where $\{ E_ i\} $ is a countable collection of prime divisors on $X$ and $c_ i>0$. Then A35A4555844E 18.1.30  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=0 \end{equation} for any closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that ( 18.1.29 ) is a finite sum. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. In this case, thanks to 3 and 4 again, we may assume that $T=[E]$ for some prime divisor $E$ on $X$. Write $[E]=	heta _{\varphi }$. Then $\varphi $ has analytic singularities thanks to proposition 5.20.4 . Therefore, $P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim \varphi $ for any $\epsilon >0$ due to proposition 16.6.22 . Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$, and choose $C>0$ so that $C\omega +	heta _ i$ are Kähler forms for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Then \[   egin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\  =&  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ X \left([E]+\epsilon \omega ight)\wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =& \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  \leq & \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+C\omega ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+C\omega ight)\  =& 0, \end{aligned}  \] where the inequality step follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and the fact that $P_{	heta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq 0$ for all $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Step 2 . We prove the case where $\{ E_ i\} $ is infinite. We may assume that $i$ runs over $\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Write $T_ i=	heta _{i}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$ as before. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta _ i+\omega $ is a Kähler form for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find $N_0>0$ so that for any $N\geq N_0$, the class of \[  \epsilon \omega + \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }c_ i[E_ i]  \] is Kähler. Take a Kähler form $\omega _ N$ in this class. Then the currents \[  \sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega  \] all lie in the same cohomology class. Moreover, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N.  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity in 5 , followed by the finite divisorial case of Step 1, \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(T+\epsilon \omega ,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \int _ X \omega _ N\wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ). \end{aligned}  \] Letting $N	o \infty $, and using $\{ \omega _ N\} 	o \{ \epsilon \omega \} $, we get \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ).  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 18.1.30 ). 6 Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$. In more concrete terms, we need to show that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ X (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n=\int _ X (	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n.  \] We may replace $\varphi $ by $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then we claim that \[  \varphi =\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] From this, our assertion follows from proposition 16.4.4 . The $\leq $ direction is clear. For the converse, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it suffices to show that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  
u (\varphi ,E)\leq 
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight).  \] We simply compute \[  
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)\geq \sup _{\epsilon >0}
u \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)=
u (\varphi ,E).  \] $\square$ Lemma 18.1.31 . 1AEDF3A60767 Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X,\omega ,\{ T_1\} ,\ldots ,\{ T_ n\} $ such that \[  0\leq \operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega )-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq C\epsilon  \] for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$. Proof. By the multi-linearity established in proposition 18.1.27 , we can write \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega ight)-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)  \] as a linear combination of the $2^ n-1$-terms: \[  \epsilon ^ m\operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} ight)  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. It suffices to show that the coefficients are bounded by a constant as above. Take $D\geq 0$ as the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} +\{ T_ i\} $ is nef for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then by the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} ight)\leq \{ \omega \} ^ m\cap \left( \{ T_{i_1}\} +D\{ \omega \}  ight) \cap \cdots \cap \left( \{ T_{i_{n-m}}\} +D\{ \omega \}  ight).  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$ Next we show that theorem 16.9.57 continues to hold even when $\varphi $ has vanishing mass. We prove a slightly more general result: Theorem 18.1.32 . A320A575BBEB Let $	heta _1,\ldots ,	heta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then BCAEFDCBCBE3 18.1.33  egin{equation}  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}ight). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $. Then for any $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}ight)  \] as a consequence of corollary 16.9.36 , theorem 16.9.30 and theorem 16.9.49 . Now thanks to 18.1.31 , there is $C>0$ so that for each $k\in I$, \[   egin{aligned}  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}ight)-\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}ight)\leq C\epsilon ,\  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (	heta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}ight)-\operatorname{vol}\left( 	heta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , 	heta _{n,\varphi _ n}ight)\leq C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, ( 18.1.33 ) follows. $\square$ Corollary 18.1.34 . 3305393E4400 Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form representing a big cohomology class. Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Then 55BF10D53948 18.1.35  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}	heta _{\varphi _ j}	o \operatorname{vol}	heta _{\varphi },\quad \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi _ j}^ n	o \int _ X 	heta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. The first part of ( 18.1.35 ) is a special case of theorem 18.1.32 , while the second part of ( 18.1.35 ) is a special case of theorem 16.9.30 . $\square$ The mixed volume has a log-concavity property: Proposition 18.1.36 . BB7441317AAF Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n(\operatorname{vol}T_ i)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, we need to show that \[   egin{split} & \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  \geq &  \prod _{i=1}^ n\left(\int _ X \left(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^ n ight)^{1/n}. \end{split}  \] This is a special case of theorem 13.13.5 . $\square$ Next, we also study how the mixed volume behaves under bimeromorphic transforms. Proposition 18.1.37 . 24049C5AD956 Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ to $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\pi ^*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*T_ night)=\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ night).  \] Proof. Using the definition of the mixed volume, we may easily reduce to the case where $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. By proposition 16.6.10 , we know that if we write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$, then \[  \pi ^*P_{	heta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\pi ^*	heta _ i}[\pi ^*\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In particular, \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi ^*T_ i=\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0.  \] Our assertion follows from the bimeromorphic invariance of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.13.4 . $\square$ As for pushforward, we also have a similar result. We need a preliminary result: Lemma 18.1.38 . 30F0E1037DAE Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then for any non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $Y$, we have \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T=T+\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]  \] for finitely many $\pi $-exceptional divisors $E_ i$ and $c_ i>0$. Proof. Let $E$ be the exceptional locus of $\pi $. Then \[  T=\mathds {1}_{Y\setminus E}\pi ^* \pi _* T.  \] Therefore, \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T-T=\mathds {1}_ E\pi ^* \pi _* T,  \] which has the stated form, due to the support theorems, see [ Section 8 , DemBook ] . $\square$ Corollary 18.1.39 . F7A7811A159E Let $\pi \colon Xightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Then 4A8B3C0B6CE6 18.1.40  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation} Proof. Observe that we may assume that $T_ i=\operatorname{Reg}T_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In fact, since the pushforward of the divisorial part of $T_ i$ is divisorial as well, hence by proposition 18.1.27 5 , they do not contribute to the volumes. Now by proposition 18.1.37 , it remains to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi ^*\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*\pi _*T_ n).  \] By 18.1.38 , the difference $\pi ^*\pi _*T_ i-T_ i$ is divisorial, hence our desired equality follows from proposition 18.1.27 5 . $\square$ A particular corollary of corollary 18.1.39 will be useful later. Corollary 18.1.41 . 1F0FA3B61EBC Let $\pi \colon Xightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Assume that $T$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then so is $\pi _*T$. Proof. We may assume that $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then by corollary 18.1.39 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\operatorname{vol}T>0  \] as well. Since $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}T=\int _ X T^ n.  \] But $\int _ X T^ n=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n$, so \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n>0.  \] It follows that $\pi _*T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. $\square$ Finally we establish a semicontinuity property of the mixed volumes. Theorem 18.1.42 . 763BE634A054 Let $(\varphi _ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) be nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$, and $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$). Assume that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in J} 
u \left(\varphi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night).  \] Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i^ j)>0$ and $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $\varphi _ i^ j$'s and the $\varphi _ i$'s are $\mathcal{I}$-model for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Our assertion becomes 055370851A43 18.1.43  egin{equation}  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1ight) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{equation} For each $j\in J$, define \[  \psi _ i^ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i^ k,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Observe that $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good thanks to proposition 18.1.19 , since after the preceding reduction the tail family is bounded above by $0$. It follows from corollary 5.16.9 and our assumption that \[  \lim _{j\in J}
u \left(\psi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Moreover, for each $j\in J$, the same formula gives $\varphi _ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi _ i^ j$. Since $\varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model and $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, proposition 16.8.17 gives \[  \varphi _ i\leq P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we define \[  \psi _ i=\inf _{j\in J}P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] In particular, $\psi _ i\geq \varphi _ i$, so $\int _ X	heta _{i,\psi _ i}^ n>0$. Since $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, $P_{	heta _ i}[\psi _ i^ j]$ is both model and $\mathcal{I}$-model. Due to proposition 16.6.29 , $\psi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Thanks to proposition 16.4.4 , we know \[  
u (\psi _ i,E)=
u (\varphi _ i,E)  \] for any $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and any prime divisor $E$ over $X$. In other words, $\psi _ i\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi _ i$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. But both $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, therefore, \[  \psi _ i\sim _{P} \varphi _ i,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] By proposition 16.8.22 , we have \[  \int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n).  \] Next by proposition 16.8.22 again, \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight). \end{split}  \] On the other hand, due to proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 , for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \psi _ i^ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ i.  \] We conclude from theorem 16.9.30 that \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n).  \] Putting these equations together, ( 18.1.43 ) follows. Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, from Step 1, we know that \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{split}  \] Using 18.1.31 , we have \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] But since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Lemma 18.1.23
text: Lemma 18.1.23 . 20316D4886CF 4642B46CE130 The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. 2AE20B98C203 For any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have 7F052390F186 18.1.24 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right). \end{equation} D321C1B261ED Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$ with positive volumes, then 7.10 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} 7787D4E19E46 Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ with positive volumes and $\lambda > 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] DAD3C89C5ACC Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.11 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} Proof. 1 This follows from the symmetry of the mixed non-pluripolar product in ( 18.1.22 ), cf. proposition 13.11.4 2 . 2 For each $i$ and each $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }\left[P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] as a consequence of example 18.1.11 . Hence using proposition 16.8.22 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 6 , \[  \begin{aligned} & \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega )\\  =& \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\int _ X \left(\theta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 3 We write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ as before for each $i$ and $T_1'=\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1'$. The potentials $P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal I}$ and $P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal I}$ are $\mathcal I$-model with positive masses, hence $\mathcal I$-good. By proposition 18.1.17 , their sum is $\mathcal I$-good. Moreover, it is $\mathcal I$-equivalent to $\varphi _1+\varphi _1'$. Then thanks to proposition 18.1.17 , \[  P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}\left[P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right]_{\mathcal{I}} = P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}\left[\varphi _1+\varphi _1'\right]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] Thus by proposition 16.8.22 , we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\\  =& \int _ X \left( \theta _1+\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1+\theta _1'}[\varphi _1+\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right)\wedge \left( \theta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \\ & \wedge \left( \theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =& \int _ X \left( \theta _1+\theta _1'+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1'}[\varphi _1']_{\mathcal{I}} \right)\wedge \left( \theta _2+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _2}[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \\ & \wedge \left( \theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  =&  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{aligned}  \] 4 This follows from ( 18.1.22 ), proposition 16.6.27 1 and proposition 13.11.4 6 . 5 Our assertion follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$

title: Proposition 18.1.27
text:
Proposition 18.1.27 . DF8A923E8F3E 74EAB3B1411B The mixed volume is symmetric in its $n$-variables. AEBD6B8A6D3F Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,T_1'$ on $X$, then 7.22  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1+T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)+\operatorname{vol}(T_1',T_2,\ldots ,T_ n). \end{equation} 439CA74101C3 Consider closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$, then \[  \operatorname{vol}(\lambda T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)=\lambda \operatorname{vol}(T_1,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] CB1FF7FB0BEC Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n,S_1,\ldots ,S_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ such that $T_ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S_ i$ and $\{ T_ i\} =\{ S_ i\} $ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7.23  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq \operatorname{vol}(S_1,\ldots ,S_ n). \end{equation} 5BDABA896DC6 Suppose that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then 7.24  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\operatorname{Reg}T_1,\ldots ,\operatorname{Reg}T_ n ight). \end{equation} EF34C0318EDD For any closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$, we have 1BAF68507D97 18.1.28  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T,\ldots ,T)=\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} Proof. 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 are immediate consequences of the corresponding properties proved in 18.1.23 . 5 Using 3 and 4 , it suffices to establish the following: Suppose that 5EAAF326E66A 18.1.29  egin{equation}  T=\sum _ i c_ i[E_ i] \end{equation} is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$, where $\{ E_ i\} $ is a countable collection of prime divisors on $X$ and $c_ i>0$. Then A35A4555844E 18.1.30  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n ight)=0 \end{equation} for any closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that ( 18.1.29 ) is a finite sum. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. In this case, thanks to 3 and 4 again, we may assume that $T=[E]$ for some prime divisor $E$ on $X$. Write $[E]=	heta _{\varphi }$. Then $\varphi $ has analytic singularities thanks to proposition 5.20.4 . Therefore, $P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim \varphi $ for any $\epsilon >0$ due to proposition 16.6.22 . Write $T_ i=	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$, and choose $C>0$ so that $C\omega +	heta _ i$ are Kähler forms for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Then \[   egin{aligned} & \operatorname{vol}(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ n)\  =&  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ X \left([E]+\epsilon \omega ight)\wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  =& \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _2+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _2]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\wedge \cdots \ & \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}ight)\  \leq & \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge \left( 	heta _2+C\omega ight)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left( 	heta _ n+C\omega ight)\  =& 0, \end{aligned}  \] where the inequality step follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and the fact that $P_{	heta _ i+\epsilon \omega }[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq 0$ for all $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Step 2 . We prove the case where $\{ E_ i\} $ is infinite. We may assume that $i$ runs over $\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Write $T_ i=	heta _{i}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$ as before. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $	heta _ i+\omega $ is a Kähler form for each $i=2,\ldots ,n$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. We can find $N_0>0$ so that for any $N\geq N_0$, the class of \[  \epsilon \omega + \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }c_ i[E_ i]  \] is Kähler. Take a Kähler form $\omega _ N$ in this class. Then the currents \[  \sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega  \] all lie in the same cohomology class. Moreover, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty } c_ i [E_ i]+\epsilon \omega \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N.  \] Therefore, by the monotonicity in 5 , followed by the finite divisorial case of Step 1, \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(T+\epsilon \omega ,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]+\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  =&  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega _ N,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\  \leq &  \int _ X \omega _ N\wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ). \end{aligned}  \] Letting $N	o \infty $, and using $\{ \omega _ N\} 	o \{ \epsilon \omega \} $, we get \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T,T_2,\ldots ,T_ night)\leq \epsilon \int _ X \omega \wedge (	heta _2+\omega )\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\omega ).  \] Since $\epsilon >0$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 18.1.30 ). 6 Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$. In more concrete terms, we need to show that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ X (	heta +\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n=\int _ X (	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})^ n.  \] We may replace $\varphi $ by $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Then we claim that \[  \varphi =\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] From this, our assertion follows from proposition 16.4.4 . The $\leq $ direction is clear. For the converse, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it suffices to show that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  
u (\varphi ,E)\leq 
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight).  \] We simply compute \[  
u \left(\inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)\geq \sup _{\epsilon >0}
u \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},Eight)=
u (\varphi ,E).  \] $\square$

title: Lemma 18.1.31
text: Lemma 18.1.31 . 1AEDF3A60767 Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $X,\omega ,\{ T_1\} ,\ldots ,\{ T_ n\} $ such that \[  0\leq \operatorname{vol}(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega )-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\leq C\epsilon  \] for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$. Proof. By the multi-linearity established in proposition 18.1.27 , we can write \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots , T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right)-\operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)  \] as a linear combination of the $2^ n-1$-terms: \[  \epsilon ^ m\operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} \right)  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. It suffices to show that the coefficients are bounded by a constant as above. Take $D\geq 0$ as the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} +\{ T_ i\} $ is nef for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then by the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\omega ^ m, T_{i_1},\ldots ,T_{i_{n-m}} \right)\leq \{ \omega \} ^ m\cap \left( \{ T_{i_1}\} +D\{ \omega \}  \right) \cap \cdots \cap \left( \{ T_{i_{n-m}}\} +D\{ \omega \}  \right).  \] Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 18.1.32
text: Theorem 18.1.32 . A320A575BBEB Let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ n$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms representing big cohomology classes. Suppose that $(\varphi _ j^ k)_{k\in I}$ are nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ and $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _ j)$ for $j=1,\ldots ,n$. We assume that $\varphi _ j^ k\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j$ for each $j=1,\ldots ,n$. Then BCAEFDCBCBE3 18.1.33 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\right). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $. Then for any $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  \lim _{k\in I}\operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\right)  \] as a consequence of corollary 16.9.36 , theorem 16.9.30 and theorem 16.9.49 . Now thanks to 18.1.31 , there is $C>0$ so that for each $k\in I$, \[  \begin{aligned}  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n^ k}\right)-\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1^ k},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n^ k}\right)\leq C\epsilon ,\\  0\leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left( (\theta _1+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _1},\ldots , (\theta _ n+\epsilon \omega )_{\varphi _ n}\right)-\operatorname{vol}\left( \theta _{1,\varphi _1},\ldots , \theta _{n,\varphi _ n}\right)\leq C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, ( 18.1.33 ) follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 18.1.34
text: Corollary 18.1.34 . 3305393E4400 Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form representing a big cohomology class. Then 55BF10D53948 18.1.35 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}\to \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi },\quad \int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n\to \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. The first part of ( 18.1.35 ) is a special case of theorem 18.1.32 , while the second part of ( 18.1.35 ) is a special case of theorem 16.9.30 . $\square$

title: Proposition 18.1.36
text: Proposition 18.1.36 . BB7441317AAF Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n(\operatorname{vol}T_ i)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, we need to show that \[  \begin{split} & \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _1}[\varphi _1]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\wedge \cdots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ n}[\varphi _ n]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)\\  \geq &  \prod _{i=1}^ n\left(\int _ X \left(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} \right)^ n \right)^{1/n}. \end{split}  \] This is a special case of theorem 13.13.5 . $\square$

title: Proposition 18.1.37
text: Proposition 18.1.37 . 24049C5AD956 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$ to $X$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(\pi ^*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*T_ n\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n\right).  \] Proof. Using the definition of the mixed volume, we may easily reduce to the case where $\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. By proposition 16.6.10 , we know that if we write $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i$, then \[  \pi ^*P_{\theta _ i}[\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\pi ^*\theta _ i}[\pi ^*\varphi _ i]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In particular, \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi ^*T_ i=\operatorname{vol}T_ i>0.  \] Our assertion follows from the bimeromorphic invariance of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.13.4 . $\square$

title: Lemma 18.1.38
text: Lemma 18.1.38 . 30F0E1037DAE Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then for any non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $Y$, we have \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T=T+\sum _{i=1}^ N c_ i [E_ i]  \] for finitely many $\pi $-exceptional divisors $E_ i$ and $c_ i>0$. Proof. Let $E$ be the exceptional locus of $\pi $. Then \[  T=\mathds {1}_{Y\setminus E}\pi ^* \pi _* T.  \] Therefore, \[  \pi ^* \pi _* T-T=\mathds {1}_ E\pi ^* \pi _* T,  \] which has the stated form, due to the support theorems, see [ Section 8 , DemBook ] . $\square$

title: Corollary 18.1.39
text: Corollary 18.1.39 . F7A7811A159E Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Then 4A8B3C0B6CE6 18.1.40 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation} Proof. Observe that we may assume that $T_ i=\operatorname{Reg}T_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$. In fact, since the pushforward of the divisorial part of $T_ i$ is divisorial as well, hence by proposition 18.1.27 5 , they do not contribute to the volumes. Now by proposition 18.1.37 , it remains to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi ^*\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi ^*\pi _*T_ n).  \] By 18.1.38 , the difference $\pi ^*\pi _*T_ i-T_ i$ is divisorial, hence our desired equality follows from proposition 18.1.27 5 . $\square$

title: Equation 18.1.40
text: 4A8B3C0B6CE6 18.1.40 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n)=\operatorname{vol}(\pi _*T_1,\ldots ,\pi _*T_ n). \end{equation}

title: Corollary 18.1.41
text: Corollary 18.1.41 . 1F0FA3B61EBC Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Assume that $T$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then so is $\pi _*T$. Proof. We may assume that $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then by corollary 18.1.39 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\operatorname{vol}T>0  \] as well. Since $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}T=\int _ X T^ n.  \] But $\int _ X T^ n=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n$, so \[  \operatorname{vol}\pi _*T=\int _ Z (\pi _*T)^ n>0.  \] It follows that $\pi _*T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. $\square$

title: Theorem 18.1.42
text:
Theorem 18.1.42 . 763BE634A054 Let $(\varphi _ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) be nets in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$, and $\varphi _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _ i)$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$). Assume that for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we have \[  \lim _{j\in J} 
u \left(\varphi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Then \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night).  \] Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i^ j)>0$ and $\operatorname{vol}(	heta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ i)>0$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the $\varphi _ i^ j$'s and the $\varphi _ i$'s are $\mathcal{I}$-model for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $j\in J$. Our assertion becomes 055370851A43 18.1.43  egin{equation}  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \leq \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1ight) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{equation} For each $j\in J$, define \[  \psi _ i^ j\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{k\geq j}{}\! {}^{*} \varphi _ i^ k,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Observe that $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good thanks to proposition 18.1.19 , since after the preceding reduction the tail family is bounded above by $0$. It follows from corollary 5.16.9 and our assumption that \[  \lim _{j\in J}
u \left(\psi _ i^ j,Eight)=
u \left(\varphi _ i,Eight),\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] Moreover, for each $j\in J$, the same formula gives $\varphi _ i\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi _ i^ j$. Since $\varphi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model and $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, proposition 16.8.17 gives \[  \varphi _ i\leq P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] For each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we define \[  \psi _ i=\inf _{j\in J}P_{	heta _ i}\left[\psi _ i^ jight].  \] In particular, $\psi _ i\geq \varphi _ i$, so $\int _ X	heta _{i,\psi _ i}^ n>0$. Since $\psi _ i^ j$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, $P_{	heta _ i}[\psi _ i^ j]$ is both model and $\mathcal{I}$-model. Due to proposition 16.6.29 , $\psi _ i$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Thanks to proposition 16.4.4 , we know \[  
u (\psi _ i,E)=
u (\varphi _ i,E)  \] for any $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and any prime divisor $E$ over $X$. In other words, $\psi _ i\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi _ i$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. But both $\varphi _ i$ and $\psi _ i$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, therefore, \[  \psi _ i\sim _{P} \varphi _ i,\quad i=1,\ldots ,n.  \] By proposition 16.8.22 , we have \[  \int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n).  \] Next by proposition 16.8.22 again, \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight). \end{split}  \] On the other hand, due to proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 , for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, we have \[  \psi _ i^ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\psi _ i.  \] We conclude from theorem 16.9.30 that \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1^ jight)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n^ j ight)=\int _ X (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ n).  \] Putting these equations together, ( 18.1.43 ) follows. Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, from Step 1, we know that \[   egin{split} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight) \  \leq &  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night). \end{split}  \] Using 18.1.31 , we have \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j ight)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\epsilon \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)\  \leq & \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1, \dots ,	heta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ night)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] But since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Equation 18.1.43
text: 055370851A43 18.1.43 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{j\in J} \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1^ j\right)\wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n^ j \right) \leq \int _ X \left(\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\right) \wedge \dots \wedge \left(\theta _ n+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ n\right). \end{equation}

title: 18.1.44 The volumes of Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles
search_title: The volumes of Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Definition 18.1.45 . 4B65B5AA614D A Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L,h)$ on a complex manifold $Y$ consists of a holomorphic line bundle $L$ on $Y$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $h$ on $L$. Theorem 18.1.46 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula) . FEA63C5AE11F Let $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$ and $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. We have A09BDD8C8D10 18.1.47 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation} In particular, the limit exists. For the proof, let us fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h_0)$. We identify $h$ with $h_0\exp (-\varphi )$ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. See section 5.20 for the relevant notations. Recall that when $X$ admits a big line bundle, it is necessarily projective. See [ Theorem 2.2.26 , MM07 ] . We first handle the case where $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. Proposition 18.1.48 . A51A6DE92117 Under the assumptions of theorem 18.1.46 , assume furthermore that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then ( 18.1.47 ) holds. Proof. Step 1 . Reduce to the case of log singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a log resolution of $\varphi $. In this case, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  h^0\Bigl (X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\Bigr )=h^0\Bigl (Y,K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T\otimes \pi ^*L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\pi ^*\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] By proposition 16.6.10 , we have \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)=\operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*h).  \] Therefore, it suffices to argue ( 18.1.47 ) with $K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T$, $\pi ^*L$ and $\pi ^*h$ in place of $T$, $L$ and $h$. Note that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is no longer a Kähler current, but it still has positive mass. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $D$. We may assume that $D$ is simple normal crossing by replacing $X$ by a modification and $D$ by the pull-back. We decompose $D$ into irreducible components, say \[  D=\sum _{i=1}^ N a_ iD_ i.  \] In this case, we can easily compute \[  \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Observe that $L-D$ is nef (see 5.18.5 ). Choose an integer $q>0$ so that $qD$ is integral. For each residue class $s=0,\ldots ,q-1$, we have \[  \left\lfloor (mq+s)D\right\rfloor =mqD+\lfloor sD\rfloor .  \] Hence, on the residue class $k=mq+s$, the line bundle \[  T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] is a fixed twist of $\left(q(L-D)\right)^ m$. Applying the asymptotic Riemann–Roch theorem [ Corollary 1.4.41 , PAG1 ] to the nef line bundle $q(L-D)$ and then letting $m\to \infty $ in each residue class, we conclude that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)\right)= (L-D)^ n.  \] Observe that by proposition 5.20.4 , \[  \theta _{\varphi }=[D]+S,  \] where $S$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential. Therefore, \[  (L-D)^ n=\int _ X S^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By example 18.1.10 , we know that the right-hand side is exactly $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$. $\square$ Proof of theorem 18.1.46 . Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Fix a Kähler form $\omega \geq \theta $ on $X$ such that $\theta _{\varphi }\geq 2\delta \omega $ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}\geq \delta \omega $ for all $j$. From proposition 18.1.48 , we know that for each $j\geq 1$, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}.  \] It follows from theorem 18.1.2 and theorem 16.9.57 that the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$ as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] Conversely, fix an integer $N>\delta ^{-1}$. From theorem 18.1.2 and theorem 16.9.30 , we know that 17BF54CBA55B 18.1.49 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n>0. \end{equation} Therefore, by 13.13.30 , we can find $j_0>0$ such that for $j\geq j_0$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ (depending on $j$) with 1375552B142A 18.1.50 \begin{equation}  (1-N^{-1})\varphi _ j+N^{-1}\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} For each $k>0$, we write $k=k'N-r$, where $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then we compute for $j\geq j_0$ and large enough $k$ (to be specified shortly) that \[  \begin{aligned} &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'(\psi +(N-1)\varphi _ j)\right)\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right), \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows from ( 18.1.50 ), the fourth line can be argued as follows: For large enough $k$, there is a non-zero section $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'\psi ))$ by 13.13.48 . It follows from 5.18.15 that for large enough $k$, \[  \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right).  \] It follows that multiplication by $s$ gives an injective map \[  \begin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right)\hookrightarrow \\  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'\psi +k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right)\right). \end{split}  \] Next observe that \[  (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j= N\theta _{\varphi _ j}-\theta \geq N\delta \omega -\theta \geq (N\delta -1)\omega .  \] Since $N>\delta ^{-1}$, this is a Kähler current. Hence proposition 18.1.48 is applicable. We let $k\to \infty $ to conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) \geq &  N^{-n}\int _{X} \left( (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \left((1-N^{-1})\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n -C N^{-1}, \end{aligned}  \] where $C$ is a constant independent of $N$ and $j$. Letting $j\to \infty $ and then $N\to \infty $ and using ( 18.1.49 ), we find that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n.  \] Therefore, ( 18.1.47 ) follows. Step 2 . We handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. First observe that $L$ is big by proposition 13.13.3 . Hence $X$ is projective. Take a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(A)$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A=\omega $. Fix $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We decompose any $k>0$ as $k=k'N+r$ with $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then \[  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes A^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  =&  \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)^{n}, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line uses multiplication by a non-zero section of $A^{k'}$, and we have applied Step 1 to the Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L^ N\otimes A,h^{\otimes N}\otimes h_ A)$ on the fourth line. On the other hand, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 18.1.11 , 18.1.8 gives \[  P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ].  \] It follows from proposition 16.3.10 that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ n.  \] Letting $N\to \infty $, we conclude \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] It remains to argue the reverse inequality. Choose $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. The existence of $\psi $ is guaranteed by 13.13.47 . Then for any $t\in (0,1)$, we set \[  \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t\psi .  \] It follows again from Step 1 that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ t)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}.  \] On the other hand, by theorem 18.1.32 and corollary 16.9.38 , \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] So we find \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] We conclude ( 18.1.47 ) in this case. Step 3 . We finally handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }=0$. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Assume that ( 18.1.47 ) fails. That is, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\right)\geq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)>0,  \] then $L$ is a big line bundle and hence $X$ is projective. Fix a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(A)$. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ of rational numbers with limit $0$ and a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )_{>0}$. We claim that as $j\to \infty $, the sequence $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $. It is clear that this sequence is decreasing. Let $\psi $ denote its limit for the moment. It is also clear that $\psi \geq \varphi $. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it remains to show that $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Fix $\lambda >0$. By strong openness, choose $\lambda '>\lambda $ such that $\mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )=\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )$. For $j$ large enough, the quasi-equisingularity of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ gives \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ),  \] where the first inclusion uses $\psi \leq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ and $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi _ j$. Thus $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, and the claim follows. By our claim, proposition 16.3.10 and proposition 16.4.4 , we find that 56B91126C3D7 18.1.51 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Fix $j>0$, take an integer $N>0$ so that $N\epsilon _ j$ is an integer. Then we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes A^{k'N\epsilon _ j}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  =&  \frac{1}{N^ n}\int _ X \left( N\theta +\epsilon _ jN\omega +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows by writing $k=Nk'+a$ as before, we applied Step 2 on the last line. Dividing by $N^ n$, we find that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n.  \] Since we know ( 18.1.51 ), letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=0,  \] which is a contradiction. Hence ( 18.1.47 ) is established in full generality. $\square$ Corollary 18.1.52 . DA9EAE05F341 Let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$, and let $h$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Then we have 8448EC5F2FB3 18.1.53 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\right)=\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n. \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to observe that 9E9E2CC55B5A 18.1.54 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\right) \end{equation} for all $k>0$, since for any holomorphic section $s$ of $L^ k$, the function $\log |s|_{h^ k}^2$ is $\theta $-psh thanks to proposition 5.20.4 and therefore, we have \[  \frac{1}{k}\log |s|_{h^ k}^2\preceq V_{\theta }.  \] In particular, $s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(kV_{\theta }\right) \right)$. $\square$ This common quantity is the volume of $L$, usually denoted by $\operatorname{vol}L$. In view of definition 16.6.16 , we have 18274B986369 18.1.55 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}L=\operatorname{vol}c_1(L). \end{equation} Example 18.1.56 . 35A211AC3973 If $X$ is a smooth projective toric variety and $\theta $ is invariant under the action of the compact torus, then any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}_{\mathrm{tor}}(X,\theta )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. Thanks to 18.1.8 , we may assume that $\theta \in c_1(L)$ for some toric invariant ample line bundle $L$. In this case, the result follows from theorem 18.1.2 , theorem 18.1.46 and theorem 21.12.31 . $\square$

title: Definition 18.1.45
text: Definition 18.1.45 . 4B65B5AA614D A Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L,h)$ on a complex manifold $Y$ consists of a holomorphic line bundle $L$ on $Y$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $h$ on $L$.

title: Theorem 18.1.46 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula)
text: Theorem 18.1.46 (Asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula) . FEA63C5AE11F Let $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$ and $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. We have A09BDD8C8D10 18.1.47 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation} In particular, the limit exists. Proof of theorem 18.1.46 . Step 1 . We first handle the case where $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Fix a Kähler form $\omega \geq \theta $ on $X$ such that $\theta _{\varphi }\geq 2\delta \omega $ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}\geq \delta \omega $ for all $j$. From proposition 18.1.48 , we know that for each $j\geq 1$, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ j}.  \] It follows from theorem 18.1.2 and theorem 16.9.57 that the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$ as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] Conversely, fix an integer $N>\delta ^{-1}$. From theorem 18.1.2 and theorem 16.9.30 , we know that 17BF54CBA55B 18.1.49 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ X \theta _{\varphi _ j}^ n=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n>0. \end{equation} Therefore, by 13.13.30 , we can find $j_0>0$ such that for $j\geq j_0$, there is $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ (depending on $j$) with 1375552B142A 18.1.50 \begin{equation}  (1-N^{-1})\varphi _ j+N^{-1}\psi \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} For each $k>0$, we write $k=k'N-r$, where $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then we compute for $j\geq j_0$ and large enough $k$ (to be specified shortly) that \[  \begin{aligned} &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'(\psi +(N-1)\varphi _ j)\right)\right)\\  \geq &  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right), \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows from ( 18.1.50 ), the fourth line can be argued as follows: For large enough $k$, there is a non-zero section $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'\psi ))$ by 13.13.48 . It follows from 5.18.15 that for large enough $k$, \[  \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right).  \] It follows that multiplication by $s$ gives an injective map \[  \begin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'(N-1)}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'N\varphi _ j\right)\right)\hookrightarrow \\  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{-r}\otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k'\psi +k'(N-1)\varphi _ j\right)\right). \end{split}  \] Next observe that \[  (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j= N\theta _{\varphi _ j}-\theta \geq N\delta \omega -\theta \geq (N\delta -1)\omega .  \] Since $N>\delta ^{-1}$, this is a Kähler current. Hence proposition 18.1.48 is applicable. We let $k\to \infty $ to conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) \geq &  N^{-n}\int _{X} \left( (N-1)\theta +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n\\  =&  \int _ X \left((1-N^{-1})\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n -C N^{-1}, \end{aligned}  \] where $C$ is a constant independent of $N$ and $j$. Letting $j\to \infty $ and then $N\to \infty $ and using ( 18.1.49 ), we find that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^{k}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}}^ n.  \] Therefore, ( 18.1.47 ) follows. Step 2 . We handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. First observe that $L$ is big by proposition 13.13.3 . Hence $X$ is projective. Take a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(A)$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A=\omega $. Fix $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We decompose any $k>0$ as $k=k'N+r$ with $k'\in \mathbb {N}$ and $r\in \{ 0,1,\ldots ,N-1\} $. Then \[  h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k'^ nN^ n} h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ r \otimes L^{k'N}\otimes A^{k'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(k'N\varphi )\right)\\  =&  \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)^{n}, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line uses multiplication by a non-zero section of $A^{k'}$, and we have applied Step 1 to the Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle $(L^ N\otimes A,h^{\otimes N}\otimes h_ A)$ on the fourth line. On the other hand, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 18.1.11 , 18.1.8 gives \[  P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +N^{-1}\omega }[\varphi ].  \] It follows from proposition 16.3.10 that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(N^{-1}\omega +\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \right)^ n.  \] Letting $N\to \infty $, we conclude \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] It remains to argue the reverse inequality. Choose $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. The existence of $\psi $ is guaranteed by 13.13.47 . Then for any $t\in (0,1)$, we set \[  \varphi _ t=(1-t)\varphi +t\psi .  \] It follows again from Step 1 that \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ t)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}.  \] On the other hand, by theorem 18.1.32 and corollary 16.9.38 , \[  \lim _{t\to 0+}\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi _ t}=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] So we find \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\geq \operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] We conclude ( 18.1.47 ) in this case. Step 3 . We finally handle the case where $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }=0$. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. Assume that ( 18.1.47 ) fails. That is, \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\right)\geq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)>0,  \] then $L$ is a big line bundle and hence $X$ is projective. Fix a very ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(A)$. Take a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ of rational numbers with limit $0$ and a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ with $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )_{>0}$. We claim that as $j\to \infty $, the sequence $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $. It is clear that this sequence is decreasing. Let $\psi $ denote its limit for the moment. It is also clear that $\psi \geq \varphi $. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, it remains to show that $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. Fix $\lambda >0$. By strong openness, choose $\lambda '>\lambda $ such that $\mathcal{I}(\lambda \psi )=\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )$. For $j$ large enough, the quasi-equisingularity of $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ gives \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ),  \] where the first inclusion uses $\psi \leq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]$ and $P_{\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega }[\varphi _ j]\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi _ j$. Thus $\psi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, and the claim follows. By our claim, proposition 16.3.10 and proposition 16.4.4 , we find that 56B91126C3D7 18.1.51 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n=0. \end{equation} Fix $j>0$, take an integer $N>0$ so that $N\epsilon _ j$ is an integer. Then we compute \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{a=0,\ldots ,N-1}\varlimsup _{k'\to \infty } \frac{n!}{(k'N)^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ a\otimes L^{Nk'}\otimes A^{k'N\epsilon _ j}\otimes \mathcal{I}(Nk'\varphi _ j)\right)\\  =&  \frac{1}{N^ n}\int _ X \left( N\theta +\epsilon _ jN\omega +N\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where the third line follows by writing $k=Nk'+a$ as before, we applied Step 2 on the last line. Dividing by $N^ n$, we find that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\leq \int _ X \left(\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)^ n.  \] Since we know ( 18.1.51 ), letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=0,  \] which is a contradiction. Hence ( 18.1.47 ) is established in full generality. $\square$

title: Equation 18.1.47
text: A09BDD8C8D10 18.1.47 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(h^ k)\right)=\operatorname{vol}\left(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\right). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 18.1.48
text: Proposition 18.1.48 . A51A6DE92117 Under the assumptions of theorem 18.1.46 , assume furthermore that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current, then ( 18.1.47 ) holds. Proof. Step 1 . Reduce to the case of log singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a log resolution of $\varphi $. In this case, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  h^0\Bigl (X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\Bigr )=h^0\Bigl (Y,K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T\otimes \pi ^*L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\pi ^*\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] By proposition 16.6.10 , we have \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)=\operatorname{vol}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*h).  \] Therefore, it suffices to argue ( 18.1.47 ) with $K_{Y/X}\otimes \pi ^*T$, $\pi ^*L$ and $\pi ^*h$ in place of $T$, $L$ and $h$. Note that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is no longer a Kähler current, but it still has positive mass. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $D$. We may assume that $D$ is simple normal crossing by replacing $X$ by a modification and $D$ by the pull-back. We decompose $D$ into irreducible components, say \[  D=\sum _{i=1}^ N a_ iD_ i.  \] In this case, we can easily compute \[  \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Observe that $L-D$ is nef (see 5.18.5 ). Choose an integer $q>0$ so that $qD$ is integral. For each residue class $s=0,\ldots ,q-1$, we have \[  \left\lfloor (mq+s)D\right\rfloor =mqD+\lfloor sD\rfloor .  \] Hence, on the residue class $k=mq+s$, the line bundle \[  T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)  \] is a fixed twist of $\left(q(L-D)\right)^ m$. Applying the asymptotic Riemann–Roch theorem [ Corollary 1.4.41 , PAG1 ] to the nef line bundle $q(L-D)$ and then letting $m\to \infty $ in each residue class, we conclude that \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X\left(-\sum _{i=1}^ N\lfloor k a_ i \rfloor D_ i\right)\right)= (L-D)^ n.  \] Observe that by proposition 5.20.4 , \[  \theta _{\varphi }=[D]+S,  \] where $S$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential. Therefore, \[  (L-D)^ n=\int _ X S^ n=\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] By example 18.1.10 , we know that the right-hand side is exactly $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }$. $\square$
