title: 20.2 The trace operator
text: The goal of this chapter is to give a meaning to the restriction of a quasi-psh singularity to a subvariety. If $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ and $Y\subseteq X$ is a subvariety, the naive restriction $\varphi |_ Y$ is often unsatisfactory: it may be identically $-\infty $, or it may fail to preserve quasi-equisingular approximations. There is a useful analogy with the trace operator in real analysis. A Sobolev function on a domain cannot, in general, be restricted pointwise to the boundary; instead, it admits a trace obtained by approximation using smooth functions, and the trace is well-defined modulo almost everywhere equality. 20.2 summarizes the corresponding dictionary. Real analysis Pluripotential theory smooth functions potentials with analytic singularities Sobolev functions potentials with $\mathcal I$-good singularities Sobolev convergence $d_ S$-convergence equality almost everywhere $P$-equivalence Table 8.1 A dictionary for the trace operator. The situation here is similar. A singular quasi-psh function need not have a meaningful pointwise restriction to $Y$, but after replacing it by quasi-equisingular approximants and passing to the appropriate $d_ S$-limit of the pointwise restriction of these approximants to $Y$, one obtains a well-defined $P$-singularity type. This is the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$. The trace operator is designed to be compatible with the two comparison theories developed earlier. It depends only on the $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type of $\varphi $, and itself is well-defined modulo $P$-equivalence. The first part of the chapter defines the trace and proves its basic properties: independence of the quasi-equisingular approximation, monotonicity, linearity, compatibility with bimeromorphic pullback, and continuity under decreasing $d_ S$-limits. These results provide the analytic foundation for later applications. The second part relates the trace operator to restricted volumes. For a big class $\alpha $ and a subvariety $Y$ not contained in the non-Kähler locus, the classical restricted volume $\operatorname{vol}_{X|Y}(\alpha )$ can be expressed as the non-pluripolar volume of the trace of a potential with minimal singularities. We also prove an asymptotic Riemann–Roch formula for the restricted multiplier ideal sheaves. The final part develops analytic Bertini-type statements. These results describe when multiplier ideals restrict correctly to a general hypersurface and when $\mathcal I$-goodness is preserved under restriction.

title: 20.2.1 The definition of the trace operator
search_title: The definition of the trace operator
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. The trace operator gives a way to restrict a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on $X$ to $\widetilde{Y}$, the normalization of $Y$. It follows from [ Proposition 3.6 , GK20 ] that $\widetilde{Y}$ is a normal Kähler space. We refer to section 9.10 for the pluripotential theory on unibranch Kähler spaces. For later applications, we need this generality even if initially we are only interested in the smooth case. Before diving into the trace operator, let us try to understand what goes wrong with the naive restriction procedure: simply take $\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}$. Both examples below are local, but can easily be globalized since the singularities are isolated. Example 20.2.2 . 482E170F0825 Consider the case where $\varphi $ has log-log singularities as in example 16.3.22 . Locally we can take $\varphi (z)=-\log (-\log |z|^2)$. We have $

text: Proposition 20.2.12 . B293F74D2022 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ such that $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Assume that $\varphi |_ Y\not\equiv -\infty $. Then \[  \varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ such that $\omega _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j>0}$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. We may assume that $\varphi _ j\leq 0$ for all $j\geq 1$. Then D2EC0F645F1C 20.2.13 \begin{equation}  \varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\leq P_{\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left[\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right] \end{equation} for all $j\geq 1$. In particular, \[  \varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}\leq \inf _{j\geq 1}P_{\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}\left[\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right].  \] Thanks to corollary 16.9.14 , 9C0808B7B91F 20.2.14 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\sim _ P \inf _{j\geq 1} P_{\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}[\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}]. \end{equation} We conclude our assertion. $\square$

title: Example 20.2.15
text: Example 20.2.15 . 917FA516701F Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ such that $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. Then \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\sim _ P \varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}.  \]

title: Example 20.2.16
text: Example 20.2.16 . 50B7DFD48C9D Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Take a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ X(\varphi )\sim _ P P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}},\quad \operatorname{Tr}^{\theta }_ X(\varphi ) = P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] In particular, the trace operator can be regarded as a generalization of the $\mathcal{I}$-envelope.

title: Example 20.2.17
text: Example 20.2.17 . 2272C87A04CE Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for some closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$, $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$ and 4411B718BF44 20.2.18 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\epsilon \searrow 0} \int _{\widetilde{Y}} \left( \theta |_{\widetilde{Y}} +\epsilon \omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\epsilon \omega }(\varphi )\right)^{\dim Y} >0 \end{equation} for any arbitrary choice of a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then it follows from proposition 16.4.4 that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )$ is defined, and its mass is exactly the above limit. As a consequence, we have the following formula: 8.9 \begin{equation}  \int _{\widetilde{Y}} \left(\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^{\dim Y}=\lim _{\epsilon \searrow 0} \int _{\widetilde{Y}} \left( \theta |_{\widetilde{Y}} +\epsilon \omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\epsilon \omega }(\varphi )\right)^{\dim Y}, \end{equation} where the left-hand side is understood as $0$ if $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )$ is not defined.

title: Remark 20.2.19
text: Remark 20.2.19 . ECCF7648C028 The trace operator allows us to introduce the following extension of the moving Seshadri constant. For $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ and $x\in X$, define \[  \epsilon (T,x)\coloneqq \inf _{V\ni x}\left(\frac{\operatorname{vol}\operatorname{Tr}_ V^{\alpha |_{\widetilde{V}}} T}{\operatorname{mult}_ x V} \right)^{\frac{1}{\dim V}},  \] where $\operatorname{vol}\operatorname{Tr}_ V^{\alpha |_{\widetilde{V}}} T=0$ if $\operatorname{Tr}_ V^{\alpha |_{\widetilde{V}}} T$ is not defined. Here $V$ runs over all positive-dimensional closed irreducible analytic subsets of $X$ containing $x$.

title: 20.2.20 Properties of the trace operator
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We prove a few elementary properties of the trace operator. Proposition 20.2.21 . F2C3DD7D449E Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$, $\lambda >0$. Assume that $
u (\varphi ,Y)=
u (\psi ,Y)=0$. Then we have the following: C2434E03D2CC Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $. Then $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi )$. 2C348D36BD1E We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi +\psi )\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )+\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi ).  \] 11F393C1BB1A We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\lambda \varphi )\sim _ P \lambda \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] 4C6B27F676F6 We have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi \lor \psi )\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )\lor \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\psi ).  \] As a consequence of 1 , the $P$-equivalence class of $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$ depends only on the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\varphi $. Proof. Take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ such that $	heta _{\varphi }$, $	heta _{\psi }$ are both Kähler currents. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ and $(\psi _ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $ and $\psi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ respectively. We may assume that $\varphi _ j\leq 0$ and $\psi _ j\leq 0$ for all $j\geq 1$. 1 We choose the quasi-equisingular approximations compatibly. By theorem 5.18.11 , we may take $\varphi _ j$ and $\psi _ j$ with analytic singularities of types \[  \left(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi )ight), \quad \left(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\psi )ight),  \] respectively. Since $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal I}\psi $, we have \[  \mathcal I(2^ j\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal I(2^ j\psi )  \] for every $j$. Hence $\varphi _ j\preceq \psi _ j$ for every $j$. Since $\lambda _ j/\lambda 	o 1$, 16.9.25 gives \[  d_ S\left((\lambda _ j/\lambda )\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}},\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}ight)	o 0.  \] After scaling the background class, 16.9.41 shows that $\lambda _ j\varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ and $\lambda \varphi _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}$ have the same $d_ S$-limit. The assertion follows. 4 By proposition 16.9.42 , we have \[  \varphi _ j\lor \psi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] By proposition 16.6.27 and proposition 18.1.17 , we have \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{	heta }[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\sim _ P P_{	heta }[\varphi \lor \psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Therefore, our assertion follows exactly as in the proof of 2 . $\square$ The trace operator is continuous along $d_ S$-convergent decreasing sequences. Proposition 20.2.22 . 58627BFD2457 Let $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that there exists a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ such that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ for each $j\in I$. Assume that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ and $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Then \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ j)\xrightarrow {d_ S}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] In view of corollary 18.1.14 , the trace operator preserves the property of being a quasi-equisingular approximation, thereby solving the problem in example 20.2.2 . Proof. It is enough to prove the sequential assertion. Indeed, suppose that the net statement fails. Then there is $\delta >0$ such that for every $i_0\in I$ one can find $i\geq i_0$ with \[  d_ S(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ i),\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\geq \delta .  \] Using also $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, we may choose an increasing sequence $i_ j\in I$ such that \[  d_ S(\varphi _{i_ j},\varphi )<j^{-1},\quad d_ S(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _{i_ j}),\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\geq \delta .  \] The sequence $(\varphi _{i_ j})_ j$ is decreasing and converges to $\varphi $ in $d_ S$, contradicting the sequential assertion. Thus we assume that $(\varphi _ j)_{j\geq 1}$ is a decreasing sequence and that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )_{>0}$. Replacing $\varphi _ j$ by $P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]$, we may then assume that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a decreasing sequence of model potentials. By proposition 16.9.47 , we have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]=\inf _{j\geq 1}\varphi _ j.  \] By proposition 16.9.6 , we may assume from now on that \[  \varphi =\inf _{j\geq 1}\varphi _ j.  \] After adding a Kähler form to $\omega $, we may assume that $\omega _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. It follows from the compatibility in $j$ and from $k_ j\geq k_{j-1}$ that $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is decreasing in singularity types. Let us consider the case $X=\mathbb {P}^2$ with coordinates $(z_1,z_2)$ on $\mathbb {C}^2\subseteq X$. Let $\omega _{\mathrm{{FS}}}$ denote the Fubini–Study metric. The subvariety $Y\cong \mathbb {P}^1$ is defined by $z_2=0$. Consider an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}})$, whose potentials near $(0,0)$ are given by \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2ight)+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] The pointwise restriction of these potentials to $Y$ are given locally by \[  \log |z_1|^2+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] On the other hand, locally \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2ight)	o 0  \] almost everywhere as $j	o \infty $. So the trace operator is not continuous along the sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$. Lemma 20.2.24 . DDEF49346283 Let $\pi \colon Zightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism, where $Z$ is a connected Kähler manifold. Assume that $W$ (resp. $Y$) is an irreducible analytic subset of $Z$ (resp. $X$) such that the restriction $\Pi \colon Wightarrow Y$ of $\pi $ is defined and is bimeromorphic, so that we have the following commutative diagram Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $

u (\pi ^*\varphi ,W)=0$. So the right-hand side of ( 20.2.25 ) makes sense. Step 1 . Assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. From Step 1, we know that for each $j$, \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^*\operatorname{Tr}_{Y}(\varphi _ j)\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\varphi _ j).  \] Letting $j	o \infty $, the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\varphi )$ by the definition of the trace operator. DB90B2D3ADEB Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Assume that $Y$ is smooth. Then for any $\lambda >0$, we have E9AC29FB30B6 20.2.27  egin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(\lambda \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ). \end{equation} See definition 5.16.23 for the definition of $\operatorname{Res}_ Y$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\omega _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. For each $j\geq 1$, we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ) \preceq _ P \varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Indeed, $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$ is $P$-equivalent to the decreasing $d_ S$-limit of the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ Y$, hence it is more singular than each $\varphi _ j|_ Y$. For any $\lambda '>\lambda >0$, we can find $j>0$ so that \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ).  \] By corollary 16.8.14 and theorem 5.16.26 , we have \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j|_ Y)\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ).  \] Thanks to the strong openness theorem theorem 5.16.21 , we conclude ( 20.2.27 ). $\square$ Lastly, we turn our attention to global sections. For this we will need the following global Ohsawa–Takegoshi extension theorem for the trace operator: Theorem 20.2.28 . 71AECE2E70ED Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and let $	heta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing $c_1(L)$. Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Assume that $Y$ is smooth and $
u (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Let $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k_0$ such that for all $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )))$, there exists an extension $	ilde s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. It is of interest to know whether one can control the $L^2$-norm of $	ilde{s}$ in the above result. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a Hermitian metric $h_ T$ on $T$. We may assume that $Y
eq X$ and that $	heta _{\varphi } \geq 3\delta \omega $ for some $\delta >0$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be the decreasing quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. We can assume that $	heta _{\varphi _ j} \geq 2\delta \omega $ for all $j\geq 1$. Also, there exists $\epsilon _0 >0$ such that $	heta _{(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j} \geq \delta \omega $ for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. Take $k_0=k_0(\delta ,h_ T)$ as in theorem 5.20.16 . We fix $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )))$. By theorem 5.16.21 , there exists $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$ such that $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )))$. Since $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi ) \preceq _ P \varphi _ j|_ Y$, corollary 16.8.14 implies that $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y))$. By theorem 5.20.16 , there exists $	ilde s_ j \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j))$ such that $	ilde s_ j|_ Y =s$, for all $j$. But by definition of quasi-equisingular approximation, we obtain that for high enough $j$ the inclusion $\mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j) \subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$ holds. As a result, $	ilde s_ j \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for high enough $j$, finishing the argument. $\square$

Using the standard construction in theorem 5.18.11 , we may choose these approximations compatibly in $j$, so that for each fixed $k$, \[  \varphi _{j+1}^ k\preceq \varphi _ j^ k  \] We shall choose an increasing sequence of integers $k_ j$ and put \[  \eta _ j\coloneqq \varphi _ j^{k_ j}.  \] The sequence $(k_ j)_ j$ is chosen inductively: Choose $k_1>1$, for $j>1$, we choose $k_ j$ large enough so that 1BA5628DE09C $k_{j}\geq k_{j-1}$; C590440C99EE $d_{S,\omega }(\eta _ j,P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}})\leq 1/(j-1)$; 5061729EE0BF $d_{S,\omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}}(\eta _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}},\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\omega }(\varphi _ j))<1/(j-1)$. It follows from the compatibility in $j$ and from $k_ j\geq k_{j-1}$ that $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is decreasing in singularity types. Indeed, \[  \eta _{j+1}=\varphi _{j+1}^{k_{j+1}}\preceq \varphi _{j+1}^{k_ j}\preceq \varphi _ j^{k_ j}=\eta _ j.  \] By theorem 16.9.49 , we have \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xlongrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] By 2 and corollary 18.1.14 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Observe that by proposition 16.9.47 , \[  P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\inf _{j>0} P_{\omega }\left[\eta _ j\right].  \] By proposition 16.6.22 , for each $j>0$, $P_{\omega }[\eta _ j]$ has analytic singularities. By theorem 16.9.59 , $(P_{\omega }[\eta _ j])_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $P_{\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Therefore, by definition of the trace operator and proposition 20.2.21 1 , \[  \eta _ j|_{\widetilde{Y}}\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] It follows from 3 that \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ j)\xrightarrow {d_ S}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ).  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$

title: Example 20.2.23
text: Example 20.2.23 . 531FFD6D4B64 The trace operator is not continuous along increasing sequences. Let us consider the case $X=\mathbb {P}^2$ with coordinates $(z_1,z_2)$ on $\mathbb {C}^2\subseteq X$. Let $\omega _{\mathrm{{FS}}}$ denote the Fubini–Study metric. The subvariety $Y\cong \mathbb {P}^1$ is defined by $z_2=0$. Consider an increasing sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}})$, whose potentials near $(0,0)$ are given by \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2\right)+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] The pointwise restriction of these potentials to $Y$ are given locally by \[  \log |z_1|^2+\mathcal{O}(1).  \] On the other hand, locally \[  \log |z_1|^2\lor \left( j^{-1}\log |z_2|^2\right)\to 0  \] almost everywhere as $j\to \infty $. So the trace operator is not continuous along the sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$.

title: Lemma 20.2.24
text: Lemma 20.2.24 . DDEF49346283 Let $\pi \colon Z\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism, where $Z$ is a connected Kähler manifold. Assume that $W$ (resp. $Y$) is an irreducible analytic subset of $Z$ (resp. $X$) such that the restriction $\Pi \colon W\rightarrow Y$ of $\pi $ is defined and is bimeromorphic, so that we have the following commutative diagram Then for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$, we have 3B7501D970A6 20.2.25 \begin{equation}  \widetilde{\Pi }^*\operatorname{Tr}_{Y}(\varphi )\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. We first observe that by Zariski's main theorem, $\nu (\pi ^*\varphi ,W)=0$. So the right-hand side of ( 20.2.25 ) makes sense. Step 1 . Assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. It suffices to apply example 20.2.15 to reformulate ( 20.2.25 ) as \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^*(\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}})\sim _ P(\pi ^*\varphi )|_{\widetilde{W}}.  \] In fact, the strict equality holds, which is nothing but the functoriality of pullbacks. Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Choose a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. By corollary 18.1.15 , $(\pi ^*\varphi _ j)_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\pi ^*\varphi $. From Step 1, we know that for each $j$, \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^*\operatorname{Tr}_{Y}(\varphi _ j)\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\varphi _ j).  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, the right-hand side converges to $\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\varphi )$ by the definition of the trace operator. On the left-hand side, the $d_ S$-convergence of $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi _ j)$ to $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$, together with 16.8.26 and corollary 16.9.11 , implies ( 20.2.25 ). $\square$

title: Proposition 20.2.26
text: Proposition 20.2.26 . DB90B2D3ADEB Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Assume that $Y$ is smooth. Then for any $\lambda >0$, we have E9AC29FB30B6 20.2.27 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(\lambda \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ). \end{equation} Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\omega _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. For each $j\geq 1$, we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ) \preceq _ P \varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Indeed, $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi )$ is $P$-equivalent to the decreasing $d_ S$-limit of the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ Y$, hence it is more singular than each $\varphi _ j|_ Y$. For any $\lambda '>\lambda >0$, we can find $j>0$ so that \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ).  \] By corollary 16.8.14 and theorem 5.16.26 , we have \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\varphi ))\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j|_ Y)\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda '\varphi _ j)\subseteq \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ).  \] Thanks to the strong openness theorem theorem 5.16.21 , we conclude ( 20.2.27 ). $\square$

title: Theorem 20.2.28
text: Theorem 20.2.28 . 71AECE2E70ED Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing $c_1(L)$. Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Assume that $Y$ is smooth and $\nu (\varphi ,Y)=0$. Let $T$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k_0$ such that for all $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$, there exists an extension $\tilde s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a Hermitian metric $h_ T$ on $T$. We may assume that $Y\neq X$ and that $\theta _{\varphi } \geq 3\delta \omega $ for some $\delta >0$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be the decreasing quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We can assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j} \geq 2\delta \omega $ for all $j\geq 1$. Also, there exists $\epsilon _0 >0$ such that $\theta _{(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j} \geq \delta \omega $ for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. Take $k_0=k_0(\delta ,h_ T)$ as in theorem 5.20.16 . We fix $k \geq k_0$ and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$. By theorem 5.16.21 , there exists $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$ such that $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )))$. Since $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi ) \preceq _ P \varphi _ j|_ Y$, corollary 16.8.14 implies that $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y))$. By theorem 5.20.16 , there exists $\tilde s_ j \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j))$ such that $\tilde s_ j|_ Y =s$, for all $j$. But by definition of quasi-equisingular approximation, we obtain that for high enough $j$ the inclusion $\mathcal{I}(k(1+\epsilon )\varphi _ j) \subseteq \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$ holds. As a result, $\tilde s_ j \in \mathrm{H}^0(X, T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for high enough $j$, finishing the argument. $\square$

Therefore, using proposition 20.2.22 , we find \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y\left( V_{	heta +\epsilon \omega } ight) \xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y\left(V_{	heta }ight).  \] Set \[  M\coloneqq \lim _{\epsilon _0	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\epsilon _0\omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta +\epsilon _0\omega }(V_{	heta })}.  \] By example 20.2.17 , if $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta })$ is defined, then \[  M=\int _ Y (	heta |_ Y)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta })},  \] whereas if $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(V_{	heta })$ is not defined, then $M=0$. Thus $M$ is the last term of ( 20.2.35 ), with the convention made in the statement. Thanks to theorem 16.9.30 , for any $\epsilon _0>0$, we have \[   egin{aligned}  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _0 \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _0 \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega })} & = \int _ Y (	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _0 \omega |_ Y)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _0 \omega }(V_{	heta })}. \end{aligned}  \] By the definition of $M$, this implies the existence of $(\epsilon _ j)_{j>0}$ such that $0<\epsilon _ j<1/j$ and 6EEF71F49B54 20.2.36  egin{equation}  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + j^{-1}\omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + j^{-1} \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } = M. \end{equation} Moreover, for each $j>0$, E74D68200A33 20.2.37  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + j^{-1} \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + j^{-1} \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } \geq &  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _ j \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _ j\omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } \  \geq &  M. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Indeed, the first inequality follows from the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 . For the second one, if $M=0$ there is nothing to prove; if $M>0$, then example 20.2.17 shows that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^	heta (V_	heta )$ is defined, and the inequality follows from the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 and the monotonicity theorem proposition 16.8.22 . Putting ( 20.2.36 ) and ( 20.2.37 ) together, it follows that \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon _ j \omega |_ Yight)^ m_{\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon _ j \omega }) } = M.  \] Finally, since $\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }) ight)^ m$ depends monotonically on $\epsilon >0$, we conclude that \[  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y + \epsilon \omega |_ Y + \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta + \epsilon \omega }(V_{	heta + \epsilon \omega }) ight)^ m=M.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: 20.2.38 Restricted volumes of line bundles
text:
Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n$ and $Y\subseteq X$ be a connected submanifold of dimension $m$. Consider a big line bundle $L$ on $X$, a Hermitian metric $h_0$ on $L$ with $	heta =c_1(L,h_0)$. Let $A$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. Take a Hermitian metric $h_ A$ on $A$ such that $\omega =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A$ is a Kähler form. Using the trace operator, one could prove the following generalization of theorem 18.1.46 : Theorem 20.2.39 . 230AF20F8E84 Let $h$ be a (singular) plurisubharmonic metric on $L$ with $
u (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h,Y)=0$. Assume that 92546FA16294 20.2.40  egin{equation}  \lim _{\epsilon 	o 0+} \int _ Y\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)+\epsilon \omega |_ Y} igl (c_1(L,h) igr ) ight)^ m>0. \end{equation} Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have 97B6F891A18A 20.2.41  egin{equation}  \int _ Y \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)} igl (c_1(L,h) igr )ight)^ m = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(h^{k})ight) ight). \end{equation} Recall that $\operatorname{Res}_ Y$ is defined in definition 5.16.23 . Observe that by example 20.2.17 , ( 20.2.40 ) implies that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)}(c_1(L,h))$ is defined. So ( 20.2.41 ) is defined. We will identify $h$ with $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ as in ( 5.20.9 ). For the proof, recall that the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_{\infty }$ is introduced in definition 5.18.13 . Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. After possibly replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there exists $\epsilon _0 \in (0,1)\cap \mathbb {Q}$ such that the $	heta _{(1-\epsilon ) \varphi _ j}$'s are also Kähler currents for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. For any rational $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$, and sufficiently large $k$, we have \[   egin{aligned} &  rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m \  =&  \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight) \quad 	extup{by theorem \href{../../tag/FEA63C5AE11F/}{18.1.46}}\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight) \quad 	extup{ by proposition \href{../../tag/DB90B2D3ADEB/}{20.2.26}}\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi _ jight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ jight)ight) \quad 	extup{by \href{../../tag/2E0432C779A0/}{5.18.15}}\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j|_ Yight)ight)\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left((1-\epsilon ) k\varphi _ j|_ Yight) ight)\  = &   rac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+(1-\epsilon )\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m\quad 	extup{by theorem \href{../../tag/FEA63C5AE11F/}{18.1.46}}. \end{aligned}  \] Here we used the observation that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with analytic singularities with $\psi |_ Y
ot\equiv -\infty $, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_ Y \mathcal{I}_{\infty }(\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(\psi |_ Yight).  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, 16.9.25 gives \[  (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Hence, by theorem 16.9.30 , the last term converges to \[   rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m.  \] We conclude that \[   egin{aligned}   rac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m\leq &  \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight)\  \leq &   rac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Yight)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $j	o \infty $, we conclude ( 20.2.41 ). Step 2 . We handle the general case. After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Using proposition 20.2.26 and theorem 18.1.46 we obtain that \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m & = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight)\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight). \end{aligned}  \] Now we address the other direction in ( 20.2.41 ). Let $\phi \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$ be a section that does not vanish identically on $Y$. Such $\phi $ exists since $A$ is very ample. We fix $k_0 \in \mathbb {N}$. For any $k \geq 0$, we have $k = q k_0 + r$ with $q,r \in \mathbb {N}$ and $r \in \{ 0,\ldots , k_0-1\} $. Also, we have an injective linear map \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight)\xrightarrow {\cdot \phi ^{\otimes q}} \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight).  \] Therefore, \[   egin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi ight)ight) \  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi ight)ight) \  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1} rac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q	o \infty }  rac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left((qk_0+r)\varphi ight)ight)\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1} rac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q	o \infty }  rac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k_0q \varphi ight)ight)\  = &  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta +k_0^{-1}\omega }(\varphi )ight)^ m\  =&  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where the maximum is taken over the finitely many residue classes $k=qk_0+r$, the following inequality uses $k_0q\leq k$, the first equality follows by applying Step 1 for each $r$ to the big line bundle $L^{k_0} \otimes A$, the Kähler current $k_0 	heta _{\varphi } + \omega $, and twisting bundle $T \otimes L^ r$, and the second equality follows from proposition 16.3.10 . Letting $k_0	o \infty $ and using the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 6 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi ight)ight)\leq \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Theorem 20.2.42 . 4F486DDB8BD0 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $
u (\varphi ,Y) =0$. Assume that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have \[  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} .  \] Proof. This is a consequence of theorem 18.1.46 , theorem 20.2.28 and theorem 20.2.39 : \[   egin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m &  = \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)ight)\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} \ &  \leq \varlimsup _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)ight\} \ &  \leq \lim _{k 	o \infty }  rac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y ,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)\ &  = \int _ Y \left(	heta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{	heta }(\varphi )ight)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Remark 20.2.43 . DB535DD3B5A9 One could also show that when ( 20.2.40 ) fails, the right-hand side of ( 20.2.41 ) is $0$. See [ DX24 ] .

title: Theorem 20.2.39
text: Theorem 20.2.39 . 230AF20F8E84 Let $h$ be a (singular) plurisubharmonic metric on $L$ with $\nu (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h,Y)=0$. Assume that 92546FA16294 20.2.40 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ Y\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)+\epsilon \omega |_ Y}\bigl (c_1(L,h)\bigr ) \right)^ m>0. \end{equation} Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have 97B6F891A18A 20.2.41 \begin{equation}  \int _ Y \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{c_1(L|_ Y)}\bigl (c_1(L,h)\bigr )\right)^ m = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(h^{k})\right) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. After possibly replacing $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ by a subsequence, there exists $\epsilon _0 \in (0,1)\cap \mathbb {Q}$ such that the $\theta _{(1-\epsilon ) \varphi _ j}$'s are also Kähler currents for any $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$. For any rational $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon _0)$, and sufficiently large $k$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m \\  =&  \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right) \quad \textup{by theorem \href{../../tag/FEA63C5AE11F/}{18.1.46}}\\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right) \quad \textup{ by proposition \href{../../tag/DB90B2D3ADEB/}{20.2.26}}\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi _ j\right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j\right)\right) \quad \textup{by \href{../../tag/2E0432C779A0/}{5.18.15}}\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left((1-\epsilon )k\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left((1-\epsilon ) k\varphi _ j|_ Y\right) \right)\\  = &  \frac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+(1-\epsilon )\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m\quad \textup{by theorem \href{../../tag/FEA63C5AE11F/}{18.1.46}}. \end{aligned}  \] Here we used the observation that for any $\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ with analytic singularities with $\psi |_ Y\not\equiv -\infty $, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_ Y \mathcal{I}_{\infty }(\psi )\subseteq \mathcal{I}_{\infty }\left(\psi |_ Y\right).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$, 16.9.25 gives \[  (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j|_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi _ j|_ Y.  \] Hence, by theorem 16.9.30 , the last term converges to \[  \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m.  \] We conclude that \[  \begin{aligned}  \frac{1}{m!}\int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m\leq &  \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{1}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y, T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right)\\  \leq &  \frac{1}{m!} \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ Y\right)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $j\to \infty $, we conclude ( 20.2.41 ). Step 2 . We handle the general case. After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$. Using proposition 20.2.26 and theorem 18.1.46 we obtain that \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m & = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right)\\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right). \end{aligned}  \] Now we address the other direction in ( 20.2.41 ). Let $\phi \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$ be a section that does not vanish identically on $Y$. Such $\phi $ exists since $A$ is very ample. We fix $k_0 \in \mathbb {N}$. For any $k \geq 0$, we have $k = q k_0 + r$ with $q,r \in \mathbb {N}$ and $r \in \{ 0,\ldots , k_0-1\} $. Also, we have an injective linear map \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right)\xrightarrow {\cdot \phi ^{\otimes q}} \mathrm{H}^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right).  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned} & \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi \right)\right) \\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k\varphi \right)\right) \\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1}\frac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q\to \infty } \frac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left((qk_0+r)\varphi \right)\right)\\  \leq &  \max _{r=0,\ldots ,k_0-1}\frac{1}{k_0^ m} \varlimsup _{q\to \infty } \frac{m!}{q^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^{q k_0} \otimes A|_ Y^ q\otimes L|_ Y^{r}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k_0q \varphi \right)\right)\\  = &  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +k_0^{-1}\omega }(\varphi )\right)^ m\\  =&  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+k_0^{-1}\omega |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m, \end{aligned}  \] where the maximum is taken over the finitely many residue classes $k=qk_0+r$, the following inequality uses $k_0q\leq k$, the first equality follows by applying Step 1 for each $r$ to the big line bundle $L^{k_0} \otimes A$, the Kähler current $k_0 \theta _{\varphi } + \omega $, and twisting bundle $T \otimes L^ r$, and the second equality follows from proposition 16.3.10 . Letting $k_0\to \infty $ and using the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar product proposition 13.11.4 6 , we conclude that \[  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y \otimes L|_ Y^ k \otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}\left(k \varphi \right)\right)\leq \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Theorem 20.2.42
text: Theorem 20.2.42 . 4F486DDB8BD0 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\nu (\varphi ,Y) =0$. Assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then for any holomorphic line bundle $T$ on $X$ we have \[  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} .  \] Proof. This is a consequence of theorem 18.1.46 , theorem 20.2.28 and theorem 20.2.39 : \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m &  = \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(k \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)\right)\\ &  \leq \varliminf _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} \\ &  \leq \varlimsup _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} \dim _{\mathbb C}\left\{  s|_ Y: s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\right\} \\ &  \leq \lim _{k \to \infty } \frac{m!}{k^ m} h^0\left(Y ,T|_ Y\otimes L|_ Y^ k\otimes \operatorname{Res}_ Y\mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\\ &  = \int _ Y \left(\theta |_ Y+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta }(\varphi )\right)^ m. \end{aligned}  \] This completes the proof. $\square$
