title: 20.2.44 Analytic Bertini theorems
text:
Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$. The analytic Bertini theorem handles the restriction along a generic subvariety. Theorem 20.2.45 . 7931695F46E8 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Let $p\colon Xightarrow \mathbb {P}^ N$ be a morphism ($N\geq 1$). Define \[  \mathcal{G}\coloneqq \Bigl \{ H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|: H'\coloneqq H\cap X 	extup{ is smooth and } \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H'})=\operatorname{Res}_{H'} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr \} .  \] Then $\mathcal{G}\subseteq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ is co-pluripolar. Recall that co-pluripolar sets are defined in definition 5.47.2 . We adopt the convention that $\mathcal{I}(-\infty )=0$. Remark 20.2.46 . 6A24558044D5 Here and in the sequel, we slightly abuse the notation by writing $H\cap X$ for $p^{-1}H$, the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $H$. In other words, $H\cap X\coloneqq H	imes _{\mathbb {P}^ N} X$. By definition, any $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ such that $p^{-1}H=\emptyset $ lies in $\mathcal{G}$. Proof. Take an ample line bundle $L$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ such that $c_1(L,h)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq 0$, where $c_1(L,h)$ is the first Chern form of $(L,h)$, namely the curvature form of $h$. We introduce $\Lambda \coloneqq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ to simplify our notations. Step 1 . We prove that the following set is co-pluripolar: \[   egin{split}  \mathcal{G}_{L}\coloneqq \left\{ H\in \Lambda : H\cap X 	ext{ is smooth and } \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )= ight.\  \left. \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr )ight\} . \end{split}  \] Here $\omega _{H\cap X}$ denotes the dualizing sheaf of $H\cap X$. Let $U\subseteq \Lambda 	imes X$ be the closed subvariety whose $\mathbb {C}$-points correspond to pairs $(H,x)\in \Lambda 	imes X$ with $p(x)\in H$. Let $\pi _1\colon Uightarrow \Lambda $ be the natural projection. We may assume that $\pi _1$ is surjective, as otherwise there is nothing to prove. Observe that $U$ is a local complete intersection scheme by Krull's Hauptidealsatz and a fortiori a Cohen–Macaulay scheme. It follows from miracle flatness [ Theorem 23.1 , Mat89 ] that the natural projection $\pi _2\colon Uightarrow X$ is flat. As the fibers of $\pi _2$ over closed points of $X$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb {P}^{N-1}$, it follows that $\pi _2$ is smooth. Thus, $U$ is smooth as well. Moreover, observe that 62AF47325D23 20.2.47  egin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )=\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) \end{equation} by proposition 5.16.22 . In the following, we will construct pluripolar sets $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Sigma _2 \subseteq \Sigma _3\subseteq \Sigma _4\subseteq \Lambda $ such that the behavior of $\pi _1$ is improved successively on the complement of $\Sigma _ i$. Step 1.1 . The usual Bertini theorem shows that there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\pi _1$ has smooth fibers outside $\Sigma _1$. Enlarging $\Sigma _1$, we may guarantee that $\pi _1$ and $\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ are both flat outside $\Sigma _1$. See [ Théorème 6.9.1 , EGAIV2 ] . Then after further enlarging $\Sigma _1$ we may assume that $p^{-1}(H)$ avoids all associated points of $\mathcal{O}_ X/\mathcal{I}(\varphi )$, for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Let $\pi _{1,H}$ denote the fiber of $\pi _1$ at $H$ and write $i_ H\colon \pi _{1,H}ightarrow U$ for the inclusion morphism. We arrive at \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ))=i_ H^*\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )  \] for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. 3 Step 1.2 . By Grauert's coherence theorem, \[  \mathcal{F}^ i\coloneqq R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L\otimes \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ) ight)  \] is coherent for all $i$. Here $\omega _{U/\Lambda }$ denotes the relative dualizing sheaf of the morphism $Uightarrow \Lambda $. Thus, there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _2\subseteq \Lambda $ such that 94B9B26CA79D $\Sigma _2\supseteq \Sigma _1$. 0FC04CC0A41E The $\mathcal{F}^ i$'s are locally free outside $\Sigma _2$. We write $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}^0$. By cohomology and base change [ Theorem III.12.11 , Har ] , for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _2$, the fiber $\mathcal{F}|_ H$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is given by \[  \mathcal{F}|_ H= \mathrm{H}^0\left(\pi _{1,H},\omega _{U/\Lambda }|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \pi _2^*L|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )) ight).  \] Step 1.3 . In order to proceed, we need to make use of the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ on $\mathcal{F}$ defined in [ HPS18 ] . We briefly recall its definition in our setting. By [ Section 22 , HPS18 ] , we can find a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _3\subseteq \Lambda $ such that 4DF0186C50EB $\Sigma _3\supseteq \Sigma _2$, 77E34EDD06F8 $\pi _1$ is smooth outside $\Sigma _3$, DC4E272A416D both $\mathcal{F}$ and $\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)/\mathcal{F}$ are locally free outside $\Sigma _3$, and 254A2D20904E for each $i$, \[  R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)  \] is locally free outside $\Sigma _3$. Then for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, \[   egin{gathered} \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})ight)\ \subseteq \mathcal{F}|_ H\subseteq \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}ight). \end{gathered}  \] See [ Lemma 22.1 , HPS18 ] . Now we can give the definition of the Hodge metric on $\Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$. Given any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, any $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}|_ H$, the Hodge metric is defined as \[  h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha ):=\int _{X\cap H} |\alpha |^2_{h}\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\in [0,\infty ].  \] Observe that $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )<\infty $ if and only if $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^0(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X}))$. Moreover, $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )>0$ if $\alpha 
eq 0$. It is shown in [ HPS18 ] (cf. [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] ) that $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is indeed a singular Hermitian metric, and it extends to a positive metric on $\mathcal{F}$. Step 1.4 . The determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )
eq \mathcal{F}|_ H.  \] As the map $\pi _2$ is smooth, we have $\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )= \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ by proposition 5.16.22 . Under the identification $\pi _{1,H}\cong H\cap X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}\Bigl (\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr )\cong \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\Bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] Thus, we have the following inclusions: \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  \subseteq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ), \end{split}  \] the right-hand side being $\mathcal{F}|_ H$. Recall that the first inclusion follows from theorem 5.16.26 . Hence, $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|\setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  
eq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Let $\Sigma _4$ be the union of $\Sigma _3$ and the set of all such $H$. Since the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is positive ( [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] and [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS18 ] ), its determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is also positive ( [ Proposition 1.3 , Rau15 ] and [ Proposition 25.1 , HPS18 ] ), it follows that $\Sigma _4$ is pluripolar. As a consequence, $\mathcal{G}_{L}$ is co-pluripolar. Step 2 . Fix an ample invertible sheaf $S$ on $X$. The same result holds with $L\otimes S^{\otimes a}$ in place of $L$. Thus, the set \[  A\coloneqq  igcap _{a=0}^{\infty }\mathcal{G}_{L\otimes S^{\otimes a}}  \] is co-pluripolar. For each $H\in \Lambda $ such that $X\cap H$ is smooth and $\mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})
eq \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}(\mathcal{I}(\varphi ))$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be the following cokernel: \[  0ightarrow \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)ightarrow \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )ightarrow \mathcal{K}ightarrow 0.  \] By Serre vanishing theorem, taking $a$ large enough, we may guarantee that \[  \mathrm{H}^1\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})\Bigr )=0  \] and \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{K}\Bigr )
eq 0.  \] Then \[   egin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)\Bigr )
eq \  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Thus, $H
ot\in A$. We conclude that $\mathcal{G}$ is co-pluripolar. $\square$ 3. ↩ This subtle point was overlooked in the proof of [ XiaBer ] . Remark 20.2.48 . E131A2FB1C6A More generally, the same technique implies the following general result: Let $f\colon Xightarrow Y$ be a projective morphism between complex manifolds and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Then for quasi-every 4 $y\in Y$, the fiber $X_ y$ is smooth and \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda h|_{X_ y})=\operatorname{Res}_{X_ y}\left( \mathcal{I}(\lambda h) ight).  \] 4. ↩ That is, for all $y$ outside a pluripolar subset of $Y$. In the sequel of this section, we fix a base-point free linear system $\Lambda $ on $X$. For the results below that assert connectedness, we assume in addition that the set of connected smooth members of $\Lambda $ is co-pluripolar in $\Lambda $. Corollary 20.2.49 . 50ABF7A3834B Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, we have $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $. Proof. For quasi-every $H$, theorem 20.2.45 gives \[  \mathcal I(\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_ H\mathcal I(\varphi ).  \] After removing the hyperplanes meeting the associated points of $\mathcal O_ X/\mathcal I(\varphi )$ improperly, the right-hand side is non-zero. Since $\mathcal I(-\infty )=0$, this implies $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $. $\square$ Corollary 20.2.50 . B590E31078F3 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, satisfies $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi |_ H.  \] The connectedness assumption on $H$ is used here because we developed most of the trace theory above for connected submanifolds. Proof. First observe that the set $\{ x\in X:
u (\varphi ,x)>0\} $ is a countable union of proper analytic subsets by Siu's semicontinuity theorem theorem 5.16.7 . It follows that a very general element in $\Lambda $ is not contained in this set. Fix an ample line bundle $L$ so that there is a smooth Hermitian metric $h_ L$ such that $c_1(L,h_ L)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Thanks to theorem 20.2.45 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies the following: 51A1BB87BE61 $H$ is smooth and connected; FB6AE3B7BE82 $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; 0B98F656C5AC $\mathcal{I}(k\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_{H}(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for all $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Put $\alpha _ H\coloneqq c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H$. It follows from theorem 20.2.39 and theorem 18.1.46 that \[  \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{c_1(L,h_ L)}(\varphi )ight)^{n-1} = \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}\left[\varphi |_ Hight]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^{n-1}.  \] Since $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ by proposition 20.2.12 , we also have $\varphi |_ H\preceq _{\mathcal I}\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$. Hence \[  P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\varphi |_ H]_{\mathcal I}\leq P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The trace is $\mathcal I$-good, so the right-hand side agrees with its $P$-envelope. The equality of the masses above and theorem 16.3.15 then imply that the two sides have the same $P$-singularity type, hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] $\square$ Lemma 20.2.51 . CB547C0AF98F Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $T|_ H$ is well-defined and satisfies \[  \int _ H T|_ H^{n-1}>0.  \] Proof. Write $T=	heta _{\varphi }$ for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Thanks to 13.13.47 , we can find $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ such that $	heta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. By corollary 20.2.49 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: E5EC90FDBEC6 $H$ is smooth and connected; 97B532CFCEDC the restriction $\psi |_ H$ is not identically $-\infty $. Since $	heta _\psi $ is a Kähler current, its restriction to such an $H$ has positive non-pluripolar mass. As $\psi |_ H\leq \varphi |_ H$, theorem 13.13.11 gives \[  \int _ H(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H)^{n-1} \geq \int _ H(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H)^{n-1}>0.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$ Corollary 20.2.52 . 3AEE64F8D403 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{\{ T\} |_ H}(T)$ is well-defined and has positive volume. Proof. Write $T=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and set $\psi =P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Then $\psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ and \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\psi }^{n}=\operatorname{vol}T>0.  \] By 20.2.51 , for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, the hypersurface $H$ is connected and smooth, $\psi |_ H$ is well-defined, and \[  \int _ H \left(	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ Hight)^{n-1}>0.  \] For such $H$, corollary 20.2.50 gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi |_ H$. Since $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, proposition 20.2.21 also gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )$. The assertion now follows from example 20.2.17 . $\square$ Proposition 20.2.53 . A2BD7EA3B4B4 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \psi |_ H$. Proof. Thanks to 16.8.13 , we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. It suffices to show that $\varphi |_ H\sim _ P \psi |_ H$ for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $. Take a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $	heta $ on $X$ so that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. It suffices to compare $\varphi $ and $\psi $ with $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]$, so without loss of generality, we may assume that $\psi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Up to adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may then assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. It follows from 13.13.30 that we can find a sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ such that \[  j^{-1}\eta _ j+\left(1-j^{-1}ight)\psi \leq \varphi  \] for all $j\geq 2$. By corollary 20.2.49 , 20.2.51 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: 402CADA317DA $H$ is smooth and connected; 001701E8EE1D $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 2$ and $\psi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 16.4.2 into account, we arrive at \[  j^{-1} P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\eta _ j|_ H igr ]+\left(1-j^{-1}ight)P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\psi |_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ]  \] for all $j\geq 2$. The normalized envelopes $P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are uniformly bounded in $L^1$, hence \[  j^{-1}P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\xrightarrow {L^1} 0.  \] We conclude that \[  P_{	heta |_ H}[\psi |_ H]\leq P_{	heta |_ H}[\varphi |_ H]  \] and hence $\psi |_ H\preceq _ P \varphi |_ H$. $\square$ Lemma 20.2.54 . A172685DB2AD Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $	heta $ be a closed smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class and $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Furthermore, assume that $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j$ for each $j>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $\varphi _ j|_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $ for all $j\geq 1$, $\varphi |_ H
ot\equiv -\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 , we may assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Using 13.13.30 , we can find a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $(0,1)$ with limit $0$ and $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ such that $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j$ and \[  \epsilon _ j\eta _ j+(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] By corollary 20.2.49 , 20.2.51 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: BE6DEC237CA9 $H$ is smooth and connected; A069E69D0FE9 $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 1$ and $\varphi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 16.4.2 into account, we arrive at \[  \epsilon _ j P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\eta _ j|_ H igr ]+\left(1-\epsilon _ jight)P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi _ j|_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ].  \] Since the normalized envelopes $P_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are relatively compact in $L^1$, we have $\epsilon _ jP_{	heta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]	o 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $j	o \infty $, we get \[  \lim _{j	o \infty } P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi _ j|_ H igr ]\leq P_{	heta |_ H} igl [\varphi |_ H igr ].  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, so we get an equality here. By theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 16.4.4 , we conclude that \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\int _ H \Bigl (	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}=\int _ H \Bigl (	heta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}.  \] Therefore, using corollary 16.9.14 , we conclude that $\varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H$. $\square$ Corollary 20.2.55 . 8F47DBEBF9D3 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be an $\mathcal{I}$-good potential. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ satisfies: 313ACC732701 $H$ is connected and smooth; B1E793618E4A $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good; 90D0D13FF7DE $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; 68C9040B8FC9 $\operatorname{Tr}_ H \varphi \sim _ P \varphi |_ H$. Furthermore, if $	heta $ is a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, then we can further guarantee, on the same co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. Proof. Choose a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $	heta _0$ representing a big class such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _0)$ and $	heta _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta _0)_{>0}$. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal I$-good, corollary 18.1.14 , theorem 18.1.2 , proposition 16.9.6 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi .  \] Applying 20.2.54 , we find a co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $ such that $H$ is connected and smooth, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are not identically $-\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] For such an $H$, the potentials $\varphi _ j|_ H$ have analytic singularities, hence are $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.10 . It follows from corollary 18.1.9 that $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal I$-good. On the other hand, corollary 20.2.50 gives, after intersecting with another co-pluripolar set of parameters $H$, that $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] The trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 20.2.8 . Since both $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are $\mathcal I$-good, their $\mathcal I$-equivalence identifies their $\mathcal I$-envelopes, which agree with their $P$-envelopes. Hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\varphi |_ H.  \] Finally corollary 20.2.52 shows, after intersecting with one more co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative in $\mathrm{PSH}(H,	heta |_ H)_{>0}$. $\square$ For later use, let us also prove a reverse Bertini theorem here. Lemma 20.2.56 (Reverse Bertini theorem) . A7BAA368EEF9 Let $X$ be a complex manifold, $f\colon Xightarrow \Delta ^*$ be a projective surjective morphism to the punctured unit disk $\Delta ^*$. Let $(L,h)$, $(L,h')$ be Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles on $X$ with the same underlying line bundle. Assume that there is a biholomorphic $S^1$-action on $(X,L)$ making $f$ equivariant and such that $h$ and $h'$ are invariant under this action. Assume that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, $X_ z$ is smooth and $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$. Then $h\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'$. Proof. We need to show that $\mathcal{I}(kh)=\mathcal{I}(kh')$ for every positive integer $k$. It suffices to prove the case $k=1$, since our assumptions are invariant after replacing $h$ and $h'$ by $h^ k$ and $h'^ k$. We will therefore prove $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. First observe that it suffices to prove that 133BE510F62F 20.2.57  egin{equation}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr )=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \end{equation} as subsheaves of $f_*(K_{X}\otimes L)$. In fact, suppose that ( 20.2.57 ) holds. Let $H$ be a $f$-ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Then ( 20.2.57 ) also holds with $L\otimes H^ m$ in place of $L$. It follows from Grauert–Remmert's version of Serre vanishing theorem [ Theorem 2.1(A) , BS76 ] that $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. It remains to prove ( 20.2.57 ). Observe that both sides of ( 20.2.57 ) are locally free by [ Corollary 1.5 , Mat16 ] . We claim that it suffices to show that C42AE95D23AF 20.2.58  egin{equation}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z) \end{equation} for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$. In fact, this implies that the same holds outside a countable subset of $\Delta ^*$. But the set where ( 20.2.58 ) fails has to be $S^1$-invariant, it has to be empty. By cohomology and base change together with the analytic Bertini theorem 20.2.48 , for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, we have \[   egin{split}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h|_{X_ z})\Bigr ),\  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h'|_{X_ z})\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] But we assumed that for quasi-every $z$, $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$, it follows that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, ( 20.2.58 ) holds. The proof is complete. $\square$

title: Theorem 20.2.45
text: Theorem 20.2.45 . 7931695F46E8 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Let $p\colon X\rightarrow \mathbb {P}^ N$ be a morphism ($N\geq 1$). Define \[  \mathcal{G}\coloneqq \Bigl \{ H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|: H'\coloneqq H\cap X \textup{ is smooth and } \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H'})=\operatorname{Res}_{H'}\bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\bigr )\Bigr \} .  \] Then $\mathcal{G}\subseteq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ is co-pluripolar.

title: Remark 20.2.46
text:
Remark 20.2.46 . 6A24558044D5 Here and in the sequel, we slightly abuse the notation by writing $H\cap X$ for $p^{-1}H$, the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $H$. In other words, $H\cap X\coloneqq H	imes _{\mathbb {P}^ N} X$. By definition, any $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ such that $p^{-1}H=\emptyset $ lies in $\mathcal{G}$. Proof. Take an ample line bundle $L$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ such that $c_1(L,h)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq 0$, where $c_1(L,h)$ is the first Chern form of $(L,h)$, namely the curvature form of $h$. We introduce $\Lambda \coloneqq |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|$ to simplify our notations. Step 1 . We prove that the following set is co-pluripolar: \[   egin{split}  \mathcal{G}_{L}\coloneqq \left\{ H\in \Lambda : H\cap X 	ext{ is smooth and } \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )= ight.\  \left. \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr )ight\} . \end{split}  \] Here $\omega _{H\cap X}$ denotes the dualizing sheaf of $H\cap X$. Let $U\subseteq \Lambda 	imes X$ be the closed subvariety whose $\mathbb {C}$-points correspond to pairs $(H,x)\in \Lambda 	imes X$ with $p(x)\in H$. Let $\pi _1\colon Uightarrow \Lambda $ be the natural projection. We may assume that $\pi _1$ is surjective, as otherwise there is nothing to prove. Observe that $U$ is a local complete intersection scheme by Krull's Hauptidealsatz and a fortiori a Cohen–Macaulay scheme. It follows from miracle flatness [ Theorem 23.1 , Mat89 ] that the natural projection $\pi _2\colon Uightarrow X$ is flat. As the fibers of $\pi _2$ over closed points of $X$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb {P}^{N-1}$, it follows that $\pi _2$ is smooth. Thus, $U$ is smooth as well. Moreover, observe that 62AF47325D23 20.2.47  egin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )=\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) \end{equation} by proposition 5.16.22 . In the following, we will construct pluripolar sets $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Sigma _2 \subseteq \Sigma _3\subseteq \Sigma _4\subseteq \Lambda $ such that the behavior of $\pi _1$ is improved successively on the complement of $\Sigma _ i$. Step 1.1 . The usual Bertini theorem shows that there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _1\subseteq \Lambda $ such that $\pi _1$ has smooth fibers outside $\Sigma _1$. Enlarging $\Sigma _1$, we may guarantee that $\pi _1$ and $\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ are both flat outside $\Sigma _1$. See [ Théorème 6.9.1 , EGAIV2 ] . Then after further enlarging $\Sigma _1$ we may assume that $p^{-1}(H)$ avoids all associated points of $\mathcal{O}_ X/\mathcal{I}(\varphi )$, for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. Let $\pi _{1,H}$ denote the fiber of $\pi _1$ at $H$ and write $i_ H\colon \pi _{1,H}ightarrow U$ for the inclusion morphism. We arrive at \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ))=i_ H^*\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )  \] for all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _1$. 3 Step 1.2 . By Grauert's coherence theorem, \[  \mathcal{F}^ i\coloneqq R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L\otimes \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi ) ight)  \] is coherent for all $i$. Here $\omega _{U/\Lambda }$ denotes the relative dualizing sheaf of the morphism $Uightarrow \Lambda $. Thus, there is a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _2\subseteq \Lambda $ such that 94B9B26CA79D $\Sigma _2\supseteq \Sigma _1$. 0FC04CC0A41E The $\mathcal{F}^ i$'s are locally free outside $\Sigma _2$. We write $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}^0$. By cohomology and base change [ Theorem III.12.11 , Har ] , for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _2$, the fiber $\mathcal{F}|_ H$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is given by \[  \mathcal{F}|_ H= \mathrm{H}^0\left(\pi _{1,H},\omega _{U/\Lambda }|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \pi _2^*L|_{\pi _{1,H}}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}(\mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )) ight).  \] Step 1.3 . In order to proceed, we need to make use of the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ on $\mathcal{F}$ defined in [ HPS18 ] . We briefly recall its definition in our setting. By [ Section 22 , HPS18 ] , we can find a proper Zariski closed set $\Sigma _3\subseteq \Lambda $ such that 4DF0186C50EB $\Sigma _3\supseteq \Sigma _2$, 77E34EDD06F8 $\pi _1$ is smooth outside $\Sigma _3$, DC4E272A416D both $\mathcal{F}$ and $\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)/\mathcal{F}$ are locally free outside $\Sigma _3$, and 254A2D20904E for each $i$, \[  R^ i\pi _{1*}\left(\omega _{U/\Lambda }\otimes \pi _2^*L ight)  \] is locally free outside $\Sigma _3$. Then for any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, \[   egin{gathered} \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})ight)\ \subseteq \mathcal{F}|_ H\subseteq \mathrm{H}^0\left(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}ight). \end{gathered}  \] See [ Lemma 22.1 , HPS18 ] . Now we can give the definition of the Hodge metric on $\Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$. Given any $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$, any $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}|_ H$, the Hodge metric is defined as \[  h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha ):=\int _{X\cap H} |\alpha |^2_{h}\mathrm{e}^{-\varphi }\in [0,\infty ].  \] Observe that $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )<\infty $ if and only if $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^0(H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X}))$. Moreover, $h_{\mathcal{H}}(\alpha ,\alpha )>0$ if $\alpha 
eq 0$. It is shown in [ HPS18 ] (cf. [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] ) that $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is indeed a singular Hermitian metric, and it extends to a positive metric on $\mathcal{F}$. Step 1.4 . The determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in \Lambda \setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{H\cap X})\Bigr )
eq \mathcal{F}|_ H.  \] As the map $\pi _2$ is smooth, we have $\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )= \mathcal{I}(\pi _2^*\varphi )$ by proposition 5.16.22 . Under the identification $\pi _{1,H}\cong H\cap X$, we have \[  \operatorname{Res}_{\pi _{1,H}}\Bigl (\pi _2^*\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr )\cong \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\Bigl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi )\Bigr ).  \] Thus, we have the following inclusions: \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  \subseteq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ), \end{split}  \] the right-hand side being $\mathcal{F}|_ H$. Recall that the first inclusion follows from theorem 5.16.26 . Hence, $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is singular at all $H\in |\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^ N}(1)|\setminus \Sigma _3$ such that \[   egin{split} & \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{H\cap X}ight)\Bigr )\  
eq &  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (H\cap X,\omega _{H\cap X}\otimes L|_{H\cap X}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Let $\Sigma _4$ be the union of $\Sigma _3$ and the set of all such $H$. Since the Hodge metric $h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is positive ( [ Theorem 3.3.5 , PT18 ] and [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS18 ] ), its determinant $\det h_{\mathcal{H}}$ is also positive ( [ Proposition 1.3 , Rau15 ] and [ Proposition 25.1 , HPS18 ] ), it follows that $\Sigma _4$ is pluripolar. As a consequence, $\mathcal{G}_{L}$ is co-pluripolar. Step 2 . Fix an ample invertible sheaf $S$ on $X$. The same result holds with $L\otimes S^{\otimes a}$ in place of $L$. Thus, the set \[  A\coloneqq  igcap _{a=0}^{\infty }\mathcal{G}_{L\otimes S^{\otimes a}}  \] is co-pluripolar. For each $H\in \Lambda $ such that $X\cap H$ is smooth and $\mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})
eq \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}(\mathcal{I}(\varphi ))$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be the following cokernel: \[  0ightarrow \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)ightarrow \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X} igl (\mathcal{I}(\varphi ) igr )ightarrow \mathcal{K}ightarrow 0.  \] By Serre vanishing theorem, taking $a$ large enough, we may guarantee that \[  \mathrm{H}^1\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}(\varphi |_{X\cap H})\Bigr )=0  \] and \[  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{K}\Bigr )
eq 0.  \] Then \[   egin{split}  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \mathcal{I}\left(\varphi |_{X\cap H}ight)\Bigr )
eq \  \mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X\cap H,\omega _{X\cap H}\otimes (L\otimes S^{\otimes a})|_{X\cap H}\otimes \operatorname{Res}_{H\cap X}\left(\mathcal{I}(\varphi )ight)\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] Thus, $H
ot\in A$. We conclude that $\mathcal{G}$ is co-pluripolar. $\square$ 3. ↩ This subtle point was overlooked in the proof of [ XiaBer ] .

title: Remark 20.2.48
text: Remark 20.2.48 . E131A2FB1C6A More generally, the same technique implies the following general result: Let $f\colon X\rightarrow Y$ be a projective morphism between complex manifolds and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$. Then for quasi-every 4 $y\in Y$, the fiber $X_ y$ is smooth and \[  \mathcal{I}(\lambda h|_{X_ y})=\operatorname{Res}_{X_ y}\left( \mathcal{I}(\lambda h) \right).  \] 4. ↩ That is, for all $y$ outside a pluripolar subset of $Y$.

title: Corollary 20.2.49
text: Corollary 20.2.49 . 50ABF7A3834B Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, we have $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $. Proof. For quasi-every $H$, theorem 20.2.45 gives \[  \mathcal I(\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_ H\mathcal I(\varphi ).  \] After removing the hyperplanes meeting the associated points of $\mathcal O_ X/\mathcal I(\varphi )$ improperly, the right-hand side is non-zero. Since $\mathcal I(-\infty )=0$, this implies $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.2.50
text:
Corollary 20.2.50 . B590E31078F3 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, satisfies $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$ and we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. First observe that the set $\{ x\in X:
u (\varphi ,x)>0\} $ is a countable union of proper analytic subsets by Siu's semicontinuity theorem theorem 5.16.7 . It follows that a very general element in $\Lambda $ is not contained in this set. Fix an ample line bundle $L$ so that there is a smooth Hermitian metric $h_ L$ such that $c_1(L,h_ L)+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Thanks to theorem 20.2.45 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies the following: 51A1BB87BE61 $H$ is smooth and connected; FB6AE3B7BE82 $
u (\varphi ,H)=0$; 0B98F656C5AC $\mathcal{I}(k\varphi |_ H)=\operatorname{Res}_{H}(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ for all $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Put $\alpha _ H\coloneqq c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H$. It follows from theorem 20.2.39 and theorem 18.1.46 that \[  \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{c_1(L,h_ L)}(\varphi )ight)^{n-1} = \int _ H \left( \alpha _ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}\left[\varphi |_ Hight]_{\mathcal{I}} ight)^{n-1}.  \] Since $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ by proposition 20.2.12 , we also have $\varphi |_ H\preceq _{\mathcal I}\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$. Hence \[  P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\varphi |_ H]_{\mathcal I}\leq P_{c_1(L,h_ L)|_ H}[\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The trace is $\mathcal I$-good, so the right-hand side agrees with its $P$-envelope. The equality of the masses above and theorem 16.3.15 then imply that the two sides have the same $P$-singularity type, hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] $\square$

title: Lemma 20.2.51
text: Lemma 20.2.51 . CB547C0AF98F Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\int _ X T^ n>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $T|_ H$ is well-defined and satisfies \[  \int _ H T|_ H^{n-1}>0.  \] Proof. Write $T=\theta _{\varphi }$ for some smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Thanks to 13.13.47 , we can find $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\theta _{\psi }$ is a Kähler current and $\psi \leq \varphi $. By corollary 20.2.49 and the connectedness assumption on $\Lambda $, we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that each $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: E5EC90FDBEC6 $H$ is smooth and connected; 97B532CFCEDC the restriction $\psi |_ H$ is not identically $-\infty $. Since $\theta _\psi $ is a Kähler current, its restriction to such an $H$ has positive non-pluripolar mass. As $\psi |_ H\leq \varphi |_ H$, theorem 13.13.11 gives \[  \int _ H(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H)^{n-1} \geq \int _ H(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H)^{n-1}>0.  \] We conclude the proof. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.2.52
text: Corollary 20.2.52 . 3AEE64F8D403 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$ with $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\operatorname{Tr}_ H^{\{ T\} |_ H}(T)$ is well-defined and has positive volume. Proof. Write $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ and set $\psi =P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Then $\psi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ and \[  \int _ X \theta _{\psi }^{n}=\operatorname{vol}T>0.  \] By 20.2.51 , for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $, the hypersurface $H$ is connected and smooth, $\psi |_ H$ is well-defined, and \[  \int _ H \left(\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi |_ H\right)^{n-1}>0.  \] For such $H$, corollary 20.2.50 gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi |_ H$. Since $\varphi \sim _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, proposition 20.2.21 also gives $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\psi )$. The assertion now follows from example 20.2.17 . $\square$

title: Proposition 20.2.53
text: Proposition 20.2.53 . A2BD7EA3B4B4 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$. Assume that $\varphi \preceq _ P \psi $. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, and $\varphi |_ H\preceq _ P \psi |_ H$. Proof. Thanks to 16.8.13 , we may replace $\varphi $ by $\varphi \lor \psi $ and assume that $\varphi \sim _ P \psi $. It suffices to show that $\varphi |_ H\sim _ P \psi |_ H$ for quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $. Take a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ so that $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. It suffices to compare $\varphi $ and $\psi $ with $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, so without loss of generality, we may assume that $\psi $ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Up to adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may then assume that $\varphi \leq \psi $. It follows from 13.13.30 that we can find a sequence $(\eta _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  j^{-1}\eta _ j+\left(1-j^{-1}\right)\psi \leq \varphi  \] for all $j\geq 2$. By corollary 20.2.49 , 20.2.51 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: 402CADA317DA $H$ is smooth and connected; 001701E8EE1D $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 2$ and $\psi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 16.4.2 into account, we arrive at \[  j^{-1} P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\eta _ j|_ H\bigr ]+\left(1-j^{-1}\right)P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\psi |_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ]  \] for all $j\geq 2$. The normalized envelopes $P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are uniformly bounded in $L^1$, hence \[  j^{-1}P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\xrightarrow {L^1} 0.  \] We conclude that \[  P_{\theta |_ H}[\psi |_ H]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}[\varphi |_ H]  \] and hence $\psi |_ H\preceq _ P \varphi |_ H$. $\square$

title: Lemma 20.2.54
text: Lemma 20.2.54 . A172685DB2AD Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class and $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. Furthermore, assume that $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j$ for each $j>0$. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ is connected and smooth, $\varphi _ j|_ H\not\equiv -\infty $ for all $j\geq 1$, $\varphi |_ H\not\equiv -\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] Proof. By corollary 16.9.36 , we may assume that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Using 13.13.30 , we can find a decreasing sequence $(\epsilon _ j)_ j$ in $(0,1)$ with limit $0$ and $\eta _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that $\eta _ j\leq \varphi _ j$ and \[  \epsilon _ j\eta _ j+(1-\epsilon _ j)\varphi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] By corollary 20.2.49 , 20.2.51 , we can find a co-pluripolar set $\Lambda '\subseteq \Lambda $ such that any $H\in \Lambda '$ satisfies: BE6DEC237CA9 $H$ is smooth and connected; A069E69D0FE9 $\eta _ j|_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$ for all $j\geq 1$ and $\varphi |_ H\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Therefore, taking proposition 16.4.2 into account, we arrive at \[  \epsilon _ j P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\eta _ j|_ H\bigr ]+\left(1-\epsilon _ j\right)P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi _ j|_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ].  \] Since the normalized envelopes $P_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]$ are relatively compact in $L^1$, we have $\epsilon _ jP_{\theta |_ H}[\eta _ j|_ H]\to 0$ in $L^1$. Letting $j\to \infty $, we get \[  \lim _{j\to \infty } P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi _ j|_ H\bigr ]\leq P_{\theta |_ H}\bigl [\varphi |_ H\bigr ].  \] The reverse inequality is trivial, so we get an equality here. By theorem 13.13.11 and proposition 16.4.4 , we conclude that \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\int _ H \Bigl (\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j|_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}=\int _ H \Bigl (\theta |_ H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi |_ H\Bigr )^{n-1}.  \] Therefore, using corollary 16.9.14 , we conclude that $\varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H$. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.2.55
text: Corollary 20.2.55 . 8F47DBEBF9D3 Assume that $n\geq 2$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ be an $\mathcal{I}$-good potential. Then quasi-every $H\in \Lambda $ satisfies: 313ACC732701 $H$ is connected and smooth; B1E793618E4A $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good; 90D0D13FF7DE $\nu (\varphi ,H)=0$; 68C9040B8FC9 $\operatorname{Tr}_ H \varphi \sim _ P \varphi |_ H$. Furthermore, if $\theta $ is a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then we can further guarantee, on the same co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\in \mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. Proof. Choose a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta _0$ representing a big class such that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _0)$ and $\theta _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta _0)_{>0}$. Since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal I$-good, corollary 18.1.14 , theorem 18.1.2 , proposition 16.9.6 gives \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi .  \] Applying 20.2.54 , we find a co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $ such that $H$ is connected and smooth, the restrictions $\varphi _ j|_ H$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are not identically $-\infty $, and \[  \varphi _ j|_ H\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi |_ H.  \] For such an $H$, the potentials $\varphi _ j|_ H$ have analytic singularities, hence are $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.10 . It follows from corollary 18.1.9 that $\varphi |_ H$ is $\mathcal I$-good. On the other hand, corollary 20.2.50 gives, after intersecting with another co-pluripolar set of parameters $H$, that $\nu (\varphi ,H)=0$ and \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _{\mathcal I}\varphi |_ H.  \] The trace $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 20.2.8 . Since both $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ and $\varphi |_ H$ are $\mathcal I$-good, their $\mathcal I$-equivalence identifies their $\mathcal I$-envelopes, which agree with their $P$-envelopes. Hence \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )\sim _ P\varphi |_ H.  \] Finally corollary 20.2.52 shows, after intersecting with one more co-pluripolar set of $H\in \Lambda $, that $\operatorname{Tr}_ H(\varphi )$ has a representative in $\mathrm{PSH}(H,\theta |_ H)_{>0}$. $\square$

title: Lemma 20.2.56 (Reverse Bertini theorem)
text: Lemma 20.2.56 (Reverse Bertini theorem) . A7BAA368EEF9 Let $X$ be a complex manifold, $f\colon X\rightarrow \Delta ^*$ be a projective surjective morphism to the punctured unit disk $\Delta ^*$. Let $(L,h)$, $(L,h')$ be Hermitian pseudo-effective line bundles on $X$ with the same underlying line bundle. Assume that there is a biholomorphic $S^1$-action on $(X,L)$ making $f$ equivariant and such that $h$ and $h'$ are invariant under this action. Assume that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, $X_ z$ is smooth and $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$. Then $h\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'$. Proof. We need to show that $\mathcal{I}(kh)=\mathcal{I}(kh')$ for every positive integer $k$. It suffices to prove the case $k=1$, since our assumptions are invariant after replacing $h$ and $h'$ by $h^ k$ and $h'^ k$. We will therefore prove $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. First observe that it suffices to prove that 133BE510F62F 20.2.57 \begin{equation}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr )=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \end{equation} as subsheaves of $f_*(K_{X}\otimes L)$. In fact, suppose that ( 20.2.57 ) holds. Let $H$ be a $f$-ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Then ( 20.2.57 ) also holds with $L\otimes H^ m$ in place of $L$. It follows from Grauert–Remmert's version of Serre vanishing theorem [ Theorem 2.1(A) , BS76 ] that $\mathcal{I}(h)=\mathcal{I}(h')$. It remains to prove ( 20.2.57 ). Observe that both sides of ( 20.2.57 ) are locally free by [ Corollary 1.5 , Mat16 ] . We claim that it suffices to show that C42AE95D23AF 20.2.58 \begin{equation}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z) \end{equation} for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$. In fact, this implies that the same holds outside a countable subset of $\Delta ^*$. But the set where ( 20.2.58 ) fails has to be $S^1$-invariant, it has to be empty. By cohomology and base change together with the analytic Bertini theorem 20.2.48 , for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, we have \[  \begin{split}  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h)\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h|_{X_ z})\Bigr ),\\  f_*\Bigl (K_{X}\otimes L\otimes \mathcal{I}(h')\Bigr ) \otimes \mathbb {C}(z)=\mathrm{H}^0\Bigl (X_ z,K_{X}|_{X_ z}\otimes L|_{X_ z}\otimes \mathcal{I}(h'|_{X_ z})\Bigr ). \end{split}  \] But we assumed that for quasi-every $z$, $h|_{X_ z}\sim _{\mathcal{I}}h'|_{X_ z}$, it follows that for quasi-every $z\in \Delta ^*$, ( 20.2.58 ) holds. The proof is complete. $\square$

title: 17.11 Test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: A geodesic ray $(\varphi _ t)_{t\in [0,\infty )}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ records the asymptotic behavior of singularities along a path of potentials. In this chapter we encode the same information in the dual variable $\tau $. Instead of recording the potential at time $t$, the Legendre transform records, for each slope $\tau $, the model potential determined by the part of the ray growing at least linearly with slope $\tau $. This produces a concave decreasing family $\tau \mapsto \Gamma _\tau $ of model potentials; more precisely, a test curve $\Gamma $ is a concave decreasing family $(\Gamma _\tau )_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}$ of model potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. The central result is a correspondence initiated by Ross and Witt Nyström 1 . It is the pluripotential-theoretic analogue of Legendre duality: a test curve gives a geodesic ray by taking a Legendre transform, and a suitable geodesic ray gives back a test curve by the inverse transform. Thus test curves provide an intrinsic language for the singularity data carried by geodesic rays. 1. ↩ Witt and Nyström are both family names of a single person. Some Swedes have double family names. It should not be spelled as Witt-Nyström as some people do in the literature. We first develop test curves as self-contained objects. In section 17.12 we introduce their basic properties, including independence of the auxiliary form, behavior under bimeromorphic morphisms, closedness in the parameter $\tau $, log-concavity of the mass function and the $P$-equivalence relation on test curves. The Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence is proved in section 17.13 , where the Legendre transform is shown to give a bijection between test curves and geodesic rays. The later sections adapt this picture to the singularity types needed elsewhere in the book. In section 17.14 we develop the $\mathcal I$-model version of the theory, including the $\mathcal I$-envelope of a test curve, the transition from $P$-model to $\mathcal I$-model test curves, and the corresponding notion of maximal geodesic ray. Finally, section 17.15 studies sums, translations, maxima, suprema, infima and rescalings of test curves. These operations are needed in the non-Archimedean theory of section 22.1 , where test curves provide the analytic input for the construction of non-Archimedean potentials. Throughout the chapter we freely use the convex-analytic results of section 21.11 . Those results are stated for convex functions; when they are applied to concave functions here, they are applied to the negatives.

title: 17.12 The notion of test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Recall that the notion of model potentials is defined in definition 16.3.18 . Definition 17.12.1 . C8399F09D86D A test curve $\Gamma $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ consists of a real number $\Gamma _{\max }$ together with a map $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ denoted by $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }$ satisfying the following conditions: D665BBFA648A The map $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }$ is concave and decreasing; 99E7A7AB790A $P_{	heta }[\Gamma _{	au }]=\Gamma _{	au }$; 28110BFBC4C9 the potential E3D67CAF2F52 17.12.2  egin{equation}  \Gamma _{-\infty }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma _{	au } \end{equation} satisfies \[  \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }ight)^ n>0.  \] Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. The set of test curves $\Gamma $ with $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\phi $ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. The union of all $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$'s for various model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. By 2 , $\sup _{X}\Gamma _{	au }=0$ for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. So $\Gamma _{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ by proposition 5.14.2 . Thanks to corollary 13.13.12 and 3 , there is $C<\Gamma _{\max }$ so that whenever $	au <C$, we have $\Gamma _{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then it follows that $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is a model potential by proposition 16.4.9 . Remark 17.12.3 . 3D73AB2E32CB Sometimes it is convenient to extend $\Gamma _{	au }$ to $	au \geq \Gamma _{\max }$ as well. This can be done as follows: for $	au >\Gamma _{\max }$, we set $\Gamma _{	au }\equiv -\infty $. For $	au =\Gamma _{\max }$, we set \[  \Gamma _{	au }\coloneqq \inf _{	au '<\Gamma _{\max }}\Gamma _{	au '}\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ).  \] Note that $\Gamma _{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ by corollary 5.17.5 . In general, for any $x\in X$, the map $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ falls into one of the following three categories: A67F5048890E $\Gamma _{	au }(x)\equiv -\infty $; E2DED6E870B0 $\Gamma _{	au }(x)>-\infty $ for all $	au \leq \Gamma _{\max }$; F51FF55AD767 there is $	au (x)\in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max }]$ so that $\Gamma _{	au }(x)>-\infty $ for all $	au \in (-\infty ,	au (x))$, and $\Gamma _{	au }(x)=-\infty $ for all $	au \geq 	au (x)$. The last two possibilities are illustrated in 17.12.4 . 9BE4C00F2E15 17.12.4 The last two pointwise possibilities for $	au \mapsto \Gamma _	au (x)$. Note that 2 is the generic situation. It occurs whenever $x
otin \{ \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}=-\infty \} $. In particular, when this situation occurs, $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ is finite concave, and hence continuous. As a consequence, for any $	au \in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$, we have 5EFADBE6069E 17.12.5  egin{equation}  \Gamma _{	au }=\inf _{	au '<	au }\Gamma _{	au '},\quad \Gamma _{	au }=\operatorname *{sup}_{	au '\in (	au ,\Gamma _{\max })}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma _{	au '} \end{equation} almost everywhere and hence everywhere due to proposition 5.14.6 . Recall that according to our general principle, we speak of model potentials only when a potential has positive mass. Lemma 17.12.6 . 348ACDBCB24E Assume that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have F4B7B1DBBE89 17.12.7  egin{equation}  \int _ X \left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{	au }ight)^ n>0. \end{equation} In particular, $\Gamma _{	au }$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. The notations in the proof below are summarized in 17.12.8 . 20FE43CB91F9 17.12.8 The test curve $\Gamma $. Proof. Fix $	au \in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. By assumption, $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ has positive mass. By corollary 13.13.12 , we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{	au 	o -\infty }\int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n.  \] In particular, for a sufficiently small $	au _0<	au $, we have \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n>0.  \] Now take $	au '\in (	au , \Gamma _{\max })$ and $t\in (0,1)$ so that \[  	au =(1-t)	au '+t	au _0.  \] From the concavity of $\Gamma $, we find that \[  \Gamma _{	au }\geq (1-t)\Gamma _{	au '}+t\Gamma _{	au _0}.  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 , \[  \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n\geq \int _ X 	heta _{(1-t)\Gamma _{	au '}+t\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n\geq t^ n \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au _0}}^ n>0  \] and ( 17.12.7 ) follows. $\square$ Proposition 17.12.9 . B7CD1B90CFDA Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then the map \[  [-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathbb {R},\quad 	au \mapsto \log \int _ X 	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n  \] is continuous and concave on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. Proof. The concavity of this function follows from theorem 13.13.5 and theorem 13.13.11 . The continuity at $-\infty $ is a consequence of corollary 13.13.12 . The continuity on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$ follows from the fact that finite concave functions on open intervals are continuous. $\square$ Definition 17.12.10 . 69529F41AA18 Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is said to be bounded if for $	au $ small enough, $\Gamma _{	au }=\phi $. The subset of bounded test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;\phi )$. In this case, we write 3578A2265BDC 17.12.11  egin{equation}  \Gamma _{\min }\coloneqq \sup \{ 	au \in \mathbb {R}:\Gamma _{	au }=\phi \} . \end{equation} A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is said to have finite energy if 942AC971E484 17.12.12  egin{equation}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max } \int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ n+\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\int _ X	heta _{\Gamma _{	au }}^ n-\int _ X 	heta _{\phi }^ night)\, \mathrm{d}	au >-\infty . \end{equation} When $\phi =V_{	heta }$, we write $\mathbf{E}$ instead of $\mathbf{E}^{\phi }$. The subset of test curves with finite energy in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Example 17.12.13 . 1A17E2EECB2D Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, there is a canonically associated test curve $\Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;V_{	heta })$: Set $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$ and \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }_{	au }=  egin{cases}  V_{	heta },& 	extup{if }	au \leq -1;\  P_{	heta }\left[ (1+	au )\varphi -	au V_{	heta } ight],&  	extup{if }-1<	au <0. \end{cases}  \] Note that $\Gamma ^{\varphi }$ is indeed a test curve, as follows from proposition 16.4.2 . Indeed, the concavity and monotonicity in $	au $ follow from proposition 16.4.2 , and $\Gamma ^\varphi _{-\infty }=V_	heta $ has positive mass. We first observe that the notion of test curves does not really depend on the choice of $	heta $ within its cohomology class. Proposition 17.12.14 . B015D2EA4B4F Let $	heta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $	heta $. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. Let $\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')_{>0}$ be the unique model potential satisfying $\phi \sim \phi '$. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ').  \] This bijection induces the following bijections: \[  \mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^1(X,	heta ';\phi '),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,	heta ';\phi ').  \] These bijections satisfy the obvious cocycle conditions. Proof. Choose $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$ such that $	heta '=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. Given any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$, we observe that $\Gamma '\colon (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ')$ defined as \[  	au \mapsto P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _{	au }-g]  \] lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ')$. In fact, the concavity and monotonicity of $\Gamma '$ follow from proposition 16.4.2 . Moreover, applying proposition 16.4.9 to the increasing net obtained as $	au 	o -\infty $ gives \[  \Gamma '_{-\infty }=P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _{-\infty }-g]=P_{	heta '}[\phi -g]=\phi '.  \] Thus $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ';\phi ')$. Moreover, the choice of $g$ is irrelevant since for any other choice of $g$, say $g'$, we have \[  \Gamma _{	au }-g\sim \Gamma _{	au }-g'  \] for all $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. The inverse construction is obtained by replacing $g$ with $-g$. The boundedness condition is clearly preserved. Finally, by proposition 16.3.10 , for every $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \int _ X(	heta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_	au )^ n=\int _ X(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n,  \] and the same holds for $\phi $ and $\phi '$. Hence the finite energy condition is preserved. The cocycle condition is immediate from the uniqueness of the model representative in a fixed singularity type. $\square$ Proposition 17.12.15 . 2059587BD91B Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xlongrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(Y,\pi ^*	heta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. The bijectivity on the underlying potentials follows from proposition 5.17.8 . The compatibility with model potentials follows from proposition 16.4.1 . These two facts also preserve concavity, monotonicity and the value of $\Gamma _{-\infty }$, hence give the asserted bijection of test curves. $\square$ Next we verify the closedness of a test curve as a family of concave functions, so that no pathology arises in the Legendre transforms considered below. The notion of closedness is recalled in definition 21.11.15 . Proposition 17.12.16 . 7AF1F81E928C Let $\Gamma $ be a test curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. For each $x\in X$, the map $\mathbb {R} 
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$ is a closed concave function. Moreover, the map is proper as long as $\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}(x)
eq -\infty $. Proof. We prove closedness. Fix $x\in X$. Assume that $\Gamma _{	au }(x)
eq -\infty $ for some $	au \in \mathbb {R}$. We only need to argue the upper semicontinuity of $	au \mapsto \Gamma _{	au }(x)$. The upper semicontinuity is clear at $	au \geq \Gamma _{\max }$, so we are reduced to prove the following: E703D3F2D79D 17.12.17  egin{equation}  \Gamma _{	au }=\inf _{	au '<	au }\Gamma _{	au '} \end{equation} for any $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$. Take $	au ''\in (	au ,\Gamma _{\max })$. Outside the polar locus of $\Gamma _{	au ''}$, we know that ( 17.12.17 ) holds by continuity of real-valued concave functions. So ( 17.12.17 ) holds everywhere by proposition 5.14.6 . The final assertion follows from properness of a finite closed concave function on its effective domain. $\square$ Definition 17.12.18 . 37432F25600E Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a smooth closed real positive $(1,1)$-form. Then we define $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta +\omega )_{>0}$ as follows: A6773BF32868 Define \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max };  \] 240BD675E3E0 for each $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, define \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{	au }=P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma _{	au }].  \] It follows from proposition 16.4.2 that the family $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]$ is concave and decreasing. Moreover, since $\omega $ is positive, \[  \int _ X(	heta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n \geq \int _ X(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _	au )^ n>0  \] for every $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, and hence $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_	au $ is a model potential by corollary 16.3.20 . Thus $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta +\omega )_{>0}$. Proposition 17.12.19 . 724BF0CAE002 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{-\infty }=P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma _{-\infty }].  \] Proof. This follows from proposition 16.4.9 . $\square$

title: Definition 17.12.1

text: Definition 17.12.1 . C8399F09D86D A test curve $\Gamma $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ consists of a real number $\Gamma _{\max }$ together with a map $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ denoted by $\tau \mapsto \Gamma _{\tau }$ satisfying the following conditions: D665BBFA648A The map $\tau \mapsto \Gamma _{\tau }$ is concave and decreasing; 99E7A7AB790A $P_{\theta }[\Gamma _{\tau }]=\Gamma _{\tau }$; 28110BFBC4C9 the potential E3D67CAF2F52 17.12.2 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _{-\infty }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma _{\tau } \end{equation} satisfies \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }\right)^ n>0.  \] Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. The set of test curves $\Gamma $ with $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\phi $ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. The union of all $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$'s for various model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$.

text: Remark 17.12.3 . 3D73AB2E32CB Sometimes it is convenient to extend $\Gamma _{\tau }$ to $\tau \geq \Gamma _{\max }$ as well. This can be done as follows: for $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$, we set $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $. For $\tau =\Gamma _{\max }$, we set \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{\tau '<\Gamma _{\max }}\Gamma _{\tau '}\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] Note that $\Gamma _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by corollary 5.17.5 .

title: Lemma 17.12.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.12.6 . 348ACDBCB24E Assume that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then for each $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have F4B7B1DBBE89 17.12.7 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n>0. \end{equation} In particular, $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is a model potential in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proof. Fix $\tau \in (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. By assumption, $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ has positive mass. By corollary 13.13.12 , we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{\tau \to -\infty }\int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n.  \] In particular, for a sufficiently small $\tau _0<\tau $, we have \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau _0}}^ n>0.  \] Now take $\tau '\in (\tau , \Gamma _{\max })$ and $t\in (0,1)$ so that \[  \tau =(1-t)\tau '+t\tau _0.  \] From the concavity of $\Gamma $, we find that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\geq (1-t)\Gamma _{\tau '}+t\Gamma _{\tau _0}.  \] By the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 and the multi-linearity of the non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 , \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n\geq \int _ X \theta _{(1-t)\Gamma _{\tau '}+t\Gamma _{\tau _0}}^ n\geq t^ n \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau _0}}^ n>0  \] and ( 17.12.7 ) follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 17.12.9

text: Proposition 17.12.9 . B7CD1B90CFDA Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the map \[  [-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathbb {R},\quad \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n  \] is continuous and concave on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$. Proof. The concavity of this function follows from theorem 13.13.5 and theorem 13.13.11 . The continuity at $-\infty $ is a consequence of corollary 13.13.12 . The continuity on $(-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })$ follows from the fact that finite concave functions on open intervals are continuous. $\square$

title: Definition 17.12.10

text: Definition 17.12.10 . 69529F41AA18 Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is said to be bounded if for $\tau $ small enough, $\Gamma _{\tau }=\phi $. The subset of bounded test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, we write 3578A2265BDC 17.12.11 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _{\min }\coloneqq \sup \{ \tau \in \mathbb {R}:\Gamma _{\tau }=\phi \} . \end{equation} A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is said to have finite energy if 942AC971E484 17.12.12 \begin{equation}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max } \int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n+\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n\right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau >-\infty . \end{equation} When $\phi =V_{\theta }$, we write $\mathbf{E}$ instead of $\mathbf{E}^{\phi }$. The subset of test curves with finite energy in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$.

title: Example 17.12.13
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Example 17.12.13 . 1A17E2EECB2D Given $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, there is a canonically associated test curve $\Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;V_{\theta })$: Set $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$ and \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  V_{\theta },& \textup{if }\tau \leq -1;\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta } \right],&  \textup{if }-1<\tau <0. \end{cases}  \] Note that $\Gamma ^{\varphi }$ is indeed a test curve, as follows from proposition 16.4.2 . Indeed, the concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 16.4.2 , and $\Gamma ^\varphi _{-\infty }=V_\theta $ has positive mass.

title: Proposition 17.12.14
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.12.14 . B015D2EA4B4F Let $\theta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $\theta $. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. Let $\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ be the unique model potential satisfying $\phi \sim \phi '$. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ').  \] This bijection induces the following bijections: \[  \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ';\phi '),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim }\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ';\phi ').  \] These bijections satisfy the obvious cocycle conditions. Proof. Choose $g\in C^{\infty }(X)$ such that $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. Given any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we observe that $\Gamma '\colon (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')$ defined as \[  \tau \mapsto P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _{\tau }-g]  \] lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ')$. In fact, the concavity and monotonicity of $\Gamma '$ follow from proposition 16.4.2 . Moreover, applying proposition 16.4.9 to the increasing net obtained as $\tau \to -\infty $ gives \[  \Gamma '_{-\infty }=P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _{-\infty }-g]=P_{\theta '}[\phi -g]=\phi '.  \] Thus $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ';\phi ')$. Moreover, the choice of $g$ is irrelevant since for any other choice of $g$, say $g'$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }-g\sim \Gamma _{\tau }-g'  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. The inverse construction is obtained by replacing $g$ with $-g$. The boundedness condition is clearly preserved. Finally, by proposition 16.3.10 , for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \int _ X(\theta '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_\tau )^ n=\int _ X(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _\tau )^ n,  \] and the same holds for $\phi $ and $\phi '$. Hence the finite energy condition is preserved. The cocycle condition is immediate from the uniqueness of the model representative in a fixed singularity type. $\square$

title: Proposition 17.12.15
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.12.15 . 2059587BD91B Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xlongrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{TC}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. The bijectivity on the underlying potentials follows from proposition 5.17.8 . The compatibility with model potentials follows from proposition 16.4.1 . These two facts also preserve concavity, monotonicity and the value of $\Gamma _{-\infty }$, hence give the asserted bijection of test curves. $\square$

title: Remark 17.13.4

text: Remark 17.13.4 . ABB931E35703 Here we do not discuss the case $t<0$ because its behavior is straightforward: take $x\in X$; if $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, then $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=-\infty $; otherwise, $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=\infty $.

title: Proposition 17.13.5
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.13.5 . 1F48BF7602CA Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then 24A2034A1287 17.13.6 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{t>0} \left(\Gamma ^*_ t-t\tau \right) \end{equation} for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Proof. Fix $x\in X$. We want to establish ( 17.13.6 ) at $x$. We distinguish two cases. First suppose that $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ and hence all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. In this case, we have $\Gamma _ t^*(x)=-\infty $ for all $t>0$. Therefore, ( 17.13.6 ) follows trivially. Otherwise, by 17.13.4 , we know that $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)=\infty $ for all $t<0$. The relative interior of the domain of $t\mapsto \Gamma ^*_ t(x)$ is contained in $(0,\infty )$. Therefore, ( 17.13.6 ) follows from theorem 21.11.24 , proposition 17.12.16 . $\square$

title: Lemma 17.13.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.13.7 . BC74B8EA334F Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all $t>0$. In fact, $\Gamma ^*$ is upper semicontinuous as a function of $X\times (0,\infty )$. Proof. We first observe that for each $x\in X$, we have \[  \Gamma _ t^*(x)\leq t\Gamma _{\max }<\infty .  \] Let $R=\{ a+\mathrm{i}b\in \mathbb {C}:a>0,b\in \mathbb {R}\} $. We consider \[  F\colon X\times R\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ),\quad (x,a+\mathrm{i}b)\mapsto \Gamma _ a^*(x).  \] Let $\pi \colon X\times R\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Observe that the upper semicontinuous regularization $G$ of $F$ is $\pi ^*\theta $-psh by proposition 5.14.2 . It suffices to show that $F=G$. We let \[  E\coloneqq \left\{  (x,z)\in X\times R: F(x,z)<G(x,z) \right\} .  \] We want to argue that $E=\varnothing $. Since $F$ is invariant under translations in the imaginary direction of $R$, the same is true for its upper semicontinuous regularization $G$. So $E$ can be written as $B\times \mathrm{i}\mathbb {R}$ for some set $B\subseteq X\times (0,\infty )$. Since $E$ is a pluripolar set by proposition 5.14.5 , it has zero Lebesgue measure. Hence, $B$ has zero Lebesgue measure. For each $x\in X$, write \[  B_ x=\left\{ t\in (0,\infty ): (x,t)\in B \right\} .  \] By Fubini's theorem, $B_ x$ has vanishing $1$-dimensional Lebesgue measure for all $x\in X\setminus Z$, where $Z\subseteq X$ is a subset of measure $0$. We may assume that $Z\supseteq \{ \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}=-\infty \} $ so that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)\neq -\infty $ for all $t>0$. For any $x\in X\setminus Z$, both $t\mapsto F(x,t)$ and $G(x,t)$ are convex functions with values in $\mathbb {R}$ on $(0,\infty )$. They agree almost everywhere, hence everywhere by their continuity. It follows that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have $B_ x=\varnothing $. By proposition 17.13.5 , for any $x\in X$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} (F(x,t)-t\tau ),\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] On the other hand, let DBF41B839C63 17.13.8 \begin{equation}  \chi _{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} (G(x,t)-t\tau ),\quad \tau < \Gamma _{\max },\quad x\in X. \end{equation} By Kiselman's principle proposition 5.14.15 , $\chi _{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. But on $X\setminus Z$, we already know that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\chi _{\tau }$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. By proposition 5.14.6 , \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\chi _{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] Now we conclude that $F(x,t)=G(x,t)$ by corollary 21.11.26 . $\square$
