title: Corollary 17.13.9
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 17.13.9 . 4B87EF03E3EA Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ for all $t>0$. Proof. Fix $t>0$. We already know that $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by 17.13.7 . It suffices to show that \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\sim _ P \phi .  \] From ( 17.13.2 ) and proposition 16.8.28 , we know that \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\sim _ P \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma _{\tau }=\phi .  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Lemma 17.13.10
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.13.10 . C6092031D5B3 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then \[  \sup _ X \Gamma _ t^*=t\Gamma _{\max }  \] for all $t>0$. In particular, $t\mapsto \Gamma ^*_ t-t\Gamma _{\max }$ is a decreasing function in $t>0$. Proof. Since $\Gamma _{\tau }\leq 0$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \sup _ X \Gamma _ t^*\leq t\Gamma _{\max }  \] for all $t>0$. Conversely, for each $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \sup _ X\Gamma _ t^*\geq \sup _ X(t\tau +\Gamma _{\tau })=t\tau .  \] Letting $\tau \to \Gamma _{\max }$ gives the reverse inequality. The final assertion follows directly from the formula \[  \Gamma _ t^*-t\Gamma _{\max }=\sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}\Bigl (\Gamma _\tau -t(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau )\Bigr ).  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Lemma 17.13.11
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.13.11 . 9C6538C4298E Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Proof. It follows from 17.13.7 , ( 17.13.2 ) and proposition 5.14.2 that the restriction of $\Gamma ^*$ to each compact subinterval of $(0,\infty )$ is a subgeodesic. By corollary 17.13.9 , for any $t>0$, $\Gamma ^*_ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. First observe that as $t\to 0+$, we have E5C60BE9B124 17.13.12 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _ t^*\xrightarrow {L^1}\phi . \end{equation} By 17.13.10 and proposition 5.17.3 , it suffices to show each $L^1$-cluster point $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ of $\Gamma _ t^*$ as $t\to 0$ is equal to $\phi $. To see this, first observe that by ( 17.13.2 ), for any fixed $t>0$, \[  \Gamma _ t^*\leq t\Gamma _{\max }+\phi .  \] Therefore, $\psi \leq \phi $. On the other hand, for any fixed $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, by ( 17.13.2 ), we have \[  \Gamma ^*_ t\geq \Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau  \] for any $t>0$. So $\psi \geq \Gamma _{\tau }$ almost everywhere and hence everywhere by proposition 5.14.6 . It follows that $\psi \geq \phi $. Therefore, $\psi =\phi $. Assume that $\Gamma ^*$ is not a geodesic ray. Then we can find $0\leq a<b$ such that $(\Gamma ^*_ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$ differs from the geodesic $(\eta _ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$ from $\Gamma ^*_ a$ to $\Gamma ^*_ b$. The existence of $(\eta _ t)_ t$ is guaranteed by proposition 17.10.24 . We consider the subgeodesic $(\ell _ t)_{t>0}$ given by $\ell _ t=\eta _ t$ for $t\in (a,b)$ and $\ell _ t=\Gamma ^*_ t$ otherwise. Note that $\ell $ is a subgeodesic due to the gluing lemma 17.10.16 . Consider the Legendre transform \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }=\inf _{t>0} (\ell _ t-t\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}.  \] Then $\Gamma '_{\tau }\geq \Gamma _{\tau }$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ by proposition 5.14.15 for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. We claim that BD13D6DEBB93 17.13.13 \begin{equation}  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _{\tau }+(b-a)(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau ),\quad \tau \in \mathbb {R}. \end{equation} Observe that $\Gamma '_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ when $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$ by 17.13.10 . Thus it suffices to consider $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$. Put \[  C_{\tau }\coloneqq (b-a)(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau )\geq 0.  \] For any $s\in [a,b]$, the monotonicity of $t\mapsto \Gamma _ t^*-t\Gamma _{\max }$ from 17.13.10 gives \[  \Gamma _ b^*-b\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau }.  \] Since $\ell _ b=\Gamma _ b^*$, we get \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _ b^*-b\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau },\quad s\in [a,b].  \] For $s\notin [a,b]$, we have $\ell _ s=\Gamma _ s^*$, hence \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau \leq \Gamma _ s^*-s\tau +C_{\tau }.  \] Taking the infimum over all $s>0$ gives \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }\leq \Gamma _{\tau }+C_{\tau }.  \] Therefore, ( 17.13.13 ) follows. In particular, for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have $\Gamma '_{\tau }\sim \Gamma _{\tau }$. Moreover, $\sup _ X\ell _ t\leq t\Gamma _{\max }$ for all $t>0$: this is clear outside $(a,b)$ from 17.13.10 , and on $(a,b)$ it follows from the convexity of subgeodesics applied to the geodesic $(\eta _ t)_{t\in (a,b)}$. Hence, for $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, \[  \sup _ X(\ell _ t-t\tau )\leq t(\Gamma _{\max }-\tau ).  \] Letting $t\to 0+$ gives $\Gamma '_{\tau }\leq 0$. It follows from the fact that $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is a model potential that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\Gamma '_{\tau }$ for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Therefore, by theorem 21.11.24 , we have $\Gamma ^*_ t=\ell _ t$ for all $t>0$, which is a contradiction. $\square$

title: Lemma 17.13.15

text: Lemma 17.13.15 . 7B83BD1D5FB9 Given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, then $\ell ^*=(\ell ^*_\tau )_{\tau <\sup _ X \ell _1}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Proof. Note that it follows from proposition 5.14.15 that $\ell ^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. It is clear that $\mathbb {R}\ni \tau \mapsto \ell ^*_{\tau }$ is a decreasing and concave function. By proposition 17.10.39 , \[  \sup _ X\ell _ t= t\sup _ X \ell _1 \quad \forall t\geq 0.  \] Set $C=\sup _ X\ell _1$. By proposition 17.10.39 , $\sup _ X(\ell _ t-Ct)=0$ for all $t>0$. For each $x$ outside a pluripolar set, the function $t\mapsto \ell _ t(x)-Ct$ is convex on $(0,\infty )$ and bounded above by $0$, hence it is decreasing. By proposition 5.14.6 , the same monotonicity holds as an inequality of $\theta $-psh functions. Thus $(\ell _ t-Ct)_{t>0}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Its infimum is not identically $-\infty $, since the family is normalized by $\sup _ X(\ell _ t-Ct)=0$ and is compact in $L^1$ by proposition 5.17.3 . Therefore \[  \ell ^*_{C}=\inf _{t>0}(\ell _ t-Ct)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )  \] by proposition 5.14.2 . On the other hand, for $\tau >\sup _ X \ell _1$, the same argument shows that \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\equiv -\infty .  \] Therefore, $\ell ^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ if and only if $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }\coloneqq \sup _ X \ell _1$. We claim that $(\ell ^*_{\tau })_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}$ is a test curve. We first observe that for $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \ell _1-\tau \sim _ P \phi .  \] Therefore, 5BF1777D23C2 17.13.16 \begin{equation}  \ell ^*_{\tau }\preceq _ P \phi ,\quad \forall \tau <\ell ^*_{\max }. \end{equation} Also observe that for any $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }$ and any $t>0$, we have \[  \sup _ X \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \sup _ X \ell _ t-t\tau =\ell ^*_{\max }t-t\tau .  \] Letting $t\to 0+$, we find that for any $\tau \leq \ell ^*_{\max }$, we have 6F01D0840C12 17.13.17 \begin{equation}  \sup _ X \ell ^*_{\tau }\leq 0. \end{equation} Fix $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$. We want to argue that 59C9610616F1 17.13.18 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta }\left[\ell ^*_{\tau }\right]=\ell ^*_{\tau }. \end{equation} First we claim that for any $C>0$, we have 25F16D030FA9 17.13.19 \begin{equation}  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi =(\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }. \end{equation} The $\leq $ direction is trivial. We argue the reverse inequality, which reduces to \[  \phi \geq (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }.  \] Since $\phi $ is model and $(\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }\leq 0$, it suffices to show that \[  \phi \succeq _ P (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta },  \] which follows from ( 17.13.16 ). Therefore, ( 17.13.19 ) is established. Thanks to ( 17.13.17 ), we have the obvious inequality \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land V_{\theta }\geq \ell ^*_{\tau }  \] for any $C>0$. Therefore, in order to prove ( 17.13.18 ), it remains to argue that for any $C>0$, CBA3E07AB082 17.13.20 \begin{equation}  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi \leq \ell ^*_{\tau }. \end{equation} For this purpose, let us consider the following geodesics: For any $M>0$ and $t\in [0,1]$, let \[  \ell ^{1,M}_ t= \ell _{tM}-tM\tau ,\quad \ell ^{2,M}_ t= (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Ct.  \] It is clear that at $t=0,1$, we have $\ell ^{2,M}_ t\leq \ell ^{1,M}_ t$. Hence, the same holds for all $t\in [0,1]$. In particular, for any fixed $s\in (0,1]$, we have \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Cs\leq \ell _{sM}-sM\tau  \] for all $M>0$. Taking infimum with respect to $M>0$, we find \[  (\ell ^*_{\tau }+C)\land \phi -Cs\leq \ell ^*_{\tau }.  \] Since $s\in (0,1]$ is arbitrary, we conclude ( 17.13.20 ). Finally, we check the condition at $-\infty $. Set \[  \psi \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\ell ^*_{\tau }.  \] The family $(\ell ^*_{\tau })_{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}$ is locally uniformly bounded from above, so $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Thanks to corollary 17.10.9 , outside a pluripolar set, the function $t\mapsto \ell _ t(x)$ is a finite closed convex function on $[0,\infty )$ with value $\phi (x)$ at $t=0$. Applying the one-variable Legendre duality gives \[  \psi (x)=\adjustlimits \sup _{\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }}\inf _{t>0}\bigl (\ell _ t(x)-t\tau \bigr )=\ell _0(x)=\phi (x)\quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Hence $\psi =\phi $ by proposition 5.14.6 . In particular, $\ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi $ has positive mass. $\square$

title: Theorem 17.13.21
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Theorem 17.13.21 . B28F0A28CB3E The Legendre transform in definition 17.13.1 is a bijection 6D5BA4827FF5 17.13.22 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation} Moreover, this bijection restricts to the following bijections: AE510D6D0C2F 17.13.23 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi ),\quad \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ). \end{equation} For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we have 4884EC5C8FA9 17.13.24 \begin{equation}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^*). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first establish ( 17.13.22 ). It follows from 17.13.11 that the forward map is well-defined. The inverse map is given by ( 17.13.14 ). We show that the inverse map is also well-defined. Given $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we know from 17.13.15 that $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We need to show that $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. The equality $\ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi $ was proved in 17.13.15 . Therefore, $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as expected. The two operations are inverse to each other thanks to corollary 21.11.26 . Hence, ( 17.13.22 ) is established. Step 2 . Next we consider the bounded situation. Namely, we want to establish the second half of ( 17.13.23 ). Suppose that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Take $\tau _0\in \mathbb {R}$ so that $\Gamma _{\tau }=\phi $ for all $\tau \leq \tau _0$. It follows from ( 17.13.2 ) that \[  \Gamma _ t^*\geq \phi +t\tau _0  \] for all $t>0$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^*_ t\sim \phi $ for all $t>0$ and hence $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Conversely, suppose that $\ell \in \mathcal{R}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Thanks to proposition 17.10.37 , there is a constant $C>0$ such that \[  \ell _ t\geq \phi -Ct.  \] Therefore, according to ( 17.13.14 ), we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }\geq \inf _{t>0} \Bigl ( \phi -(C+\tau )t \Bigr )=\phi  \] if $\tau \leq -C$. Therefore, $\ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi $ for all $\tau \leq -C$. Step 3 . We establish ( 17.13.24 ) and the first half of ( 17.13.23 ). Step 3.1 . We reduce to the case where $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Suppose that we define \[  \Gamma '_{\tau }=\Gamma _{\tau +\Gamma _{\max }},\quad \forall \tau <0.  \] Then $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as well and for all $t>0$, \[  \Gamma '^*_ t=\sup _{\tau <0} \left( t\tau +\Gamma '_{\tau } \right)=\sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left( t\tau +\Gamma _{\tau } \right)-t\Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma ^*_ t-t\Gamma _{\max }.  \] Therefore, \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }\left(\Gamma '^*\right)=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*\right)-\Gamma _{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] by ( 16.5.13 ). Using ( 17.12.12 ), we also have \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ')=& \int _{-\infty }^0 \left( \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma '_{\tau }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\left( \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n \right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )-\Gamma _{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, it suffices to establish ( 17.13.24 ) for $\Gamma '$ in place of $\Gamma $. Step 3.2 . We assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$ and $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$. We prove ( 17.13.24 ). For $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $M \in \mathbb {Z}$, we introduce the following: \[  \Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t \coloneqq \max _{\substack {k \in \mathbb {Z} \\ k \leq M}} \left(\Gamma _{k/2^ N} + tk/2^ N\right)\in \mathcal{E}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi ),\quad t>0.  \] We first claim that for all $t>0$, $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and $M\in \mathbb {Z}_{<0}$, 1C55A624E61E 17.13.25 \begin{equation}  \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\leq \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}. \end{equation} Assuming this, let us prove ( 17.13.24 ). Fixing $N$, let $M=\lfloor 2^{N}\Gamma _{\min }\rfloor $. Recall that $\Gamma _{\min }$ is defined in ( 17.12.11 ). Then repeated applications of ( 17.13.25 ) yield \[  \sum _{j=M+1}^0 \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}}\leq E^{\phi }_{\theta }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}\right)-E^{\phi }_{\theta }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\leq \sum _{j=M}^{-1} \frac{t}{2^ N} \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}}.  \] Since $M \leq 2^{N}\Gamma _{\min }$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t =\phi +t M/2^ N.  \] Using ( 16.5.13 ), we can continue to write \[  \sum _{j=M+1}^0 \frac{t}{2^ N} \left(\int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}} - \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\phi }\right)\leq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}\right)\leq \sum _{j=M}^{-1} \frac{t}{2^ N} \left(\int _ X \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{j/2^ N}} - \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\phi }\right).  \] We now notice that we have Riemann sums on both the left and right of the above inequality. Moreover, as $N\to \infty $, the potentials $\Gamma _ t^{*,N,0}$ increase to $\Gamma _ t^*$, hence their energies converge to $E^\phi _\theta (\Gamma _ t^*)$ by proposition 16.5.37 . Using proposition 17.12.9 , it is possible to let $N \to \infty $ and obtain 85E0D04C585D 17.13.26 \begin{equation}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*})=t\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ) \end{equation} So ( 17.13.24 ) follows as desired. It remains to argue ( 17.13.25 ). Fix $t>0$, $N\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ and $M\in \mathbb {Z}$. By proposition 16.5.36 , 877135CB19C2 17.13.27 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}}\leq &  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\\  \leq &  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Clearly $\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1} \geq \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}$. Moreover, since $\mathbb {R}\ni \tau \mapsto \Gamma _{\tau }+t\tau $ is concave, we notice that \[  U_ t \coloneqq \left\{ \Gamma ^{*,N,M+1}_ t>\Gamma ^{*,N,M}_ t\right\}  = \left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N} + 2^{-N}t >\Gamma _{M/2^ N}\right\} ,  \] and on $U_ t$ we have 23E6778F003A 17.13.28 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1} = \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N} + t (M+1)/2^{N},\quad \Gamma _ t^{*,N,M} = \Gamma _{M/2^ N} + t M /2^{N}. \end{equation} We also note that $U_ t$ is $\mathcal{F}$-open by corollary 5.15.19 . So from the lower bound in ( 17.13.27 ), we have \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}\right)-E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\geq &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}}\\  = &  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}\\  \geq &  \int _{\left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0\right\} }t2^{-N}\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}, \end{aligned}  \] where on the second line, we applied ( 17.13.28 ) and proposition 13.11.4 , on the third line, we applied the fact that $\theta _{\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}}^ n$ is supported on the set (cf. theorem 16.3.12 ) \[  \left\{ \Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}=0\right\} \subseteq U_ t\cap \left\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\right\} .  \] When $(M+1)/2^ N=0$, we use proposition 16.4.3 to see that $P_\theta [\Gamma _0]=\Gamma _0$, since $\Gamma _0$ is the decreasing limit of the model potentials $\Gamma _\tau $ as $\tau \nearrow 0$. Thus theorem 16.3.12 applies to this endpoint as well. We have deduced the first inequality in ( 17.13.25 ). Next, we apply the upper bound part in ( 17.13.27 ) and compute similarly \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1})-E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M})\leq &  \int _ X \left(\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M+1}-\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _ t^{*,N,M}}\\  =&  \int _{U_ t} \left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}-\Gamma _{M/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}\\  \leq &  \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t}\left(\Gamma _{(M+1)/2^ N}+t2^{-N}\right)\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}} \\  \leq & \int _{\{ \Gamma _{M/2^ N}=0\} \cap U_ t} t2^{-N}\, \theta ^ n_{\Gamma _{M/2^ N}}. \end{aligned}  \] We conclude the latter half of ( 17.13.25 ). Step 3.3 . We assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Now $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ only. For each $\epsilon >0$, we introduce $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\phi )$ as follows: 1E08B0569766 Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and 70863808F7A7 we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  \phi ,& \textup{if }\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1};\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _{\tau }-\epsilon \tau \phi \right],& \textup{if }\tau \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0\right). \end{cases}  \] The concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 16.4.2 . The value at $-\infty $ is $\phi $. Moreover, $\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau =\phi $ for $\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1}$, so $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{TC}^\infty (X,\theta ;\phi )$. It follows from corollary 16.9.38 and corollary 16.9.14 that for each $\tau <0$, the potentials $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }$ decrease to $\Gamma _{\tau }$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Applying proposition 16.4.4 , we have \[  \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n  \] for all $\tau <0$. Hence, by the monotone convergence theorem and Step 3.2, we find DBCF50A40C12 17.13.29 \begin{equation}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon })=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *})=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1), \end{equation} where the last equality follows from ( 17.13.26 ). Furthermore, according to proposition 21.11.36 , we have \[  \Gamma ^*_ t=\inf _{\epsilon >0} \Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_ t  \] for all $t>0$. Note that we do not have to take the closure of the right-hand side since it is automatically upper semicontinuous in $t$. Now suppose that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then by ( 17.13.29 ), as $\epsilon \to 0+$, $(\Gamma _ t^{\epsilon *})_{\epsilon }$ is a decreasing Cauchy net in $\mathcal{E}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and hence by theorem 17.10.63 for each $t>0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_ t\right)=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon ,*}_ t\right)=t\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )>-\infty ,  \] where we have applied ( 17.13.26 ) and ( 17.13.29 ). Hence, $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Moreover, ( 17.13.24 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\Gamma ^*\in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then ( 17.13.29 ) implies that \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma )=\lim _{\epsilon \to 0+} E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^{\epsilon *}_1\right) \geq E_{\theta }^{\phi }\left(\Gamma ^*_1\right)>-\infty .  \] Hence, $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. $\square$

text: Remark 17.13.30 . E10A1DEDC7AF One could also consider geodesic rays emanating from another potential $\Phi \in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In this case, one can show that these geodesic rays are in bijection with $\Phi $-twisted test curves: In definition 17.12.1 , we replace 2 by the following condition: \[  P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right](\Phi )=\Gamma _{\tau }.  \] Furthermore, we require that $\Gamma _{-\infty }=\Phi $. The above results equally work in the twisted setting. The proofs are almost identical to the untwisted case.

text: Corollary 17.13.31 . 82AB68443E01 Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\sup _ X \ell _ t=\ell ^*_{\max }t$ for any $t\geq 0$. In particular, $\ell _ t-\ell ^*_{\max }t$ is a decreasing function of $t\geq 0$. Proof. This follows from 17.13.10 and theorem 17.13.21 . $\square$

title: Example 17.13.32
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Example 17.13.32 . E2332A16AF00 Let us see what the test curve in example 17.12.13 corresponds to under the Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We claim that D50F33814868 17.13.33 \begin{equation}  \ell ^{\varphi }=\Gamma ^{\varphi *}, \end{equation} where $\ell ^{\varphi }$ is as in example 17.10.92 . We may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ since both sides are invariant after adding a constant to $\varphi $. We first prove the easy direction $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$, which is equivalent to $\ell ^{\varphi *}\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi }$. Since $\ell ^{\varphi *}$ is a test curve, the latter is equivalent to \[  \ell ^{\varphi *}_{\tau }\geq (1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }  \] for all $\tau \in (-1,0)$. By Legendre duality, this is equivalent to F5A9BEF8F7BA 17.13.34 \begin{equation}  \ell ^{\varphi }_ t\geq \sup _{\tau \in (-1,0)} \Bigl ((1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }+t\tau \Bigr )=\varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-t) \end{equation} for all $t>0$. Using the notations of example 17.10.92 , we find easily that \[  \ell ^{\varphi ,C}_ t\geq \varphi \lor (V_{\theta }-t)  \] for any $C>0$ and $t\in [0,C]$, since it holds at $t=0$ and $t=C$. Letting $C\to \infty $, we find ( 17.13.34 ). Therefore, $\ell ^{\varphi }\geq \Gamma ^{\varphi *}$ follows. In order to prove the equality in ( 17.13.33 ), it suffices to show that the two sides have the same energy, as a consequence of ( 17.10.84 ). So we compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi *}\right)=&  \mathbf{E}\left(\Gamma ^{\varphi }\right)\\  =&  \int _{-1}^0 \left(\int _ X \theta _{(1+\tau )\varphi -\tau V_{\theta }}^ n-\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n} \binom {n}{j} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j} \int _0^1 \tau ^ j (1-\tau )^{n-j}\, \mathrm{d}\tau -\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  =&  \sum _{j=0}^{n} \binom {n}{j}\frac{j!(n-j)!}{(n+1)!} \int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^{j}\wedge \theta _{V_{\theta }}^{n-j}-\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n\\  =&  \mathbf{E}(\ell ^{\varphi }), \end{aligned}  \] where in the second line we used proposition 16.3.10 , in the fourth line we used the value of the $\beta $-function 2 , and the last line is just ( 17.10.94 ). 2. ↩ Also known as Euler integral of the first kind.

title: Proposition 17.13.35 (He–Testorf–Wang)
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.13.35 (He–Testorf–Wang) . E6915C7339CD Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Given any $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $x\in X$, we have DA238F3ECC6F 17.13.36 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{I}\left(\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)_{x}=\left\{  f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}: |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t\tau )\, \mathrm{d}t \textup{ is integrable near }x \right\} . \end{equation} Proof. Fix $x\in X$, $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$ and $f\in \mathcal{O}_{X,x}$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Step 1 . We first assume that $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 17.13.36 ). Given any $y\in X$, it follows from ( 17.13.14 ) that there is $t_0>0$ with \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0\tau .  \] Observe that $t\mapsto \ell _ t-t\ell ^*_{\max }$ is decreasing in $t$ by corollary 17.13.31 , it follows that for $t\in [t_0,t_0+1]$, we have \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1-t_0(\ell ^*_{\max }-\tau )\geq \ell _{t_0}(y)-t_0\ell ^*_{\max }\geq \ell _{t}(y)-t\ell ^*_{\max }.  \] Since $\tau < \ell ^*_{\max }$ and $t_0\geq t-1$, we deduce that 77E18B7AC795 17.13.37 \begin{equation}  \ell ^*_{\tau }(y)+1+\ell ^*_{\max }-\tau \geq \ell _{t}(y)-t\tau ,\quad t\in [t_0,t_0+1]. \end{equation} Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp (-\ell _ t+t\tau )\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Applying ( 17.13.37 ), we deduce that \[  \int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] Therefore, $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau })_ x$. Step 2 . Assume that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau })_ x$. It follows from the strong openness theorem theorem 5.16.21 (cf. ( 17.12.5 )) that $f\in \mathcal{I}(\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon })_ x$ for some small enough $\epsilon >0$ with $\tau +\epsilon <\ell ^*_{\max }$. Take a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that \[  \int _ U |f|^2 \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }\right)\, \omega ^ n<\infty .  \] We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell _ t+t\tau \right)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\leq &  \int _ U |f|^2\int _0^{\infty } \exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }-t\epsilon \right)\, \mathrm{d}t\, \omega ^ n\\  =& \frac{1}{\epsilon }\int _ U |f|^2\exp \left(-\ell ^*_{\tau +\epsilon }\right)\, \omega ^ n\\  <& \infty . \end{aligned}  \] Therefore, $f$ lies in the right-hand side of ( 17.13.36 ). $\square$

title: Proposition 17.13.38 (Hisamoto)
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.13.38 (Hisamoto) . 3746B0074A79 Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Given any $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have 16A5FF346A3B 17.13.39 \begin{equation}  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\ell ^*_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} } \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$. We first observe that it suffices to show that 0893138962D7 17.13.40 \begin{equation}  \int _{\left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \right\} } \theta _{\phi }^ n=\int _{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} } \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} Assuming ( 17.13.40 ) for the moment. By theorem 17.13.21 , $\ell ^*\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. In particular, $\ell ^*_\tau $ is a model potential and \[  \ell ^*_\tau \leq \ell ^*_{-\infty }=\phi .  \] Since $\phi $ is model as well, proposition 16.3.41 gives \[  \theta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n,\quad \theta ^ n_{\phi }=\mathds {1}_{\{ \phi =0\} }\, \theta ^ n.  \] Since $\ell ^*_{\tau }\leq \phi \leq 0$, we have \[  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} }\, \theta _{\phi }^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi =0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n =\mathds {1}_{\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=0\right\} }\, \theta ^ n =\theta ^ n_{\ell ^*_{\tau }}.  \] Therefore, ( 17.13.39 ) follows from ( 17.13.40 ). In order to prove ( 17.13.40 ), it suffices to show that 7F6505CF081C 17.13.41 \begin{equation}  \left\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \right\} =\left\{ \ell ^*_{\tau }=\phi \right\} \quad \textup{outside a pluripolar set}. \end{equation} Take $x\in X$ so that $(\ell _ t(x))_{t\geq 0}$ is finite and right-differentiable at $t=0$. Note that this condition holds quasi-everywhere. Suppose that $\ell ^*_{\tau }(x)=\phi (x)$. Then \[  \dot{\ell }_0(x)=\inf _{t>0} \frac{\ell _ t(x)-\phi (x)}{t}\geq \inf _{t>0} \frac{\ell ^*_{\tau }(x)+t\tau -\phi (x)}{t}=\tau .  \] Therefore, the $\supseteq $ direction in ( 17.13.41 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $\dot{\ell }_0(x)\geq \tau $, then \[  \ell ^*_{\tau }(x)=\inf _{t>0} \left(\ell _ t(x)-t\tau \right)\geq \inf _{t>0} \left(\phi (x)+t\dot{\ell }_0(x)-t\tau \right)\geq \phi (x).  \] Together with $\ell ^*_\tau \leq \phi $, this gives $\ell ^*_\tau (x)=\phi (x)$. Therefore, the $\subseteq $ direction in ( 17.13.41 ) follows as well. $\square$

text: Corollary 17.13.42 . F147312B98B3 Let $\ell \in \mathcal{R}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then $\dot{\ell }_0\in L^1(X,\theta _{\phi }^ n)$ and DA97CC2A78DC 17.13.43 \begin{equation}  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, \theta _{\phi }^ n. \end{equation} In particular, for every $t\geq 0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\ell _ t)=t\int _ X \dot{\ell }_0\, \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Proof. Set $\Gamma =\ell ^*$. By theorem 17.13.21 , we have $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\phi )$ and \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell )=\mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\Gamma ).  \] By proposition 17.13.38 , for every $\tau <\ell ^*_{\max }$, \[  \int _ X \theta _{\Gamma _{\tau }}^ n=\int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} } \theta _{\phi }^ n.  \] Hence ( 17.12.12 ) gives \[  \mathbf{E}^{\phi }(\ell ) =\ell ^*_{\max }\int _ X \theta _{\phi }^ n-\int _{-\infty }^{\ell ^*_{\max }} \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0<\tau \} }\theta _{\phi }^ n\, \mathrm{d}\tau .  \] For $\tau >\ell ^*_{\max }$, we have $\ell ^*_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ by 17.13.15 . Then ( 17.13.40 ) shows that \[  \int _{\{ \dot{\ell }_0\geq \tau \} }\theta _{\phi }^ n=0.  \] The layer-cake formula therefore gives ( 17.13.43 ). The final assertion follows from proposition 17.10.65 , since $E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\ell _0)=E_{\theta }^{\phi }(\phi )=0$. $\square$

title: 17.14 $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Fix a model potential $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Definition 17.14.1 . 6CC72AA0EA90 A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model if for any $	au <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma _{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. The subset of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. When $\phi =V_{	heta }$, we omit $\phi $ and write $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$ instead. The union of the sets of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ for all model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Note that $\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}$ is automatically $\mathcal{I}$-model, since \[  \Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}\leq P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}ight]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq \inf _{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}=\inf _{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}\Gamma _{	au }=\Gamma _{\Gamma _{\max }}.  \] Here we write $\mathrm{NA}$ with non-Archimedean in mind. The precise relation with non-Archimedean pluripotential theory will be clear in section 22.1 . This section and the next can be skipped on a first reading; the necessary results can be consulted when reading section 22.1 . Proposition 17.14.2 . 683BF9BB4D63 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Proof. This follows from proposition 16.6.30 . $\square$ Proposition 17.14.3 . A9AB5CE3BCAB Let $	heta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $	heta $. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ')_{>0}.  \] This bijection satisfies the obvious cocycle condition. Proof. Let $	heta '=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. By proposition 17.12.14 , the canonical map sends $\Gamma $ to the test curve with levels \[  \Gamma '_	au =P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g].  \] If $\Gamma _	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model, then it is $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.11 . Note that $\Gamma _	au -g$ is $\mathcal I$-good since $\Gamma _{	au }$ is. Hence \[  P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g]=P_{	heta '}[\Gamma _	au -g]_{\mathcal I},  \] so $\Gamma '_	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model. The same argument applied to $-g$ gives the inverse map, and the cocycle condition follows from the one in proposition 17.12.14 . $\square$ Proposition 17.14.4 . 92E487FB0DA8 Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*	heta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 17.12.15 and proposition 16.6.10 . $\square$ Definition 17.14.5 . 03BED679B3AD Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$, we define its $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{	heta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta ),\quad 	au \mapsto P_{	heta }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we define $P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })ightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega ),\quad 	au \mapsto P_{	heta +\omega }\left[\Gamma _{	au }ight]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proposition 17.14.6 . BF40FB71C62C Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. Then \[  P_{	heta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;P_{	heta }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{	heta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta +\omega ;P_{	heta +\omega }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] Proof. We prove the first assertion; the second is identical, replacing $	heta $ by $	heta +\omega $. Set \[  \widetilde\Gamma _	au \coloneqq P_	heta [\Gamma _	au ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The family is decreasing by 16.6.28 . If $	au =(1-s)	au _0+s	au _1$, then the concavity of $\Gamma $ gives \[  \Gamma _	au \geq (1-s)\Gamma _{	au _0}+s\Gamma _{	au _1}.  \] Hence, by 16.6.28 and proposition 16.6.27 , \[  \widetilde\Gamma _	au \geq (1-s)\widetilde\Gamma _{	au _0}+s\widetilde\Gamma _{	au _1}.  \] Thus the family is concave. Finally, \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{	au <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\widetilde\Gamma _	au = P_	heta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}  \] follows from proposition 16.6.30 . Since $P_	heta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}\geq \phi $, its mass is positive by the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . This proves the assertion. $\square$ Definition 17.14.7 . 6C763D5B798A Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A geodesic ray $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,	heta ;\phi )$ is maximal if $\ell ^*$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, namely, if $\ell ^*\in \mathcal E^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta ;\phi )$. An important class of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves is given by filtrations. We briefly recall the corresponding terminology. Definition 17.14.8 . D6CC0BBA6D35 Let $L$ be a big line bundle. We write \[  R(X,L)= igoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)  \] for the section ring 1 of $L$. A filtration on $R(X,L)$ is a decreasing family of graded linear subspaces $(\mathcal{F}^{\lambda })_{\lambda \in \mathbb {R}}$ of $R(X,L)$ with graded pieces \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }= igoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k,  \] such that the following conditions are satisfied: The filtration is left-continuous: For any $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }= igcap _{\lambda '<\lambda }\mathcal{F}^{\lambda '};  \] the filtration is multiplicative: For any $\lambda ,\lambda '\in \mathbb {R}$ and any $k,k'\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\cdot \mathcal{F}^{\lambda '}_{k'}\subseteq \mathcal{F}^{\lambda +\lambda '}_{k+k'};  \] there is an integer $C>0$ such that F76F341D25A8 17.14.9  egin{equation}  \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation} for all $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Given a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ on $R(X,L)$, we define \[  	au _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup \left\{ \lambda \in \mathbb {R}: \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k
eq 0ight\} .  \] By Fekete's lemma, we can introduce \[  	au (\mathcal{F})=\lim _{k	o \infty } rac{1}{k}	au _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}	au _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] 1. ↩ It is more natural to replace the direct sum by a disjoint union, leading to the notion of ringoids ( annénoïdes in French), introduced by Ducros in [ Duc21 ] in the context of Temkin's graded reduction of Berkovich germs. Note that $	au (\mathcal{F})$ is bounded from above by the constant $C$ in ( 17.14.9 ), hence finite. Example 17.14.10 . 20A8C7BFE0BB Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be a filtration on $R(X,L)$. Fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ and write $	heta =c_1(L,h)$. We introduce a few auxiliary functions. For each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we introduce \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \log |s|_{h^ k}^2: s\in \mathcal{F}^{k	au }_ k, |s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1 ight\} .  \] When $k	au \leq 	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $\mathcal{F}_ k^{k	au }
eq 0$. Moreover, proposition 5.20.4 and proposition 5.14.2 imply that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,k	heta ),\quad 	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] Observe that for $k,k'\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k+k'}_{	au }\geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }+\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k'}_{	au }.  \] In particular, by Fekete's lemma, 79C9CAB675E4 17.14.11  egin{equation}  \lim _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au } \end{equation} exists for any $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. We define $(\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au })_{	au <	au (\mathcal{F})}$ as follows: \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }\coloneqq P_{	heta }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }ight]{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000078461}{2}}.  \] We claim that $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$ and is bounded. It is clear that $(-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F}))
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is decreasing. We prove its concavity. By proposition 16.4.2 , it suffices to show that \[  \Bigl (-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F})\Bigr )
i 	au \mapsto \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }  \] is concave. In other words, we need to prove the following: Given $	au _0<	au _1<	au (\mathcal{F})$ and $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}.  \] But thanks to proposition 5.14.6 and proposition 5.14.5 , it suffices to show that \[  \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}  \] for all $t\in (0,1)$. Take $s_ i\in \mathcal{F}^{k_ i	au _ i}_{k_ i}$ for $i=0,1$ with $|s_ i|_{h^{k_ i}}^2\leq 1$, where $k_0,k_1\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We need to prove that 9BF5C28825D8 17.14.12  egin{equation}  \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{equation} Approximating $t$ by rational numbers $t_ m\searrow t$, and using the decreasingness of the filtration in the parameter $\lambda $, we reduce to the case $t\in \mathbb Q$. Write $t=p/q$ with $p,q\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Then \[  s\coloneqq s_0^{k_1(q-p)}\otimes s_1^{k_0p}\in \mathcal{F}_{k_0k_1 q}^{k_0k_1	au _0(q-p)+k_0k_1	au _1 p},  \] and \[   egin{aligned} &  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q} \log |s|_{h^{k_0k_1 q}}^2\  =&  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q}\left(k_1(q-p)\log |s_0|^2+ k_0p\log |s_1|^2ight)\  = &  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{aligned}  \] So ( 17.14.12 ) follows. Note that for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $k^{-1}\Gamma _{	au }^{\mathcal{F},k}$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 18.1.19 . The family is bounded above by $0$, so it follows from the same proposition that the obstacle in the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Hence the $P$- and $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes of this obstacle agree, so $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model for each $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. It remains to show that the test curve $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}$ is bounded and lies in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$. Fix $	au \leq -C$, where $C$ is as in ( 17.14.9 ). We will show that EA5B88AFDFF1 17.14.13  egin{equation}  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }=V_{	heta }. \end{equation} This follows from the Bergman kernel technique. Based on the theory developed so far, we can also give an elementary argument. Fix $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. Since $	au \leq -C$, we have $\mathcal F^{k	au }_ k=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. Let $s\in \mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. After multiplying $s$ by a constant, we may assume that $|s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1$. By the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au $, \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au \geq \log |s|_{h^ k}^2.  \] Hence \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au )ight).  \] Since \[  k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au \geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au ,  \] we get \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight).  \] Thus \[  \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight)=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)  \] for every $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. By theorem 18.1.46 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)=\operatorname{vol}L.  \] As $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model, this volume is equal to $\int _ X\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)^ n$. Hence $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ has full Monge–Ampère mass. Since it is also model, it must be equal to $V_	heta $. This proves ( 17.14.13 ). 2. ↩ It is not clear if $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ is necessary here. When $L$ is ample, it is shown in [ Proposition 7.11 , RWN14 ] that it is not necessary. The proof in the reference relies on a Skoda division theorem [ Theorem 7.10 , RWN14 ] , which is not known in the case of big line bundles. Remark 17.14.14 . D6FC5A3046FA There is an important special case of example 17.14.10 : Suppose that $L$ is ample and $\mathcal{F}$ is the filtration induced by a smooth test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ of $(X,L)$. Then the geodesic ray $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}*}$ is exactly the Phong–Sturm geodesic ray associated with $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$. See [ Section 9 , RWN14 ] . Remark 17.14.15 . 497927DD4340 We deduce from example 17.14.10 that the ray $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}*}$ induced by a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ is maximal.

title: Definition 17.14.1
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 17.14.1 . 6CC72AA0EA90 A test curve $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model if for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. The subset of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is denoted by $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. When $\phi =V_{\theta }$, we omit $\phi $ and write $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ instead. The union of the sets of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all model potentials $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$.

title: Proposition 17.14.2
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.14.2 . 683BF9BB4D63 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma _{-\infty }$ is an $\mathcal{I}$-model potential. Proof. This follows from proposition 16.6.30 . $\square$

title: Proposition 17.14.3
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.14.3 . A9AB5CE3BCAB Let $\theta '$ be another smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing the same cohomology class as $\theta $. Then there is a canonical bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}.  \] This bijection satisfies the obvious cocycle condition. Proof. Let $\theta '=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g$. By proposition 17.12.14 , the canonical map sends $\Gamma $ to the test curve with levels \[  \Gamma '_\tau =P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g].  \] If $\Gamma _\tau $ is $\mathcal I$-model, then it is $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.11 . Note that $\Gamma _\tau -g$ is $\mathcal I$-good since $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is. Hence \[  P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g]=P_{\theta '}[\Gamma _\tau -g]_{\mathcal I},  \] so $\Gamma '_\tau $ is $\mathcal I$-model. The same argument applied to $-g$ gives the inverse map, and the cocycle condition follows from the one in proposition 17.12.14 . $\square$

title: Proposition 17.14.4
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.14.4 . 92E487FB0DA8 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a Kähler manifold $Y$. Then the pointwise pull-back induces a bijection \[  \pi ^*\colon \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ;\pi ^*\phi ).  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 17.12.15 and proposition 16.6.10 . $\square$

title: Definition 17.14.5
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 17.14.5 . 03BED679B3AD Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, we define its $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{\theta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),\quad \tau \mapsto P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we define $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\omega ),\quad \tau \mapsto P_{\theta +\omega }\left[\Gamma _{\tau }\right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \]

title: Proposition 17.14.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.14.6 . BF40FB71C62C Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ;\phi )$. Then \[  P_{\theta }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;P_{\theta }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] More generally, for any closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ;P_{\theta +\omega }[\phi ]_{\mathcal{I}}).  \] Proof. We prove the first assertion; the second is identical, replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega $. Set \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \coloneqq P_\theta [\Gamma _\tau ]_{\mathcal I}.  \] The family is decreasing by 16.6.28 . If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then the concavity of $\Gamma $ gives \[  \Gamma _\tau \geq (1-s)\Gamma _{\tau _0}+s\Gamma _{\tau _1}.  \] Hence, by 16.6.28 and proposition 16.6.27 , \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \geq (1-s)\widetilde\Gamma _{\tau _0}+s\widetilde\Gamma _{\tau _1}.  \] Thus the family is concave. Finally, \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }}{}\! {}^{*}\widetilde\Gamma _\tau = P_\theta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}  \] follows from proposition 16.6.30 . Since $P_\theta [\phi ]_{\mathcal I}\geq \phi $, its mass is positive by the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . This proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Definition 17.14.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 17.14.7 . 6C763D5B798A Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential. A geodesic ray $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ is maximal if $\ell ^*$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model, namely, if $\ell ^*\in \mathcal E^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ;\phi )$.

title: Definition 17.14.8
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Definition 17.14.8 . D6CC0BBA6D35 Let $L$ be a big line bundle. We write \[  R(X,L)=\bigoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)  \] for the section ring 1 of $L$. A filtration on $R(X,L)$ is a decreasing family of graded linear subspaces $(\mathcal{F}^{\lambda })_{\lambda \in \mathbb {R}}$ of $R(X,L)$ with graded pieces \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }=\bigoplus _{k=0}^{\infty } \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k,  \] such that the following conditions are satisfied: The filtration is left-continuous: For any $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }=\bigcap _{\lambda '<\lambda }\mathcal{F}^{\lambda '};  \] the filtration is multiplicative: For any $\lambda ,\lambda '\in \mathbb {R}$ and any $k,k'\in \mathbb {N}$, we have \[  \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\cdot \mathcal{F}^{\lambda '}_{k'}\subseteq \mathcal{F}^{\lambda +\lambda '}_{k+k'};  \] there is an integer $C>0$ such that F76F341D25A8 17.14.9 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation} for all $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Given a filtration $\mathcal{F}$ on $R(X,L)$, we define \[  \tau _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup \left\{ \lambda \in \mathbb {R}: \mathcal{F}^{\lambda }_ k\neq 0\right\} .  \] By Fekete's lemma, we can introduce \[  \tau (\mathcal{F})=\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}\tau _ k(\mathcal{F})=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}\frac{1}{k}\tau _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] 1. ↩ It is more natural to replace the direct sum by a disjoint union, leading to the notion of ringoids ( annénoïdes in French), introduced by Ducros in [ Duc21 ] in the context of Temkin's graded reduction of Berkovich germs.

title: Equation 17.14.9
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: F76F341D25A8 17.14.9 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{F}^{Cm}_{m}=0,\quad \mathcal{F}^{-Cm}_ m=\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m) \end{equation}

title: Example 17.14.10
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text:
Example 17.14.10 . 20A8C7BFE0BB Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be a filtration on $R(X,L)$. Fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ and write $	heta =c_1(L,h)$. We introduce a few auxiliary functions. For each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we introduce \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \log |s|_{h^ k}^2: s\in \mathcal{F}^{k	au }_ k, |s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1 ight\} .  \] When $k	au \leq 	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $\mathcal{F}_ k^{k	au }
eq 0$. Moreover, proposition 5.20.4 and proposition 5.14.2 imply that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,k	heta ),\quad 	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F}).  \] Observe that for $k,k'\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k+k'}_{	au }\geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }+\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k'}_{	au }.  \] In particular, by Fekete's lemma, 79C9CAB675E4 17.14.11  egin{equation}  \lim _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }=\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au } \end{equation} exists for any $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. We define $(\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au })_{	au <	au (\mathcal{F})}$ as follows: \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }\coloneqq P_{	heta }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }ight]{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000078461}{2}}.  \] We claim that $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}\in \mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$ and is bounded. It is clear that $(-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F}))
i 	au \mapsto \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is decreasing. We prove its concavity. By proposition 16.4.2 , it suffices to show that \[  \Bigl (-\infty ,	au (\mathcal{F})\Bigr )
i 	au \mapsto \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au }  \] is concave. In other words, we need to prove the following: Given $	au _0<	au _1<	au (\mathcal{F})$ and $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\operatorname *{sup}_{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}{}\! {}^{*}  rac{1}{k} \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}.  \] But thanks to proposition 5.14.6 and proposition 5.14.5 , it suffices to show that \[  \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq t\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _1}+(1-t)\sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{	au _0}  \] for all $t\in (0,1)$. Take $s_ i\in \mathcal{F}^{k_ i	au _ i}_{k_ i}$ for $i=0,1$ with $|s_ i|_{h^{k_ i}}^2\leq 1$, where $k_0,k_1\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We need to prove that 9BF5C28825D8 17.14.12  egin{equation}  \sup _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}  rac{1}{k}\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F},k}_{t	au _1+(1-t)	au _0}\geq  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{equation} Approximating $t$ by rational numbers $t_ m\searrow t$, and using the decreasingness of the filtration in the parameter $\lambda $, we reduce to the case $t\in \mathbb Q$. Write $t=p/q$ with $p,q\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Then \[  s\coloneqq s_0^{k_1(q-p)}\otimes s_1^{k_0p}\in \mathcal{F}_{k_0k_1 q}^{k_0k_1	au _0(q-p)+k_0k_1	au _1 p},  \] and \[   egin{aligned} &  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q} \log |s|_{h^{k_0k_1 q}}^2\  =&  rac{1}{k_0k_1 q}\left(k_1(q-p)\log |s_0|^2+ k_0p\log |s_1|^2ight)\  = &  rac{1-t}{k_0}\log |s_0|_{h^{k_0}}^2+ rac{t}{k_1}\log |s_1|_{h^{k_1}}^2. \end{aligned}  \] So ( 17.14.12 ) follows. Note that for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $	au \leq k^{-1}	au _ k(\mathcal{F})$, we know that $k^{-1}\Gamma _{	au }^{\mathcal{F},k}$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 18.1.19 . The family is bounded above by $0$, so it follows from the same proposition that the obstacle in the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Hence the $P$- and $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes of this obstacle agree, so $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model for each $	au <	au (\mathcal{F})$. It remains to show that the test curve $\Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}$ is bounded and lies in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,	heta )$. Fix $	au \leq -C$, where $C$ is as in ( 17.14.9 ). We will show that EA5B88AFDFF1 17.14.13  egin{equation}  \Gamma ^{\mathcal{F}}_{	au }=V_{	heta }. \end{equation} This follows from the Bergman kernel technique. Based on the theory developed so far, we can also give an elementary argument. Fix $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. Since $	au \leq -C$, we have $\mathcal F^{k	au }_ k=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. Let $s\in \mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)$. After multiplying $s$ by a constant, we may assume that $|s|_{h^ k}^2\leq 1$. By the definition of $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au $, \[  \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au \geq \log |s|_{h^ k}^2.  \] Hence \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(\Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au )ight).  \] Since \[  k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au \geq \Gamma ^{\mathcal F,k}_	au ,  \] we get \[  s\in \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight).  \] Thus \[  \mathrm H^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal I(k\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au )ight)=\mathrm H^0(X,L^ k)  \] for every $k\in \mathbb Z_{>0}$. By theorem 18.1.46 , \[  \operatorname{vol}\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)=\operatorname{vol}L.  \] As $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ is $\mathcal I$-model, this volume is equal to $\int _ X\left(	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au ight)^ n$. Hence $\Gamma ^{\mathcal F}_	au $ has full Monge–Ampère mass. Since it is also model, it must be equal to $V_	heta $. This proves ( 17.14.13 ). 2. ↩ It is not clear if $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ is necessary here. When $L$ is ample, it is shown in [ Proposition 7.11 , RWN14 ] that it is not necessary. The proof in the reference relies on a Skoda division theorem [ Theorem 7.10 , RWN14 ] , which is not known in the case of big line bundles.

title: 17.15 Operations on test curves
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta ,\theta ',\theta ''$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. In this section, we develop several general operations on test curves, anticipating the applications in non-Archimedean geometry in section 22.1 . One may read section 22.1 first and consult this section when necessary. Definition 17.15.1 . DF47E4B2060A Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, we say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if $\Gamma _{\max }\leq \Gamma '_{\max }$ and, for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have B3E2E25A3B00 17.15.2 \begin{equation}  \Gamma _{\tau }\preceq _ P \Gamma '_{\tau }. \end{equation} Observe that ( 17.15.2 ) actually holds for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ if $\theta =\theta '$. Here we use the convention that $-\infty \preceq _ P \varphi $ for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X)\cup \{ -\infty \} $. The relation $\leq $ defines a partial order on $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Lemma 17.15.3 . CA55D62C74E0 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: 7981AA897F00 $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; ED51882DAEE9 $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']$. Proof. This follows from example 16.8.6 . $\square$ Definition 17.15.4 . DAA4083947C1 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ as follows: D6CB3C2695C3 We set \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max };  \] B7E27AEC255C for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define 2 6C3AF1760F9F 17.15.5 \begin{equation}  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\right]. \end{equation} 2. ↩ There is no usc regularization in the formula. It is not a typo. Lemma 17.15.6 . 5BE2CC04AAD0 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, \[  \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ').  \] This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, ( 17.15.5 ) in definition 17.15.4 makes sense. Proof. Let \[  \eta _{\tau }=\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)=\sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Set \[  Z=\left\{ x\in X: \Gamma _{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} \cup \left\{ x\in X: \Gamma '_{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} .  \] It follows from proposition 21.11.37 that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \eta ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)+\Gamma '^*_ t(x)  \] for all $t>0$. The same trivially holds when $x\in Z$, so the equation holds everywhere. In particular, by corollary 21.11.26 and proposition 5.14.15 , we have \[  \eta _{\tau }=\left(\Gamma ^*+\Gamma '^*\right)^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')  \] when $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is a test curve. The family $\tau \mapsto \eta _\tau $ is decreasing, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 16.4.2 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then for arbitrary $\delta _0,\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\delta =(1-s)\delta _0+s\delta _1$, \[  \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\geq (1-s)(\Gamma _{\delta _0}+\Gamma '_{\tau _0-\delta _0})+s(\Gamma _{\delta _1}+\Gamma '_{\tau _1-\delta _1}).  \] Taking suprema and using proposition 16.4.2 gives the concavity of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Choose $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ with $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then \[  \eta _\tau \geq \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }.  \] By 17.12.6 , $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Hence $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ has positive $(\theta +\theta ')$-mass by the multi-linearity of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 . It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that $\eta _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. By corollary 16.3.20 , \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by proposition 5.14.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Thus $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Next, assume that $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$ are $\mathcal{I}$-model. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then for each $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ such that $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$, we know that $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ by 17.12.6 . It follows from example 18.1.11 that $\Gamma _\delta $ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ are both $\mathcal{I}$-good, hence so is $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ by proposition 18.1.17 . These sums are bounded above by $0$, so $\eta _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 18.1.19 . Set \[  M\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }.  \] For each rational number $q<M$, apply Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 to the locally uniformly bounded above family \[  \left\{ \left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q:J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)\right\} \subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] We obtain a countable subfamily $\mathcal J_ q\subseteq \operatorname{Fin}(I)$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q = \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \mathcal J_ q}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q.  \] Let \[  I'\coloneqq \bigcup _{q\in \mathbb Q, q<M} \bigcup _{J\in \mathcal J_ q}J.  \] Then $I'$ is countable and, for every rational $q<M$, \[  \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q= \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q.  \] Moreover, $\sup _{i\in I'}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }=M$, since the last equality is non-trivial for every rational $q<M$. Let $\Gamma '=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then clearly, $\Gamma '\leq \Gamma $. We claim that they are actually equal. Thanks to proposition 16.8.7 and 17.12.6 , it suffices to show that for any $\tau <\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$, we have \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n.  \] The equality is already known for all rational $\tau <M$. Since both \[  \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma '_\tau }^ n,\quad \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _\tau }^ n  \] are continuous on $(-\infty ,M)$ by proposition 17.12.9 , the equality of masses holds for every $\tau <M$. $\square$ Proposition 17.15.32 . 4D160D08BDC8 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Definition 17.15.33 . F6690BE17BAF Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$, we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$  as follows: 1297F6EE2D1D We set \[  \left(\lambda \Gamma \right)_{\max }=\lambda \Gamma _{\max };  \] 4310047CFEDD for any $\tau < \left(\lambda \Gamma \right)_{\max }$, we set \[  (\lambda \Gamma )_{\tau }=\lambda \Gamma _{\lambda ^{-1}\tau }.  \] Proposition 17.15.34 . 148305D820BC Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$. Then $\lambda \Gamma $ as defined in definition 17.15.33 lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )_{>0}$. We have 9.92 \begin{equation}  (\lambda \Gamma )_{-\infty }=\lambda \Gamma _{-\infty }. \end{equation} Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Proposition 17.15.35 . A44C0F3CE359 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. This is immediate by definition. $\square$ Lemma 17.15.36 . 9469C1C052AA Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\lambda >0$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\lambda \omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]=\lambda P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ].  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 17.15.37 . BDCF69FED30F Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Assume that 48E9DB47C37C 17.15.38 \begin{equation}  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation} and C2C47DDCADA4 17.15.39 \begin{equation}  \inf _{i\in I} \int _ X \left( \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right)^ n>0,\quad \textup{for some }\tau < \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max }. \end{equation} Then we define $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: 3E567FA790CC We set \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\max }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{\max };  \] 88EFD81042D1 for any $\tau < \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\max }$, we let \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{\tau }\coloneqq \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}_{\tau }.  \] Proposition 17.15.40 . 82DA4D86CC78 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.38 ) and ( 17.15.39 ). Then $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then so is $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}$. Proof. The first assertion is an immediate consequence of proposition 16.4.3 , except for the positivity of the mass at $-\infty $. Choose $\tau _0$ as in ( 17.15.39 ). Applying proposition 16.4.4 gives \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau _0}\right)^ n =\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i}_{\tau _0}\right)^ n>0.  \] Hence the value at $-\infty $ has positive mass by monotonicity. The last assertion follows from proposition 16.6.29 . $\square$ In general, it is not true that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^{i}_{-\infty }.  \] Lemma 17.15.41 . E141137C118E Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.38 ) and ( 17.15.39 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. First observe that \[  \left( P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right] \right)_{\max }= \left(\inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]\right)_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Then we need to show the following: 1D25957452B7 17.15.42 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\sim _ P \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation} Applying proposition 16.4.4 gives the mass convergence required in corollary 16.9.14 . Hence $\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S}\inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } $. Thanks to corollary 16.9.36 and corollary 16.9.14 , we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{j\in I} \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right],\quad P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\xrightarrow {d_ S} \inf _{j\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ j_{\tau } \right].  \] Hence, ( 17.15.42 ) follows from proposition 16.9.6 . $\square$

Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ as follows: D6CB3C2695C3 We set \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max };  \] B7E27AEC255C for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define 2 6C3AF1760F9F 17.15.5 \begin{equation}  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\right]. \end{equation} 2. ↩ There is no usc regularization in the formula. title: Lemma 17.15.6
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.15.6 . 5BE2CC04AAD0 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, for any $\tau <(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\max }$, \[  \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ').  \] This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. In particular, ( 17.15.5 ) in definition 17.15.4 makes sense. Proof. Let \[  \eta _{\tau }=\sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)=\sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Set \[  Z=\left\{ x\in X: \Gamma _{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} \cup \left\{ x\in X: \Gamma '_{\upsilon }(x)=-\infty \, \forall \upsilon \in \mathbb {R}\right\} .  \] It follows from proposition 21.11.37 that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \eta ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)+\Gamma '^*_ t(x)  \] for all $t>0$. The same trivially holds when $x\in Z$, so the equation holds everywhere. In particular, by corollary 21.11.26 and proposition 5.14.15 , we have \[  \eta _{\tau }=\left(\Gamma ^*+\Gamma '^*\right)^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')  \] when $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is a test curve. The family $\tau \mapsto \eta _\tau $ is decreasing, and the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 16.4.2 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. If $\tau =(1-s)\tau _0+s\tau _1$, then for arbitrary $\delta _0,\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\delta =(1-s)\delta _0+s\delta _1$, \[  \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\geq (1-s)(\Gamma _{\delta _0}+\Gamma '_{\tau _0-\delta _0})+s(\Gamma _{\delta _1}+\Gamma '_{\tau _1-\delta _1}).  \] Taking suprema and using proposition 16.4.2 gives the concavity of $\Gamma +\Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Choose $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ with $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then \[  \eta _\tau \geq \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }.  \] By 17.12.6 , $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Hence $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ has positive $(\theta +\theta ')$-mass by the multi-linearity of non-pluripolar products proposition 13.11.4 6 . It follows from the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that $\eta _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. By corollary 16.3.20 , \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by proposition 5.14.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Thus $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Next, assume that $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$ are $\mathcal{I}$-model. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }$. Then for each $\delta \in \mathbb {R}$ such that $\delta <\Gamma _{\max }$ and $\tau -\delta <\Gamma '_{\max }$, we know that $\Gamma _\delta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ by 17.12.6 . It follows from example 18.1.11 that $\Gamma _\delta $ and $\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }$ are both $\mathcal{I}$-good, hence so is $\Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ by proposition 18.1.17 . These sums are bounded above by $0$, so $\eta _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by proposition 18.1.19 . Since $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')_\tau =P_{\theta +\theta '}[\eta _\tau ]$, we conclude that $\Gamma +\Gamma '$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. $\square$

title: Proposition 17.15.7
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.15.7 . FBC25DBE6122 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. Moreover, 22BECA7DAF92 17.15.8 \begin{equation}  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }=P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[\Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }\right]. \end{equation} When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$, we have $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. The operation $+$ is commutative and associative. Proof. It follows immediately from 17.15.6 that $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$. It lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')_{>0}$ if $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. We argue ( 17.15.8 ). By definition, for any small enough $\tau $, we have \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{2\tau }\succeq _ P \Gamma _{\tau }+\Gamma '_{\tau }.  \] Letting $\tau \to -\infty $ and applying proposition 16.9.44 and theorem 16.9.45 , we find that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty }\succeq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] On the other hand, for each small enough $\tau $, we have \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right) \preceq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }  \] by proposition 16.8.27 and proposition 16.9.44 . We apply proposition 16.9.44 again, we conclude that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{-\infty } \preceq _ P \Gamma _{-\infty }+\Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] So ( 17.15.8 ) follows. Finally, let us show that $+$ is commutative and associative. Commutativity follows from the symmetry of the defining supremum. Let $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta '')_{>0}$. Then we want to show that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] First observe that \[  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma '' \right)_{\max }=\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '')\right)_{\max }.  \] Fix $\tau $ less than this common value. We compute that \[  \begin{aligned} & \left( (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''\right)_{\tau }\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '+\theta ''}\left[\sup _{\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}} \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\delta _1}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right)\right]\\  \sim _ P &  \sup _{\delta _1\in \mathbb {R}} \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\delta _1}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right)\\  \sim _ P &  \sup _{\delta _1,\delta _2\in \mathbb {R}} \left(\Gamma _{\delta _2}+\Gamma '_{\delta _1-\delta _2}+\Gamma ''_{\tau -\delta _1}\right), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line, we applied proposition 16.9.44 and proposition 16.8.27 . Similarly, for $\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '')\right)_{\tau }$, we get the same expression. The associativity follows. $\square$

text: Lemma 17.15.9 . 8571F1340B16 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\Gamma ' \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-forms $\omega $ and $\omega '$ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\theta '+\omega +\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '].  \] Proof. Observe that \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta +\theta '+\omega +\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']_{\max }=& \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '] \right)_{\max }\\  =& \Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }. \end{aligned}  \] Take $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this common value. We need to verify that \[  (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \Bigl ( P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma ']\Bigr )_{\tau }.  \] By definition, this means that \[  \sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\delta }+\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }\right)\sim _ P \sup _{\tau -\Gamma '_{\max }<\delta <\Gamma _{\max }}\left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _{\delta }]+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma '_{\tau -\delta }]\right).  \] This is a consequence of proposition 16.8.27 and proposition 16.8.28 . $\square$
