title: Proposition 17.15.11
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.15.11 . 6DDF81D7BEFF Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta ')_{>0}$ and $C,C'\in \mathbb {R}$. Then 7D5EA90D003B $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+C)=(\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '$; 01CBA28FD511 $\Gamma +(C+C')=(\Gamma +C)+C'$. Proof. 1 We first observe that \[  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C\right)_{\max }=\left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+C) \right)_{\max }=\left( (\Gamma +C)+\Gamma ' \right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }+\Gamma '_{\max }+C.  \] Take any $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this common value. We compute \[  \begin{aligned}  \left((\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C\right)_{\tau }=& (\Gamma +\Gamma ')_{\tau -C} = P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right],\\  \left( \Gamma +(\Gamma '+C) \right)_{\tau }=&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +(\Gamma '+C)_{\tau -\delta } \right) \right]\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right],\\  \left((\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '\right)_{\tau }=&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( (\Gamma +C)_{C+\delta }+\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right]\\  =&  P_{\theta +\theta '}\left[ \sup _{\delta \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \Gamma _\delta +\Gamma '_{\tau -C-\delta } \right) \right]. \end{aligned}  \] 2 Observe that \[  \left( \Gamma +(C+C') \right)_{\max }=\left( (\Gamma +C)+C' \right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }+C+C'.  \] For any $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than this value, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +(C+C') \right)_{\tau }=\Gamma _{\tau -C-C'}=\left( (\Gamma +C)+C' \right)_{\tau }.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

We define $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: 12F2D0314E20 We set \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }\coloneqq \Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max };  \] 08596243109D for any $\tau <(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }$, we define CFA9EE6DC1ED 17.15.13 \begin{equation}  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta }\left[ \operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 17.15.14
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Lemma 17.15.14 . 77520F48ECEB Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$, we have \[  \operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ),  \] and $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. This potential is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. In particular, ( 17.15.13 ) in definition 17.15.12 makes sense. Proof. To simplify the notation, we write \[  \psi _{\tau }=\operatorname{CE}\left( \rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho } \right)_{\tau }  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Thanks to proposition 21.11.36 , for any fixed $x\in X$, we have B75DA94B0995 17.15.15 \begin{equation}  \psi ^*_ t(x)=\Gamma ^*_ t(x)\lor \Gamma '^*_ t(x) \end{equation} for all $t>0$ as long as $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)\neq -\infty $ and $\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)\neq -\infty $ for some $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Otherwise, assume for instance that $\Gamma _{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$; then by definition, $\psi _{\tau }(x)=\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)$ for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^*_ t(x)=-\infty $ for all $t>0$ and ( 17.15.15 ) continues to hold. The case where $\Gamma '_{\tau }(x)=-\infty $ for all $\tau $ is symmetric. Therefore, we have shown that \[  \psi ^*_ t=\Gamma ^*_ t\lor \Gamma '^*_ t\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] It follows from proposition 17.10.13 that $(\psi ^*_ t)_{t\in [a,b]}$ is a subgeodesic for any $0< a<b$. Next we observe that $\psi _{\bullet }$ is closed by definition. So it follows from proposition 21.11.36 and proposition 5.14.15 that \[  \psi _{\tau }=(\psi ^*_{\bullet })^*_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} .  \] Due to proposition 17.12.16 and proposition 21.11.12 , there is a pluripolar set $Z\subseteq X$ such that for $x\in X\setminus Z$, we have \[  \begin{split}  \psi _{\tau }(x)=\sup \left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }(x)+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}(x): \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\}  \end{split}  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. It follows from proposition 5.14.6 that 1A2FC8833C52 17.15.16 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  \psi _{\tau }=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}: \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\}  \end{split} \end{equation} for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. We now check that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$ is a test curve. The function $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $ is decreasing, hence its upper concave envelope $\psi _\bullet $ is decreasing. The monotonicity of the $P$-envelope proposition 16.4.2 3 gives the decreasingness of $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Since $\psi _\bullet $ is concave by construction, proposition 16.4.2 gives the concavity of $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Fix $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$. Then either $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ or $\tau <\Gamma '_{\max }$. Since $\psi _\bullet $ is a concave majorant of $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $, we have \[  \psi _\tau \geq \Gamma _\tau \quad \text{if } \tau <\Gamma _{\max }, \qquad \psi _\tau \geq \Gamma '_\tau \quad \text{if } \tau <\Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Together with the fact that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $, these inequalities show that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. It follows from 17.12.6 and the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 that $\psi _\tau \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. By corollary 16.3.20 , \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau =P_\theta [\psi _\tau ]  \] is a model potential. Finally, $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ by proposition 5.14.2 ; since it dominates $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau $ for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }$, it has positive mass by another application of the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Thus $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. It follows from ( 17.15.16 ) that $\psi _{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, thanks to proposition 18.1.17 and proposition 18.1.19 ; the family in the upper envelope is bounded above by $0$. Since $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_\tau =P_\theta [\psi _\tau ]$, we conclude that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '$ is $\mathcal{I}$-model in this case. $\square$

title: Corollary 17.15.17
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Corollary 17.15.17 . C8D1BA787705 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and 9AB9F5A23D95 17.15.18 \begin{equation}  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }=P_{\theta }\left[\Gamma _{-\infty }\lor \Gamma '_{-\infty }\right]. \end{equation} If $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, then $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and each $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma $ and $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma '$, we have $\Gamma ''\geq \Gamma \lor \Gamma '$. Moreover, the operation $\lor $ is associative and commutative. Proof. It follows immediately from 17.15.14 that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, and it lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ if $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We argue ( 17.15.18 ). Set \[  \eta \coloneqq \Gamma _{-\infty }\lor \Gamma '_{-\infty }.  \] Since $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\geq \Gamma $ and $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\geq \Gamma '$, we have $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq \eta $. As $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }$ is a model potential, it follows that \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\geq P_\theta [\eta ].  \] Conversely, for each $\rho \in \mathbb {R}$ we have $\Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho \leq \eta $. Hence the constant curve with value $\eta $ is a concave majorant of $\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho $, and therefore \[  \operatorname{CE}\left(\rho \mapsto \Gamma _\rho \lor \Gamma '_\rho \right)_\tau \leq \eta ,\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Applying the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope and then letting $\tau \to -\infty $ gives \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{-\infty }\leq P_\theta [\eta ].  \] This proves ( 17.15.18 ). Take $\Gamma ''$ as in the statement of the corollary. First observe that \[  \Gamma ''_{\max }\geq \Gamma _{\max } \lor \Gamma '_{\max }=(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }.  \] Take $\tau <(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\max }$. We argue that \[  \Gamma ''_{\tau }\geq (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }.  \] By the concavity of $\Gamma ''$, the potential $\Gamma ''_\tau $ dominates the concave envelope \[  \operatorname{CE}\left(\rho \mapsto \Gamma _{\rho }\lor \Gamma '_{\rho }\right)_\tau .  \] Since $\Gamma ''_\tau $ is model, the monotonicity of the $P$-envelope gives \[  \Gamma ''_{\tau }\geq (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }.  \] Therefore, \[  \Gamma ''\geq \Gamma \lor \Gamma '.  \] Commutativity is immediate from the definition. Associativity follows from the least-upper-bound property just proved: both $(\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')\lor \Gamma ''$ and $\Gamma \lor (\Gamma '\lor \Gamma '')$ are the least upper bound of $\Gamma ,\Gamma ',\Gamma ''$. $\square$

title: Lemma 17.15.19

text: Lemma 17.15.19 . 5DB0F974F922 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma '].  \] Proof. We first observe that \[  \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']\right)_{\max }=\left( P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']\right)_{\max }=\Gamma _{\max }\lor \Gamma '_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. We need to show that \[  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma '] \right)_{\tau }.  \] We need the formula ( 17.15.16 ) proved in the proof of 17.15.14 : \[  \begin{split}  (\Gamma \lor \Gamma ')_{\tau }\sim _ P\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{ \lambda \Gamma _{\rho }+(1-\lambda )\Gamma '_{\rho '}: \lambda \in (0,1),\rho ,\rho '\in \mathbb {R},\lambda \rho +(1-\lambda )\rho '=\tau \right\} . \end{split}  \] A similar result holds with $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]$ and $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']$ in place of $\Gamma $ and $\Gamma '$. So our assertion is a direct consequence of proposition 16.8.27 and proposition 16.8.28 . $\square$

title: Proposition 17.15.22
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.15.22 . 88665EBBD399 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}$ as defined in definition 17.15.20 lies in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i}$ lies in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as well. Moreover, we have 75480BC1C778 17.15.23 \begin{equation}  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $\tau <\sup _ i\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$. Choose $i_0$ such that $\tau <\Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }$. On the tail $i\geq i_0$, the potentials $\Gamma ^ i_\tau $ form an increasing net of model potentials of positive mass, uniformly bounded above by $0$. Hence proposition 16.4.9 shows that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_\tau = \operatorname *{sup}_{i\geq i_0}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_\tau  \] is model. Its mass is positive by monotonicity, since it dominates $\Gamma ^{i_0}_\tau $. The decreasingness and concavity in $\tau $ follow from the directedness of the net and the corresponding properties of the curves $\Gamma ^ i$. Thus $\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}_ i\Gamma ^ i$ is a test curve. If all $\Gamma ^ i$ are $\mathcal I$-model, the same tail argument and proposition 16.6.30 show that the supremum is $\mathcal I$-model. It remains to argue ( 17.15.23 ). Fix any $i_0\in I$. Since the curves are decreasing and are extended as in 17.12.3 , the value at $-\infty $ can be computed by taking the supremum over rational $\tau <\Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }$. By proposition 5.14.5 , there is a pluripolar set $Z\subseteq X$ such that for any $x\in X\setminus Z$, \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right)_{-\infty }(x)=\sup _{\mathbb {Q}\ni \tau < \Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max }}\left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }\right)(x)=\sup _{\mathbb {Q}\ni \tau < \Gamma ^{i_0}_{\max },i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau }(x)=\sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }(x).  \] So they are equal everywhere by proposition 5.14.6 . $\square$

text: Lemma 17.15.24 . 0B89BAEA6D39 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. text: Proposition 17.15.28 . C4A77DA880D9 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). title: Proposition 17.15.31
topic: Energy, geodesics, rays, and test curves
text: Proposition 17.15.31 . 4B67ABC0083D Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.21 ). Then there is a countable subset $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. We may assume that $I$ is infinite. Set \[  M\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }.  \] For each rational number $q<M$, apply Choquet's lemma proposition 5.14.3 to the locally uniformly bounded above family \[  \left\{ \left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q:J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)\right\} \subseteq \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ).  \] We obtain a countable subfamily $\mathcal J_ q\subseteq \operatorname{Fin}(I)$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \operatorname{Fin}(I)}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q = \operatorname *{sup}_{J\in \mathcal J_ q}{}\! {}^{*}\left(\bigvee _{j\in J}\Gamma ^ j\right)_ q.  \] Let \[  I'\coloneqq \bigcup _{q\in \mathbb Q, q<M} \bigcup _{J\in \mathcal J_ q}J.  \] Then $I'$ is countable and, for every rational $q<M$, \[  \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q= \left(\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\right)_ q.  \] Moreover, $\sup _{i\in I'}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }=M$, since the last equality is non-trivial for every rational $q<M$. Let $\Gamma '=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then clearly, $\Gamma '\leq \Gamma $. We claim that they are actually equal. Thanks to proposition 16.8.7 and 17.12.6 , it suffices to show that for any $\tau <\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }$, we have \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma '_{\tau }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau }\right)^ n.  \] The equality is already known for all rational $\tau <M$. Since both \[  \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma '_\tau }^ n,\quad \tau \mapsto \log \int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _\tau }^ n  \] are continuous on $(-\infty ,M)$ by proposition 17.12.9 , the equality of masses holds for every $\tau <M$. $\square$

title: Proposition 17.15.40

text: Proposition 17.15.40 . 82DA4D86CC78 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.38 ) and ( 17.15.39 ). Then $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Moreover, if $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$, then so is $\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i}$. Proof. The first assertion is an immediate consequence of proposition 16.4.3 , except for the positivity of the mass at $-\infty $. Choose $\tau _0$ as in ( 17.15.39 ). Applying proposition 16.4.4 gives \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\tau _0}\right)^ n =\lim _{i\in I}\int _ X\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i}_{\tau _0}\right)^ n>0.  \] Hence the value at $-\infty $ has positive mass by monotonicity. The last assertion follows from proposition 16.6.29 . $\square$

text: Lemma 17.15.41 . E141137C118E Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ satisfying ( 17.15.38 ) and ( 17.15.39 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right].  \] Proof. Then we need to show the following: 1D25957452B7 17.15.42 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]\sim _ P \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^ i_{\tau } \right]. \end{equation} Applying proposition 16.4.4 gives the mass convergence required in corollary 16.9.14 . title: 19.1 The theory of Okounkov bodies
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
In this chapter, we apply our theory of singularities to the study of Okounkov bodies. We construct convex bodies $\Delta (L,\phi )$, the partial Okounkov bodies , attached to a big line bundle $L$ on a smooth projective variety $X$ together with a plurisubharmonic metric $\phi $ on $L$. These convex bodies provide a universal numerical invariant of the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\phi $, and reduce many problems in pluripotential theory to problems in convex geometry, which are often more tractable. We develop two parallel constructions: an algebraic one in section 19.4 , where $\phi $ is encoded by the multiplier ideals $\mathcal{I}(k\phi )$, and a transcendental one in section 19.5 , where $\phi $ is treated directly as an analytic object via valuations on closed positive currents. The two constructions agree when both apply, but each has its own natural domain of definition and its own range of applications. Okounkov bodies associate convex bodies to graded linear series by recording successive vanishing orders along an admissible flag. Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ and $L$ a big holomorphic line bundle on $X$. Given an admissible flag $X=Y_0\supseteq Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n$ on $X$ (definition 19.3.2 ), one attaches to $L$ a natural $n$-dimensional convex body $\Delta (L)\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$, generalizing the Newton polytope construction in toric geometry (definition 21.12.27 ). The convex body $\Delta (L)$ is the Okounkov body of $L$ with respect to the chosen flag. Concretely, the successive vanishing order along the flag defines a valuation $
u \colon \mathbb {C}(X)^{	imes }	o \mathbb {Z}^ n$, and \[  \Gamma (L)\coloneqq \left\{ (
u (s),k)\in \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}:k\in \mathbb {N},\,  s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)^{	imes } ight\}   \] is a semigroup whose closed convex cone, intersected with the slice $\{ (x,1)\} $, is $\Delta (L)$. The construction shows that $\Delta (L)$ depends only on the numerical class of $L$, and the Okounkov bodies also show that the Okounkov bodies for all flags determine this class, so $\Delta (L)$ may be regarded as a universal numerical invariant of $L$. The aim of this chapter is to perform the analogous construction at the level of singularity types of psh metrics. Setting \[  \Gamma (L,\phi )\coloneqq \left\{ (
u (s),k)\in \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}:k\in \mathbb {N},\,  s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\phi ))^{	imes } ight\} ,  \] one immediately encounters the obstruction that $\Gamma (L,\phi )$ is in general not a semigroup, so the Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă and Kaveh–Khovanskii constructions break down. The remedy is the notion of an almost semigroup : $\Gamma (L,\phi )$ does satisfy a near-semigroup property (theorem 19.4.16 ), and the convex-body construction $\Gamma \mapsto \Delta (\Gamma )$ extends continuously from semigroups to almost semigroups (theorem 19.2.10 ). The partial Okounkov body of $(L,\phi )$ is then \[  \Delta (L,\phi )\coloneqq \Delta  igl (\Gamma (L,\phi ) igr ),  \] and is a convex sub-body of $\Delta (L)$ — explaining the name partial . The universality of partial Okounkov bodies is captured by corollary 19.4.55 : the $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence class of $\phi $ is determined by the Okounkov bodies of $(L,\phi )$ for sufficiently many flags. The results in this chapter will be applied in section 21.13 to develop toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles.

title: 19.2 Almost semigroups
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
We give a brief presentation of the theory of almost semigroups. The arguments are provided in section 19.7 . Fix an integer $n\geq 0$. Fix a closed convex cone $C\subseteq \mathbb {R}^{n}\times \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0}$ such that $C\cap \{ x_{n+1}=0\} =\{ 0\} $. Here $x_{n+1}$ is the last coordinate of $\mathbb {R}^{n+1}$. Write $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ for the set of subsets of $C\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ and $\mathcal{S}(C)$ for the set of subsemigroups $S\subseteq C\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$. For $S\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ and each $k\in \mathbb {N}$ such that $S_ k\neq \varnothing $, we write \[  S_ k\coloneqq \left\{ x\in \mathbb {Z}^ n: (x,k)\in S \right\} .  \] Note that $S_ k$ is a finite set by our assumption on $C$. We introduce a pseudometric on $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ as follows: A3A5C96E566B 19.2.1 \begin{equation}  d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')\coloneqq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty } k^{-n} \left(|S_ k|+|S'_ k|-2|(S\cap S')_ k|\right). \end{equation} Here $|\bullet |$ denotes the cardinality of a finite set. The quantity $d_{\mathrm{sg}}$ defined above is a pseudometric on $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$. Given $S,S'\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$, we say $S$ is equivalent to $S'$ and write $S\sim S'$ if $d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')=0$. This is an equivalence relation. The volume of $S\in \mathcal{S}(C)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}S\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty } (ka)^{-n}|S_{ka}|=\varlimsup _{k\to \infty } k^{-n}|S_ k|,  \] where $a$ is a sufficiently divisible positive integer. The existence of the limit and its independence from $a$ both follow from theorem 19.7.20 . We define $\overline{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ as the closure of $\mathcal{S}(C)$ in $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ with respect to the topology defined by the pseudometric $d_{\mathrm{sg}}$. The function $\operatorname{vol}\colon \mathcal{S}(C)\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ admits a unique $1$-Lipschitz extension to 41423E2E726F 19.2.2 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\colon \overline{\mathcal{S}}(C)\rightarrow \mathbb {R}. \end{equation} Given $S\in \hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$, we will write $C(S)\subseteq C$ for the closed convex cone generated by $S\cup \{ 0\} $. Moreover, for each $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ such that $S_ k\neq \varnothing $, we define \[  \Delta _ k(S)\coloneqq \mathrm{Conv}\left\{ k^{-1}x\in \mathbb {R}^ n:x\in S_ k \right\} \subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n.  \] Here $\mathrm{Conv}$ denotes the convex hull. Definition 19.2.3 . 923345ACA44A Let $\mathcal{S}'(C)$ be the subset of $\mathcal{S}(C)$ consisting of semigroups $S$ such that $S$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ (as an Abelian group). Note that for any $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, the cone $C(S)$ has full dimension (i.e., the topological interior is non-empty). Given a full-dimensional subcone $C'\subseteq C$, we have $C'\cap \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$. 


We recall the following definition from [ KK12 ] . Definition 19.2.4 . B62535F66376 Given $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, its Okounkov body is defined by \[  \Delta (S)\coloneqq \left\{ x\in \mathbb {R}^ n:(x,1)\in C(S) \right\} .  \] Theorem 19.2.5 . 37D86D761E81 For each $S\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$, we have 4E701FB8EA13 19.2.6 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}S=\lim _{k\to \infty } k^{-n}|S_ k|=\operatorname{vol}\Delta (S)>0. \end{equation} Moreover, as $k\to \infty $, A57FF2EE0305 19.2.7 \begin{equation}  \Delta _{k}(S)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta (S). \end{equation} Corollary 19.2.8 . 9FB3E8CE18F7 Let $S,S'\in \mathcal{S}'(C)$. Assume that $\operatorname{vol}(S\cap S')>0$. Then we have \[  d_{\mathrm{sg}}(S,S')=\operatorname{vol}(S)+\operatorname{vol}(S')-2\operatorname{vol}(S\cap S').  \] Definition 19.2.9 . 78B565EC56CF We define $\overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ as the set of elements in the closure of $\mathcal{S}'(C)$ in $\hat{\mathcal{S}}(C)$ with positive volume. An element in $\overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ is called an almost semigroup in $C$. Recall that the volume here is defined in ( 19.2.2 ). Theorem 19.2.10 . 2534E787147E The Okounkov body map $\Delta \colon \mathcal{S}'(C) \rightarrow \mathcal{K}_ n$ as defined in definition 19.2.4 admits a unique continuous extension 64FC27991307 19.2.11 \begin{equation}  \Delta \colon \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}\rightarrow \mathcal{K}_ n. \end{equation} Moreover, for any $S\in \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$, we have 882FE1F63B29 19.2.12 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}S=\operatorname{vol}\Delta (S). \end{equation} Corollary 19.2.13 . 511230BE9AE5 Suppose that $S,S'\in \overline{\mathcal{S}'(C)}_{>0}$ with $S\subseteq S'$. Then 4552E8E96799 19.2.14 \begin{equation}  \Delta (S)\subseteq \Delta (S'). \end{equation}

We define the valuation of $T$ along $Y_{ ullet }$ as \[

u (T,Y_1)[Y_1])ight)_{i-1}.  \] Proposition 19.3.7 . FE522E15C1BA Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then $

u (T,Y_1)\eqqcolon c.  \] By the inductive hypothesis, we have 92459CED0BC1 19.3.16  egin{equation}  \mu '\Bigl (\Pi ^{*} \operatorname{Tr}_{Y_1}(T-c[Y_1])\Bigr )=\mu \Bigl (\operatorname{Tr}_{Y_1}(T-c[Y_1])\Bigr )\operatorname{cor}\left(Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n,\Pi ight), \end{equation} where $\Pi \colon W_1ightarrow Y_1$ is the restriction of $\pi $. Since $\pi ^*[Y_1]=[W_1]+(\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])$, 20.2.24 and proposition 20.2.21 give \[   egin{split}  \operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*T-c[W_1] igr )\sim _ P& \operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*(T-c[Y_1]) igr )\ & +c \operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1] igr )\  \sim _ P& \Pi ^{*}\operatorname{Tr}_{Y_1} igl (T-c[Y_1] igr )+c \operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1] igr ). \end{split}  \] So \[  \mu '\Bigl (\operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*T-c[W_1] igr )\Bigr )=\mu '\Bigl (\Pi ^{*}\operatorname{Tr}_{Y_1} igl (T-c[Y_1] igr )\Bigr )+c\mu '\Bigl (\operatorname{Tr}_{W_1} igl (\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1] igr )\Bigr ).  \] Combining the above with ( 19.3.16 ), we see that ( 19.3.15 ) follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 19.3.17

text:
Proposition 19.3.17 . 8D2910CD1CEC Let $\pi \colon Z\rightarrow X$, $p\colon Z'\rightarrow Z$ be proper bimeromorphic morphisms with $Z$ and $Z'$ being Kähler manifolds. Assume that $Y_{\bullet }$ admits a lifting $W_{\bullet }$ (resp. $W_{\bullet }'$) to $Z$ (resp. $Z'$). Then 1C158885A628 19.3.18 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{cor}(Y_{\bullet },\pi \circ p)=\operatorname{cor}(Y_{\bullet },\pi )\operatorname{cor}(W_{\bullet },p). \end{equation} Proof. We let $\pi '=\pi \circ p$. Then $W'_{\bullet }$ is also the lifting of $W_{\bullet }$ with respect to $p$. We argue by induction on $n\geq 1$. The case $n=1$ is trivial. Assume that $n\geq 2$ and the case $n-1$ has been solved. Then by ( 19.3.13 ), the desired formula ( 19.3.18 ) can be reformulated as \[  \begin{aligned} & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n,\pi '|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow Y_1) 

\end{bmatrix}=\\ & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n}((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n,\pi |_{W_1}:W_1\rightarrow Y_1) 

\end{bmatrix}\cdot \\ & \begin{bmatrix}  1 

&  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'})

\\  0 

&  \operatorname{cor}(W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n,p|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow W_1) 

\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}.  \] By the inductive hypothesis, this is equivalent to \[  \begin{split}  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)= \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)+\\  \nu _{W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n}\left((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1}\right)\operatorname{cor}\left(W_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n,p|_{W_1'}:W_1'\rightarrow W_1\right), \end{split}  \] which, thanks to proposition 19.3.14 , can be further rewritten as \[  \begin{split}  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)= \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left((p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}\right)+\\  \nu _{W_1'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ n'}\left(p|_{W_1'}^*\left((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1} \right)\right). \end{split}  \] Indeed, as divisors on $W_1'$, \[  (\pi '^*[Y_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}=(p^*[W_1]-[W_1'])|_{W_1'}+p|_{W_1'}^*((\pi ^*[Y_1]-[W_1])|_{W_1}).  \] The desired equality is therefore exactly the additivity of the valuation, proposition 19.3.9 . $\square$

title: Theorem 19.3.19
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 19.3.19 . B00AB5301F7A Let $\pi \colon Z\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a reduced complex space $Z$. Then there is a modification $W\rightarrow X$ dominating $Z\rightarrow X$ such that $Y_{\bullet }$ admits a lifting to $W$. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem 9.10.8 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. We begin by setting $W_0=Z$. We will construct $W_ i$ inductively for each $i$. Assume that for $0\leq i<n$ a smooth partial flag $W_0\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_ i$ has been constructed on a modification $\pi _ i:Z_ i\rightarrow Z$ so that $\pi \circ \pi _ i$ restricts to bimeromorphic morphisms $W_ j\rightarrow Y_ j$ for each $j=0,\ldots ,i$. By Zariski's main theorem, $W_ i\rightarrow Y_ i$ is an isomorphism outside a codimension $2$ subset of $Y_ i$. We let $W_{i+1}$ be the strict transform of $Y_{i+1}$ in $W_ i$. The problem is that $W_{i+1}$ is not necessarily smooth. We will further modify $Z_ i$ and lift $W_1,\ldots , W_{i+1}$ in order to make the flag smooth. Take the embedded resolution of $(W_{j},W_{i+1})$, say $W_ j'\rightarrow W_ j$ for each $j=0,\ldots ,i$. We have canonical embeddings $W_{i}'\hookrightarrow W_{i-1}'\hookrightarrow \cdots \hookrightarrow W_0'$ making the following diagram commutative: Let $W_{i+1}'$ be the strict transform of $W_{i+1}$ in $W_ i'$. It suffices to define $\pi _{i+1}$ as the morphism $W_0'\rightarrow Z_ i\rightarrow Z$ and replace $W_0\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_{i+1}$ by $W_0'\supseteq \cdots \supseteq W_{i+1}'$. $\square$

Choose a proper bimeromorphic morphism  $h\colon \widehat Z\rightarrow Z$ from a compact Kähler manifold such that $Y_{\bullet }$ admits a lifting $(W_{\bullet },g)$ to $\widehat Z$ with respect to $\pi \circ h$, where \[  g=\operatorname{cor}(Y_{\bullet },\pi \circ h).  \] We define 9DE3455479DE 19.3.21 \begin{equation}  \nu _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\coloneqq \nu _{W_{\bullet }}(h^*S)g^{-1}\in \mathbb {R}^ n. \end{equation}

title: Lemma 19.3.22
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Lemma 19.3.22 . 24E66EB949E4 The definition in definition 19.3.20 is independent of the choice of $h$. Moreover, if $p\colon Z'ightarrow Z$ is a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a normal compact Kähler space, then, with respect to the model $\pi \circ p\colon Z'ightarrow X$, \[  
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(p^*S)=
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S).  \] Proof. We first prove independence of the choice of $h$. Let $h_ i\colon \widehat Z_ iightarrow Z$, $i=1,2$, be two choices, and let $(W^ i_{ ullet },g_ i)$ be the corresponding liftings, with $g_ i=\operatorname{cor}(Y_{ ullet },\pi \circ h_ i)$. Choose a common modification over $Z$, $q_ i\colon Uightarrow \widehat Z_ i$ such that $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting $W_{ ullet }$ to $U$. Then $W_{ ullet }$ is also the lifting of $W^ i_{ ullet }$ with respect to $q_ i$. Put \[  G_ i=\operatorname{cor}(W^ i_{ ullet },q_ i).  \] By proposition 19.3.14 , proposition 19.3.17 , \[   egin{aligned}  
u _{W_{ ullet }} igl (q_ i^*h_ i^*S igr ) \operatorname{cor}(Y_{ ullet },\pi \circ h_ i\circ q_ i)^{-1} & = 
u _{W^ i_{ ullet }}(h_ i^*S)G_ i(g_ iG_ i)^{-1} \ & = 
u _{W^ i_{ ullet }}(h_ i^*S)g_ i^{-1}. \end{aligned}  \] Since $h_1\circ q_1=h_2\circ q_2$, the left-hand side is independent of $i$. This proves that ( 19.3.21 ) is well-defined. For the birational invariance, choose a proper bimeromorphic morphism $q\colon \widehat Zightarrow Z'$ from a compact Kähler manifold such that $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting to $\widehat Z$ with respect to $\pi \circ p\circ q$. Computing $
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(p^*S)$ using $q$, and computing $
u _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)$ using $p\circ q$, gives the same expression. $\square$

text: Let $X$ be a connected smooth complex projective variety of dimension $n$ and $(L,h)$ be a Hermitian big line bundle on $X$. Let $h_0$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$. Let $\theta =c_1(L,h_0)$. Then we can identify $h$ with a function $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We will use interchangeably the notations $(\theta ,\varphi )$ and $(L,h)$. We assume that $\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }>0$ in this section. Fix a rank $n$ valuation $\nu \colon \mathbb {C}(X)^{\times }\rightarrow \mathbb {Z}^ n$, which without loss of generality can be assumed to be surjective. We shall frequently use the standard fact that such a full-rank valuation has one-dimensional leaves: for every finite-dimensional subspace $V\subset \mathbb C(X)$, \[  \# \nu (V^\times )=\dim V.  \] See [ Lemma 1.3 , LM09 ] for instance. We will adopt the notations of section 19.2 .

title: Proposition 19.4.7
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Proposition 19.4.7 . 632B1323B741 There is a convex body $\Delta \in \mathcal{K}_ n$ such that $\Gamma (L)\in \mathcal{S}'(\Delta )$. Proof. Step 1 . We first show that there is $\Delta \in \mathcal{K}_ n$ such that $\Delta _ k(L)\subseteq \Delta $. For this purpose, using 19.3.3 , we may assume that $
u $ is induced by an admissible flag $Y_{ ullet }$ on $X$. We may further assume that each $Y_ i$ is smooth. Fix $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k)^{	imes }$ for some $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Assume that $s
eq 0$. We need to show that for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$, $
u (s)_ i\leq Ck$ for some constant $C>0$, independent of the choices of $k$ and $s$. Fix an ample divisor $H$ on $X$. Take a large enough integer $b_1>0$ such that \[  (L-b_1 Y_1)\cdot H^{n-1}<0.  \] Then $
u (s)_1\leq b_1 k$. Next take a large enough integer $b_2$ such that, for every $a\in [0,b_1]$, \[  \left((L-aY_1)|_{Y_1}-b_2Y_2ight) \cdot H^{n-2}<0.  \] After removing the first vanishing order of $s$ along $Y_1$, the resulting section on $Y_1$ is a section of $k((L-aY_1)|_{Y_1})$ for some $a\in [0,b_1]$. Hence $
u (s)_2\leq b_2k$. Continuing in this manner and choosing the constants uniformly over the compact ranges of the preceding normalized vanishing orders, we conclude that $
u (s)_ i/k$ is bounded for each $i$. Here the expressions involving $L-aY_1$ are understood numerically. At the $i$-th step the previous normalized vanishing orders lie in a compact polytope, and the intersection number is continuous in these parameters; hence the constants $b_ i$ can be chosen uniformly. Step 2 . Observe that $\Gamma (L)$ is clearly a semigroup. It remains to show that $\Gamma (L)$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$ as an Abelian group. For this purpose, take two very ample divisors $A$ and $B$ so that $L=\mathcal{O}_ X(A-B)$. After choosing $A$ and $B$ ample enough, we may guarantee that there exist sections $s_0\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,A)$, $t_ i\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,B)$ for $i=0,\dots ,n$ such that \[  
u (s_0)=
u (t_0)=0  \] and $
u (t_ i)$ is the $i$-th unit vector $e_ i\in \mathbb {R}^ n$ for $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Since $L$ is big, we can find $m_0>0$ such that for any $m\geq m_0$, we can find an effective divisor $F_ m$ on $X$ linearly equivalent to $mL-B$. Let $f_ m=
u ([F_ m])$. Then \[  (f_ m,m),(f_ m+e_1,m),\dots ,(f_ m+e_ n,m)\in \Gamma (L).  \] Since $(m+1)L$ is linearly equivalent to $A+F_ m$, we have \[  (f_ m,m+1)\in \Gamma (L).  \] It follows that $\Gamma (L)$ generates $\mathbb {Z}^{n+1}$. $\square$

text: Proposition 19.4.32 . CFE94018A80A Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a modification. Then \[  \Delta _{\nu }(\pi ^*L,\pi ^*h)=\Delta _{\nu }(L,h).  \] Proof. Thanks to proposition 16.6.10 , we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model. By theorem 18.1.2 , we can find a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ with analytic singularities in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. It is clear that $\pi ^*\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. By theorem 19.4.30 , we may then reduce to the case where $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. In this case, it suffices to apply 19.4.23 . $\square$

title: Theorem 19.4.51
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 19.4.51 . 7CC4ADAC32DC Let $E$ be a prime divisor on $X$. Let $Y_{\bullet }$ be an admissible flag with $E=Y_1$. Then CA1290F03811 19.4.52 \begin{equation}  \nu (\varphi ,E)=\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1. \end{equation} Proof. Replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, we may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. By theorem 18.1.2 , we can find a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with analytic singularities such that $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $. It follows from theorem 19.4.30 that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi ).  \] Therefore, by 19.7.10 , \[  \lim _{j\to \infty }\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j)}x_1=\min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1.  \] In view of theorem 16.9.55 , it suffices to prove ( 19.4.52 ) with $\varphi _ j$ in place of $\varphi $. Step 2 . Assume that $\varphi $ has analytic singularities. In view of proposition 19.4.32 and theorem 5.18.8 , after replacing $X$ by a modification, we may assume that $\varphi $ has log singularities along an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor $F$. Perturbing $L$ by an ample $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle by proposition 19.4.39 , we may assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Therefore, $L-F$ is ample by 5.18.5 . Finally, by rescaling, we may assume that $F$ is a divisor and $L$ is a line bundle. By theorem 19.4.41 , we know that \[  \min _{x\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1=\adjustlimits \lim _{k\to \infty }\min _{x\in \Delta _ k(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1.  \] By definition, \[  \min _{x\in \Delta _ k(\theta ,\varphi )}x_1=k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right).  \] In view of proposition 5.16.15 , it remains to show that 0450C5C72C83 19.4.54 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=\lim _{k\to \infty }k^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_ E \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ). \end{equation} The $\geq $ direction is trivial, we prove the converse. Observe that \[  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)=\mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X(-kF)\right),\quad \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )=\mathcal{O}(-kF).  \] As $L-F$ is ample, for large enough $k$, the line bundle $k(L-F)$ is globally generated. Hence we can choose a section of $k(L-F)$ which does not vanish at the generic point of $E$. Viewed as a section of $L^ k\otimes \mathcal O_ X(-kF)$, it has vanishing order exactly $\operatorname{ord}_ E(kF)$ along $E$. Therefore, \[  \operatorname{ord}_ E \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes \mathcal{O}_ X(-kF)\right)=\operatorname{ord}_ E(kF).  \] Thus, ( 19.4.54 ) follows. $\square$

text: Corollary 19.4.55 . C3CA9BD5D216 Let $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. If \[  \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\theta ,\pi ^*\varphi )\subseteq \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\theta ,\pi ^*\psi )  \] for all modifications $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ and all admissible flags $W_{\bullet }$ on $Y$, then $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \psi $. Proof. By theorem 19.4.51 , the assumed inclusions imply that for every prime divisor $E$ on every modification $\pi $, \[  \nu (\pi ^*\varphi ,E)\geq \nu (\pi ^*\psi ,E).  \] Hence $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $ by proposition 16.8.9 . $\square$

title: 19.5 Transcendental partial Okounkov bodies
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n>0$. Fix a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$ on $X$. We will extend the theory of partial Okounkov bodies in the previous section to the transcendental setting.

title: 19.5.1 The traditional approach to the Okounkov body problem

topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Definition 19.5.2 . AD7EC900552C Let $\alpha $ be a big cohomology class on $X$. We define the Okounkov body of $\alpha $ with respect to the flag $Y_{\bullet }$ as 5F949352BAF6 19.5.3 \begin{equation}  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )\coloneqq \overline{\left\{ \nu _{Y_{\bullet }}(S): S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha ),S\textup{ has gentle analytic singularities} \right\} }. \end{equation} See definition 5.18.10 for the definition of gentle analytic singularities. 


The results of [ DRWNXZ ] can be summarized as follows: Theorem 19.5.4 . E839B4A35A2A For any big cohomology class $\alpha $ on $X$, the set $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$ is a convex body satisfying the following properties: D06584225E6D We have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}\alpha ;  \] 046A9D0BEEA7 given another big cohomology class $\alpha '$ on $X$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )+\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ')\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha +\alpha ');  \] 7D58AF38EA3C let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism where $Y$ is a Kähler manifold. Assume that $(W_{\bullet },g)$ is the lifting of $Y_{\bullet }$ to $Y$. Then \[  \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*\alpha )=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )g;  \] 35F74103F4DE the map $\alpha \mapsto \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )$ is continuous in the big cone with respect to the Hausdorff metric; 111D84FB6B1C for any small enough $t>0$, we have \[  \left\{  y\in \mathbb {R}^{n-1}: (t,y)\in \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ) \right\} =\Delta _{Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n}\Bigl ((\alpha -t\{ Y_1\} )|_{Y_1}\Bigr ).  \] See definition 19.3.12 for the notion of lifting. The proof requires some techniques not covered in the current book; this theorem may be used as a black box.

title: 19.5.5 Definitions of partial Okounkov bodies
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class $\alpha $. Let $T=\theta _{\varphi }\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. We shall define a convex body $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$, which is also written as $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi )$. This convex body is called the partial Okounkov body of $T$ with respect to the flag $Y_{\bullet }$.

Definition 19.5.7 . 31DAEE985011 When $T$ is a Kähler current with analytic singularities, we take a modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ so that 141D51CBF55B 9AA6F51E3D18 19.5.8  egin{equation}  \pi ^*T=[D]+R, \end{equation} where $D$ is an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor on $Y$ and $R$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential, and AE57180E327B the lifting $(Z_{ ullet },g)$ of $Y_{ ullet }$ to $Y$ exists. Define 326D63AB3B8C 19.5.9  egin{equation}  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\coloneqq \Delta _{Z_{ ullet }}(\{ R\} )g^{-1}+
u _{Z_{ ullet }}([D])g^{-1}. \end{equation} The existence of $\pi $ is guaranteed by theorem 5.18.8 and theorem 19.3.19 . Lemma 19.5.10 . 32DCABF4D374 The convex body $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$ defined in definition 19.5.7 is independent of the choice of $\pi $. Proof. Take another map $\pi '\colon Y'ightarrow X$ with the same properties. We want to show that $\pi $ and $\pi '$ define the same $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$. We may assume that $\pi '$ dominates $\pi $ through $p\colon Y'ightarrow Y$, so that we have a commutative diagram We take $D$ and $R$ as in ( 19.5.8 ). Then \[  \pi '^*T=[p^*D]+p^*R.  \] Write $(Z_{ ullet },g)$ and $(Z_{ ullet }',g')$ for the liftings of $Y_{ ullet }$ to $Y$ and $Y'$ respectively. We need to prove that \[  \Delta _{Z_{ ullet }}(\{ R\} )g^{-1}+
u _{Z_{ ullet }}([D])g^{-1}=\Delta _{Z_{ ullet }'}(\{ p^*R\} )g'^{-1}+
u _{Z_{ ullet }'}([p^*D])g'^{-1}.  \] By theorem 19.5.4 , applied to the class $\{ R\} $, we have \[  \Delta _{Z'_ ullet }(\{ p^*R\} )=\Delta _{Z_ ullet }(\{ R\} )\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] By proposition 19.3.14 , applied to the divisor current $[D]$, we also have \[  
u _{Z'_ ullet }([p^*D])=
u _{Z_ ullet }([D])\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] Finally, proposition 19.3.17 gives \[  g'=g\, \operatorname{cor}(Z_ ullet ,p).  \] Multiplying by $(g')^{-1}$ gives the desired equality. $\square$ The above proof also describes the bimeromorphic behavior of $\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)$: Lemma 19.5.11 . F1FC05EF0A7C Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_{+}(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current with analytic singularities. Let $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism and $(W_{ ullet },g)$ be the lifting of $Y_{ ullet }$ to $Y$. Then \[  \Delta _{W_{ ullet }}(\pi ^*T)=\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)g.  \] Lemma 19.5.12 . 5F65C388181A Assume that $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ are two Kähler currents with analytic singularities and $T\preceq S$. Then \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ).  \] Moreover, B544FB9D12E6 19.5.13  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)= rac{1}{n!} \int _ X T^ n. \end{equation} Proof. We first show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(S).  \] Using 19.5.11 , we may assume that $T$ and $S$ have log singularities along effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors $E$ and $F$ respectively. By assumption, $E\geq F$. Replacing $T$ and $S$ by $T-[F]$ and $S-[F]$ respectively, we may assume that $F=0$, cf. ( 19.5.9 ). In this case, we need to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha )\supseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha -\{ E\} )+
u _{Y_{ ullet }}([E]),  \] which is obvious. Next we prove that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ).  \] By 19.5.11 and theorem 19.5.4 again, we may assume that $T$ has log singularities. We take $D$ and $R$ as in ( 19.5.8 ). We need to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha -\{ D\} )+
u _{Y_{ ullet }}([D])\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}(\alpha ),  \] which is again obvious. Finally, ( 19.5.13 ) follows immediately from theorem 19.5.4 . $\square$

title: 19.5.14 The case of Kähler currents
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Definition 19.5.15 . 24F2B706F011 Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ be a Kähler current. Take a quasi-equisingular approximation $(T_ j)_ j$ of $T$ in $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. Then we define \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\coloneqq \bigcap _{j=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T_ j).  \] Lemma 19.5.16 . 08C830D7FB38 The convex body $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$ in definition 19.5.15 is independent of the choices of the $T_ j$'s. In particular, if $T$ also has analytic singularities, then the $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$'s defined in definition 19.5.15 and in definition 19.5.7 coincide. Proof. It is more convenient to use the language of $\theta $-psh functions at this point. Let $\psi _ k$ (resp. $\varphi _ k$) denote the potentials in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ corresponding to $S_ k$ (resp. $T_ k$) for each $k\geq 1$. Note that $\psi _ k$ and $\varphi _ k$ are unique up to additive constants. By proposition 5.18.12 , for any small rational $\epsilon >0$, $j>0$, we can find $k>0$ so that \[  \psi _ k\preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j.  \] By 19.5.12 , \[  \bigcap _{k=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\psi _ k)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,(1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j).  \] On the other hand, observe that \[  \bigcap _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}\text{ small enough}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,(1-\epsilon )\varphi _ j)=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\varphi _ j).  \] In fact, the $\supseteq $ direction follows from 19.5.12 , so it suffices to show that the two sides have the same volume, which follows from ( 19.5.13 ). title: 19.5.23 The general case
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text:
Definition 19.5.24 . 75695A1B0FB3 Let $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We define C022629C737B 19.5.25 \begin{equation}  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\bigcap _{j=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+j^{-1}\omega ). \end{equation} The same definition makes sense when $\alpha $ is only pseudo-effective. This definition is clearly independent of the choice of $\omega $ by 19.5.20 . Moreover, it extends definition 19.5.15 and definition 19.5.7 as a result of 19.5.20 . 


The main properties of $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$ are summarized as follows: Theorem 19.5.26 . 944BC14A8246 The convex bodies $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$ satisfy the following properties: 15D38B2026CE Suppose that $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$. We have E0BB6985CB53 19.5.27 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}T. \end{equation} 802F287FEE19 For $T,S \in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ satisfying $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}S$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ).  \] 50506C1C2B02 For any current $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ with minimal singularities, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha ).  \] 9D03BAD80E42 The map $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}\rightarrow \mathcal{K}_ n$ given by $T\mapsto \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$ is continuous, where we endow the $d_ S$-pseudometric on $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$ and the Hausdorff topology on $\mathcal{K}_ n$. D4C7EBFD1762 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism, where $Y$ is a Kähler manifold. Assume that the lifting $(W_{\bullet },g)$ of $Y_{\bullet }$ to $Y$ exists. Then for any $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$, we have \[  \Delta _{W_{\bullet }}(\pi ^*T)=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)g.  \] 8185D18AFE2D For $T,S\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$, we have 0696155A37C7 19.5.28 \begin{equation}  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)+\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+S). \end{equation} Proof. 1 By ( 19.5.25 ) and ( 19.5.19 ), for any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, \[  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)=\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+j^{-1}\omega )=\frac{1}{n!}\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}(T+j^{-1}\omega ).  \] The right-hand side is computed in proposition 18.1.27 . Hence, ( 19.5.27 ) follows. 2 Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By corollary 19.5.17 , for each $j\geq 1$, \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T+j^{-1}\omega )\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(S+j^{-1}\omega )\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha +j^{-1}\{ \omega \} ).  \] It remains to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha )=\bigcap _{j=1}^{\infty }\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\alpha +j^{-1}\{ \omega \} ).  \] The $\subseteq $ direction is clear. Comparing the volumes using theorem 19.5.4 , we conclude that equality holds. 3 This follows from 1 and 2 . 4 Let $(T_ j)_ j$ be a sequence in $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$ converging to $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$ with respect to $d_ S$. We want to show that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T_ j)\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$. By 2 , replacing the potential of each current by its $\mathcal I$-model representative does not change its partial Okounkov body. Thus we may represent the singularity types by model potentials of uniformly positive mass. Applying proposition 16.9.17 , after passing to a subsequence we may sandwich the sequence between an increasing and a decreasing sequence converging to $T$ in $d_ S$. Hence it suffices to treat the monotone cases. In either monotone case, 2 gives monotonicity of the convex bodies, while 1 and corollary 16.9.13 give convergence of their volumes to $\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$. Every Hausdorff cluster point is therefore a monotone limit with the same volume as $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$, hence is equal to $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(T)$. 5 We may assume that $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. It follows from 4 and theorem 18.1.2 that we may reduce to the case where $T$ has analytic singularities. Our assertion follows from 19.5.11 . 6 By ( 19.5.25 ), in order to prove ( 19.5.28 ), we may assume that $T$ and $S$ are both Kähler currents. Take quasi-equisingular approximations $(T_ j)_ j$ and $(S_ j)_ j$ of $T$ and $S$ respectively. By theorem 16.9.45 , $T_ j+S_ j\xrightarrow {d_ S} T+S$. By 4 , we may therefore assume that $T$ and $S$ have analytic singularities. Replacing $X$ by a suitable modification, we may assume that $T$ and $S$ both have log singularities, say \[  T=[D]+R,\quad S=[D']+R',  \] where $D$ and $D'$ are $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors on $X$ and $R$ and $R'$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents with bounded potentials. We need to show that \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} )+\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R'\} )+\nu _{Y_{\bullet }}([D])+\nu _{Y_{\bullet }}([D'])\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R+R'\} )+\nu _{Y_{\bullet }}([D+D']).  \] By proposition 19.3.9 , this is equivalent to \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R\} )+\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R'\} )\subseteq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\{ R+R'\} ),  \] which is already proved in theorem 19.5.4 . $\square$ Corollary 19.5.29 . 68273CCE4042 Assume that $L$ is a big line bundle on $X$ and $h$ is a plurisubharmonic metric on $L$ with positive volume. Then 46A0E609C71E 19.5.30 \begin{equation}  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)=\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(L,h). \end{equation} Similarly, the definition ( 19.4.38 ) is compatible with the definition in definition 19.5.24 . Proof. We may assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ has positive mass and is $\mathcal{I}$-good. By the $d_ S$-continuity of both sides of ( 19.5.30 ) as proved in theorem 19.5.26 and theorem 19.4.30 , together with theorem 18.1.2 , we may assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ has analytic singularities. In this case, using the birational invariance of both sides of ( 19.5.30 ) as proved in proposition 19.4.32 and theorem 19.5.26 , we may assume that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ has log singularities. Finally, after all these reductions, the equality ( 19.5.30 ) holds by construction. $\square$

Then 66140D1891EC 19.5.33  egin{equation}  \left\{  y\in \mathbb {R}^{n-1}: (0,y)\in \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}( eta )ight\} =\Delta _{Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n}( eta |_{Y_1}). \end{equation} Here the right-hand side is understood in the sense of definition 19.5.24 when $ eta |_{Y_1}$ is not big. Proof. Step 1 . We first reduce to the case where $ eta $ is a Kähler class. Take a Kähler class $\alpha $ on $X$. It follows from the volume formula in theorem 19.5.4 that \[  \Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}( eta )= igcap _{\epsilon >0}\Delta _{Y_{ ullet }}( eta +\epsilon \alpha ).  \] Since $ eta |_{Y_1}$ is nef, hence pseudo-effective, definition 19.5.24 similarly gives \[  \Delta _{Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n}( eta |_{Y_1})=  igcap _{\epsilon >0}\Delta _{Y_1\supseteq \cdots \supseteq Y_ n}( eta |_{Y_1}+\epsilon \alpha |_{Y_1}).  \] So it suffices to prove ( 19.5.33 ) with $ eta +\epsilon \alpha $ in place of $ eta $. Let $\pi \colon Zightarrow X$ be a modification such that 90254E23C2B2 $Y_{ ullet }$ admits a lifting $(W_{ ullet },g)$, and CA8486D14D75 $\pi ^*T=[D]+R$, where $D$ is an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor on $Z$ and $R$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with bounded potential. Fix $n\in \mathbb {N}$. Let $\Delta ,\Delta '\subseteq \mathbb {R}^ n$ be convex bodies with positive volumes. The standard Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb {R}^ n$ is denoted by $\operatorname{vol}$. We refer to section 19.7 for the basic properties of these objects. We study the notion of Okounkov test curves in this section; this leads to the definition of the Duistermaat–Heckman measure of a non-Archimedean metric in subsection 22.1.54 below. This section can be skipped on a first reading. Definition 19.6.1 . An Okounkov test curve $\Delta _{ ullet }$ relative to $\Delta $ is bounded if $\Delta _{	au }=\Delta $ when $	au $ is small enough. title: Proposition 19.6.4
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Proposition 19.6.4 . 29A7DDA38CA2 Any Okounkov test curve $(\Delta _{\tau })_{\tau < \Delta _{\max }}$ relative to $\Delta $ is continuous in $\tau $. Moreover, $\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }>0$ for all $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$. Proof. We first claim that $\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau '}>0$ for all $\tau '<\Delta _{\max }$. By Condition (2b) in definition 19.6.1 and theorem 19.7.5 , we know that $\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau ''}>0$ when $\tau ''$ is small enough. Fix one such $\tau ''$. We may assume that $\tau ''\leq \tau '$ since otherwise there is nothing to prove. Next take $\tau '''\in (\tau ',\Delta _{\max })$. Take $t\in (0,1)$ such that $\tau '=t\tau '''+(1-t)\tau ''$. It follows that \[  \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau '}\geq \operatorname{vol}\left( t\Delta _{\tau '''}+(1-t)\Delta _{\tau ''}\right)\geq (1-t)^ n\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau ''}>0.  \] Next we claim that $\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }$ is continuous for $\tau < \Delta _{\max }$. In fact, it follows from theorem 19.7.14 that $(-\infty ,\Delta _{\max }) \ni \tau \mapsto \log \operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }$ is concave, but we already know that it is finite, hence the continuity follows. Next we show that \[  \Delta _{\tau }=\bigcap _{\tau '<\tau }\Delta _{\tau '}.  \] The $\subseteq $ direction is obvious. By the continuity of the volume, both sides have the same volume and the volume is positive, we therefore obtain the equality. Similarly, we have \[  \Delta _{\tau }=\overline{\bigcup _{\tau '>\tau }\Delta _{\tau '}}.  \] The continuity of $\Delta _{\tau }$ at $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$ is proved. $\square$

text: Definition 19.6.5 . F0D4BAA63D8A A test function on $\Delta $ is a function $G\colon \Delta \rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ such that 2212D5E6C89A $G$ is concave, C997089AF9F7 $G$ is finite on $\operatorname{Int}\Delta $, and 3129698B7A89 $G$ is upper semicontinuous. A test function $G$ is bounded if $G$ is bounded from below. A test function $G$ has finite energy if 6B100556700A 19.6.6 \begin{equation}  \mathbf{E}(G)\coloneqq n!\int _{\Delta } G\, \mathrm{d}\lambda >-\infty . \end{equation}

title: Definition 19.6.7

text: Definition 19.6.7 . 7B20D9977149 Let $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$. We define its Legendre transform as \[  G[\Delta _{\bullet }] \colon \Delta \rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ),\quad a\mapsto \sup \left\{ \tau <\Delta _{\max }:a\in \Delta _{\tau }\right\} .  \] Given a test function $G\colon \Delta \rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$, we define its inverse Legendre transform $\Delta [G]_{\bullet }$ as the Okounkov test curve relative to $\Delta $ defined as follows: 76C68DFB458D $\Delta [G]_{\max }=\sup _{\Delta } G$, and 41620508AE71 for each $\tau <\sup _{\Delta } G$, we set \[  \Delta [G]_{\tau }=\{ x\in \Delta :G\geq \tau \} .  \]

title: Equation 19.6.8

text: CEDFEF97CB74 19.6.8 \begin{equation}  G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)=\max \left\{ \tau \leq \Delta _{\max }: a\in \Delta _{\tau }\right\} ,\textup{ if } G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)>-\infty . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 19.6.9
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Lemma 19.6.9 . 21BC38898B4A Let $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$. Then $G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$ defined in definition 19.6.7 is a test function. Similarly, if $G\colon \Delta \rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ is a test function, then $\Delta [G]_{\bullet }$ is an Okounkov test curve. Proof. First suppose that $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$. We want to verify that $G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$ satisfies the conditions in definition 19.6.5 . We first verify the concavity. Take $a,b\in \Delta $. We want to prove that for any $t\in (0,1)$, B1CF3E81D382 19.6.10 \begin{equation}  G[\Delta _{\bullet }](ta+(1-t)b)\geq tG[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)+(1-t)G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b). \end{equation} There is nothing to prove if $G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)$ or $G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b)$ is $-\infty $. So we assume that both are finite. In this case, by ( 19.6.8 ), \[  a\in \Delta _{G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)},\quad b\in \Delta _{G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b)}.  \] Thus, \[  ta+(1-t)b\in t \Delta _{G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)}+(1-t)\Delta _{G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b)}\subseteq \Delta _{tG[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)+(1-t)G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b)}.  \] We deduce that \[  G[\Delta _{\bullet }](ta+(1-t)b)\geq tG[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)+(1-t)G[\Delta _{\bullet }](b).  \] Therefore, ( 19.6.10 ) follows. It is clear that $G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$ is finite on the interior of $\Delta $. It remains to argue that $G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$ is upper semicontinuous. Let $(a_ i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a sequence in $\Delta $ with limit $a\in \Delta $. Define $\tau _ i=G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a_ i)$. Let $\tau =\varlimsup _ i \tau _ i$. We need to show that 910A774B0CAE 19.6.11 \begin{equation}  G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)\geq \tau . \end{equation} There is nothing to prove if $\tau =-\infty $. We assume that this is not the case. Passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $\tau _ i\to \tau $. In particular, we can assume that $\tau _ i\neq -\infty $ for all $i\geq 1$. It follows from ( 19.6.8 ) that $a_ i\in \Delta _{\tau _ i}$ for all $i\geq 1$. If $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$, then $\Delta _{\tau _ i}\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{\tau }$, so theorem 19.7.6 implies that $a\in \Delta _{\tau }$. If $\tau =\Delta _{\max }$, then the same conclusion follows from the definition $\Delta _{\Delta _{\max }}=\bigcap _{\tau '<\Delta _{\max }}\Delta _{\tau '}$. Thus, ( 19.6.11 ) follows. Conversely, suppose that $G\colon \Delta \rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ is a test function. We argue that $\Delta [G]_{\bullet }$ is an Okounkov test curve. We verify the conditions in definition 19.6.1 . Firstly, for each $\tau < \sup _{\Delta }G$, the set $\Delta [G]_{\tau }$ is a convex body as $G$ is concave and usc. Moreover, $\Delta [G]_{\tau }$ is clearly decreasing in $\tau $. Secondly, for each $a\in \Delta $, we can write $a=\lim _{i}a_ i$ with $a_ i\in \operatorname{Int}\Delta $. By assumption, $G$ is finite at $a_ i$. Thus, \[  a\in \overline{\{ G>-\infty \} }=\overline{\bigcup _{\tau <\sup _{\Delta }G}\Delta [G]_{\tau }}.  \] By theorem 19.7.6 , $\Delta [G]_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta $ as $\tau \to -\infty $. Thirdly, $\Delta [G]$ is concave. To see this, take $\tau ,\tau '< \Delta _{\max }$. We need to prove that for any $t\in (0,1)$, 8B16FED9C73C 19.6.12 \begin{equation}  \Delta [G]_{t\tau +(1-t)\tau '}\supseteq t\Delta [G]_{\tau }+(1-t)\Delta [G]_{\tau '}. \end{equation} Let $a\in \Delta [G]_{\tau }$ and $b\in \Delta [G]_{\tau '}$. We have $G(a)\geq \tau $ and $G(b)\geq \tau '$. As $G$ is concave, we have $G(ta+(1-t)b)\geq t\tau +(1-t)\tau '$. Thus, \[  ta+(1-t)b\in \Delta [G]_{t\tau +(1-t)\tau '}  \] and ( 19.6.12 ) follows. $\square$

title: Theorem 19.6.13
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 19.6.13 . 2584C29ED70F The Legendre transform and inverse Legendre transform are inverse to each other, defining a bijection between $\mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$ and the set of test functions on $\Delta $. Under this bijection, $\mathrm{TC}^1(\Delta )$ corresponds to test functions on $\Delta $ with finite energy and $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(\Delta )$ corresponds to bounded test functions on $\Delta $. Proof. Thanks to 19.6.9 , in order to prove the first assertion, it only remains to see that the Legendre transform and the inverse Legendre transform are inverse to each other, which is immediate by definition. It is obvious that $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(\Delta )$ corresponds to bounded test functions. Moreover, a direct computation shows that if $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$, then \[  \mathbf{E}(\Delta _{\bullet })=\mathbf{E}(G[\Delta _{\bullet }]),  \] concluding the $\mathrm{TC}^{1}(\Delta )$ case. $\square$

title: Proposition 19.6.14
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Proposition 19.6.14 . 7B4552909292 Let $(\Delta ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathcal{K}_ n$ such that $\Delta \subseteq \bigcap _{i\in I}\Delta ^ i$. Consider a decreasing net $(\Delta ^ i_{\bullet })_{i\in I}$ with $\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta ^ i)$ for all $i\in I$ such that there is $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$ satisfying the following properties: A929D98DE380 $\Delta _{\max }= \lim _{i\in I}\Delta ^ i_{\max }$; 791125E2CC9D for any $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$, we have $\Delta ^ i_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{\tau }$. Then for any $a\in \Delta $, we have E0766167D753 19.6.15 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I} G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a)=G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a). \end{equation} Proof. Fix $a\in \Delta $. It follows immediately from the definition of $G$ that the net $(G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a))_{i\in I}$ is decreasing and the $\geq $ direction in ( 19.6.15 ) holds. Let us prove the reverse inequality. Let $\tau $ denote the left-hand side of ( 19.6.15 ) for the moment. By definition, for any $\epsilon >0$ and any $i\in I$, we have $a\in \Delta ^ i_{\tau -\epsilon }$. It follows that \[  a\in \Delta _{\tau -\epsilon }.  \] Therefore, \[  \tau \leq G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a).  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Equation 19.6.15

text: E0766167D753 19.6.15 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I} G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a)=G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 19.6.16
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Proposition 19.6.16 . D70EFA3100C9 Let $(\Delta ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathcal{K}_ n$ with Hausdorff limit $\Delta $ such that $\operatorname{vol}\Delta ^ i>0$ for all $i\in I$. Consider an increasing net $(\Delta ^ i_{\bullet })_{i\in I}$ with $\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta ^ i)$ for all $i\in I$. Let $\Delta _{\max }=\lim _{i\in I}\Delta ^ i_{\max }$. For any $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$, let $\Delta _{\tau }$ be the Hausdorff limit of $\Delta ^ i_{\tau }$. Then $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$ and FDE24E7623A9 19.6.17 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a)=G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a) \end{equation} for any $a\in \operatorname{Int}\Delta $. Proof. It is obvious that $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$. Fix $a\in \operatorname{Int}\Delta $. Since $\Delta ^ i\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta $, we have $a\in \Delta ^ i$ for all large enough $i$. By definition, the net $(G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a))_{i\in I}$ is increasing and the $\leq $ direction in ( 19.6.17 ) holds. Let us write $\tau =G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)$ for the time being. By definition of $G$, for any $\epsilon >0$, we have \[  a\in \Delta _{\tau -\epsilon /2}.  \] The concavity of $\Delta _{\bullet }$ guarantees that \[  a\in \operatorname{Int}\Delta _{\tau -\epsilon }.  \] Indeed, choose $\sigma \ll 0$ so that a small ball around $a$ is contained in $\Delta _\sigma $. Since $a\in \Delta _{\tau -\epsilon /2}$ and \[  \tau -\epsilon =t\sigma +(1-t)(\tau -\epsilon /2)  \] for a suitable $t\in (0,1)$, concavity gives a small ball around $a$ contained in $\Delta _{\tau -\epsilon }$. Since $\Delta ^ i_{\tau -\epsilon }\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{\tau -\epsilon }$ and $a\in \operatorname{Int}\Delta _{\tau -\epsilon }$, it follows that for all large enough $i\in I$, \[  a\in \Delta ^ i_{\tau -\epsilon }.  \] Therefore, \[  \tau -\epsilon \leq G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a)  \] for all large enough $i$. Taking the limit with respect to $i$ and then with respect to $\epsilon $, we conclude the desired inequality. $\square$

title: Equation 19.6.17

text: FDE24E7623A9 19.6.17 \begin{equation}  \lim _{i\in I}G[\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }](a)=G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a) \end{equation}

title: Definition 19.6.18
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Definition 19.6.18 . 51940EF88F4F Let $\Delta _{\bullet }$ be an Okounkov test curve relative to $\Delta $. We define the Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })$ as \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })\coloneqq G[\Delta _{\bullet }]_*(\operatorname{vol}).  \] It is a Radon measure on $\mathbb {R}$, since $G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$ is finite on $\operatorname{Int}\Delta $.

title: Proposition 19.6.19
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Proposition 19.6.19 . F397AFA38927 Let $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$. Let $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Then the following extended moment identity holds: FCEE1C9E921F 19.6.20 \begin{equation}  \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })(x)=\Delta _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Delta +m\int _{-\infty }^{\Delta _{\max }} \tau ^{m-1}(\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }-\operatorname{vol}\Delta )\, \mathrm{d}\tau \end{equation} and 842F6248A5C4 19.6.21 \begin{equation}  \int _{\mathbb {R}}\operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })=\operatorname{vol}\Delta . \end{equation} Proof. In fact, ( 19.6.21 ) follows immediately from the definition. Let $G=G[\Delta _{\bullet }]$. We first assume that $G$ is bounded from below. Then ( 19.6.20 ) follows from a straightforward computation: \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })(x)\\  =&  \int _{\Delta } G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}(a)\\  =&  \int _{\Delta } \left( \Delta _{\max }^ m-\int _{G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a)}^{\Delta _{\max }} m\tau ^{m-1}\, \mathrm{d}\tau \right)\, \mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}(a)\\  =&  \Delta _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Delta -m\int _{\mathbb {R}}\int _{\Delta } \mathds {1}_{[G[\Delta _{\bullet }](a),\Delta _{\max }]}(\tau )\tau ^{m-1}\, \mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}(a)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \Delta _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Delta -m\int _{-\infty }^{\Delta _{\max }}\int _{\Delta \setminus \Delta _{\tau }} \tau ^{m-1}\, \mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}(a)\, \mathrm{d}\tau \\  =&  \Delta _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Delta -m\int _{-\infty }^{\Delta _{\max }} \tau ^{m-1}\left(\operatorname{vol}\Delta -\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }\right)\, \mathrm{d}\tau . \end{aligned}  \] In general, set $G_ A=G\lor (-A)$. The same pointwise identity applied to $G_ A$ gives \[  \int _{\Delta }G_ A^ m\, \mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}=\Delta _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Delta +m\int _{-A}^{\Delta _{\max }}\tau ^{m-1}(\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{\tau }-\operatorname{vol}\Delta )\, \mathrm{d}\tau .  \] Letting $A\to \infty $ gives ( 19.6.20 ): if $m$ is even, this follows from monotone convergence applied to $G_ A^ m\nearrow G^ m$; if $m$ is odd, apply monotone convergence to $\Delta _{\max }^ m-G_ A^ m\nearrow \Delta _{\max }^ m-G^ m$. Thus both sides of ( 19.6.20 ) are interpreted in the corresponding extended sense. $\square$
