title: Lemma 19.6.22
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Lemma 19.6.22 . 9C05354365F4 Let $(\Delta ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a decreasing sequence in $\mathcal{K}_ n$ with limit $\Delta $. Suppose that $(\Delta _{\bullet }^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is a decreasing sequence with $\Delta _{\bullet }^ i\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta ^ i)$. Suppose that there is $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$ such that F07CC70BB07B $\Delta _{\max }=\lim _{i\to \infty }\Delta ^ i_{\max }$; 3DC79FD56F54 for any $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$, we have $\Delta ^ i_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{\tau }$. Then $\operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet }^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet })$. Proof. Let $f\in C_ c(\mathbb {R})$. It follows from proposition 19.6.14 that \[  G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i]\to G[\Delta _{\bullet }]  \] pointwise on $\Delta $. Hence the dominated convergence theorem gives \[  \int _{\Delta } f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda \to \int _{\Delta } f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda .  \] Since $\Delta ^ i\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta $, theorem 19.7.5 gives $\operatorname{vol}(\Delta ^ i\setminus \Delta )\to 0$. The contribution of $\Delta ^ i\setminus \Delta $ is bounded by $\| f\| _{\infty }\operatorname{vol}(\Delta ^ i\setminus \Delta )$, so \[  \int _{\Delta ^ i} f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda \to \int _{\Delta } f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda .  \] This is the weak convergence. $\square$

title: Lemma 19.6.23
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Lemma 19.6.23 . 22B2EF8281A7 Let $(\Delta ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ be an increasing sequence in $\mathcal{K}_ n$ with Hausdorff limit $\Delta $ such that $\operatorname{vol}\Delta ^ i>0$ for all $i\geq 1$. Consider an increasing sequence $(\Delta ^ i_{\bullet })_{i\geq 1}$ with $\Delta ^ i_{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta ^ i)$ for all $i\geq 1$. Let $\Delta _{\bullet }\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta )$ be defined as 445E9FE5A513 $\Delta _{\max }=\lim _{i\to \infty }\Delta ^ i_{\max }$; 92900E34BF7D for any $\tau <\Delta _{\max }$, $\Delta _{\tau }$ is the Hausdorff limit of $\Delta ^ i_{\tau }$. Then we have \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet }^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Delta _{\bullet }).  \] Proof. Let $f\in C_ c(\mathbb {R})$. It follows from proposition 19.6.16 that \[  G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i]\to G[\Delta _{\bullet }]  \] almost everywhere on $\Delta $. Extending $f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i])$ by $0$ outside $\Delta ^ i$, we also have $\mathds {1}_{\Delta ^ i}\to \mathds {1}_{\Delta }$ almost everywhere on $\Delta $, since the boundary of the convex body $\Delta $ has Lebesgue measure zero. The dominated convergence theorem gives \[  \int _{\Delta ^ i} f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }^ i])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda \to \int _{\Delta } f(G[\Delta _{\bullet }])\, \mathrm{d}\lambda .  \] This is the weak convergence. $\square$

title: Theorem 19.6.24
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Theorem 19.6.24 . 74133E3920A2 Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class $\alpha $. Let $Y_{\bullet }$ be a smooth flag on $X$ and $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then the map \[  (-\infty ,\Gamma _{\max })\ni \tau \mapsto \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )_{\tau }\coloneqq \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })  \] defines an Okounkov test curve relative to $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty })$. If furthermore $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^1(X,\theta ;\Gamma _{-\infty })$ (resp. $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\Gamma _{-\infty })$), then we have $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\in \mathrm{TC}^1(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$ (resp. $\mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$). Proof. Consider $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We need to verify that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )$ is an Okounkov test curve relative to $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty })$. First observe that $\tau \mapsto \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })$ is concave and decreasing for $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. The decreasing property follows from theorem 19.5.26 2 . For concavity, use the valuative characterization theorem 19.5.40 together with the additivity of valuations in proposition 19.3.9 : if $x\in \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )$ and $y\in \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau '})$, then $tx+(1-t)y$ is obtained from the current $tS+(1-t)S'$, which is more singular than $\Gamma _{t\tau +(1-t)\tau '}$. Hence \[  t\Delta _{Y_\bullet }\left(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau \right)+(1-t)\Delta _{Y_\bullet }\left(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau '}\right)\subseteq \Delta _{Y_\bullet }\left(\theta ,\Gamma _{t\tau +(1-t)\tau '}\right).  \] Next we show that as $\tau \to -\infty $, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }).  \] By theorem 19.5.26 2 , the bodies $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })$ are contained in $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty })$ and increase as $\tau \to -\infty $. Thus it suffices to compute their volumes: \[  \begin{split}  \lim _{\tau \to -\infty }\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })=\frac{1}{n!}\lim _{\tau \to -\infty }\operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau })=\frac{1}{n!}\operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }) \\  =\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }), \end{split}  \] where we applied theorem 19.5.26 and theorem 16.9.57 . When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(X,\theta ;\Gamma _{-\infty })$, it is clear that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\in \mathrm{TC}^{\infty }(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$. When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{TC}^{1}(X,\theta ;\Gamma _{-\infty })$, by theorem 19.5.26 1 , ( 17.12.12 ) and ( 19.6.2 ), we have \[  \mathbf{E}^{\Gamma _{-\infty }}(\Gamma )=\mathbf{E}(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )).  \] Indeed, by theorem 19.5.26 1 , \[  n!\operatorname{vol}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )=\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _\tau }^ n  \] for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, and the same identity holds at $\tau =-\infty $. Comparing ( 17.12.12 ) with ( 19.6.2 ) gives the asserted equality of energies. So $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\in \mathrm{TC}^1(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$. $\square$

title: Remark 19.6.25
topic: Sections, graded series, and Okounkov bodies
text: Remark 19.6.25 . 731294EE36CA As a special case of this construction, suppose that $\Gamma $ is the test curve induced by a test configuration as in example 17.14.10 and 17.14.14 , then for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau })$ is the Okounkov body of a graded linear series \[  \bigoplus _{k=0}^{\infty }\mathcal{F}^{k\tau }_ k,  \] where $\mathcal{F}$ is the filtration induced by the test configuration. See [ Theorem 5.28 , Xia21 ] for the details. In particular, in this case, our theory of partial Okounkov bodies recovers the Okounkov bodies of the filtered linear series in the sense of [ BC11 ] .

title: 20.1 The theory of b-divisors
text: The purpose of this chapter is to translate the singularity theory developed in the preceding chapters into the language of b-divisors. A b-divisor records, on all proper bimeromorphic models of $X$, the cohomological data attached to a singular object. Given a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$, we associate to it a b-divisor $\mathbb D(T)$ by taking, on each modification $\pi \colon Y\to X$, the cohomology class of the regular part of $\pi ^*T$ with respect to Siu's decomposition. This construction removes divisorial components and keeps track of the moving positivity of $T$ on every model. The resulting b-divisor is nef in a suitable sense, and its volume agrees with the volume of $T$. The first part of the chapter develops this construction and studies its basic properties. We prove that $d_ S$-convergence of currents implies convergence of the associated b-divisors, and we compare the $P$- and $\mathcal I$-orders through their b-divisorial data. This gives a birational way to read some of the singularity information encoded by envelopes and multiplier ideals. The second part relates b-divisors to $\mathcal I$-good currents. In the big case, $\mathcal I$-good non-divisorial currents give rise to big and nef b-divisors, and conversely big and nef b-divisors can be represented by such currents. The final part defines mixed intersection numbers of nef b-divisors. For big and nef b-divisors this is done through the corresponding $\mathcal I$-good currents and the mixed volume formalism of section 18.1 ; the general nef case is obtained by Kähler perturbation. We prove symmetry, multilinearity, monotonicity, continuity under decreasing nets, and upper semicontinuity. These results provide the b-divisorial counterpart of the mixed volume theory.

title: 20.1.1 The notion of b-divisors
text: The b-divisors defined in this section are sometimes called b-divisor classes. We always omit the word classes to save space. Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Let us recall the following elementary result regarding how cohomology behaves under blow-up. Proposition 20.1.2 . 7E1DC3BE93AF Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a blow-up with connected smooth center of codimension at least $2$ with exceptional divisor $E$. Then there is a natural identification 73D0C455ED1D 20.1.3 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})\oplus \mathbb {R}\{ E\} . \end{equation} See [ RYY19 ] for a much more general result.

title: 20.1.4 Nef b-divisors
text: Definition 20.1.5 . 178D74F44C30 A (Weil) b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is an assignment $(\mathbb {D}_{\pi })_{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X}$, where $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ runs over all modifications of $X$ such that 81114DDA7CAF $\mathbb {D}_{\pi }\in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$; EC0926110C34 The classes are compatible under push-forwards: If $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ and $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ are both modifications of $X$ and $\pi '$ dominates $\pi $ through $g\colon Z\rightarrow Y$, then $g_*\mathbb {D}_{\pi '}=\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$. We also write $\mathbb {D}_ Y=\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$ if there is no risk of confusion. Given two Weil b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ over $X$, we say $\mathbb {D}\leq \mathbb {D}'$ if for each modification $\pi $ of $X$, we have $\mathbb {D}_{\pi }\leq \mathbb {D}'_{\pi }$. Recall that by definition, this means the class $\mathbb {D}'_{\pi }-\mathbb {D}_{\pi }$ is pseudo-effective. A Weil b-divisor with $\mathbb {D}\geq 0$ is called pseudo-effective . The class $\mathbb {D}_ X$ is called the root of $\mathbb {D}$. The set of Weil b-divisors over $X$ has the natural structure of a real vector space. Definition 20.1.6 . E6F6681E7170 The volume of a pseudo-effective Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}\coloneqq \lim _{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y.  \] The right-hand side is a decreasing net due to proposition 16.6.17 , hence the limit always exists. The volume of a non-pseudo-effective Weil b-divisor is defined to be $0$. We say $\mathbb {D}$ is big if $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0$. Lemma 20.1.7 . F5B2C1F1E318 Let $(\mathbb {D}_ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net of pseudo-effective b-divisors converging to a Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$. Then 3BFB2E87E034 20.1.8 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{i\in I}\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\leq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}. \end{equation} If the net is decreasing, then \[  \lim _{i\in I}\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Here we say $(\mathbb {D}_ i)_{i\in I}$ converges to $\mathbb {D}$ if for any modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we have $\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}\to \mathbb {D}_ Y$ with respect to the Euclidean topology. Proof. First observe that $\mathbb {D}$ is pseudo-effective, since $\mathbb {D}_ i\geq 0$ for all $i$. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a modification. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}\geq \varlimsup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i.  \] The inequality ( 20.1.8 ) follows. As for the decreasing case, it suffices to observe that both sides of ( 20.1.8 ) can be written as \[  \inf _ i \inf _{\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Example 20.1.9 . 7AF528B0FB3B In general, equality need not hold in ( 20.1.8 ). Let $X=\mathbb {P}^2$, and let $H=c_1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb {P}^2}(1))$. Choose a sequence of points $p_ i\in X$ converging to the generic point in the following sense: for every algebraic curve $C\subseteq X$, the set of indices $i$ with $p_ i\in C$ is finite. Let \[  \pi _ i\colon X_ i\rightarrow X  \] be the blow-up of $X$ at $p_ i$, with exceptional divisor $E_ i$. Let $\mathbb {D}_ i$ be the Cartier b-divisor realized on $X_ i$ by the nef class \[  \pi _ i^*H-\{ E_ i\} ,  \] and let $\mathbb {D}$ be the Cartier b-divisor realized on $X$ by $H$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ i\to \mathbb {D}$. Indeed, for any fixed modification $\rho \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the morphism $\rho $ is an isomorphism over $p_ i$ for all large enough $i$, hence the trace of $\mathbb {D}_ i$ on $Y$ is $\rho ^*H$ for all large enough $i$. On the other hand, \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i=\left(\pi _ i^*H-\{ E_ i\} \right)^2=0  \] for all $i$, whereas \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}=H^2=1.  \] Thus the inequality in ( 20.1.8 ) is strict for this sequence. Definition 20.1.10 . 908967DFB37E A Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is a Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ such that there exists a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ and a class $\alpha _ Y\in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$ so that for each $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Z$ is the pull-back of $\alpha _ Y$. Any such $(\pi ,\alpha _ Y)$ is called a realization of $\mathbb {D}$. By abuse of language, we also say $(Y,\alpha _ Y)$ is a realization of $\mathbb {D}$. The realization is not unique in general. Definition 20.1.11 . FB2640F8F828 A Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is nef if there exists a realization $(\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X, \alpha _ Y)$ of $\mathbb {D}$ such that $\alpha _ Y$ is nef. Definition 20.1.12 . 890427BD65D5 A Weil b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ is nef if it is the limit of a net of nef Cartier b-divisors $(\mathbb {D}_ i)_ i$ over $X$. In other words, for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we have $\mathbb {D}_{i,Y}\to \mathbb {D}_ Y$. Note that thanks to proposition 5.19.17 , each $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is necessarily modified nef, but it is not nef in general. The notion of modified nef classes is defined in definition 5.19.15 . A priori , for a Cartier b-divisor, nefness could mean either the notion defined by definition 20.1.11 or the one defined by definition 20.1.12 . We will show in corollary 20.1.35 that they are actually equivalent. Before that, by a nef Cartier b-divisor, we always mean nefness in the sense of definition 20.1.11 . Our definition definition 20.1.12 amounts to defining the set of Weil b-divisors as the closure of the set of Cartier b-divisors in $\varprojlim _{\pi }\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$ with respect to the projective limit topology. In particular, the limit of a converging net of nef b-divisors is still nef.

It follows from 18.1.38 that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(g_*T_ Y)=g_*T_ Y\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that 6E5120AB2EE3 20.1.26  egin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}T_ Y\geq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0. \end{equation} Next we claim that the $P$-singularity types of the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ form a decreasing net. To see this, let us fix a diagram as ( 20.1.25 ). We need to show that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\preceq _ P \pi '_*T_ Z.  \] Since $T_ Z$ has minimal singularities, we have $g_*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} T_ Z$. In particular, 20.1.23 guarantees that $\pi _*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi '_*T_ Z$. But by corollary 18.1.41 and example 18.1.11 , both $\pi _*T_ Y$ and $\pi '_*T_ Z$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, so there is no difference between the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal{I}$-preorder in this case. Our assertion follows. Next observe that the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder and has a $d_ S$-limit as a consequence of ( 20.1.26 ) and corollary 16.9.24 . Take a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$ such that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}T.  \] It follows from proposition 20.1.19 that \[  \mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)	o \mathbb {D}(T).  \] Therefore, we conclude that \[  \mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}.  \] Thanks to theorem 20.1.15 , $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Write $T=	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, then \[  T'\coloneqq 	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] is $\mathcal{I}$-good, non-divisorial and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}(T)$. $\square$ Corollary 20.1.27 . 362BC48145F6 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a b-divisor over $X$. Then the following are equivalent: 8A20F7F86FDD $\mathbb {D}$ is nef; DB94EB61358E for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Suppose that 1 holds. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Then we need to show that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Since modified nefness is a closed condition, after approximating $\mathbb {D}$ by nef Cartier b-divisors, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ itself is a nef Cartier b-divisor. We can then find a modification $\pi '\colon Zightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $ so that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by a nef class $\alpha $ on $Z$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is nothing but the pushforward of $\alpha $, and hence modified nef thanks to proposition 5.19.17 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . Suppose that 2 holds. We need to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to show that $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is nef for each $\epsilon >0$. After replacing $\mathbb {D}$ by the latter, we may further assume that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is big for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, and $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y$ has a uniform positive lower bound. In this case, the argument of theorem 20.1.24 shows that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some closed positive $(1,1)$-current in $\mathbb {D}_ X$. Therefore, $\mathbb {D}$ is nef, thanks to theorem 20.1.15 . $\square$ Let $\alpha $ be a modified nef class on $X$. We write $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )$ for the set of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T$ on $X$ with $T=\operatorname{Reg}T\in \alpha $ and $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Theorem 20.1.28 . C3EFB85C68F6 There is a natural bijection from $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$ to the set of big and nef b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ with $\mathbb {D}_ X=\alpha $. Proof. Given $T\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$, we associate the b-divisor $\mathbb {D}(T)$. It is big and nef due to theorem 20.1.15 . This map clearly descends to $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$. This map is surjective by theorem 20.1.24 . Now we show that it is injective. Let $T,T'\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$. Assume that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}(T')$, we want to show that $T\sim _{\mathcal{I}} T'$. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$, it suffices to show that 79F72595C6AE 20.1.29  egin{equation}  
u (T,E)=
u (T',E). \end{equation} We may assume that $E$ is not a prime divisor on $X$, as otherwise both sides vanish. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers \[  Y\coloneqq X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}ightarrow \cdots ightarrow X_0\coloneqq X  \] so that $E$ is a prime divisor on $Y$, exceptional with respect to $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. Denote the composition by $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. Thanks to proposition 20.1.2 , \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_ k,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X_{k-1},\mathbb {R})\oplus \mathbb {R}\{ E_ k\} ,  \] where $E_ k=E$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ kightarrow X_{k-1}$. By induction, \[  \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})=\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})\oplus  igoplus _{i=1}^{k} \mathbb {R} \{ E_ i\} ,  \] where $E_ i$ is the exceptional divisor of $X_ iightarrow X_{i-1}$. Now by 18.1.38 , F7913C6F4559 20.1.30  egin{equation}  \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T=\pi ^*T-\sum _{i=1}^ k 
u (T,E_ i)[E_ i]. \end{equation} In particular, the cohomology class of $\operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T$ determines $
u (T,E)$. Hence, ( 20.1.29 ) follows. $\square$ Corollary 20.1.31 . 1D8C494FD558 The set of nef b-divisors over $X$ with root $\alpha $ can be naturally identified with \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} ight),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$ (with respect to the preorder of reverse domination), and given two Kähler forms $\omega \leq \omega '$ the transition map \[  \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}ightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}  \] is induced by the map $\mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )ightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')$ sending $T$ to $T+\omega '-\omega $. Proof. For each Kähler form $\omega $, theorem 20.1.28 identifies $\mathcal G(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal I}$ with the set of big and nef b-divisors whose root on $X$ is $\alpha +\{ \omega \} $. The transition map is exactly addition of $\mathbb D(\omega '-\omega )$. Passing to the inverse limit gives precisely nef b-divisors with root $\alpha $. $\square$ It is tempting to extend these results to more general currents, not necessarily non-divisorial ones. For this purpose, we introduce the following definition: Definition 20.1.32 . AB54064E3778 An augmented nef b-divisor over $X$ is a pair $(\mathbb {D},D)$, where 581F18AC54FD $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$; 96DE0B4EFD35 $D$ is a formal sum \[  D=\sum _{E} c_ E E,\quad c_ E\in \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0},  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$, such that the following condition is satisfied: \[  \sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\}   \] is convergent as a sum in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. The cohomology class of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \mathbb {D}_ X+\sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R}).  \] The volume of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathbb {D},D)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Recall that we defined $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )$ as the set of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T\in \alpha $ in definition 5.19.3 . We introduce a further notation here: \[  \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}\coloneqq \left\{ T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha ): \operatorname{vol}T>0ight\} .  \] Corollary 20.1.33 . F249270AD497 There is a canonical bijection between the following sets: 3563A85C2134 The set $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$; B8F46AEB80BF the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with positive volume with cohomology class $\alpha $. More precisely, given a current $T\in \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}$, we associate $(\mathbb {D},D)$ as follows: \[  \mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T),\quad D=\sum _ E 
u (T,E)E,  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$. Proof. This is a direct consequence of theorem 20.1.28 and Siu's decomposition 5.19.12 . $\square$ In fact, corollary 20.1.33 can also be reformulated in an elementary manner, without referring to b-divisors at all. Suppose that we are given a big cohomology class $\alpha $ on $X$ and a non-negative real number $c_ E$ for each prime divisor $E$ over $X$. A natural question is: When is there a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \alpha $ with positive volume such that $
u (T,E)=c_ E$ for every $E$? Then corollary 20.1.33 says that $T$ exists if and only if the following two conditions hold: D223F2001058 \[  \lim _{\pi \colon Yightarrow X} \operatorname{vol}\left( \pi ^*\alpha -\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\}  ight)>0{}^{\href{#sgpt-a0000097338}{1}},  \] where $\pi $ runs over all modifications of $X$; 1. ↩ In particular, implicitly, the sum $\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\} $ converges in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$. 5A99823F6D1A for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the class $ \pi ^*\alpha -\sum _{E\subseteq Y} c_ E \{ E\} $ is modified nef. Similarly, we have the following generalization of corollary 20.1.31 . Corollary 20.1.34 . 5108D6DF4DAE There is a canonical bijection between the following two sets: 43F5185C6427 The set of \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha +\omega )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} ight),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$; 11B8881EEBEC the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. Apply corollary 20.1.31 to the non-divisorial parts and use Siu's decomposition on $X$ to record the divisorial part. The convergence condition in definition 20.1.32 is exactly the condition that the roots of the non-divisorial parts converge to the prescribed cohomology class $\alpha $. $\square$ Corollary 20.1.35 . DF4E1BF96D34 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a Cartier b-divisor over $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 if and only if it is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 . Proof. We only handle the nontrivial implication. Assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 . We want to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 . After replacing $X$ by a realization of $\mathbb {D}$, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by $(X,\alpha )$ for some cohomology class $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. We first assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is big. Choose a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$. Now $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ means that for each modification $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$, the current $\pi ^*T$ is non-divisorial. In particular, $T$ has vanishing generic Lelong number along each prime divisor over $X$, see ( 20.1.30 ). Equivalently, $T$ has vanishing Lelong number everywhere. By Demailly's regularization theorem, a pseudo-effective class carrying a positive current with vanishing Lelong number at every point is nef. Hence $\alpha =\{ T\} $ is nef. In the general case, fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on the realization of $\mathbb {D}$. For every $\epsilon >0$, the Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is big and nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 , hence is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 by the big case. Thus $\alpha +\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ is nef for all $\epsilon >0$, and the closedness of the nef cone shows that $\alpha $ is nef. $\square$ Corollary 20.1.36 . BF517753D33B Let $T$ and $T'$ be non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Suppose that $\{ T\} =\{ T'\} $. Then the following are equivalent: 5014A568828A $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$; 16D6081BA03D $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$. Proof. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers as in the proof of theorem 20.1.28 , so that $E$ appears as one of the exceptional prime divisors on the resulting model $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. By ( 20.1.30 ), the difference \[  \mathbb {D}(T')_ Y-\mathbb {D}(T)_ Y  \] is represented in the relative cohomology by \[  \sum _ i\left(
u (T,E_ i)-
u (T',E_ i)ight)\{ E_ i\} .  \] Using proposition 20.1.2 inductively, or equivalently the negativity lemma for exceptional classes, pseudo-effectivity of this exceptional class is equivalent to the non-negativity of all coefficients. Hence $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$ is equivalent to \[  
u (T,E)\geq 
u (T',E)  \] for every prime divisor $E$ over $X$, which is exactly $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$ by proposition 16.8.9 . $\square$ Corollary 20.1.37 . 926F05B89741 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then there is a decreasing sequence of nef and big Cartier b-divisors $\mathbb {D}_ i$ over $X$ with limit $\mathbb {D}$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By theorem 20.1.24 , for each $i>0$, we can find a non-divisorial Kähler current $T_ i\in \mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ such that \[  \mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega ).  \] We observe that $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}$ have the same $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type. Indeed, applying corollary 20.1.36 to $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}+(i^{-1}-(i+1)^{-1})\omega $ shows that these two currents are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent; adding the smooth form does not change the singularity type. Let $(T_ i^ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $T_ i$ such that 7B39195D3D69 $T_ i^ j$ is a Kähler current in $\mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ for $j\geq j_0(i)$, and CD8709C3E97A for each fixed $j$, the singularity type of $T_ i^ j$ is independent of $i$. Note that 2 is possible by using the Bergman kernel construction of the quasi-equisingular approximations, since the $T_ i$'s have the same multiplier ideals. For fixed $j$, the b-divisor \[  \mathbb {B}_ j\coloneqq \mathbb {D}(T_ i^ j)-i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )  \] is independent of $i$. Since the quasi-equisingular approximations are decreasing in $j$, the sequence $(\mathbb {B}_ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and proposition 20.1.19 gives $\mathbb {B}_ j	o \mathbb {D}$. It suffices to take $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {B}_{j_ i}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )=\mathbb {D}(T_ i^{j_ i})$, where $j_ i$ is chosen to be a sufficiently fast increasing sequence of positive integers with $j_ i\geq j_0(i)$. $\square$

title: Definition 20.1.14
text: Definition 20.1.14 . 165D43352903 Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Given any modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we define 11.3 \begin{equation}  \mathbb {D}(T)_ Y\coloneqq \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\pi ^*T \right\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R}). \end{equation} We call $\mathbb {D}(T)$ the b-divisor of $T$ .

title: Theorem 20.1.15
text: Theorem 20.1.15 . 6EB1B4E1D222 Let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef. Moreover, 1D610D16E240 20.1.16 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}T=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T). \end{equation} Proof. Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Step 1 . Reduce to the case where $T$ is a Kähler current. Note that $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is the Cartier b-divisor realized by $(X,\{ \omega \} )$. The b-divisors $\mathbb {D}(T+\epsilon \omega )=\mathbb {D}(T)+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ decrease to $\mathbb {D}(T)$ as $\epsilon \searrow 0$. Hence, by 20.1.7 and proposition 18.1.27 , it suffices to prove our assertion with $T+\epsilon \omega $ in place of $T$. Step 2 . We prove the assertion under the additional assumption that $T$ has analytic singularities. Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a modification so that \[  \pi ^*T=[D]+R,  \] where $D$ is an effective $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor on $Y$ and $R$ is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current with locally bounded potentials. See theorem 5.18.8 for the existence of $\pi $. Then $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is the nef Cartier b-divisor realized by $(\pi ,\{ R\} )$. Note that ( 20.1.16 ) is immediate in this case. Step 3 . We prove the assertion for a general Kähler current $T$. Next, take a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ in the cohomology class of $T$ and write $T=\theta _{\varphi }$ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Since $T$ is a Kähler current, we choose the quasi-equisingular approximation $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ of $\varphi $ so that, after discarding finitely many terms, each $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ is a Kähler current. This is possible by Demailly regularization, in the form used in the proof of theorem 18.1.2 . We claim that 35EFEAF9683D 20.1.17 \begin{equation}  \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\to \mathbb {D}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi ). \end{equation} By definition of this convergence, we need to establish the following: for every modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we have \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\right)\right\} \to \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )\right)\right\} .  \] This follows immediately from theorem 16.9.55 if $\operatorname{Sing}(\pi ^*T)$ has only finitely many components. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$. We want to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $j_0>0$ so that when $j\geq j_0$, 725B7EF61286 20.1.18 \begin{equation}  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j)\right)\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\left(\pi ^*(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )\right)\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega _ Y\} . \end{equation} Write the divisorial part of $\pi ^*\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi _ j$ and $\pi ^*\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\pi ^*\varphi $ as \[  \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i^ j [E_ i],\quad \sum _{i=1}^{\infty }a_ i [E_ i].  \] Then $a_ i^ j\leq a_ i$. We can find an integer $N>0$ large enough so that, in the pseudo-effective order of cohomology classes, \[  \sum _{i=N+1}^{\infty }a_ i \{ E_ i\} \leq \frac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] By theorem 16.9.55 , we can take $j_0$ large enough so that for $j>j_0$, \[  \sum _{i=1}^{N}(a_ i-a_ i^ j)\{ E_ i\} \leq \frac{\epsilon }{2}\{ \omega _ Y\} .  \] Then ( 20.1.18 ) follows, and ( 20.1.17 ) is established. As a consequence, $\mathbb {D}(T)$ is nef and the volume can be computed using 20.1.7 : \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}(T)=\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}\left( \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j \right)=\lim _{j\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j\right)=\operatorname{vol}T.  \] Hence, ( 20.1.16 ) follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 20.1.19
text: Proposition 20.1.19 . 87D0CCEB6DF9 Let $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $(\varphi _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. If $\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 64E2A79320D9 20.1.20 \begin{equation}  \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right). \end{equation} Proof. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to establish the following: 808CB322D92D 20.1.21 \begin{equation}  \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right)_ Y\to \mathbb {D}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right)_ Y. \end{equation} As a map from the pseudometric space $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ to the finite-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(Y,\mathbb {R})$, the continuity of $\mathbb {D}(\bullet )_ Y$ can be tested on sequences. Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume that $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is a sequence and $I=\mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. It is enough to prove that every subsequence has a further subsequence for which ( 20.1.22 ) holds. By corollary 16.9.11 , $\pi ^*\varphi _ i\xrightarrow {d_ S}\pi ^*\varphi $. Hence it suffices to prove the claim on $Y$, so we may assume that $\pi $ is the identity. Therefore, we are reduced to the following assertion: 762B9BFFA0ED 20.1.22 \begin{equation}  \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i} \right\} \to \left\{  \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi } \right\} . \end{equation} After adding a Kähler form to $\theta $, we may also assume that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. By theorem 16.9.49 , replacing all potentials by their $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes does not change the divisorial parts and preserves $d_ S$-convergence. The masses are then bounded from below along a tail, so after passing to a subsequence proposition 16.9.17 supplies increasing and decreasing envelopes $\eta _ i\leq \varphi _ i\leq \psi _ i$ which both converge to $\varphi $ in $d_ S$. Since \[  \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\eta _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\varphi _ i})_ X\leq \mathbb {D}(\theta _{\psi _ i})_ X,  \] it is enough to treat the case where $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is monotone. Write the divisorial parts of $\theta _{\varphi _ i}$ and $\theta _{\varphi }$ as \[  \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m^ i[D_ m],\quad \sum _{m=1}^{\infty }a_ m[D_ m].  \] By theorem 16.9.55 , $a_ m^ i\to a_ m$ for each fixed $m$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is decreasing, then $a_ m^ i\leq a_ m$ for all $i,m$. The finite-tail argument in the proof of ( 20.1.18 ) then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. If $(\varphi _ i)_ i$ is increasing, then $a_ m\leq a_ m^ i\leq a_ m^1$. We first choose $N$ so that the tails of both $\sum _ m a_ m[D_ m]$ and $\sum _ m a_ m^1[D_ m]$ are at most $(\epsilon /3)\{ \omega \} $ in the pseudo-effective order. The convergence of the finitely many coefficients $a_ m^ i$, $m\leq N$, then gives \[  \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi }\right\} \leq \left\{ \operatorname{Reg}\theta _{\varphi _ i}\right\} +\epsilon \{ \omega \}   \] for all sufficiently large $i$. This proves ( 20.1.22 ). $\square$

title: Lemma 20.1.23
text: Lemma 20.1.23 . 476687DD2394 Let $\pi \colon X\rightarrow Z$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from $X$ to a Kähler manifold $Z$. Consider non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$ currents $T,S$ on $X$ in the same cohomology class. If $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} S$, then $\pi _*T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi _*S$. Proof. By Hironaka's Chow lemma theorem 9.10.8 and 16.8.26 , we may assume that $\pi $ is a modification. By 18.1.38 , \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T,\quad \pi ^*\pi _*S=S+F_ S,  \] where $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ are effective $\pi $-exceptional divisors. Since $\{ T\} =\{ S\} $, the exceptional divisors $F_ T$ and $F_ S$ have the same cohomology class. Factoring $\pi $ into blow-ups and using proposition 20.1.2 at each step, the classes of $\pi $-exceptional prime divisors are linearly independent in the relative cohomology; hence $F_ T=F_ S$. It follows that \[  \pi ^*\pi _*T=T+F_ T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}S+F_ S=\pi ^*\pi _*S.  \] Our assertion then follows from 16.8.26 . $\square$

title: Theorem 20.1.24
text: Theorem 20.1.24 . EA1E72841C6D Each big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ can be realized as $\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$. Furthermore, we may always assume that $T$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good. Proof. Fix a big and nef b-divisor $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$. For each $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, we take a current with minimal singularities $T_ Y$ in $\mathbb {D}_ Y$. We claim that $\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)$ coincides with $\mathbb {D}$ up to the level of $Y$: For any modification $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominated by $\pi $ through a morphism $g\colon Y\rightarrow Z$, we have \[  \mathbb {D}_ Z=\mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Z.  \] The notations are summarized in the following commutative diagram: 36BC6A8ED233 20.1.25 After unfolding the definitions, this means \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^*\pi _*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y).  \] Due to proposition 5.19.17 and proposition 16.6.17 , we know that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef and big. In particular, $T_ Y$ is non-divisorial, hence so is $g_*T_ Y$ by 5.19.18 . It follows from 18.1.38 that \[  \operatorname{Reg}(\pi '^* \pi '_* g_*T_ Y)=\operatorname{Reg}(g_*T_ Y)=g_*T_ Y\in \mathbb {D}_ Z.  \] Note that 6E5120AB2EE3 20.1.26 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}T_ Y\geq \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}>0. \end{equation} Next we claim that the $P$-singularity types of the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ form a decreasing net. To see this, let us fix a diagram as ( 20.1.25 ). We need to show that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\preceq _ P \pi '_*T_ Z.  \] Since $T_ Z$ has minimal singularities, we have $g_*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} T_ Z$. In particular, 20.1.23 guarantees that $\pi _*T_ Y\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \pi '_*T_ Z$. But by corollary 18.1.41 and example 18.1.11 , both $\pi _*T_ Y$ and $\pi '_*T_ Z$ are $\mathcal{I}$-good, so there is no difference between the $P$-preorder and the $\mathcal{I}$-preorder in this case. Our assertion follows. Next observe that the net $(\pi _*T_ Y)_ Y$ is decreasing with respect to the $P$-preorder and has a $d_ S$-limit as a consequence of ( 20.1.26 ) and corollary 16.9.24 . Take a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T\in \mathbb {D}_ X$ such that \[  \pi _*T_ Y\xrightarrow {d_ S}T.  \] It follows from proposition 20.1.19 that \[  \mathbb {D}(\pi _*T_ Y)\to \mathbb {D}(T).  \] Therefore, we conclude that \[  \mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}.  \] Thanks to theorem 20.1.15 , $\operatorname{vol}T>0$. Write $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for some $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, then \[  T'\coloneqq \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] is $\mathcal{I}$-good, non-divisorial and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}(T)$. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.1.27
text: Corollary 20.1.27 . 362BC48145F6 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a b-divisor over $X$. Then the following are equivalent: 8A20F7F86FDD $\mathbb {D}$ is nef; DB94EB61358E for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the class $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Proof. 1 $\implies $ 2 . Suppose that 1 holds. Fix a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$. Then we need to show that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is modified nef. Since modified nefness is a closed condition, after approximating $\mathbb {D}$ by nef Cartier b-divisors, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ itself is a nef Cartier b-divisor. We can then find a modification $\pi '\colon Z\rightarrow X$ dominating $\pi $ so that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by a nef class $\alpha $ on $Z$. Then $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is nothing but the pushforward of $\alpha $, and hence modified nef thanks to proposition 5.19.17 . 2 $\implies $ 1 . Suppose that 2 holds. We need to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. It suffices to show that $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is nef for each $\epsilon >0$. After replacing $\mathbb {D}$ by the latter, we may further assume that $\mathbb {D}_ Y$ is big for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, and $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ Y$ has a uniform positive lower bound. In this case, the argument of theorem 20.1.24 shows that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ for some closed positive $(1,1)$-current in $\mathbb {D}_ X$. Therefore, $\mathbb {D}$ is nef, thanks to theorem 20.1.15 . $\square$

title: Theorem 20.1.28
text:
Theorem 20.1.28 . C3EFB85C68F6 There is a natural bijection from $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$ to the set of big and nef b-divisors $\mathbb {D}$ over $X$ with $\mathbb {D}_ X=\alpha $. Proof. Given $T\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$, we associate the b-divisor $\mathbb {D}(T)$. It is big and nef due to theorem 20.1.15 . This map clearly descends to $\mathcal{G}(\alpha )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$. This map is surjective by theorem 20.1.24 . Now we show that it is injective. Let $T,T'\in \mathcal{G}(\alpha )$. Assume that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}(T')$, we want to show that $T\sim _{\mathcal{I}} T'$. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$, it suffices to show that 79F72595C6AE 20.1.29  egin{equation}

title: Corollary 20.1.31
text: Corollary 20.1.31 . 1D8C494FD558 The set of nef b-divisors over $X$ with root $\alpha $ can be naturally identified with \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \right),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$ (with respect to the preorder of reverse domination), and given two Kähler forms $\omega \leq \omega '$ the transition map \[  \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\rightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}  \] is induced by the map $\mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega )\rightarrow \mathcal{G}(\alpha +\omega ')$ sending $T$ to $T+\omega '-\omega $. Proof. For each Kähler form $\omega $, theorem 20.1.28 identifies $\mathcal G(\alpha +\omega )/\sim _{\mathcal I}$ with the set of big and nef b-divisors whose root on $X$ is $\alpha +\{ \omega \} $. The transition map is exactly addition of $\mathbb D(\omega '-\omega )$. Passing to the inverse limit gives precisely nef b-divisors with root $\alpha $. $\square$

title: Definition 20.1.32
text: Definition 20.1.32 . AB54064E3778 An augmented nef b-divisor over $X$ is a pair $(\mathbb {D},D)$, where 581F18AC54FD $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$; 96DE0B4EFD35 $D$ is a formal sum \[  D=\sum _{E} c_ E E,\quad c_ E\in \mathbb {R}_{\geq 0},  \] where $E$ runs over the set of prime divisors on $X$, such that the following condition is satisfied: \[  \sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\}   \] is convergent as a sum in $\mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. The cohomology class of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \mathbb {D}_ X+\sum _{E}c_ E \{ E\} \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R}).  \] The volume of $(\mathbb {D},D)$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{vol}(\mathbb {D},D)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \]

title: Corollary 20.1.33
text: Corollary 20.1.33 . F249270AD497 There is a canonical bijection between the following sets: 3563A85C2134 The set $\mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}}$; B8F46AEB80BF the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with positive volume with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. This is a direct consequence of theorem 20.1.28 and Siu's decomposition 5.19.12 . $\square$

title: Corollary 20.1.34
text: Corollary 20.1.34 . 5108D6DF4DAE There is a canonical bijection between the following two sets: 43F5185C6427 The set of \[  \varprojlim _{\omega } \left( \mathcal{Z}_+(X,\alpha +\omega )_{>0}/\sim _{\mathcal{I}} \right),  \] where $\omega $ runs over the directed set of Kähler forms on $X$; 11B8881EEBEC the set of augmented nef b-divisors over $X$ with cohomology class $\alpha $. Proof. Apply corollary 20.1.31 to the non-divisorial parts and use Siu's decomposition on $X$ to record the divisorial part. The convergence condition in definition 20.1.32 is exactly the condition that the roots of the non-divisorial parts converge to the prescribed cohomology class $\alpha $. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.1.35
text: Corollary 20.1.35 . DF4E1BF96D34 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a Cartier b-divisor over $X$. Then $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 if and only if it is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 . Proof. We only handle the nontrivial implication. Assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 . We want to show that $\mathbb {D}$ is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 . After replacing $X$ by a realization of $\mathbb {D}$, we may assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is realized by $(X,\alpha )$ for some cohomology class $\alpha \in \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. We first assume that $\mathbb {D}$ is big. Choose a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$. Now $\mathbb {D}=\mathbb {D}(T)$ means that for each modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$, the current $\pi ^*T$ is non-divisorial. In particular, $T$ has vanishing generic Lelong number along each prime divisor over $X$, see ( 20.1.30 ). Equivalently, $T$ has vanishing Lelong number everywhere. By Demailly's regularization theorem, a pseudo-effective class carrying a positive current with vanishing Lelong number at every point is nef. Hence $\alpha =\{ T\} $ is nef. In the general case, fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on the realization of $\mathbb {D}$. For every $\epsilon >0$, the Cartier b-divisor $\mathbb {D}+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega )$ is big and nef in the sense of definition 20.1.12 , hence is nef in the sense of definition 20.1.11 by the big case. Thus $\alpha +\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ is nef for all $\epsilon >0$, and the closedness of the nef cone shows that $\alpha $ is nef. $\square$

title: Corollary 20.1.36
text:
Corollary 20.1.36 . BF517753D33B Let $T$ and $T'$ be non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Suppose that $\{ T\} =\{ T'\} $. Then the following are equivalent: 5014A568828A $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$; 16D6081BA03D $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$. Proof. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$. Choose a sequence of blow-ups with smooth connected centers as in the proof of theorem 20.1.28 , so that $E$ appears as one of the exceptional prime divisors on the resulting model $\pi \colon Yightarrow X$. By ( 20.1.30 ), the difference \[  \mathbb {D}(T')_ Y-\mathbb {D}(T)_ Y  \] is represented in the relative cohomology by \[  \sum _ i\left(
u (T,E_ i)-
u (T',E_ i)ight)\{ E_ i\} .  \] Using proposition 20.1.2 inductively, or equivalently the negativity lemma for exceptional classes, pseudo-effectivity of this exceptional class is equivalent to the non-negativity of all coefficients. Hence $\mathbb {D}(T)\leq \mathbb {D}(T')$ is equivalent to \[  
u (T,E)\geq 
u (T',E)  \] for every prime divisor $E$ over $X$, which is exactly $T\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}T'$ by proposition 16.8.9 . $\square$

title: Corollary 20.1.37
text: Corollary 20.1.37 . 926F05B89741 Let $\mathbb {D}$ be a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then there is a decreasing sequence of nef and big Cartier b-divisors $\mathbb {D}_ i$ over $X$ with limit $\mathbb {D}$. Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. By theorem 20.1.24 , for each $i>0$, we can find a non-divisorial Kähler current $T_ i\in \mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ such that \[  \mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega ).  \] We observe that $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}$ have the same $\mathcal{I}$-singularity type. Indeed, applying corollary 20.1.36 to $T_ i$ and $T_{i+1}+(i^{-1}-(i+1)^{-1})\omega $ shows that these two currents are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent; adding the smooth form does not change the singularity type. Let $(T_ i^ j)_ j$ be quasi-equisingular approximations of $T_ i$ such that 7B39195D3D69 $T_ i^ j$ is a Kähler current in $\mathbb {D}_ X+i^{-1}\{ \omega \} $ for $j\geq j_0(i)$, and CD8709C3E97A for each fixed $j$, the singularity type of $T_ i^ j$ is independent of $i$. Note that 2 is possible by using the Bergman kernel construction of the quasi-equisingular approximations, since the $T_ i$'s have the same multiplier ideals. For fixed $j$, the b-divisor \[  \mathbb {B}_ j\coloneqq \mathbb {D}(T_ i^ j)-i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )  \] is independent of $i$. Since the quasi-equisingular approximations are decreasing in $j$, the sequence $(\mathbb {B}_ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and proposition 20.1.19 gives $\mathbb {B}_ j\to \mathbb {D}$. It suffices to take $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {B}_{j_ i}+i^{-1}\mathbb {D}(\omega )=\mathbb {D}(T_ i^{j_ i})$, where $j_ i$ is chosen to be a sufficiently fast increasing sequence of positive integers with $j_ i\geq j_0(i)$. $\square$

title: 20.1.38 Properties of the intersection product
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$. Recall that the mixed volume of currents is studied in subsection 18.1.20 . Definition 20.1.39 . BFB26AC5F975 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as \[  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n),  \] where $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents in $\mathbb {D}_{1,X},\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_{n,X}$ respectively such that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_{i}$. The definition makes sense thanks to theorem 20.1.24 . It does not depend on the choices of $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ since they are uniquely defined up to $\mathcal{I}$-equivalence, as proved in theorem 20.1.28 . Lemma 20.1.40 . DFC2368D5436 0B43092BD979 The product in definition 20.1.39 is symmetric in its $n$ variables. 3FE06BA1D6F2 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n,\mathbb {D}'_1$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1+\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+\left(\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] 6704C2A24387 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$. Then \[  \left(\lambda \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\lambda \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] 41087E4D84EF Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_1\leq \mathbb {D}'$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq \left(\mathbb {D}',\mathbb {D}_2,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Proof. 1 , 2 and 3 follow immediately from the corresponding results for mixed volumes, as proved in proposition 18.1.27 . 4 Take $\mathcal{I}$-good non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ and $T'$ so that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}'$. Furthermore, we may assume that the $T_ i$'s and $T'$ are Kähler currents by the perturbation argument. Let $(T_{i}^ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $T_ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$. It follows from theorem 16.9.30 that \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n=\lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] It suffices to show that for all $j\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j\leq \int _ X T'\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] Therefore, we have reduced to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have analytic singularities. After a resolution, we may assume that they have log singularities along $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors. By proposition 18.1.27 5 , we can further reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have bounded local potentials. Perturbing $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ by a Kähler form, we may further assume that $\{ T_2\} ,\ldots , \{ T_ n\} $ are Kähler classes. By proposition 18.1.27 4 , we finally reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ are Kähler forms. In this case, the assertion follows from the pseudo-effectivity of $\{ T'\} -\{ T_1\} $. $\square$ In general, we can extend the definition of the intersection product to nef b-divisors as follows: Definition 20.1.41 . 60343D71D40A Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as 33927991E020 20.1.42 \begin{equation}  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$. Note that as $\epsilon \to 0+$, $\left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)$ is decreasing, as a consequence of 20.1.40 4 . Similarly, by 20.1.40 4 again, the definition is independent of the choice of $\omega $. Proposition 20.1.43 . AEC81016D4BC 413103745994 The product in definition 20.1.41 is symmetric in its $n$ variables. E21CF2D200CF Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n,\mathbb {D}'_1$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1+\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+\left(\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] F1CD812A96DA Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$. Then \[  \left(\lambda \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\lambda \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] B5FA9D24DE24 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_1\leq \mathbb {D}'$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq \left(\mathbb {D}',\mathbb {D}_2,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] 2960B6AF1379 Let $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$. Then \[  \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}(T_1),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}(T_ n) \Bigr )= \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n).  \] Proof. 1 , 2 , 3 and 4 These are immediate consequences of the corresponding results in the big and nef case established in 20.1.40 . 5 By ( 18.1.26 ) and ( 20.1.42 ), we may assume that $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are Kähler currents. In this case, the assertion follows from the definitions. $\square$ Lemma 20.1.44 . D57BEED0545E Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Fix a compact set $K\subseteq \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_{i,X}\in K$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then there is a constant $C$ depending only on $X,K,\{ \omega \} $ such that for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$, we have \[  0\leq \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr )-\left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq C\epsilon .  \] Proof. By 20.1.40 4 , the left-hand side is non-negative. For the upper bound, by the multi-linearity of the product proved in proposition 20.1.43 , we can rewrite the difference as a sum of $2^ n-1$ terms like \[  \epsilon ^{m} \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}(\omega )^{m}, \mathbb {D}_{i_1},\ldots , \mathbb {D}_{i_{n-m}} \Bigr ),  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. We need to show that these coefficients are uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on the given data. For this purpose, we add $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ to each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ and then replace $K$ by $K+\{ \omega \} $. Therefore, we reduce to the case where each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ is nef and big, and hence $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {D}(T_ i)$ for some $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes. Then we need to bound \[  \int _ X \omega ^ m\wedge T_{i_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{i_{n-m}}.  \] For this purpose, let $D\geq 0$ be the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} -\alpha $ is nef for any $\alpha \in K$. Then the integral is bounded by the cohomological intersection $\{ \omega \} ^ m\cap (D\{ \omega \} )^{n-m}$. Our assertion follows. $\square$ We first make a consistency check. Proposition 20.1.45 . 9D4AD4B277B4 Suppose that $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then \[  \left( \mathbb {D},\ldots ,\mathbb {D} \right)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Proof. Using 20.1.44 and 20.1.7 , we may easily reduce to the case where $\mathbb {D}$ is nef and big. In this case, take a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ in $\mathbb {D}_ X$ such that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}$. Then we need to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}=\operatorname{vol}T,  \] which is proved in theorem 20.1.15 . $\square$ Proposition 20.1.46 . 2E8615B14EC8 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\right)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, our assertion follows from proposition 18.1.36 . $\square$ Proposition 20.1.47 . 754B050BFA6C The product in definition 20.1.41 is upper semicontinuous in the following sense. Suppose that $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ are nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7E0BA3EB7A39 20.1.48 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right)\leq \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that the $\mathbb D_ i^ j$'s and the $\mathbb D_ i$'s are all big. Choose $\mathcal I$-good non-divisorial currents $T_ i^ j$ and $T_ i$ such that $\mathbb D(T_ i^ j)=\mathbb D_ i^ j$ and $\mathbb D(T_ i)=\mathbb D_ i$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and fix $\epsilon >0$. Since $\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j\to \mathbb D_{i,X}$, for all sufficiently large $j$ the class \[  \mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} -\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j  \] is Kähler. Choose a Kähler form $\chi _ i^ j$ in this class and set $S_ i^ j=T_ i^ j+\chi _ i^ j$. Then $S_ i^ j$ lies in the fixed class $\mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ and has the same divisorial Lelong numbers as $T_ i^ j$. Hence, by theorem 18.1.42 and proposition 18.1.27 2 , \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (T_1^ j,\ldots ,T_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (S_1^ j,\ldots ,S_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right).  \] Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\Bigl (\mathbb D_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \Bigl (\mathbb D_1+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega )\Bigr ).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ gives ( 20.1.48 ). Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then by 20.1.44 , for any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right) \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 20.1.49 . FE8A163BAA22 The product in definition 20.1.41 is continuous along decreasing nets in each variable. In other words, if $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ ($i=1,\ldots ,n$) are decreasing nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$, then \[  \lim _{j\in J} \left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j\right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n\right).  \] Proof. This is a straightforward consequence of 20.1.40 4 and proposition 20.1.47 . $\square$ Remark 20.1.50 . D7547FA69C91 The algebraic nef b-divisors are equipped with the corresponding algebraic intersection theory. It is a straightforward application of the results proved in this section that our transcendental intersection theory coincides with theirs in the algebraic setting.

title: Definition 20.1.39
text: Definition 20.1.39 . BFB26AC5F975 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as \[  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \operatorname{vol}(T_1,\ldots ,T_ n),  \] where $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ are closed positive $(1,1)$-currents in $\mathbb {D}_{1,X},\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_{n,X}$ respectively such that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_{i}$.

title: Lemma 20.1.40
text: Lemma 20.1.40 . DFC2368D5436 0B43092BD979 The product in definition 20.1.39 is symmetric in its $n$ variables. 3FE06BA1D6F2 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n,\mathbb {D}'_1$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1+\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+\left(\mathbb {D}_1',\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] 6704C2A24387 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ and $\lambda \geq 0$. Then \[  \left(\lambda \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)=\lambda \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] 41087E4D84EF Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ and $\mathbb {D}'$ be big and nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_1\leq \mathbb {D}'$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq \left(\mathbb {D}',\mathbb {D}_2,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right).  \] Proof. 1 , 2 and 3 follow immediately from the corresponding results for mixed volumes, as proved in proposition 18.1.27 . 4 Take $\mathcal{I}$-good non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-currents $T_1,\ldots ,T_ n$ and $T'$ so that $\mathbb {D}(T_ i)=\mathbb {D}_ i$ for all $i=1,\ldots ,n$ and $\mathbb {D}(T')=\mathbb {D}'$. Furthermore, we may assume that the $T_ i$'s and $T'$ are Kähler currents by the perturbation argument. Let $(T_{i}^ j)_ j$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $T_ i$ for $i=2,\ldots ,n$. It follows from theorem 16.9.30 that \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n=\lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] It suffices to show that for all $j\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X T_1\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j\leq \int _ X T'\wedge T_2^ j\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ n^ j.  \] Therefore, we have reduced to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have analytic singularities. After a resolution, we may assume that they have log singularities along $\mathbb {Q}$-divisors. By proposition 18.1.27 5 , we can further reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ have bounded local potentials. Perturbing $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ by a Kähler form, we may further assume that $\{ T_2\} ,\ldots , \{ T_ n\} $ are Kähler classes. By proposition 18.1.27 4 , we finally reduce to the case where $T_2,\ldots ,T_ n$ are Kähler forms. In this case, the assertion follows from the pseudo-effectivity of $\{ T'\} -\{ T_1\} $. $\square$

title: Definition 20.1.41
text: Definition 20.1.41 . 60343D71D40A Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then we define their intersection as 33927991E020 20.1.42 \begin{equation}  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\coloneqq \lim _{\epsilon \to 0+}\Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ is a Kähler form on $X$. Note that as $\epsilon \to 0+$, $\left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)$ is decreasing, as a consequence of 20.1.40 4 . Similarly, by 20.1.40 4 again, the definition is independent of the choice of $\omega $.

title: Lemma 20.1.44
text: Lemma 20.1.44 . D57BEED0545E Let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$. Fix a compact set $K\subseteq \mathrm{H}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb {R})$. Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$ such that $\mathbb {D}_{i,X}\in K$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then there is a constant $C$ depending only on $X,K,\{ \omega \} $ such that for any $\epsilon \in [0,1]$, we have \[  0\leq \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \Bigr )-\left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\leq C\epsilon .  \] Proof. By 20.1.40 4 , the left-hand side is non-negative. For the upper bound, by the multi-linearity of the product proved in proposition 20.1.43 , we can rewrite the difference as a sum of $2^ n-1$ terms like \[  \epsilon ^{m} \Bigl ( \mathbb {D}(\omega )^{m}, \mathbb {D}_{i_1},\ldots , \mathbb {D}_{i_{n-m}} \Bigr ),  \] where $J\subseteq \{ 1,\ldots ,n\} $ is a non-empty subset of cardinality $m$, and $\{ i_1,\ldots ,i_{n-m}\} $ is the complement of $J$. We need to show that these coefficients are uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on the given data. For this purpose, we add $\mathbb {D}(\omega )$ to each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ and then replace $K$ by $K+\{ \omega \} $. Therefore, we reduce to the case where each $\mathbb {D}_ i$ is nef and big, and hence $\mathbb {D}_ i=\mathbb {D}(T_ i)$ for some $\mathcal{I}$-good closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on $X$ with positive volumes. Then we need to bound \[  \int _ X \omega ^ m\wedge T_{i_1}\wedge \cdots \wedge T_{i_{n-m}}.  \] For this purpose, let $D\geq 0$ be the minimal non-negative number so that $D\{ \omega \} -\alpha $ is nef for any $\alpha \in K$. Then the integral is bounded by the cohomological intersection $\{ \omega \} ^ m\cap (D\{ \omega \} )^{n-m}$. Our assertion follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 20.1.45
text: Proposition 20.1.45 . 9D4AD4B277B4 Suppose that $\mathbb {D}$ is a nef b-divisor over $X$. Then \[  \left( \mathbb {D},\ldots ,\mathbb {D} \right)=\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}.  \] Proof. Using 20.1.44 and 20.1.7 , we may easily reduce to the case where $\mathbb {D}$ is nef and big. In this case, take a non-divisorial closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ in $\mathbb {D}_ X$ such that $\mathbb {D}(T)=\mathbb {D}$. Then we need to show that \[  \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}=\operatorname{vol}T,  \] which is proved in theorem 20.1.15 . $\square$

title: Proposition 20.1.46
text: Proposition 20.1.46 . 2E8615B14EC8 Let $\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n$ be nef b-divisors over $X$. Then \[  \left(\mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)\geq \prod _{i=1}^ n \left( \operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i\right)^{1/n}.  \] Proof. We may assume that $\operatorname{vol}\mathbb {D}_ i>0$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$ since there is nothing to prove otherwise. In this case, our assertion follows from proposition 18.1.36 . $\square$

title: Proposition 20.1.47
text: Proposition 20.1.47 . 754B050BFA6C The product in definition 20.1.41 is upper semicontinuous in the following sense. Suppose that $(\mathbb {D}_ i^ j)_{j\in J}$ are nets of nef b-divisors over $X$ with limits $\mathbb {D}_ i$ for each $i=1,\ldots ,n$. Then 7E0BA3EB7A39 20.1.48 \begin{equation}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right)\leq \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right). \end{equation} Proof. Step 1 . We first assume that the $\mathbb D_ i^ j$'s and the $\mathbb D_ i$'s are all big. Choose $\mathcal I$-good non-divisorial currents $T_ i^ j$ and $T_ i$ such that $\mathbb D(T_ i^ j)=\mathbb D_ i^ j$ and $\mathbb D(T_ i)=\mathbb D_ i$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and fix $\epsilon >0$. Since $\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j\to \mathbb D_{i,X}$, for all sufficiently large $j$ the class \[  \mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} -\mathbb D_{i,X}^ j  \] is Kähler. Choose a Kähler form $\chi _ i^ j$ in this class and set $S_ i^ j=T_ i^ j+\chi _ i^ j$. Then $S_ i^ j$ lies in the fixed class $\mathbb D_{i,X}+\epsilon \{ \omega \} $ and has the same divisorial Lelong numbers as $T_ i^ j$. Hence, by theorem 18.1.42 and proposition 18.1.27 2 , \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (T_1^ j,\ldots ,T_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \varlimsup _{j\in J}\operatorname{vol}\Bigl (S_1^ j,\ldots ,S_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \operatorname{vol}\left(T_1+\epsilon \omega ,\ldots ,T_ n+\epsilon \omega \right).  \] Therefore, \[  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\Bigl (\mathbb D_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n^ j\Bigr )\leq \Bigl (\mathbb D_1+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb D_ n+\epsilon \mathbb D(\omega )\Bigr ).  \] Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ gives ( 20.1.48 ). Step 2 . Next we handle the general case. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then by 20.1.44 , for any $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j \right) \leq &  \varlimsup _{j\in J}\left(\mathbb {D}_1^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n^ j+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ),\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n+\epsilon \mathbb {D}(\omega ) \right)\\  \leq &  \left( \mathbb {D}_1,\ldots ,\mathbb {D}_ n \right)+C\epsilon . \end{aligned}  \] Since $\epsilon $ is arbitrary, our assertion follows. $\square$

title: 21.13 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
search_title: Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
section: 21.13 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: This chapter extends the toric pluripotential theory of section 21.12 from ample toric line bundles to big toric line bundles. Let $L=\mathcal O_ X(D)$ be a big toric line bundle on a smooth projective toric variety $X$, and let $P_ D\subseteq M_{\mathbb R}$ be the polytope associated with the toric divisor $D$. In the ample case, $P_ D$ is a smooth lattice polytope and its faces correspond directly to toric strata. This direct correspondence breaks down. This is the main new feature of the chapter. The first goal is to recover a usable toric-convex dictionary in this more flexible setting. We begin by recalling the big toric setup, the Cartier data of $D$, and the stable base locus. We then compare the Newton body of a toric psh metric with its partial Okounkov body. The main computation, theorem 21.13.39 , identifies the partial Okounkov body of a toric singularity with its Newton body, up to the natural affine transformation determined by the chosen toric flag. This result is the bridge between the general Okounkov-body theory of section 19.1 and the explicit convex geometry of toric metrics. Once this comparison is established, several pluripotential-theoretic consequences follow. The Newton body computes non-pluripolar mass, describes Lelong numbers along toric divisors, and gives an explicit description of the potential with minimal singularities. In this way the abstract constructions of previous chapters become concrete convex-geometric statements in the toric setting. The second half of the chapter develops the full toric pluripotential theory in a big class. Toric $\theta $-psh potentials are identified with proper convex functions on $N_{\mathbb R}$ satisfying the appropriate growth condition determined by $P_ D$. Under this correspondence, sums, rooftop envelopes, suprema, decreasing limits and $P$-equivalence all have convex interpretations. We also describe toric subgeodesics, geodesics and the toric Ross–Witt Nyström correspondence. The final sections study restriction and intersection theory in the toric setting. The trace operator along toric strata is computed by slicing Newton bodies, and its volume formula becomes a statement about the Euclidean volume of faces and slices. We also prove a mixed-volume formula for Newton bodies and recover the augmented base locus from the convex data. Throughout the chapter we use the notation and conventions of section 21.12 . The partial Okounkov body machinery of section 19.1 is used repeatedly.

text: Proposition 21.13.8 . 111BC1BBBDE6 The base locus $\operatorname{Bs}(D)$ (with the reduced complex structure) of $D$ is a toric-invariant (possibly reducible) subvariety given by the union of $V(\tau )$, where $\tau $ runs over elements in $\Sigma $ satisfying the following condition: 0AA0B0B933FC 21.13.9 \begin{equation}  a_{\rho }+\langle m, u_{\rho }\rangle >0\quad \textup{for some }\rho \in \tau (1) \end{equation} for each $m\in M\cap P_ D$. title: 21.13.21 Toric partial Okounkov bodies
section: 21.13 Toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles
text: We continue to use the notations in subsection 21.13.1 . In order to study the toric-invariant singular plurisubharmonic metrics on $L$, we need to fix a reference toric-invariant smooth Hermitian metric, so that the psh metrics can be identified with quasi-psh functions. Unlike the ample case studied in section 21.12 , in the case of big line bundles, there does not seem to be a natural choice of a smooth Hermitian metric on $L$ similar to Guillemin's metric. We shall fix a $T_ c$-invariant Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ so that $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. The first observation is the following: Lemma 21.13.22 . A11981674229 There is a smooth function $F_{\theta }\colon N_{\mathbb {R}}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ such that \[  \theta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\operatorname{Trop}^*F_{\theta }\quad \textup{on }T(\mathbb {C}).  \] Proof. Step 1 . We first prove the existence of $F_{\theta }$ for a specific choice of $h$. Write $D$ as the difference of two toric-invariant ample divisors, say $D_1-D_2$. Let $h_1$ and $h_2$ be the associated Guillemin's metrics on $D_1$ and $D_2$ respectively. We define $h=h_1\otimes h_2^{-1}$. In this case, our assertion follows since it holds in the case of Guillemin's metrics. Step 2 . In general, fix $h_0$ as in Step 1. Then the general $h$ can be written as $h_0\exp (-g)$ for some smooth function $g$ on $X$. Since both metrics are $T_ c$-invariant, so is $g$, and on the open torus we may write $g=\operatorname{Trop}^* r$ for some smooth function $r$ on $N_{\mathbb {R}}$. Hence it suffices to modify $F_{\theta }$ in Step 1 by $r$ to conclude. $\square$ Note that $F_{\theta }$ is well-defined up to a linear term. Next, we make an additional requirement on $F_{\theta }$ to fix the linear term. Let $s_ D$ be a rational section of $L$ corresponding to $D$. Then $s_ D$ is well-defined up to a non-zero multiple. By Lelong–Poincaré formula proposition 5.20.4 , we have \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\left( \operatorname{Trop}^*F_{\theta }+\log |s_ D|_ h^2 \right)=0  \] on $T(\mathbb {C})$. Therefore, $\operatorname{Trop}^*F_{\theta }+\log |s_ D|_ h^2$ is the tropicalization of a linear function. Hence, after adding a linear function to $F_{\theta }$, we can guarantee that CDCD55296D94 21.13.23 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{Trop}^*F_{\theta }+\log |s_ D|_ h^2=0 \end{equation} from now on. Note that a different choice of $s_ D$ means adding a constant to $F_{\theta }$. Summarizing the situation, we have chosen the following data in addition to the fan $\Sigma $ so far: A divisor $D$, a Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ and a rational section $s_ D$ of $L$ subject to various conditions.
