title: Proposition 22.1.5
text: Proposition 22.1.5 . B80F3474DB2F Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then given $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ with $\omega \geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } \right]_{\mathcal{I}} = \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }.  \] Proof. Since for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potential $\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau }$ is $\mathcal{I}$-good by example 18.1.11 , it follows that \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]=P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}_{\tau } \right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Our assertion follows from proposition 16.4.9 and proposition 16.6.30 . $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.6
text: Proposition 22.1.6 . 2CB4FA8703B1 There is a natural injective map \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ),\quad \Gamma \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\right)_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}.  \] Proof. The map is well-defined by the compatibility of the transition maps. It suffices to argue its injectivity. Suppose that $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}  \] for some Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Then $\Gamma _{\max }=\Gamma '_{\max }$ and for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{\tau }\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\Gamma '_{\tau }  \] by proposition 16.8.17 . It follows again from proposition 16.8.17 that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\Gamma '_{\tau }.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Definition 22.1.7
text: Definition 22.1.7 . A92D6DFAC0CF Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define its volume as follows: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \coloneqq \lim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)} \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n\in [0,\infty ).  \]

title: Proposition 22.1.8
text: Proposition 22.1.8 . 47A4DA9EBA71 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X \left(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{-\infty }\right)^ n.  \] Proof. This follows from proposition 16.4.4 , corollary 16.4.8 and proposition 17.12.19 . $\square$

title: Lemma 22.1.9
text: Lemma 22.1.9 . 587EEDE88F4F Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, let $\omega $ be a Kähler form on $X$, and let $0<t\leq 1$. Then for every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  \leq {}& \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Proof. For $\sigma \in \{ -\infty ,\tau \} $, put \[  S_ t^\sigma =\theta +t\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 22.1.5 , example 18.1.11 , proposition 16.3.10 , projecting $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\sigma }$ to the class $\theta +\omega $ does not change the total mass computed in the larger class. Thus \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\sigma }\right)^ n = \int _ X \left(S_ t^\sigma +(1-t)\omega \right)^ n.  \] Expanding the right-hand side and subtracting the two identities for $\sigma =-\infty $ and $\sigma =\tau $, we get \[  \begin{aligned} & \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\\  ={}& \sum _{a=0}^ n \binom {n}{a}(1-t)^{n-a} \left(\int _ X (S_ t^{-\infty })^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}-\int _ X (S_ t^\tau )^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}\right). \end{aligned}  \] Since $\Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{-\infty }\geq \Gamma ^{\theta +t\omega }_{\tau }$, each summand is non-negative by the monotonicity theorem for mixed non-pluripolar products. Keeping only the term $a=n$ gives the desired inequality. $\square$

title: Lemma 22.1.10
text: Lemma 22.1.10 . 9A2678C2C223 The image of the canonical injection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] is given by the set of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. Proof. By proposition 22.1.8 , every element in the image has positive volume. Conversely, take $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with positive volume. We want to construct $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ representing $\Gamma $. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Define 717C364BF812 22.1.11 \begin{equation}  \Gamma '_{\tau }\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty }\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }. \end{equation} We claim that it suffices to show 80067294986D 22.1.12 \begin{equation}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n>0 \end{equation} for some $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. If this holds, then the argument of 17.12.6 implies that the same holds for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. Then proposition 16.4.4 , proposition 16.6.29 guarantee that $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ and represents $\Gamma $. It remains to argue ( 22.1.12 ). Let $\epsilon =\operatorname{vol}\Gamma >0$. Take $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$ so that \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] Therefore, by 22.1.9 , for any $k\geq 1$, \[  \int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{-\infty }\right)^ n-\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n<\epsilon /2.  \] By the definition of $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma $, the first integral in the preceding line tends to $\epsilon $ as $k\to \infty $. Hence \[  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n\geq \epsilon /2>0,  \] which proves ( 22.1.12 ). $\square$

title: Equation 22.1.11
text: 717C364BF812 22.1.11 \begin{equation}  \Gamma '_{\tau }\coloneqq \lim _{k\to \infty }\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau },\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }. \end{equation}

title: Equation 22.1.12
text: 80067294986D 22.1.12 \begin{equation}  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \left(\theta +k^{-1}\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{\theta +k^{-1}\omega }_{\tau }\right)^ n>0 \end{equation}

title: Example 22.1.13
text: Example 22.1.13 . 796F447D96B6 Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We can define an associated non-Archimedean metric \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )  \] as follows: FB0E6FB2D0F7 $\Gamma ^{\varphi }_{\max }=0$; 7A4B948C1C94 for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$ and any $\tau <0$, we set \[  \Gamma ^{\varphi ,\theta +\omega }_{\tau }=P_{\theta +\omega }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Such non-Archimedean metrics are called homogeneous non-Archimedean metrics. Observe that \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\varphi }=\operatorname{vol}\theta _{\varphi }.  \] See proposition 18.1.27 and the footnote there.

title: Definition 22.1.14
text: Definition 22.1.14 . CCAAC9DA4E2F Let $\omega $ be a closed real smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. We define the map \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}\colon \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\rightarrow \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )  \] as follows: Given $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ as the element such that for any $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega +\omega '}.  \]

title: Proposition 22.1.15
text: Proposition 22.1.15 . 3943AA7119C5 The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 22.1.14 together induce a bijection 29D3530031C6 22.1.16 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ). \end{equation} Proof. It is a tautology that the maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 22.1.14 are compatible with the transition maps. So the map ( 22.1.16 ) is well-defined. It is injective by the same argument as proposition 22.1.6 . We argue the surjectivity. By unfolding the definitions, an object in the target of ( 22.1.16 ) is an assignment: With each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we associate a family $(\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '})_{\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ satisfying: 5067A37E976E $\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega +\omega ')_{>0}$ for each $\omega ,\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$; CDB9ED278B54 for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega ''\geq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega '}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''};  \] 3EBB3E3A9CF6 for each $\omega ,\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ satisfying $\omega \leq \omega '$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega '+\omega ''}\left[\Gamma ^{\omega ,\omega ''}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\omega ',\omega ''}.  \] The preimage of such an object is given by the family $(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega })_{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ given by \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\omega /2,\omega /2}.  \] The fact that the image of $\Gamma $ is as expected follows directly from the definitions. $\square$

title: Equation 22.1.16
text: 29D3530031C6 22.1.16 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ). \end{equation}

title: Proposition 22.1.17
text: Proposition 22.1.17 . 817C1BB3E570 The maps $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ in definition 22.1.14 and the injective maps proposition 22.1.6 together induce bijections 258B0F2A2F95 22.1.18 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ), \end{equation} where $\omega $ runs over either the partially ordered set of all smooth closed real positive $(1,1)$-forms with positive volume 2 on $X$ or $\textup{Käh}(X)$. 2. ↩ This partially ordered set is not directed.

title: Equation 22.1.18
text: 258B0F2A2F95 22.1.18 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}\xrightarrow {\sim } \varprojlim _{\omega }\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ), \end{equation}

title: Corollary 22.1.19
text: Corollary 22.1.19 . 347399E47277 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then $\pi ^*$ induces a bijection \[  \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )\xrightarrow {\sim } \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(Y,\pi ^*\theta ).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from proposition 22.1.17 . $\square$

title: 22.1.20 Operations on non-Archimedean metrics
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta ,\theta ',\theta ''$ be closed real smooth $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ representing big cohomology classes. This section relies heavily on section 17.15 . We shall use the notions introduced in that section without further explanations. Definition 22.1.21 . DA2917901B54 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. We say $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ if for some $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega } \leq \Gamma '{}^{\theta '+\omega }.  \] This notion is independent of the choice of $\omega $ thanks to 17.15.3 . 


Moreover, we have the following: Proposition 22.1.22 . 8C5A487B9CCC Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: A1B3616B9907 $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$; 3EAAE9BE6F17 $P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\leq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}$. Proof. This follows immediately from 17.15.3 . $\square$ Observe that this definition coincides with the corresponding definition in definition 17.15.1 when $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Proposition 22.1.23 . F7D709A21AE1 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma \leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '.  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for any Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }\leq \operatorname{vol}\Gamma '{}^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is an immediate consequence of theorem 13.13.11 . $\square$ Definition 22.1.24 . 93939D1E527C Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Then we define $\Gamma +\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +\Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\theta '+2\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+\Gamma '^{\theta '+\omega }.  \] This definition yields an element in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\theta ')$ by 17.15.9 and it extends the definition in definition 17.15.4 by 17.15.9 as well. Proposition 22.1.25 . 06DFF1DE1519 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. Suppose that $\omega ,\omega '$ are two smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-forms on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega +\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma +\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+P_{\theta '+\omega '}[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 17.15.9 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.26 . E9E94041F68D The operation $+$ is commutative and associative: For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta '')$, we have \[  \Gamma +\Gamma '=\Gamma '+\Gamma ,\quad (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 17.15.7 . $\square$ Definition 22.1.27 . D1E32864F8F0 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. We define $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma +C \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }+C.  \] It is obvious from definition 17.15.10 that $\Gamma +C\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. It is also obvious that this definition extends definition 17.15.10 . Proposition 22.1.28 . ECFDC5EDD4F2 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Suppose that $\omega $ is a smooth closed positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma +C]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Proposition 22.1.29 . 87CB041BFCA3 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $C,C'\in \mathbb {R}$. Then 80F4957A059F $(\Gamma +\Gamma ')+C=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+C)=(\Gamma +C)+\Gamma '$; 036FE960D3D0 $\Gamma +(C+C')=(\Gamma +C)+C'$. Proof. This is a direct consequence of proposition 17.15.11 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.30 . 11099644479B Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C).  \] Proof. It suffices to show that for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }=\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C)^{\theta +\omega }_{-\infty },  \] which is obvious. $\square$ Definition 22.1.31 . B819F1A85E09 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we define $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \Gamma \lor \Gamma ' \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }\lor \Gamma '^{\theta +\omega }.  \] It follows from 17.15.19 that $\Gamma \lor \Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and this definition extends the corresponding definition in definition 17.15.12 . Proposition 22.1.32 . 9CACCE9D7690 Let $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\omega $ be a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma \lor \Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}\lor P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ']_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 17.15.19 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.33 . 04004F65B932 The operation $\lor $ is commutative and associative. In particular, given a finite non-empty family $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, we then define $\bigvee _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i$ in the obvious way. Proof. This is a direct consequence of corollary 17.15.17 . $\square$ Definition 22.1.34 . C172DAF1B3E6 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that AB5F1151338C 22.1.35 \begin{equation}  \sup _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }<\infty . \end{equation} Then we define $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] It follows immediately from 17.15.30 that $\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and this definition extends definition 17.15.25 . Moreover, this definition clearly extends definition 22.1.31 as well. Proposition 22.1.36 . 74CC0BF97B41 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This is a direct consequence of 17.15.30 . $\square$ We also have a non-Archimedean version of Choquet's lemma. Proposition 22.1.37 . 21737B0303A5 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then there exists a countable subfamily $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$. For each $m\geq 1$, proposition 17.15.31 gives a countable subfamily $I_ m\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I_ m}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Set $I'=\bigcup _{m\geq 1}I_ m$. This is countable. We claim that it works. Let $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$. Choose $m$ so large that $\omega '\geq m^{-1}\omega _0$. By proposition 22.1.36 and the compatibility of the transition maps, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}} =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{aligned}  \] Thus the two non-Archimedean metrics have the same component in every class $\theta +\omega '$, and the assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 22.1.38 . 938848E420F9 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 17.15.32 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.39 . 15E20104530B Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then AA5696D80091 22.1.40 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} Proof. The $\geq $ direction in ( 22.1.40 ) is a direct consequence of proposition 22.1.23 . It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Note that ( 22.1.40 ) holds when $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i>0$ for each $i\in I$, as a consequence of proposition 17.15.22 , corollary 16.9.12 and theorem 16.9.57 . In particular, for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega } \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] For our purpose, we need to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $\omega $ so that \[  \sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon .  \] We shall show that it is possible to choose $\omega $ so that the stronger statement holds: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon ,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Equivalently, we need to choose $\omega $ so that for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $X$ dominated by $\omega $, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }+\epsilon /2,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\Omega $ such that $\Omega \geq \theta +\omega _0$. It is enough to take $\omega =\delta \omega _0$ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. If $\omega '$ is dominated by $\omega $, then $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $. Set \[  T_ i\coloneqq \theta +\omega '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 17.12.19 , the potential $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }$ has the same $P$-singularity type in the class $\theta +\omega $ as $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }$. Hence its mass can be computed as \[  \int _ X\left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } =& \int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n-\int _ X T_ i^ n\\  =&  \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X T_ i^ a\wedge \left( \omega -\omega '\right)^{n-a}\\  \leq & \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X \Omega ^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}. \end{aligned}  \] In the last inequality we used the facts that $0\leq \omega -\omega '\leq \omega $ and $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . We can choose $\omega $ so that the right-hand side is less than $\epsilon /2$. Our assertion then follows. $\square$ Definition 22.1.41 . 65E2E07550F1 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that 827FE14EA1A0 22.1.42 \begin{equation}  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i_{\max }>-\infty , \end{equation} then we define $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ as the unique element such that for each $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have 341067287939 22.1.43 \begin{equation}  \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }. \end{equation} We observe that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)^{\theta +\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega )_{>0}.  \] This follows from proposition 17.15.40 . Moreover, by 17.15.41 , we have $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, and this definition extends definition 17.15.37 . In general, \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)\leq \lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i  \] as a consequence of proposition 22.1.23 . But the reverse inequality fails in general. Proposition 22.1.44 . 07B251D899EF Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows from 17.15.41 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.45 . C8734FD15163 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\leq \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 22.1.46 . EB1311598A32 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \lambda \Gamma \right)^{\lambda \theta +\omega }=\lambda \Gamma ^{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }.  \] It follows immediately from 17.15.36 that $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ and this definition extends definition 17.15.33 . Proposition 22.1.47 . 68FB6124EEB2 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\lambda P_{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from 17.15.36 . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.48 . EDFB2682E78E Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] If $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ), then \[  \lambda \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\inf _{i\in I}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. Everything except the last assertion follows from proposition 17.15.35 . The last assertion follows directly from the definition. $\square$ Proposition 22.1.49 . 1743F9AEA475 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \lambda \Gamma \right)=\lambda ^ n \operatorname{vol}\Gamma .  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$ Definition 22.1.50 . C0E37055D126 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We say that the trace operator of $\Gamma $ along $Y$ is well-defined if \[  \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0  \] for all sufficiently negative $\tau $ and every $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. We define \[  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0\right\} .  \] Here $\omega $ is any Kähler form on $X$; this number is independent of the choice of $\omega $ by the compatibility of the transition maps. In this case, we define $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ 3 as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(\widetilde{Y})$, the component 6697E3349082 22.1.51 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega )_{>0} \end{equation} is defined as follows: 5517A8C43D97 We let 284D786E2B4E 22.1.52 \begin{equation}  \left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega } \right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }; \end{equation} E0B260D169B4 for each $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than $\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }$, we define \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\left[ \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right) \right]_{\mathcal{I}},  \] where $\tilde{\omega }$ is an arbitrary Kähler form on $X$ such that $\omega \geq \tilde{\omega }|_{\widetilde{Y}}$. 3. ↩ Here $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y$ is the normalization of $Y$. It follows from [ Proposition 3.6 , GK20 ] that $\widetilde{Y}$ is a normal Kähler space and hence $\tilde{\omega }$ exists. We observe that the choice of the trace operator $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right)$ is irrelevant since two different choices are $\mathcal{I}$-equivalent. Moreover, ( 22.1.51 ) holds as a consequence of proposition 20.2.8 and proposition 20.2.21 . It is therefore clear that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$. Here when $\widetilde{Y}$ is not smooth, we understand $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ as the set of non-Archimedean metrics on a resolution of $\widetilde{Y}$, which is independent of the choice of the resolution by proposition 20.2.21 . See section 9.10 for more details. Proposition 22.1.53 . E7009D90BCC6 Let $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ be a proper bimeromorphic morphism from a compact Kähler manifold $Y$. Then all definitions in this section are invariant under pullback to $Y$. The meaning is clear in most cases. In the case of the trace operator, this means the following: Suppose that $Z\subseteq X$ is an analytic subset and $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ has non-trivial restriction to $Z$. Suppose that $Z$ is not contained in the non-isomorphism locus of $\pi $ so that the strict transform $W$ of $Z$ is defined. If we write $\Pi \colon W\rightarrow Z$ for the restriction of $\pi $ and $\widetilde{\Pi }\colon \widetilde{W}\rightarrow \widetilde{Z}$ the strict transform of $\Pi $, then we have \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )=\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma ).  \] The relevant notations are summarized in the following diagram: Proof. We only prove the assertion for the trace operator, as the other proofs are similar. We shall use the notations above. Observe that for any closed positive smooth $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$ with positive mass, we have \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },Z\right)=0 \right\} ,  \] and \[  \begin{aligned}  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=& \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left((\pi ^*\Gamma )^{\pi ^*\theta +\pi ^*\omega }_{\tau },W\right)=0 \right\} \\  =& \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\pi ^*\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },W\right)=0 \right\} \\  =&  \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau },Z\right)=0 \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] Here we implicitly used proposition 22.1.17 . Therefore, \[  \left(\widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)_{\max }.  \] Let $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ be less than this common value. Take a Kähler form $\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}$ (resp. $\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$) on $\widetilde{Z}$ (resp. $\widetilde{W}$). Take a Kähler form $\omega _ Y$ on $Y$ (resp. $\omega _ X$ on $X$) such that \[  \omega _{\widetilde{Z}}\geq \omega _ X|_{\widetilde{Z}},\quad \omega _{\widetilde{W}} \geq \omega _ Y|_{\widetilde{W}},\quad \omega _ Y \geq \pi ^*\omega _ X.  \] We want to show that, after projection to the common background $(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}$, \[  P_{(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}\left[\widetilde{\Pi }^*\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Z(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Z}}+\omega _{\widetilde{Z}}}_\tau \right)\right]_{\mathcal I} \sim _ P \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ W(\pi ^*\Gamma )\right)^{(\pi ^*\theta )|_{\widetilde{W}}+\omega _{\widetilde{W}}}_\tau .  \] Unfolding the definitions, we reduce to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z^{\theta +\omega _ X}\left( \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega _ X}_{\tau } \right)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}^{\pi ^*\theta +\omega _ Y}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma \right)^{\pi ^*\theta +\omega _ Y}_{\tau }\right).  \] Using proposition 20.2.21 , this is equivalent to \[  \widetilde{\Pi }^* \operatorname{Tr}_ Z\left( \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega _ X}_{\tau } \right)\sim _ P \operatorname{Tr}_{W}\left( \left( \pi ^*\Gamma \right)^{\pi ^*\theta +\pi ^*\omega _ X}_{\tau }\right).  \] This is a consequence of 20.2.24 . $\square$

title: Definition 22.1.24

title: Proposition 22.1.25
text: Proposition 22.1.25 . 06DFF1DE1519 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$. title: Proposition 22.1.26

E9E94041F68D The operation $+$ is commutative and associative: For any $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ and $\Gamma ''\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta '')$, we have \[  \Gamma +\Gamma '=\Gamma '+\Gamma ,\quad (\Gamma +\Gamma ')+\Gamma ''=\Gamma +(\Gamma '+\Gamma '').  \] Proof. title: Proposition 22.1.28

title: Proposition 22.1.30
text: Proposition 22.1.30 . 11099644479B Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma +C).  \] Proof. title: Proposition 22.1.36
text: Proposition 22.1.36 . 74CC0BF97B41 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Assume that $\omega $ is a closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Then \[  P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}= \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} P_{\theta +\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. title: Proposition 22.1.37
text: Proposition 22.1.37 . 21737B0303A5 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then there exists a countable subfamily $I'\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$. For each $m\geq 1$, proposition 17.15.31 gives a countable subfamily $I_ m\subseteq I$ such that \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I_ m}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Set $I'=\bigcup _{m\geq 1}I_ m$. This is countable. We claim that it works. Let $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$. Choose $m$ so large that $\omega '\geq m^{-1}\omega _0$. By proposition 22.1.36 and the compatibility of the transition maps, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}} =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +m^{-1}\omega _0}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}\\  =& \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I'}{}\! {}^{*}P_{\theta +\omega '}[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{aligned}  \] Thus the two non-Archimedean metrics have the same component in every class $\theta +\omega '$, and the assertion follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.38
text: Proposition 22.1.38 . 938848E420F9 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i\leq \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is an immediate consequence of proposition 17.15.32 . $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.39
text: Proposition 22.1.39 . 15E20104530B Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be an increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then AA5696D80091 22.1.40 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^ i \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} Proof. The $\geq $ direction in ( 22.1.40 ) is a direct consequence of proposition 22.1.23 . It remains to prove the reverse inequality. Note that ( 22.1.40 ) holds when $\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i>0$ for each $i\in I$, as a consequence of proposition 17.15.22 , corollary 16.9.12 and theorem 16.9.57 . In particular, for each Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*} \Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega } \right)=\lim _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }.  \] For our purpose, we need to show that for any $\epsilon >0$, we can find $\omega $ so that \[  \sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\sup _{i\in I} \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon .  \] We shall show that it is possible to choose $\omega $ so that the stronger statement holds: \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i}+\epsilon ,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Equivalently, we need to choose $\omega $ so that for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $X$ dominated by $\omega $, we have \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }<\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }+\epsilon /2,\quad \forall i\in I.  \] Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\Omega $ such that $\Omega \geq \theta +\omega _0$. It is enough to take $\omega =\delta \omega _0$ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. If $\omega '$ is dominated by $\omega $, then $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $. Set \[  T_ i\coloneqq \theta +\omega '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }.  \] By the transition compatibility and proposition 17.12.19 , the potential $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }$ has the same $P$-singularity type in the class $\theta +\omega $ as $\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }$. Hence its mass can be computed as \[  \int _ X\left(\theta +\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty }\right)^ n=\int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n.  \] Therefore, \[  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega }_{-\infty }-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^{i,\theta +\omega '}_{-\infty } =& \int _ X \left(T_ i+\omega -\omega '\right)^ n-\int _ X T_ i^ n\\  =&  \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X T_ i^ a\wedge \left( \omega -\omega '\right)^{n-a}\\  \leq & \sum _{a=0}^{n-1} \binom {n}{a} \int _ X \Omega ^ a\wedge \omega ^{n-a}. \end{aligned}  \] In the last inequality we used the facts that $0\leq \omega -\omega '\leq \omega $ and $\theta +\omega '\leq \Omega $, and the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . We can choose $\omega $ so that the right-hand side is less than $\epsilon /2$. Our assertion then follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.45
text: Proposition 22.1.45 . C8734FD15163 Let $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ). Let $C\in \mathbb {R}$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I} (\Gamma ^ i+C)=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma ^ i+C.  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma '^ i)_{i\in I}$ is another decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ). Suppose that $\Gamma ^ i\leq \Gamma '^ i$ for all $i\in I$. Then \[  \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i\leq \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma '^ i.  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$

title: Definition 22.1.46
text: Definition 22.1.46 . EB1311598A32 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then we define $\lambda \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\lambda \theta )$ as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we have \[  \left( \lambda \Gamma \right)^{\lambda \theta +\omega }=\lambda \Gamma ^{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }.  \]

title: Proposition 22.1.47
text: Proposition 22.1.47 . 68FB6124EEB2 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then for any closed smooth positive $(1,1)$-form $\omega $ on $X$, we have \[  P_{\lambda \theta +\omega }[\lambda \Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}=\lambda P_{\theta +\lambda ^{-1}\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Proof. This follows immediately from 17.15.36 . $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.48
text: Proposition 22.1.48 . EDFB2682E78E Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, $\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta ')$, $C\in \mathbb {R}$ and $\lambda ,\lambda '>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  \lambda (\Gamma +\Gamma ')=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda \Gamma ',\\  (\lambda \lambda ')\Gamma =& \lambda (\lambda '\Gamma ),\\  \lambda (\Gamma +C)=& \lambda \Gamma +\lambda C. \end{aligned}  \] Suppose that $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a non-empty family in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.35 ). Then \[  \lambda \left( \operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\operatorname *{sup}_{i\in I}{}\! {}^{*}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] If $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\in I}$ is a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfying ( 22.1.42 ), then \[  \lambda \left( \inf _{i\in I}\Gamma ^ i \right)=\inf _{i\in I}(\lambda \Gamma ^ i).  \] Proof. Everything except the last assertion follows from proposition 17.15.35 . The last assertion follows directly from the definition. $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.49
text: Proposition 22.1.49 . 1743F9AEA475 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb {R}_{>0}$. Then \[  \operatorname{vol}\left( \lambda \Gamma \right)=\lambda ^ n \operatorname{vol}\Gamma .  \] Proof. This is clear by definition. $\square$

title: Definition 22.1.50
text: Definition 22.1.50 . C0E37055D126 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. We say that the trace operator of $\Gamma $ along $Y$ is well-defined if \[  \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0  \] for all sufficiently negative $\tau $ and every $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. We define \[  \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }\coloneqq \sup \left\{  \tau <\Gamma _{\max }: \nu \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega },Y\right)=0\right\} .  \] Here $\omega $ is any Kähler form on $X$; this number is independent of the choice of $\omega $ by the compatibility of the transition maps. In this case, we define $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}})$ 3 as the unique element such that for any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(\widetilde{Y})$, the component 6697E3349082 22.1.51 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\widetilde{Y},\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega )_{>0} \end{equation} is defined as follows: 5517A8C43D97 We let 284D786E2B4E 22.1.52 \begin{equation}  \left( \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega } \right)_{\max }=\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }; \end{equation} E0B260D169B4 for each $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$ less than $\left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )\right)_{\max }$, we define \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta |_{\widetilde{Y}}+\omega }\left[ \operatorname{Tr}_ Y^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}\left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\tilde{\omega }}_{\tau }\right) \right]_{\mathcal{I}},  \] where $\tilde{\omega }$ is an arbitrary Kähler form on $X$ such that $\omega \geq \tilde{\omega }|_{\widetilde{Y}}$. 3. ↩ Here $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y$ is the normalization of $Y$.

title: 22.1.54 Duistermaat–Heckman measures
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a big cohomology class. Definition 22.1.55 . 9ADEFD2FF381 Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma $ is defined as \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq n!\cdot \operatorname{DH}\left(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\right).  \] Recall that $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )\in \mathrm{TC}(\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{-\infty }))$ is the Okounkov test curve defined in theorem 19.6.24 . See definition 19.6.18 for the definition of the Duistermaat–Heckman measure of an Okounkov test curve. Theorem 22.1.56 . 0AD7F80A793D Assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. The Duistermaat–Heckman measure $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ of $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ in definition 22.1.55 is independent of the choice of the smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Furthermore, for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, the following moment identity holds: A51020D58E6F 22.1.57 \begin{equation}  \int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)=\Gamma _{\max }^ m\operatorname{vol}\Gamma +m\int _{-\infty }^{\Gamma _{\max }}\tau ^{m-1}\Bigl ( \operatorname{vol}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Gamma _{\tau })-\operatorname{vol}\Gamma \Bigr )\, \mathrm{d}\tau , \end{equation} and 51031202809C 22.1.58 \begin{equation}  \int _{\mathbb {R}}\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=\operatorname{vol}\Gamma . \end{equation} For each $m\in \mathbb {N}$, $\int _{\mathbb {R}}x^ m\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )(x)$ is indeed $n!$ times the $m$-th moment of the random variable $G[\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma )]$, by definition 22.1.55 , definition 19.6.18 . Proof. We observe that ( 22.1.57 ) holds by the computations in proposition 19.6.19 and theorem 19.5.26 1 . It is independent of the choice of the flag. Furthermore, ( 22.1.58 ) follows immediately from theorem 19.5.26 1 . Assume first that $\Gamma $ is bounded. Since the Duistermaat–Heckman measure has bounded support in this case (cf. theorem 19.6.13 ), we conclude that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is uniquely determined. By translating the parameter, it suffices to treat the case $\Gamma _{\max }=0$. Indeed, if $a=\Gamma _{\max }$ and \[  \widetilde\Gamma _\tau \coloneqq \Gamma _{\tau +a},  \] then $\widetilde\Gamma _{\max }=0$, and the associated test function is translated by $a$. Consequently, \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=(x\mapsto x+a)_*\operatorname{DH}(\widetilde\Gamma ).  \] Thus independence of the flag and the moment identity for $\widetilde\Gamma $ imply the corresponding assertions for $\Gamma $. For each $\epsilon >0$, we define $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ as follows: 36B347B9186A Let $\Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\max }=0$, and 12A1009F3470 we set \[  \Gamma ^{\epsilon }_{\tau }= \begin{cases}  \Gamma _{-\infty },& \text{ if }\tau \leq -\epsilon ^{-1},\\  P_{\theta }\left[ (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _{\tau }-\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty } \right],& \text{ if }\tau \in \left(-\epsilon ^{-1},0\right). \end{cases}  \] Let us check that $\Gamma ^\epsilon $ is indeed an element of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. The concavity and monotonicity in $\tau $ follow from proposition 16.4.2 . Since the $\Gamma _\tau $'s are $\mathcal I$-model, they are $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.11 ; hence \[  (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _\tau -\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty }  \] is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 18.1.17 . Therefore its $P$-envelope is also its $\mathcal I$-envelope, and the corresponding level is $\mathcal I$-model. The value at $-\infty $ is $\Gamma _{-\infty }$. Thus $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each fixed $\tau <0$, the argument of theorem 17.13.21 Step 3.3 gives \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau \searrow \Gamma _\tau \quad \textup{as }\epsilon \to 0+.  \] By proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 , this convergence is in $d_ S$. Hence theorem 19.5.26 4 gives \[  \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau )\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )  \] for every $\tau <0$. Since \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _{-\infty }=\Gamma _{-\infty }  \] for all $\epsilon $, the underlying convex body is fixed. Therefore 19.6.22 applies and gives \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^\epsilon )\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ).  \] It follows that $\operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )$ is independent of the choice of the flag. $\square$ More generally, when $X$ does not admit a smooth flag, we may choose a modification $\pi \colon Y\rightarrow X$ so that $Y$ admits a flag. We define 665B92171EA8 22.1.59 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )\coloneqq \operatorname{DH}(\pi ^*\Gamma ). \end{equation} It follows from theorem 19.5.26 5 that this measure is independent of the choice of $\pi $. Proposition 22.1.60 . 492A145E9067 Let \[  (\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}\subseteq \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0},\quad \Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] Assume one of the following conditions holds: 577BE71DB8C5 The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is decreasing and $\Gamma =\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i$. Assume that E10A583B2E40 22.1.61 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i. \end{equation} 75E1B24CB49A The sequence $(\Gamma ^ i)_{i\geq 1}$ is increasing and $\Gamma =\operatorname *{sup}_{i\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*}\Gamma ^ i$. Then 636AFE1086C1 22.1.62 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ^ i)\rightharpoonup \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma ). \end{equation} Proof. We may assume that $X$ admits a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$. Assume 1 . Let \[  \eta \coloneqq \inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] Since $\Gamma _\tau \leq \Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }$ for every $i$ and every $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta .  \] By proposition 16.4.4 , the decreasing limit $\eta $ is model and \[  \int _ X\theta _\eta ^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }}^ n=\lim _{i\to \infty }\operatorname{vol}\Gamma ^ i.  \] Using ( 22.1.61 ), this equals \[  \operatorname{vol}\Gamma =\int _ X\theta _{\Gamma _{-\infty }}^ n.  \] Since $\Gamma _{-\infty }\leq \eta $ and both potentials are model, proposition 16.8.7 gives \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\eta .  \] Thus \[  \Gamma _{-\infty }=\inf _{i\geq 1}\Gamma ^ i_{-\infty }.  \] We want to derive ( 22.1.62 ) from 19.6.22 . It boils down to prove the following: For any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}} \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] For fixed $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, the potentials $\Gamma ^ i_\tau $ decrease to $\Gamma _\tau $. By proposition 16.4.4 , their masses converge to the mass of $\Gamma _\tau $; hence $\Gamma ^ i_\tau \xrightarrow {d_ S}\Gamma _\tau $ by corollary 16.9.14 . Applying the continuity of the partial Okounkov body map, theorem 19.5.26 4 , gives \[  \Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma ^ i_{\tau })\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta ,\Gamma _{\tau }).  \] The proof under the assumption 2 is similar. We only need to apply 19.6.23 instead of 19.6.22 . $\square$ Remark 22.1.63 . CF750A31909E When $\{ \theta \} $ is a Hodge class and $\Gamma $ is induced by a test configuration as in example 17.14.10 and 17.14.14 , our Duistermaat–Heckman measure coincides with the more traditional definition of [ Section 3.2 , BHJ17 ] . This is explained in [ Remark 7.17 , Xia21 ] .

We observe that ( 22.1.57 ) holds by the computations in proposition 19.6.19 and theorem 19.5.26 1 . It is independent of the choice of the flag. Consequently, \[  \operatorname{DH}(\Gamma )=(x\mapsto x+a)_*\operatorname{DH}(\widetilde\Gamma ).  \] Thus independence of the flag and the moment identity for $\widetilde\Gamma $ imply the corresponding assertions for $\Gamma $. Since the $\Gamma _\tau $'s are $\mathcal I$-model, they are $\mathcal I$-good by example 18.1.11 ; hence \[  (1+\epsilon \tau )\Gamma _\tau -\epsilon \tau \Gamma _{-\infty }  \] is $\mathcal I$-good by proposition 18.1.17 . Therefore its $P$-envelope is also its $\mathcal I$-envelope, and the corresponding level is $\mathcal I$-model. The value at $-\infty $ is $\Gamma _{-\infty }$. Thus $\Gamma ^\epsilon \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. For each fixed $\tau <0$, the argument of theorem 17.13.21 Step 3.3 gives \[  \Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau \searrow \Gamma _\tau \quad \textup{as }\epsilon \to 0+.  \] By proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 , this convergence is in $d_ S$. Hence theorem 19.5.26 4 gives \[  \Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma ^\epsilon _\tau )\xrightarrow {d_{\mathrm{Haus}}}\Delta _{Y_\bullet }(\theta ,\Gamma _\tau )  \] for every $\tau <0$. title: 22.1.65 A brief recap of Boucksom–Jonsson's theory
search_title: A brief recap of Boucksom–Jonsson's theory
text: Non-Archimedean plurisubharmonic metrics are defined by decreasing limits of Fubini–Study functions on the analytification of a projective variety. The results below relate these metrics to test curves.

title: 22.1.66 Valuations
text: Let $X$ be an irreducible reduced variety over $\mathbb {C}$ of dimension $n$. We recall the Berkovich analytification $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ of $X$ with respect to the trivial valuation on $\mathbb {C}$. Definition 22.1.67 . 433FF564E9A3 A (real-valued) valuation on $X$ (or a valuation of $\mathbb {C}(X)$) is a map $v\colon \mathbb {C}(X)\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ satisfying the following conditions: 8EDEF9CF138B For $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f)=\infty $ if and only if $f=0$; 3ACA653FD4D8 For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(fg)=v(f)+v(g)$; 4C1AC87714F3 For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f+g)\geq v(f)\land v(g)$; C9D9521A044A For $c\in \mathbb {C}^{\times }$, $v(c)=0$. The set of valuations on $X$ is denoted by $X^{\mathrm{val}}$. The center of a valuation $v$ is the scheme-theoretic point $c=c(v)$ of $X$ such that $v\geq 0$ on $\mathcal{O}_{X,c}$ and $v>0$ on the maximal ideal $\mathfrak {m}_{X,c}$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X,c}$. The center is unique if it exists, and it exists if $X$ is proper. In the remainder of this section, we assume that $X$ is projective. As a set, $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ is the set of semi-valuations on $X$, in other words, real-valued valuations $v$ on irreducible reduced subvarieties $Y$ of $X$ that are trivial on $\mathbb {C}$. We call $Y$ the support of the semi-valuation $v$. In other words, \[  X^{\mathrm{An}}=\coprod _{Y} Y^{\mathrm{val}}.  \] We will write $v_{\mathrm{triv}}\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$ for the trivial valuation on $X$: $v_{\mathrm{triv}}(f)=0$ for any $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)^{\times }$. We endow $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ with the coarsest topology such that 3E9AB9B11483 for any Zariski open subset $U\subseteq X$, the subset $U^{\mathrm{An}}$ of $X^{\mathrm{An}}$ consisting of semi-valuations whose supports meet $U$ is open; 16DC97C2CD0A for each Zariski open subset $U\subseteq X$ and each $f\in \mathrm{H}^0(U,\mathcal{O}_ X)$ (here $\mathcal{O}_ X$ is the sheaf of regular functions), the map $|f|\colon U^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ sending $v$ to $\exp (-v(f))$ is continuous. We will be most interested in divisorial valuations. Recall that a divisorial valuation on $X$ is a valuation of the form $t\operatorname{ord}_ E$, where $t\in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}$ and $E$ is a prime divisor over $X$. The set of divisorial valuations on $X$ is denoted by $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. When $\mathbb {Q}_{>0}$ is replaced by $\mathbb {R}_{>0}$, we can similarly define a space $X^{\operatorname{div}}_{\mathbb {R}}$. Given any coherent ideal $\mathfrak {a}$ on $X$ and any $v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$, we define 18B5288E3A41 22.1.68 \begin{equation}  v(\mathfrak {a})\coloneqq \min \{ v(f):f\in \mathfrak {a}_{c(v)}\} \in [0,\infty ], \end{equation} where $c(v)$ is the center of the valuation $v$ on $X$. Given any valuation $v$ on $X$, the Gauss extension of $v$ is a valuation $\sigma (v)$ on $X\times \mathbb {A}^1$: 3B8E87503101 22.1.69 \begin{equation}  \sigma (v)\left(\sum _ i f_ i t^ i\right)\coloneqq \min _ i (v(f_ i)+i). \end{equation} Here $t$ is the standard coordinate on $\mathbb {A}^1=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb {C}[t]$. The key property is that when $v$ is a divisorial valuation, then so is $\sigma (v)$. See [ Lemma 4.2 , BHJ17 ] .

title: Definition 22.1.67
text: Definition 22.1.67 . 433FF564E9A3 A (real-valued) valuation on $X$ (or a valuation of $\mathbb {C}(X)$) is a map $v\colon \mathbb {C}(X)\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ satisfying the following conditions: 8EDEF9CF138B For $f\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f)=\infty $ if and only if $f=0$; 3ACA653FD4D8 For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(fg)=v(f)+v(g)$; 4C1AC87714F3 For $f,g\in \mathbb {C}(X)$, $v(f+g)\geq v(f)\land v(g)$; C9D9521A044A For $c\in \mathbb {C}^{\times }$, $v(c)=0$.

text: 3B8E87503101 22.1.69 \begin{equation}  \sigma (v)\left(\sum _ i f_ i t^ i\right)\coloneqq \min _ i (v(f_ i)+i). \end{equation}

title: 22.1.70 Non-Archimedean plurisubharmonic functions
text:
Let $X$ be an irreducible complex projective variety of dimension $n$ and $L$ be a holomorphic pseudo-effective $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle on $X$. Through the GAGA morphism $X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow X$ of ringed spaces, $L$ can be pulled back to an analytic line bundle $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ on $X$. The purpose of this section is to study the psh metrics on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$. This description avoids the direct treatment of $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ itself. We define $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$, the set of (rational) generically finite Fubini–Study functions $\phi \colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ that are of the following form: 13.37 \begin{equation}  \phi =\frac{1}{m}\max _ j \{ \log |s_ j|+\lambda _ j\} . \end{equation} Here $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$ is an integer such that $L^ m$ is a line bundle, the $s_ j$'s are a finite collection of non-zero sections in $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ m)$, and $\lambda _ j\in \mathbb {Q}$. We follow the convention of Boucksom–Jonsson by writing $\log |s_ j|(v)=-v(s_ j)$. Definition 22.1.71 . EEADED50AAC3 A plurisubharmonic metric (or psh metric for short) on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ is a function $\phi \colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ that is not identically $-\infty $, and is the pointwise limit of a decreasing net $(\phi _ i)_{i\in I}$, where $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L_ i^{\mathrm{An}})$ for some $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundles $L_ i$ on $X$ satisfying $c_1(L_ i)\to c_1(L)$ in $\mathrm{NS}^1(X)_{\mathbb {R}}$. The set of psh metrics on $L^{\mathrm{An}}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. We endow $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ with the topology of pointwise convergence on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. This topology is Hausdorff as functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ are completely determined by their restriction on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$: Theorem 22.1.72 ( [ Theorem 4.22 , BJ22 ] ) . 0DAB63894803 Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $\psi :X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be an usc function. Assume that $\phi \leq \psi $ on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. Then the same holds on $X^{\mathrm{An}}$. Proposition 22.1.73 ( [ Theorem 4.7 , BJ22 ] ) . 8E1FC46DBC87 Let $\phi ,\phi '\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then so is their pointwise maximum $\phi \lor \phi '$. Proposition 22.1.74 . 85809FFB162F Let $H$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Consider $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Assume that for each $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. This is a special case of [ (PSH2) , BJ22 ] on Page 45. 


Next we note that we may use sequences instead of nets in the definition of $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$: Theorem 22.1.75 ( [ Corollary 12.18 , BJ22 ] ) . 6B2CF0C2744A Let $S$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a sequence of rational numbers $\varepsilon _ i\searrow 0$ and a decreasing sequence $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\varepsilon _ i S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that $\phi $ is the pointwise limit of $\phi _ i$, as $i\to \infty $. The space $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ inherits most of the expected properties of (Archimedean) psh functions ( [ Theorem 4.7 , BJ22 ] ). However, the following compactness result is not known: Conjecture 22.1.76 . 95739E70234B Assume that $X$ is unibranch. Then every bounded from above increasing net of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ converges in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. This prediction is equivalent to the so-called envelope conjecture [ Conjecture 5.14 , BJ22 ] : the regularized supremum of a bounded from above family of functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ lies in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. See [ Theorem 5.11 , BJ22 ] for the proof of the equivalence. This conjecture is proved when $X$ is smooth and $L$ is nef in [ BJ22 ] . More recently, in [ BJ22b ] , Boucksom–Jonsson further established the case when $X$ is smooth and $L$ is pseudo-effective.

text: Theorem 22.1.72 ( [ Theorem 4.22 , BJ22 ] ) . 0DAB63894803 Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $\psi :X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be an usc function. Assume that $\phi \leq \psi $ on $X^{\operatorname{div}}$. Then the same holds on $X^{\mathrm{An}}$.

title: Theorem 22.1.75
text: Theorem 22.1.75 ( [ Corollary 12.18 , BJ22 ] ) . 6B2CF0C2744A Let $S$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a sequence of rational numbers $\varepsilon _ i\searrow 0$ and a decreasing sequence $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\varepsilon _ i S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that $\phi $ is the pointwise limit of $\phi _ i$, as $i\to \infty $.

text: Conjecture 22.1.76 . 95739E70234B Assume that $X$ is unibranch. Then every bounded from above increasing net of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ converges in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$.

title: 22.1.77 The analytifications
text: Let $X$ be a connected projective manifold of dimension $n$. Let $\theta $ be a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class.

title: 22.1.78 The transcendental setting
text: Definition 22.1.79 . 322D4668B967 For $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we define the analytification $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,0]$ as follows: 2CFF9C7C56DB 22.1.80 \begin{equation}  \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq -v(\varphi )=-\lim _{k\to \infty }\frac{1}{k}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right). \end{equation} By theorem 5.16.14 and Fekete's lemma, the limit in ( 22.1.80 ) exists. Note that we can also write DFFDD4E75B4D 22.1.81 \begin{equation}  \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\inf _{k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}} -2^{-k}v\left( \mathcal{I}(2^ k\varphi )\right). \end{equation} When $v=t\operatorname{ord}_ E$ for some prime divisor $E$ over $X$, $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-t\nu (\varphi ,E)$ by proposition 5.16.15 . Definition 22.1.82 . 866728488224 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. We define the analytification $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\operatorname{div}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ of $\Gamma $ as follows: For any $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$, we define 45957E422015 22.1.83 \begin{equation}  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation} Clearly, ( 22.1.83 ) is independent of the choice of $\omega $. Note that ( 22.1.83 ) can be equivalently written as \[  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)= \sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)=\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega ,\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)  \] with $(-\infty )^{\mathrm{An}}(v) = -\infty $ understood. Proposition 22.1.84 . A87B7BF0C3D5 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\Gamma _{\max }\leq 0$. Let $\Psi $ be the complexification of $\Gamma ^*$. Then B5F5AD50A5AD 22.1.85 \begin{equation}  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=-\sigma (v)(\Psi )\quad \forall v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} See definition 17.10.17 for the definition of the complexification $\Psi \in \mathrm{QPSH}(X\times \Delta )$. Note that since $\Gamma _{\max }\leq 0$, by corollary 17.13.31 and theorem 5.14.10 , $\Psi $ extends uniquely to a quasi-psh function on $X\times \Delta $. Proof. Recall that \[  \Psi (x,\delta )=\sup _{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }} (\Gamma _{\tau }(x)-\log |\delta |^2\tau )\quad \text{for }x\in X, \delta \in \Delta ^*.  \] By ( 22.1.69 ), we have $\sigma (v)(\log |\delta |^2)=1$ and $\sigma (v)(\Gamma _{\tau })=v(\Gamma _{\tau })$ for all $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$. So we have \[  \sigma (v)(\Gamma _\tau (x) - \log |\delta |^2 \tau ) = v(\Gamma _\tau ) - \tau .  \] Lastly, since $\sigma (v)$ is a divisorial valuation on $X \times \Delta $, by corollary 5.16.9 , we conclude ( 22.1.85 ). $\square$ Definition 22.1.86 . 54C62141C0D9 Let $N\in \mathbb {N}$, and $A_{0},\ldots ,A_ N$ be a finite collection of elements in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\tau _0>\tau _1>\cdots >\tau _ N$ be finitely many real numbers. Then the piecewise linear curve $A=(A_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cup \{ -\infty \} $ associated with these data is the affine interpolation of these data: FE3BE40BF529 $A_{\tau _ i}=A_ i$ for $i=0,\ldots ,N$; 2D3D174A0348 $A_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$ for $\tau \leq \tau _ N$; B0B44E5310EA for $t\in (0,1)$ and $i=0,\ldots ,N-1$, we have \[  A_{(1-t)\tau _ i+t\tau _{i+1}}=(1-t)A_{\tau _ i}+tA_{\tau _{i+1}};  \] 8FF2573D4019 $A_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $ for $\tau >\tau _0$. The analytification of $A$ is the function $A^{\mathrm{An}}\colon X^{\mathrm{An}}\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ defined as follows: 2B233D0F0F88 22.1.87 \begin{equation}  A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)\coloneqq \sup _{\tau \leq \tau _0} (A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau )=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N} \left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right)\quad \forall v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}. \end{equation} We also say $A=(A_{\tau })_{\tau \leq \tau _0}$ is a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Remark 22.1.88 . 9911A537C86C Note that $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$ is upper semicontinuous, but not necessarily concave. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Then it can be inductively constructed as follows: D954EE804570 For $\tau \in (\tau _0,\infty )$, we let $A'_{\tau }\equiv -\infty $; 34859AD723A6 we set $A'_{\tau _0}=A_{\tau _0}$; FCE6B95F3C1F define inductively for $j=0,\ldots ,N-1$ the following: For $\tau \in [\tau _{j+1},\tau _ j)$, we set \[  A'_{\tau }=\max _{i=j+1,\ldots ,N}\left( \frac{\tau _ j-\tau }{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A_{\tau _ i}+\frac{\tau -\tau _ i}{\tau _ j-\tau _ i}A'_{\tau _ j} \right)\lor A'_{\tau _ j};  \] E47ACD33228B for $\tau \in (-\infty ,\tau _ N)$, we set $A'_{\tau }=A_{\tau _ N}$. This construction is just a reformulation of the general formula proposition 21.11.12 . In particular, $A'_{\tau }\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ for all $\tau \leq \tau _0$. Note that $A'$ is not necessarily piecewise linear. Lemma 22.1.89 . 6784060E951F Let $A$ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $(A'_{\tau })_{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}$ be the upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_{\tau }$. Define $\tilde A$ by \[  \tilde{A}^{\theta +\omega }_{\tau }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_{\tau }]_{\mathcal I}, \quad \omega \in \textup{Käh}(X),\  \tau <\tau _0.  \] Then $\tilde A\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$, and F46F1129051C 22.1.90 \begin{equation}  A^{\mathrm{An}}=\tilde{A}^{\mathrm{An}}\quad \text{on }X^{\operatorname{div}}. \end{equation} Here $\tau _0$ is as in definition 22.1.86 . Proof. We continue to use the notations in definition 22.1.86 . The fact that $\tilde{A}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ follows from 22.1.88 and the cocycle property of the $\mathcal{I}$-projection. In order to prove ( 22.1.90 ), we fix $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$ and $\omega \in \textup{Käh}(X)$. The inductive construction in 22.1.88 uses only finite maxima and positive affine combinations of the potentials $A_{\tau _ i}$. On divisorial valuations, analytification commutes with both operations. Moreover, $P_{\theta +\omega }[\bullet ]_{\mathcal I}$ does not change divisorial valuations. Hence \[  \tau \mapsto \left(P_{\theta +\omega }[A'_\tau ]_{\mathcal I}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)= (A'_\tau )^{\mathrm{An}}(v)  \] is the ordinary upper concave envelope of $\tau \mapsto A_\tau ^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$. The Legendre-type supremum over $\tau $ is therefore unchanged by passing from $A$ to $A'$, which proves ( 22.1.90 ). $\square$

title: 22.1.91 The algebraic setting
text: Let $L$ be a $\mathbb {Q}$-line bundle on $X$ and $h$ be a Hermitian metric on $L$ with $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Lemma 22.1.92 . A8896460B129 For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we have $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. After replacing $L$ with a sufficiently high power, we may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Take a very ample line bundle $H$ on $X$. By Siu's uniform global generation theorem [ Siu98 ] , [ Theorem 6.27 , Dem12 ] there exists $b>0$ large enough so that $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$ is globally generated for all $k>0$. Let $\{ s_ i\} _ i$ be a finite set of global sections that generate the sheaf $H^{b}\otimes L^ k\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )$. Then \[  v(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))=\min _ i v(s_ i).  \] It follows that $v\mapsto -k^{-1}v\left(\mathcal{I}(k\varphi ) \right)$ lies in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\frac{b}{k}H)^{\mathrm{An}})$. Using ( 22.1.81 ), we conclude that $\varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. $\square$ Lemma 22.1.93 . 9434BE558E6A Let $\Gamma $ be a piecewise linear curve in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. The result follows from ( 22.1.87 ), proposition 22.1.73 and 22.1.92 . $\square$ Lemma 22.1.94 . 76252E7717AC Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbb {C}$-algebra of finite type and $I$ be an ideal of $ R[t]$. If for any $a\in S^1$, $a^*I\subseteq I$, then $I$ is stable under the $\mathbb C^*$-action. Moreover, there are ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots \subseteq I_ m$ in $R$ so that 6126C03E6587 22.1.95 \begin{equation}  I=I_0 + I_1t+ \cdots + I_ m (t^ m). \end{equation} Proof. It suffices to argue that $I$ can be expanded as in ( 22.1.95 ). To see this, assume that $a\in I$. We can write $a=a_0+a_1t+\cdots +a_ mt^ m$ with $a_ i\in R$. Then our assumption implies that $\sum _ i a_ i \rho ^ i t^ i\in I$ as well for all $\rho \in S^1$. So by the Lagrange interpolation formula, $a_ it^ i\in I$ for all $i$. Therefore, we can write $I$ as $I_0+I_1t+I_2t^2+\cdots $ for some ideals $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq \cdots $ in $R$. But as $R$ is noetherian, there is $m\geq 0$ so that $I_{m'}=I_ m$ for $m'>m$. ( 22.1.95 ) follows. $\square$ Lemma 22.1.96 . AF0C82DE24E9 Let $X$ be a complex projective variety and $p:X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Assume that $\mathcal{I}$ is an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {C}$. Assume that $\mathcal{I}|_{X \times \mathbb C^*}=p^*\mathcal{J}$ for some coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal{J}$ on $X$. Then $\mathcal{I}$ is the analytification of an algebraic coherent ideal sheaf. Proof. Let $q:X\times (\mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} )\rightarrow X$ be the natural projection. Since $\mathbb C^* \subset \mathbb {P}^1\setminus \{ 0\} $, we can glue $q^*\mathcal{J}$ with $\mathcal{I}$ to get an analytic coherent ideal sheaf on $X\times \mathbb {P}^1$. By the GAGA principle, this ideal sheaf is necessarily algebraic, hence so is its restriction to $X\times \mathbb {C}$. $\square$ Next we point out a version of Siu's uniform global generation lemma that we will need in the proof of our next theorem: Lemma 22.1.97 . E61430B531F3 Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ such that $c_1(L) = \{ \theta \} $ and $\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X\times \Delta , p_1^*\theta )$, where $\Delta $ is the unit disk. Let $G$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Then there exists $k>0$, depending only on $X$ and $G$, such that $p_1^*(G^ k \otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal I(m \Phi )$ is globally generated for all $m \in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Proof. The argument for this is exactly the same as the one in [ Lemma 5.6 , BBJ21 ] with Nadel's vanishing theorem replaced by the family version proved by Matsumura in [ Theorem 1.7 , Mat16 ] . $\square$ Proposition 22.1.98 . 6A232EAE791C Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be a model potential and $\ell \in \mathcal{R}(X,\theta ;\phi )$ with $\sup _ X \ell _1\leq 0$. Let $\Phi $ be the complexification of $\ell $. Then the function \[  v\mapsto -\sigma (v)(\Phi ) \quad \text{for } v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}  \] admits a unique extension to an element of $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Proof. We may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 22.1.72 . Let $p_1\colon X\times \mathbb {C}\rightarrow X$ be the projection. For each $t>0$, we have $\ell _ t\in \mathcal{E}(X,\theta ;\phi )$, hence $\ell _ t\sim _ P\phi $ by theorem 16.3.15 and $\ell _ t\sim _{\mathcal{I}}\phi $ by corollary 16.8.14 . Thanks to proposition 5.16.22 and 20.2.56 , for each $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, we have \[  \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )|_{X\times \Delta ^*} = p_1^* \mathcal{I}(m\phi )|_{X\times \Delta ^*}.  \] In particular, $\mathcal{I}(m\Phi )$ admits an $S^1$-invariant coherent extension to $X\times \mathbb {C}$, obtained by gluing it with $p_1^*\mathcal{I}(m\phi )$ over $X\times \mathbb {C}^*$. From 22.1.94 and 22.1.96 , we get that 9186BF0A5F55 22.1.99 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )=\mathfrak {a}_0 +\mathfrak {a}_1 t+\cdots +\mathfrak {a}_{N-1} t^{N-1}+\mathfrak {a}_ N (t^ N)\, , \end{equation} where the $\mathfrak {a}_ i$'s are coherent ideal sheaves on $X$. Using 22.1.97 , there exists an ample line bundle $T$ over $X$ such that $p_1^* (T\otimes L^ m)\otimes \mathcal{I}(m\Phi )$ is globally generated, which is equivalent to $T\otimes L^ m\otimes \mathfrak {a}_ i$ being globally generated for all $i$. 4 We define \[  \varphi _ m(v)\coloneqq -\frac{1}{m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(m\Phi ))=-\frac{1}{m}\min _ i (v(\mathfrak {a}_ i)+i),\quad v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}.  \] From the right-hand side of the formula, $\varphi _ m$ can be extended to an element in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+m^{-1}T)^{\mathrm{An}})$, which we denote by the same symbol. For $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  -\sigma (v)(\Phi )=\lim _{m\to \infty }-\frac{1}{2^ m}\sigma (v)(\mathcal{I}(2^ m\Phi ))=\lim _{m\to \infty }\varphi _{2^ m}(v)  \] and the right-hand side defines an element in $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by definition, since $\{ \varphi _{2^ m}\} _ m$ is decreasing by the subadditivity of multiplier ideals theorem 5.16.14 . $\square$ 4. ↩ In contrast with the case where $\phi $ is bounded, explored in [ BBJ21 ] , $\mathfrak {a}_ N \neq \mathcal{O}_ X$ in general. Corollary 22.1.100 . 9D2A9B228E44 Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Then $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$ defined in definition 22.1.82 admits a unique extension to $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. The extension will be denoted by the same notation $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$. Proof. Observe that the extension is unique if it exists by theorem 22.1.72 . We may assume that $\Gamma _{\max }=0$ without loss of generality. When $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, our assertion follows from proposition 22.1.98 and proposition 22.1.84 . In general, fix an ample line bundle $H$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(H)$. Then we know that \[  \Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\left(\Gamma ^{m^{-1}\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}((L+m^{-1}H)^{\mathrm{An}})  \] for any $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. Therefore, $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ by proposition 22.1.74 . $\square$
