title: Lemma 22.1.105
text: Lemma 22.1.105 . CB69CB164255 The map ( 22.1.102 ) is order preserving. Moreover, suppose that $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ satisfies that $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \Gamma '^{\mathrm{An}}$, then $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$. In particular, the map ( 22.1.102 ) is injective. Proof. The map ( 22.1.102 ) is order preserving by definition. Let us take $\Gamma ,\Gamma '\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \Gamma '^{\mathrm{An}}$. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Let $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$ and $t \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}$. Then, using ( 22.1.83 ) and the homogeneity of divisorial valuations, we notice that 99B9B27CF451 22.1.106 \begin{equation}  t \Gamma ^\mathrm{An}\left(t^{-1} v \right) = \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+ t \tau \right). \end{equation} A similar equality holds for $\Gamma '$. Therefore, by corollary 21.11.26 , we have \[  \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}\leq \left(\Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. It follows that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }  \] by proposition 16.8.9 . Since both sides are $\mathcal{I}$-model, proposition 16.8.17 gives \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\leq \Gamma '{}_{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }  \] for all $\tau \in \mathbb {R}$. Hence $\Gamma \leq \Gamma '$ by the definition of the order. $\square$

title: Equation 22.1.106
text: 99B9B27CF451 22.1.106 \begin{equation}  t \Gamma ^\mathrm{An}\left(t^{-1} v \right) = \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}}\left( \left(\Gamma _{\tau }^{\theta +\omega }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+ t \tau \right). \end{equation}

title: Lemma 22.1.107
text: Lemma 22.1.107 . AB6A7C1FD159 Let $\phi \in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. Then there is a piecewise linear curve $A$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\phi =A^{\mathrm{An}}$. In particular, $\phi $ is in the image of ( 22.1.102 ). Proof. Let us write C18150DD4B94 22.1.108 \begin{equation}  \phi =\frac{1}{m}\max _{i=1,\ldots ,M} \left(\log |s_ i|+\lambda _ i\right), \end{equation} where $m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$, $s_{1},\ldots , s_ M$ are a finite number of sections of $L^ m$ and $\lambda _1,\ldots ,\lambda _ M\in \mathbb {Q}$. Write $I_{\tau }$ for the set of $i$ such that $m^{-1}\lambda _ i=\tau $. We denote the finitely many $\tau $ so that $I_{\tau }$ is non-empty as $\tau _0> \cdots > \tau _ N$. For each $i=0,\ldots ,N$, we write \[  A_{\tau _ i}=\frac{1}{m}\max _{j\in I_{\tau _ i}} \log |s_ j|^2_{h^ m}.  \] We define $A$ as the piecewise linear curve associated with the $A_{\tau _ i}$'s and the $\tau _ i$'s. For every $v\in X^{\mathrm{An}}$, \[  A^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\max _{i=0,\ldots ,N}\left(A_{\tau _ i}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau _ i\right) =\frac{1}{m}\max _{j=1,\ldots ,M}\left(\log |s_ j|(v)+\lambda _ j\right)=\phi (v),  \] where we used the convention $\log |s_ j|(v)=-v(s_ j)$. The final assertion follows from 22.1.89 and theorem 22.1.72 . $\square$

title: Proposition 22.1.109
text: Proposition 22.1.109 . 9F673331DE01 Let $(\Gamma _ i)_{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$. Assume that ( 22.1.42 ) is satisfied. Then \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i}^{\mathrm{An}}.  \] Proof. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. We need to show that \[  \left( \inf _{i\in I} P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma _ i]_{\mathcal{I}} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _{i\in I} \Gamma _{i}^{\mathrm{An}}.  \] Therefore, after replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega $, we may assume that $\Gamma _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ for all $i\in I$ and $\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Fix $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$. By theorem 22.1.72 , it suffices to prove that 115AEB4414B4 22.1.110 \begin{equation}  \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \left(\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)= \adjustlimits \inf _{i\in I}\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation} Write $\Gamma =\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _ i$. We first compare the two sides inside the Legendre-type supremum. If $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, then by the definition of the infimum test curve, \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }.  \] The net $(\Gamma _{i,\tau })_ i$ decreases to $\Gamma _{\tau }$. By 17.15.41 , $\Gamma _{\tau }$ is stable under $P_{\theta }[\bullet ]$. Hence proposition 16.4.4 gives convergence of the masses, and corollary 16.9.14 yields \[  \Gamma _{i,\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S}\Gamma _{\tau }.  \] Hence theorem 16.9.55 gives \[  \Gamma _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)=\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v),\quad \tau <\Gamma _{\max }.  \] If $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$, then $\Gamma _{\tau }\equiv -\infty $, and also $\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }\equiv -\infty $, since $\Gamma _{\max }=\inf _ i(\Gamma _ i)_{\max }$. Thus the same equality holds for $\tau >\Gamma _{\max }$ as well, with value $-\infty $. The possible endpoint $\tau =\Gamma _{\max }$ does not affect the supremum: for any test curve $\Lambda $ and any $v\in X^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  \sup _{\tau \leq \Lambda _{\max }}\left(\Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right) =\sup _{\tau < \Lambda _{\max }}\left(\Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right),  \] because $\Lambda _{\Lambda _{\max }}\leq \Lambda _{\tau }$ for $\tau <\Lambda _{\max }$, hence \[  \Lambda _{\Lambda _{\max }}^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\Lambda _{\max } \leq \Lambda _{\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\Lambda _{\max }  \] and we let $\tau \nearrow \Lambda _{\max }$. Consequently, in ( 22.1.110 ) we may replace $\left(\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$ by $\inf _ i\Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$ inside the supremum. The equality then follows from proposition 21.11.36 applied to the closed convex functions $-\Gamma _{i,\bullet }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)$. $\square$

title: Equation 22.1.110
text: 115AEB4414B4 22.1.110 \begin{equation}  \sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \left(\inf _{i\in I}\Gamma _{i,\tau }\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right)= \adjustlimits \inf _{i\in I}\sup _{\tau \in \mathbb {R}} \left( \Gamma _{i,\tau }^{\mathrm{An}}(v)+\tau \right). \end{equation}

title: Theorem 22.1.111
text: Theorem 22.1.111 . 9B811DBD89E3 The map ( 22.1.102 ) is an order preserving bijection. Proof. The map ( 22.1.102 ) is an order preserving injection by 22.1.105 . It remains to prove that it is surjective. Let $\phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. We want to construct $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. Let $H$ be an ample line bundle and $(\epsilon _ i)_ i$ be a decreasing sequence of rational numbers with limit $0$, $\phi _ i\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+\epsilon _ i H)^{\mathrm{An}})$ such that \[  \phi =\inf _{i>0}\phi _ i.  \] The existence of these data is guaranteed by theorem 22.1.75 . Fix a Kähler form $\omega \in c_1(H)$. Thanks to 22.1.107 , we can find $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ i \omega )$ with $(\Gamma ^ i)^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi _ i$. It follows from 22.1.105 that \[  \Gamma ^ i\geq P_{\theta +\epsilon _ i\omega }\left[ \Gamma ^{i+1} \right]_{\mathcal{I}} \geq \Gamma ^{i+1}.  \] Therefore, for any $\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)$, after discarding finitely many $i$ so that $\omega '\geq \epsilon _ i\omega $, the sequence $(P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}})_ i$ is decreasing. This does not change its infimum. We let \[  \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}=\inf _{i\gg 1}P_{\theta +\omega '}\left[ \Gamma ^{i} \right]_{\mathcal{I}}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +\omega ').  \] Note that the infimum is defined thanks to ( 22.1.104 ). It follows from proposition 22.1.109 that \[  \left(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '} \right)^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi .  \] From this, we conclude that for $\omega ',\omega ''\in \textup{Käh}(X)$ with $\omega '\leq \omega ''$, we have \[  P_{\theta +\omega ''}\left[ \Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '}\right]_{\mathcal{I}}=\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega ''}.  \] Indeed, both sides have analytification $\phi $, by ( 22.1.103 ) and ( 22.1.102 ). The injectivity part of 22.1.105 gives our assertion. It follows that $(\Gamma ^{\theta +\omega '})_{\omega '\in \textup{Käh}(X)}$ defines an element $\Gamma $ in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ and $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. $\square$

title: Theorem 22.1.112
text: Theorem 22.1.112 . CB40FF867A00 Under the bijection theorem 22.1.111 , the operations on the space $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ defined in subsection 22.1.20 all correspond to the corresponding operations on $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ in Boucksom–Jonsson's theory.

title: Theorem 22.1.113
text: Theorem 22.1.113 . D613676A36CA Let $Y\subseteq X$ be an irreducible analytic subset. Consider an element $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )$ with well-defined restriction to $Y$. Then 0C743FB2F354 22.1.114 \begin{equation}  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}=\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}|_{Y^{\operatorname{div}}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first reduce to the positive mass case. Choose a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and set $\widehat{\Gamma }=P_{\theta +\omega _0}[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Replacing $\theta $ by $\theta +\omega _0$ and $\Gamma $ by $\widehat{\Gamma }$ does not change $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}$, by ( 22.1.103 ); it also only replaces $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )$ by the corresponding $\mathcal{I}$-projection on $\widetilde{Y}$, whose analytification is unchanged. Hence we may assume that $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Let $\phi =\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}\in \mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$. By 22.1.116 , $\phi (v_{Y,\mathrm{triv}})\neq -\infty $. Take an ample line bundle $S$ on $X$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ in $c_1(S)$. Write $\phi $ as the decreasing limit of a sequence $(\phi ^{i})_ i$ of elements in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}((L+i^{-1}S)^{\mathrm{An}})$ as in theorem 22.1.75 . Take $\Gamma ^{i}\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +i^{-1}\omega )$ such that $\Gamma ^{i,\mathrm{An}}=\phi ^{i}$. Note that by 22.1.10 , $\Gamma ^ i\in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta +i^{-1}\omega )_{>0}$. Write $\widehat{\Gamma }^ i\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ^ i]_{\mathcal{I}}$ and $\widehat{\Gamma }\coloneqq P_{\theta +\omega }[\Gamma ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Applying proposition 22.1.109 to the decreasing sequence $(\widehat{\Gamma }^ i)_ i$ and then using the injectivity in 22.1.105 , we get $\inf _ i\widehat{\Gamma }^ i=\widehat{\Gamma }$. Hence, by the componentwise definition of this infimum, for any $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$, we have \[  \inf _{i\in \mathbb {N}}\widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau }=\widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }.  \] Now proposition 16.4.4 and corollary 16.9.14 give \[  \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau }\xrightarrow {d_ S} \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }.  \] for all $\tau <\Gamma _{\max }$. By 22.1.116 again, each $\widehat{\Gamma }^{i}$ has non-trivial restriction to $Y$. By proposition 20.2.22 , for any Kähler form $\omega '$ on $\widetilde{Y}$ satisfying $\omega '\geq \omega |_{\widetilde{Y}}$ we have \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau } \right)\xrightarrow {d_ S} \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau }\right)  \] for any $\tau <(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma ))_{\max }$. Thanks to theorem 16.9.55 , for every $c\operatorname{ord}_ F\in Y^{\operatorname{div}}$ and every such $\tau $, \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }_{\tau } \right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\inf _{i\geq 1}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y \left( \widehat{\Gamma }^{i}_{\tau } \right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F).  \] Applying proposition 21.11.36 to the Legendre transforms in $\tau $, and using again that $\mathcal{I}$-projection does not change analytification, we get \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\inf _{i\geq 1}\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma ^ i)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F).  \] Since also $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\inf _ i \Gamma ^{i,\mathrm{An}}$, it suffices to prove ( 22.1.114 ) with $\Gamma ^ i$ in place of $\Gamma $. In other words, we have reduced to the case where $\phi \in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb {Q}}(L^{\mathrm{An}})$ and $L$ is big. Let $\Gamma \in \mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\Gamma ^{\mathrm{An}}=\phi $. By 22.1.107 , we can find a concave curve $(\Gamma '_{\tau })_{\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }}$ such that $\Gamma '_{\tau }$ is a generalized Fubini–Study metric for each $\tau \leq \Gamma _{\max }$ and such that \[  \Gamma _{\tau }=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }]_{\mathcal{I}}=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }].  \] Here the second equality follows from example 18.1.10 , since generalized Fubini–Study metrics have analytic singularities. With the convention that $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(-\infty )=-\infty $ and $(-\infty )^{\mathrm{An}}\equiv -\infty $, it follows that for any $c\operatorname{ord}_ F\in \widetilde{Y}^{\operatorname{div}}$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \phi |_{Y^{\mathrm{An}}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=& \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\Gamma '_{\tau }{}^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\left(\Gamma '_{\tau }|_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma '_{\tau })^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \sup _{\tau <\Gamma _{\max }} \left(\operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma _{\tau })^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)+\tau \right)\\  =&  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(\Gamma )^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F). \end{aligned}  \] The third equality follows from example 20.2.15 , since $\Gamma '_{\tau }$ has analytic singularities. The fourth equality follows from $\Gamma _{\tau }=P_{\theta }[\Gamma '_{\tau }]$, proposition 20.2.21 and corollary 16.8.14 . It remains to justify the second line. Namely, we want to show that for any generalized Fubini–Study metric $\varphi $ whose restriction to $\widetilde{Y}$ is not identically $-\infty $, we have 8B0003DFBC94 22.1.115 \begin{equation}  \varphi ^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F)=\left(\varphi |_{\widetilde{Y}}\right)^{\mathrm{An}}(c\operatorname{ord}_ F). \end{equation} We can immediately reduce to the case where $\varphi $ is a Fubini–Study metric, and then to the case \[  \varphi =\log |s|_{h_0}^2,  \] where $s$ is a holomorphic section of $L$, not vanishing identically on $Y$, in which case ( 22.1.115 ) is obvious. $\square$

title: Lemma 22.1.116
18.28 Partial Bergman kernels
text:
The classical Bergman kernel of a Hermitian line bundle $L$ on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ encodes, through its asymptotic expansion as the tensor power $L^ k$ goes to infinity, deep geometric information about the underlying metric. This chapter develops the corresponding partial Bergman kernel. The word partial refers to the fact that we only use sections cut out by an ideal, typically the multiplier ideal of an auxiliary psh weight on a closed subset $K\subseteq X$. The main result is the convergence theorem theorem 18.28.49 . Given a $	heta $-psh potential $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, a closed non-pluripolar weighted subset $(K,v)$, and a Bernstein–Markov measure $\mu $, the normalized partial Bergman measures on $X$ converge weakly to the partial equilibrium measure of $(K,v,\varphi )$ as $k	o \infty $. This is the relative version of the theorem of Berman–Boucksom–Witt Nyström, corresponding to the case $\varphi =V_	heta $. The assumptions are essentially the mildest ones under which the statement makes sense. The first part of the chapter introduces the relative envelope operators. In subsection 18.28.1 we define the relative $P$-envelope $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)$ and the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$ by replacing the constraint $\eta \leq 0$ in the usual $P$- and $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes with the constraint $\eta |_ K\leq v$. We establish their basic properties, including monotonicity, mass-preservation, and the relation with the envelope operators of section 16.1 . The second part develops the equilibrium theory associated with a weighted subset $(K,v)$. In subsection 18.28.19 we show that the Monge–Ampère measure $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$ is carried by the contact locus $\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=v\} \subseteq K$, which justifies the name partial equilibrium measure . The chapter concludes in subsection 18.28.37 with the proof of the weak convergence of partial Bergman measures towards this partial equilibrium. In this section, we fix a weighted subset $(K,v)$ of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Definition 18.28.46 . C3C647253911 For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$, we introduce the partial Bergman kernels of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) as follows: For any $k\geq 1$, we introduce 14.50  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }(x) \coloneqq \sup \left\{ h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}(x):s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight),ight.\  \left. N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \leq 1 ight\} ,\quad x\in K. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We extend $B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }$ to the whole $X$ by setting it to be $0$ outside $K$. The partial Bergman measures of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) are defined as 14.53  egin{equation}   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \coloneqq  rac{n!}{k^ n} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \, \mathrm{d}\mu \end{equation} for each $k\geq 1$. Remark 18.28.47 . 129D3B333F18 Recall that in the definition of $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$, the singular metric $\varphi $ only appears through the conditions $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The pointwise norm used to define $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$ and $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is defined via $v$ not $\varphi $. This leads to the following seemingly paradoxical consequence, if $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }\leq  eta ^ k_{v,\psi ,\mu }\quad  orall \, k\geq 1.  \] We shall apply this consequence without further mention in the sequel. Observe that \[  \int _ X  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }= rac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight).  \] In particular, 889A68CCEC83 18.28.48  egin{equation}  \lim _{k	o \infty }\int _ X  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }=\operatorname{vol}\left(	heta _{\varphi }ight)=\int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \end{equation} by theorem 18.1.46 and 18.28.15 . The goal of this section is to improve this result to the convergence of the Bergman kernels themselves: Theorem 18.28.49 . EA3E101DCA5E Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then A6F9F2DF4A0D 18.28.50  egin{equation}   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty . \end{equation} The proof will be given at the end of this subsection. We shall prove a few preliminaries at first. Take a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ so that \[  \int _ X \omega ^ n = 1.  \] Proposition 18.28.51 . 4C368CFA09EB Assume here that $K=X$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. If $v \in C^\infty (X)$, then 4DF720497AC6 18.28.52  egin{equation}   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty . \end{equation} Proof. The equality part in ( 18.28.52 ) follows from corollary 18.28.14 . It remains to prove the weak convergence. Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n})_ k$. In view of ( 18.28.48 ), it suffices to show that 14347C41585E 18.28.53  egin{equation}  	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n. \end{equation} We can obtain an upper bound of $	au $ via the observation: \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq  eta ^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n}.  \] After replacing $\varphi $ by $V_{	heta }$, the corresponding problem is handled by [ Theorem 1.2 , Ber11 ] , giving us \[   eta ^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n} ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n \quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty ,  \] where the last identity is due to proposition 16.3.41 . We obtain that 1B7624ED3973 18.28.54  egin{equation}  	au \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{	heta ,X}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n. \end{equation} Now observe that it suffices to show that C700200CB6BE 18.28.55  egin{equation}  	au \left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} =0. \end{equation} Assuming this, then ( 18.28.54 ) further gives \[  	au \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)= vight\} }\, 	heta _ v^ n= 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n,  \] where the equality follows from proposition 16.3.41 , and ( 18.28.53 ) follows. It now remains to argue ( 18.28.55 ). Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Observe that \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) \sim \varphi  \] for all $\epsilon \geq 0$ by 18.28.15 and proposition 16.6.22 . The family $P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)$ is decreasing as $\epsilon 	o 0+$. Let \[  \chi \coloneqq \inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Then $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ since $\chi \geq P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v)$. Moreover $\chi \leq v$ and $\chi \preceq \varphi $. Hence \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Thus, equality holds, and \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)\searrow P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] In other words, \[  \left\{ P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} = igcup _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}}\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} .  \] So in order to show ( 18.28.55 ), we may fix $\epsilon >0$ and argue that CE5263973CB7 18.28.56  egin{equation}  	au \left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} =0. \end{equation} Let $k\geq 1$, and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(k\varphi ))$ be a section such that $N^ k_{v,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1$. Then by [ Lemma 4.1 , Ber11 ] , there exists $C>0$ such that \[  h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv} \leq B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq B^ k_{v,V_{	heta },\omega ^ n} \leq k^ n C.  \] This implies that \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \leq v +  rac{\log C }{k} + n  rac{\log k}{ k }.  \] We define $\varphi _ k$ as in proposition 5.20.17 . Take $\alpha _ k
earrow 1$ as in proposition 5.20.17 . After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $X$. After replacing $\alpha _ k$ by a subsequence, we also have $\alpha _ k\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\epsilon \omega )$ for all $k>0$, and $\alpha _ k\varphi \searrow \varphi $. Then \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\preceq \varphi _ k\preceq \alpha _ k\varphi .  \] We notice that $ rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X, 	heta + \epsilon \omega )$ for all $k \geq k_0(\epsilon )$. Indeed, \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}\left(X,	heta + k^{-1} c_1(T,h_ T)ight)  \] by proposition 5.20.4 . In particular, \[   rac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)- rac{\log C}{k}-n rac{\log k}{k}\leq P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v).  \] Now taking supremum over all candidates $s$, we obtain that 725395815923 18.28.57  egin{equation}  B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq C k^ n \mathrm{e}^{k \left(P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v)-vight)},\quad k \geq k_0. \end{equation} Now we prove ( 18.28.56 ). First observe that $\alpha _ k\varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 16.9.25 . Thus, by proposition 18.28.35 , \[  P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) \searrow P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)  \] and we get that \[   igcup _{k=1}^{\infty }\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) < vight\} =\left\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < vight\} .  \] It suffices to show that $	au $ does not put mass on the set $\{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v\} $ for each fixed $m$. Fix a positive rational $\delta >0$, it suffices to show that $	au $ puts no mass on $F\coloneqq \{ P_{	heta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v-\delta \} $. Note that $F$ is open, and ( 18.28.57 ) gives $ eta ^\ell _{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n}(F)	o 0$. Therefore, $	au $ puts no mass on $F$ as well, proving ( 18.28.56 ). $\square$ Definition 18.28.58 . A0F71B40AAE1 Take $k\geq 1$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, let $\operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ be the space of norms on the vector space $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi } \colon \operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )) 	o \mathbb R$ be the partial Donaldson functional : 14.62  egin{equation}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(H) =  rac{n!}{k^{n+1}} \log  rac{\operatorname{vol}\{ s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) : H(s) \leq 1\} }{\operatorname{vol}\left\{ s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) : N^ k_{0,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1ight\} }, \end{equation} where $\operatorname{vol}$ is a Lebesgue measure on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The normalization does not matter. Proposition 18.28.59 . F547344ACE10 Let $w,w' \in C^0(X)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then D29819040D75 18.28.60  egin{equation}  \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) ight)= \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation} In particular, 04790CD84F49 18.28.61  egin{equation}  \lim _{k	o \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 18.28.45 , for any $k\geq 1$, $N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}$ and $N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 18.28.60 ) make sense. We first assume that $w,w'\in C^\infty (X)$. To start, we make the following observation: \[   egin{aligned}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})& = \int _0^1  rac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\omega ^ n})\, \mathrm{d}t\ &  = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \,  eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\,  \mathrm{d}t. \end{aligned}  \] The second equality follows from differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}$: \[   rac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathcal L_{k,\varphi } \left(N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}ight)=\int _ X (w-w')\,  eta ^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}.  \] By proposition 18.28.51 , we have \[  \lim _{k	o \infty }\int _ X (w-w') \,  eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}=\int _ X (w-w')\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n.  \] By theorem 18.1.46 , we have \[   igl |\int _ X (w-w') eta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n} igr | \leq C \sup _ X |w - w'|.  \] Hence, by the dominated convergence theorem we obtain that \[   egin{aligned}  \lim _{k	o \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})ight) & = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n \, \mathrm{d}t\ &  = \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line we have used proposition 18.28.27 . This proves ( 18.28.60 ) for smooth weights. For general $w,w'\in C^0(X)$, choose smooth functions $w_ j,w'_ j$ converging uniformly to $w,w'$, respectively. If $\| w_ j-w\| _{C^0}\leq \delta _ j$, then \[  \mathrm{e}^{-k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}\leq N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n}\leq \mathrm{e}^{k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n},  \] and hence \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})ight| \leq  rac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)\delta _ j.  \] The same estimate holds for $w'_ j$ and $w'$. Moreover, proposition 18.28.27 shows that the energy side is Lipschitz with respect to the uniform norm of the weight. Letting first $k	o \infty $ in the smooth case, and then $j	o \infty $, proves ( 18.28.60 ) for continuous weights. Equation ( 18.28.61 ) again follows by taking $w'=0$. $\square$ Lemma 18.28.62 . 922E6C36BCC8 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then C3210B1F6DE6 18.28.63  egin{equation}  \lim _{k	o \infty }  ig ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu }) ig ) = 0\, . \end{equation} Proof. By ( 18.28.41 ) and ( 18.28.44 ), for every $\epsilon >0$ and all $k\geq 1$, \[  N^ k_{v,\mu }\leq N^ k_{v,K}\leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}N^ k_{v,\mu }.  \] The corresponding unit balls therefore satisfy inclusions with radii differing by at most the factor $C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}$. Taking logarithmic volumes and multiplying by $n!k^{-n-1}$ gives \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })ight| \leq  rac{2n!}{k^{n+1}} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight)(\log C_\epsilon +\epsilon k).  \] The right-hand side has limsup at most $2\epsilon \operatorname{vol}(	heta _\varphi )$ by theorem 18.1.46 . Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$ proves ( 18.28.63 ). $\square$ Corollary 18.28.64 . 4CE59F3C4805 Let $w \in C^0(X)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k	o \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(w).  \] Proof. eq -\infty ight\} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight). \end{equation} Proof. We prove the first equality first. We write $S=\{ \eta =-\infty \} $. By definition, $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K\leq v$, so \[  \left.\left(\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)ight|_{K\setminus S}\geq \eta |_{K\setminus S}-v|_{K\setminus S}\, .  \] This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \leq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight).  \] Conversely, observe that $\sup _ K(\eta -v)>-\infty $ as $K$ is non-pluripolar. B1F17F151050 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })= \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Our claim follows from proposition 18.28.68 and 18.28.62 . $\square$ Proposition 18.28.73 . AC691D964EDB Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as }k	o \infty .  \] Proof. For $w\in C^0(X)$, let $f_ k,g\colon \mathbb {R}ightarrow \mathbb {R}$ ($k\geq 1$) be defined as \[  f_ k(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }),\quad g(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tw).  \] By corollary 18.28.72 , for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } f_ k(t)= g(t).  \] Here we use that $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v+tw)$ for all fixed $t$, which follows from $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ and the boundedness of $tw$ on $K$. Note that $f_ k$ is concave by Hölder's inequality. For each $k$, the function $f_ k$ is differentiable and \[  f_ k'(0)=\int _ X w\,  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] This follows by differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }$. The function $g$ is differentiable at $0$ by proposition 18.28.27 , with \[  g'(0)=\int _ K w\, 	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v)}.  \] Applying 21.11.63 to the convex functions $-f_ k$ and $-g$ gives \[  \lim _{k	o \infty } f_ k'(0)=g'(0),  \] which is equivalent to $ eta ^ k_{v, \varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$, by proposition 18.28.27 . $\square$ Proposition 18.28.74 . 0DFF36A22512 Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ is such that $	heta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 7EA15066EE63 18.28.75  egin{equation}   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\quad 	extup{as } k	o \infty . \end{equation} Proof. Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $ eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$. We claim that CBCF54FCD801 18.28.76  egin{equation}  	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that this claim implies the conclusion. In fact, by theorem 18.1.46 , we have equality of the total masses, so equality holds in ( 18.28.76 ). As $	au $ is an arbitrary cluster point of the sequence $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$, we get ( 18.28.75 ). It remains to prove ( 18.28.76 ). Let $(\varphi _ j)$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. We may assume that $	heta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for all $j\geq 1$. By corollary 18.1.14 , we know that \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] The quasi-equisingular approximation is decreasing, so applying the decreasing case of proposition 18.28.35 to the limit $P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, and using the definition of the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope, we get \[  P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] In particular, FD0D14628CD8 18.28.77  egin{equation}  \lim _{j	o \infty } \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n= \int _ X 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \leq  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu }  \] for any $k \geq 1$. As $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, by proposition 18.28.73 , \[  	au \leq 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,  \] for any $j \geq 1$ fixed. By ( 18.28.77 ) and the semicontinuity theorem theorem 13.13.9 , we have \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}\left[\varphi _ jight]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ nightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n  \] as $j	o \infty $. Therefore, ( 18.28.76 ) follows. $\square$ Proof of theorem 18.28.49 . By 18.28.15 and proposition 16.6.11 , the three potentials below have the same multiplier ideals. Hence \[   egin{aligned}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )ight) & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(kP_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})ight)\ & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I\left(kP_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)ight)ight). \end{aligned}  \] This allows us to replace $\varphi $ with $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. earrow \varphi $ a.e. and $	heta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for each $j\geq 1$. This gives \[   eta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu } \leq  eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] Let $	au $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $( eta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$. Then by proposition 18.28.74 , \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq 	au .  \] By proposition 18.28.35 and corollary 13.13.12 , we have \[  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n ightharpoonup 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n.  \] Hence, 8FD19D2B07C7 18.28.78  egin{equation}  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq 	au . \end{equation} A comparison of total masses using ( 18.28.48 ) gives that equality holds in ( 18.28.78 ). title: 18.28.1 Partial envelopes
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $K \subseteq X$ be a closed non-pluripolar set. Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Definition 18.28.2 . 28F090ED5EFA Given a function $f\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we introduce the relative $P$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 19BBFEFEB969 18.28.3 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Similarly, we define the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 1F7034C27B5A 18.28.4 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} By $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, we mean that there is a pluripolar set $S\subseteq X$ so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. In general the upper envelope in ( 18.28.3 ) or ( 18.28.4 ) may be identically $\infty $. Observe that when $f$ is bounded from below, neither envelope is identically $-\infty $. The envelopes contain essentially all envelope operators that we have studied here: Example 18.28.5 . D0D0EA7C293D When $K=X$ and $f=0$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] When $K=X$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ](f).  \] These definitions reduce to the envelopes studied in section 16.1 . On the other hand, when $\varphi =V_{\theta }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) & =P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\\ & =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \begin{array}{l} \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere} \end{array} \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] In an even more special case where $\varphi =V_{\theta }$ and $K=X$, we find that \[  P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](f)=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere}\Bigr \} .  \] This is nothing but $P_{\theta }(f)$ as we studied in definition 13.13.18 . Proposition 18.28.6 . C9561913A3E8 Let $f,g\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be functions and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then we have the following: 33B49F7D21A7 We have \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] 6B1193ABBD59 assume that $f$ is bounded from above, then \[  \begin{aligned}  \left.P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\  \left. P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere}; \end{aligned}  \] 27E6FD2D7332 suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] B3B86BE1530D if $f\leq g$, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](g),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(g);  \] 13DB8823929A for any $t \in (0,1)$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f),\\  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f). \end{aligned}  \] Proof. 1 This follows from $\eta \preceq \varphi \Rightarrow \eta \preceq _{\mathcal I}\varphi $. 2 This follows from proposition 5.14.5 and 5.17.4 . 3 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 4 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 5 If $\eta ,\eta '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ are such that \[  \begin{split} & \eta |_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad \eta '|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\ & \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta '\preceq \psi , \end{split}  \] then for $t\in (0,1)$, \[  \left.\left(t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\right)\right|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad t\eta +(1-t)\eta ' \preceq t\varphi +(1-t)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\leq P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f).  \] Since $\eta $ and $\eta '$ are arbitrary, the first inequality follows. The second follows from the same argument. $\square$ Similar to the usual envelopes studied in section 16.1 , the $P$-partial envelopes are well-behaved only when $\varphi $ has positive mass. Lemma 18.28.7 . 0F9B18404274 Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ is bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 96B9EFFFBDA7 18.28.8 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} In other words, in this situation, in the definition ( 18.28.3 ), we may restrict to only those $\eta $ with positive mass. Proof. By our assumption, we can find $C>0$ so that $\varphi |_ K-C\leq f$. Then if $\eta $ is a candidate in ( 18.28.3 ), $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate, and $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Therefore, $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate for the right-hand side of ( 18.28.8 ). The equality ( 18.28.8 ) follows. $\square$ Note that in the most important cases, we can actually replace the condition $\eta \leq f$ quasi-everywhere in ( 18.28.3 ) by everywhere. Lemma 18.28.9 . A86A369D4CBF Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 226F49B219B2 18.28.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. Both $\geq $ directions in ( 18.28.10 ) are trivial. Conversely, let $\eta $ be a candidate in ( 18.28.8 ). Let $S\subseteq X$ be a pluripolar set so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. We now claim that we can choose $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\chi |_ S\equiv -\infty $ and $\chi \leq \eta $. Assume this for the moment. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, we have \[  (1-\delta )\eta |_ K+\delta \chi |_ K\leq f,\quad (1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi \preceq \varphi .  \] Hence, $(1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 18.28.10 ). Letting $\delta \to 0+$, we conclude that $\eta $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 18.28.10 ) and hence, ( 18.28.10 ) follows. It remains to construct $\chi $. Since $\varphi $ has positive mass, the class $\{ \theta \} $ is big. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\rho }\geq 2\epsilon _0\omega _0$ for some $\epsilon _0>0$. By theorem 5.13.20 , there is a quasi-psh function $q$ such that $q|_ S\equiv -\infty $. Choose $A>0$ so that $A\omega _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. For $a>0$ small enough, $\rho +aq\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and still has pole $-\infty $ on $S$. Replacing $\rho $ by $\rho +aq$, we may therefore assume that $\rho |_ S\equiv -\infty $. Since $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>0$, fixing such a $\rho $ and taking $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, we have \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }}+\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Thus, by proposition 16.3.25 and theorem 16.3.35 , we have \[  \Bigl (\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }\Bigr ) \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] It suffices to define this function as $\chi $. $\square$ Corollary 18.28.11 . 712499DFC37F Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is bounded, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there is a constant $C=C(\sup _ K f,K,X)>0$ such that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq C.  \] Proof. Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, 5.17.4 then gives a constant $C>0$, depending only on $\sup _ K f$, $K$ and $X$, such that every $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere satisfies $\eta \leq C$ on $X$. This applies to the candidates defining both envelopes. Hence both candidate families are locally uniformly bounded above, so their upper semicontinuous suprema are genuine $\theta $-psh functions. By proposition 18.28.6 2 , both envelopes are dominated by $f$ quasi-everywhere on $K$. Applying 5.17.4 once more gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(f)\leq C.  \] $\square$ Proposition 18.28.12 . A1C36A6249C7 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Proof. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be such that $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then $\eta \preceq _ P \psi $, and thanks to corollary 16.8.30 for any $C>0$, we have $\eta \land (\psi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. But then $\eta \land (\psi +C)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f)$, and we find \[  \eta \land (\psi +C)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] By corollary 16.8.30 again, we get \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\psi ](\eta )\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Our assertion follows now from 18.28.7 . $\square$ Corollary 18.28.13 . 72097BEFEC59 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. We first apply proposition 18.28.12 , \[  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\right](f)\\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split}  \] Next observe that by 18.28.7 , the latter can also be written as \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} .  \] Next we apply 18.28.9 ; the remaining statements follow. $\square$ Corollary 18.28.14 . 96B842B9BF11 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be $\mathcal{I}$-good. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)=P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Proof. In fact, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, a potential $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ if and only if $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi $. Therefore, our assertion follows from corollary 18.28.13 and ( 18.28.4 ). $\square$ Next, we make the following observations about the singularity types of our envelopes: Lemma 18.28.15 . 18E5130ACB80 Let $f \colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We have EC4A564BADAB 18.28.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first prove the $P$-part of ( 18.28.16 ). If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta \leq 0$, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 18.28.3 ), and hence, \[  \eta +\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] It follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that \[  \eta |_ K\leq f,\quad \eta \preceq \varphi .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, by 5.17.4 we can find $C=C(\sup _ K f,K, X)>0$ so that $\eta \leq C$. Hence $\eta -C$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and hence \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By 18.28.9 , this implies that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f) \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ] + C.  \] The proof of the $\mathcal{I}$-part is similar, but we spell it out since this comparison will be used below. If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \leq 0$ and $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in ( 18.28.4 ). Hence \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+\inf _ K f\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a candidate in ( 18.28.4 ). Since $K$ is non-pluripolar and $f$ is bounded, the same compactness estimate gives a constant $C>0$, independent of $\eta $, such that $\eta \leq C$. Then $\eta -C\leq 0$ and $\eta -C\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. By corollary 16.8.16 , \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Taking the upper envelope over all such $\eta $ gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$ Corollary 18.28.17 . CE1417F951E3 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then A99869D43853 18.28.18 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Take any $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, then \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f).  \] Therefore, \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right).  \] So we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 18.28.18 ). For the reverse direction, take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Then $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 18.28.6 . Hence \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] By corollary 18.28.13 , the $\geq $ direction in ( 18.28.18 ) follows. $\square$

title: Definition 18.28.2
text: Definition 18.28.2 . 28F090ED5EFA Given a function $f\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, we introduce the relative $P$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 19BBFEFEB969 18.28.3 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Similarly, we define the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope of $\varphi $ (with respect to $K,f,\theta $) as 1F7034C27B5A 18.28.4 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Equation 18.28.3
text: 19BBFEFEB969 18.28.3 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Equation 18.28.4
text: 1F7034C27B5A 18.28.4 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Example 18.28.5
text: Example 18.28.5 . D0D0EA7C293D When $K=X$ and $f=0$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(0)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] When $K=X$, we have \[  P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta }[\varphi ](f).  \] These definitions reduce to the envelopes studied in section 16.1 . On the other hand, when $\varphi =V_{\theta }$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) & =P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\\ & =\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\left\{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \begin{array}{l} \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere} \end{array} \right\} . \end{aligned}  \] In an even more special case where $\varphi =V_{\theta }$ and $K=X$, we find that \[  P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](f)=\operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere}\Bigr \} .  \] This is nothing but $P_{\theta }(f)$ as we studied in definition 13.13.18 .

title: Proposition 18.28.6
text: Proposition 18.28.6 . C9561913A3E8 Let $f,g\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be functions and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Then we have the following: 33B49F7D21A7 We have \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] 6B1193ABBD59 assume that $f$ is bounded from above, then \[  \begin{aligned}  \left.P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\  \left. P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\right|_ K\leq &  f\textup{ quasi-everywhere}; \end{aligned}  \] 27E6FD2D7332 suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f);  \] B3B86BE1530D if $f\leq g$, then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](g),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(g);  \] 13DB8823929A for any $t \in (0,1)$, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f),\\  P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\geq &  tP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)+(1-t)P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f). \end{aligned}  \] Proof. 1 This follows from $\eta \preceq \varphi \Rightarrow \eta \preceq _{\mathcal I}\varphi $. 2 This follows from proposition 5.14.5 and 5.17.4 . 3 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 4 This follows by inclusion of the defining candidate sets. 5 If $\eta ,\eta '\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ are such that \[  \begin{split} & \eta |_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad \eta '|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\\ & \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta '\preceq \psi , \end{split}  \] then for $t\in (0,1)$, \[  \left.\left(t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\right)\right|_ K\leq f\textup{ quasi-everywhere},\quad t\eta +(1-t)\eta ' \preceq t\varphi +(1-t)\psi .  \] Therefore, \[  t\eta +(1-t)\eta '\leq P_{\theta ,K}\left[t\varphi +(1-t)\psi \right](f).  \] Since $\eta $ and $\eta '$ are arbitrary, the first inequality follows. The second follows from the same argument. $\square$

title: Lemma 18.28.7
text: Lemma 18.28.7 . 0F9B18404274 Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ is bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 96B9EFFFBDA7 18.28.8 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation} Proof. By our assumption, we can find $C>0$ so that $\varphi |_ K-C\leq f$. Then if $\eta $ is a candidate in ( 18.28.3 ), $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate, and $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Therefore, $\eta \lor (\varphi -C)$ is also a candidate for the right-hand side of ( 18.28.8 ). The equality ( 18.28.8 ) follows. $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.8
text: 96B9EFFFBDA7 18.28.8 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 18.28.9
text: Lemma 18.28.9 . A86A369D4CBF Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be bounded from below, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then 226F49B219B2 18.28.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. Both $\geq $ directions in ( 18.28.10 ) are trivial. Conversely, let $\eta $ be a candidate in ( 18.28.8 ). Let $S\subseteq X$ be a pluripolar set so that $\eta |_{K\setminus S}\leq f|_{K\setminus S}$. We now claim that we can choose $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ with $\chi |_ S\equiv -\infty $ and $\chi \leq \eta $. Assume this for the moment. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$, we have \[  (1-\delta )\eta |_ K+\delta \chi |_ K\leq f,\quad (1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi \preceq \varphi .  \] Hence, $(1-\delta )\eta +\delta \chi $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 18.28.10 ). Letting $\delta \to 0+$, we conclude that $\eta $ is dominated by the right-hand side of ( 18.28.10 ) and hence, ( 18.28.10 ) follows. It remains to construct $\chi $. Since $\varphi $ has positive mass, the class $\{ \theta \} $ is big. Fix a Kähler form $\omega _0$ on $X$ and choose $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\theta _{\rho }\geq 2\epsilon _0\omega _0$ for some $\epsilon _0>0$. By theorem 5.13.20 , there is a quasi-psh function $q$ such that $q|_ S\equiv -\infty $. Choose $A>0$ so that $A\omega _0+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. For $a>0$ small enough, $\rho +aq\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and still has pole $-\infty $ on $S$. Replacing $\rho $ by $\rho +aq$, we may therefore assume that $\rho |_ S\equiv -\infty $. Since $\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>0$, fixing such a $\rho $ and taking $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, we have \[  \int _ X \theta ^ n_{\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }}+\int _ X \theta _{\eta }^ n>\int _ X \theta _{V_{\theta }}^ n.  \] Thus, by proposition 16.3.25 and theorem 16.3.35 , we have \[  \Bigl (\epsilon \rho +(1-\epsilon )V_{\theta }\Bigr ) \land \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}.  \] It suffices to define this function as $\chi $. $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.10
text: 226F49B219B2 18.28.10 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=& \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split} \end{equation}

title: Corollary 18.28.11
text: Corollary 18.28.11 . 712499DFC37F Suppose that $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is bounded, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then there is a constant $C=C(\sup _ K f,K,X)>0$ such that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq C.  \] Proof. Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, 5.17.4 then gives a constant $C>0$, depending only on $\sup _ K f$, $K$ and $X$, such that every $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfying $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere satisfies $\eta \leq C$ on $X$. This applies to the candidates defining both envelopes. Hence both candidate families are locally uniformly bounded above, so their upper semicontinuous suprema are genuine $\theta $-psh functions. By proposition 18.28.6 2 , both envelopes are dominated by $f$ quasi-everywhere on $K$. Applying 5.17.4 once more gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq C,\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(f)\leq C.  \] $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.12
text: Proposition 18.28.12 . A1C36A6249C7 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Suppose that $\varphi \preceq _{P} \psi $. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Proof. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be such that $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere and $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then $\eta \preceq _ P \psi $, and thanks to corollary 16.8.30 for any $C>0$, we have $\eta \land (\psi +C)\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. But then $\eta \land (\psi +C)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f)$, and we find \[  \eta \land (\psi +C)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] By corollary 16.8.30 again, we get \[  \eta =P_{\theta }[\psi ](\eta )\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\psi ](f).  \] Our assertion follows now from 18.28.7 . $\square$

title: Corollary 18.28.13
text: Corollary 18.28.13 . 72097BEFEC59 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then \[  \begin{aligned}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} \\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{aligned}  \] Proof. We first apply proposition 18.28.12 , \[  \begin{split}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)= &  P_{\theta ,K}\left[P_{\theta }[\varphi ]\right](f)\\  =&  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta ): \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} . \end{split}  \] Next observe that by 18.28.7 , the latter can also be written as \[  \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}\Bigl \{  \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}: \eta |_ K \leq f \textup{ quasi-everywhere and } \eta \preceq _ P \varphi \Bigr \} .  \] Next we apply 18.28.9 ; the remaining statements follow. $\square$

title: Corollary 18.28.14
text: Corollary 18.28.14 . 96B842B9BF11 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow (-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function bounded from below and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ be $\mathcal{I}$-good. Then \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)=P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Proof. In fact, since $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, a potential $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \preceq _ P \varphi $ if and only if $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}} \varphi $. Therefore, our assertion follows from corollary 18.28.13 and ( 18.28.4 ). $\square$

title: Lemma 18.28.15
text: Lemma 18.28.15 . 18E5130ACB80 Let $f \colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. We have EC4A564BADAB 18.28.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation} Proof. We first prove the $P$-part of ( 18.28.16 ). If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta \leq 0$, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in the definition ( 18.28.3 ), and hence, \[  \eta +\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] It follows that \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]+\inf _ K f \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be such that \[  \eta |_ K\leq f,\quad \eta \preceq \varphi .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, by 5.17.4 we can find $C=C(\sup _ K f,K, X)>0$ so that $\eta \leq C$. Hence $\eta -C$ is a candidate in the definition of $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]$, and hence \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ].  \] By 18.28.9 , this implies that \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f) \leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ] + C.  \] The proof of the $\mathcal{I}$-part is similar, but we spell it out since this comparison will be used below. If $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfies $\eta \leq 0$ and $\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $, then $\eta +\inf _ K f$ is a candidate in ( 18.28.4 ). Hence \[  P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+\inf _ K f\leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f).  \] Conversely, let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a candidate in ( 18.28.4 ). Since $K$ is non-pluripolar and $f$ is bounded, the same compactness estimate gives a constant $C>0$, independent of $\eta $, such that $\eta \leq C$. Then $\eta -C\leq 0$ and $\eta -C\preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $. By corollary 16.8.16 , \[  \eta -C\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] Taking the upper envelope over all such $\eta $ gives \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\leq P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}+C.  \] This completes the proof. $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.16
text: EC4A564BADAB 18.28.16 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ],\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(f)\sim P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}. \end{equation}

title: Corollary 18.28.17
text: Corollary 18.28.17 . CE1417F951E3 Let $f\colon K\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ be a bounded function, and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then A99869D43853 18.28.18 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation} Proof. Take any $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere, then \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)\leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f).  \] Therefore, \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right).  \] So we conclude the $\leq $ direction in ( 18.28.18 ). For the reverse direction, take $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$ such that \[  \eta \preceq \varphi ,\quad \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \quad \textup{quasi-everywhere}.  \] Then $\eta |_ K\leq f$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 18.28.6 . Hence \[  \eta \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f).  \] By corollary 18.28.13 , the $\geq $ direction in ( 18.28.18 ) follows. $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.18
text: A99869D43853 18.28.18 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](f)=P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]\left( P_{\theta ,K}[V_{\theta }](f) \right). \end{equation}

title: 18.28.19 Partial equilibrium measures
text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, and $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ representing a pseudo-effective cohomology class. Definition 18.28.20 . E4ED4F8B05A8 A weighted subset of $X$ is a pair $(K,v)$ consisting of a closed non-pluripolar subset $K\subseteq X$ and a function $v\in C^0(K)$. The next result motivates our terminology to call the measures $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](f)}^ n$ the partial equilibrium measures of our context: Lemma 18.28.21 . earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad \eta _ j|_ K\leq v	extup{ for all }j\geq 1.  \] Note that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)\sim V_{	heta }$ by 18.28.15 . Take $C>0$ so that \[  \left.\left( P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v) ight)ight|_ K-C\leq v.  \] Then we may replace $\eta _ j$ by $\eta _ j\lor (P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)-C)$ and assume that $\eta _ j\sim V_{	heta }$ for each $j$. In particular, $\eta _ j$ is locally bounded on $X\setminus S$. For each $j\geq 1$, let $\gamma _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ be the balayage of $\eta _ j$ on $B$, defined in proposition 5.17.9 . Note that $(\gamma _ j)_ j$ is increasing due to proposition 5.14.22 . For the first equality in ( 18.28.22 ), we may assume that $B\Subset X\setminus (S \cup K)$. It suffices to show that $	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n$ does not charge $B$. Since $B$ lies outside $K$ by assumption, we also have $\gamma _ j|_ K=\eta _ j|_ K \leq v$ for all $j\geq 1$. In particular, $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. It follows that $\gamma _ j 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$ almost everywhere as well. Testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$ and using theorem 13.13.9 , we find that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$, as desired. We next prove the second equality in ( 18.28.22 ). The proof is essentially the same as that of 13.13.21 . It suffices to show that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge the set $K\cap \{ P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K<v\} $. Let $x\in (X\setminus S) \cap K$ be a point such that $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)(x)<v(x)-\epsilon $ for some $\epsilon >0$. We may assume that $x\in B$ and $B'$ is small enough, so that B2B18BBFA88D $P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_{\overline{B'}}<v(x)-\epsilon $. D0D5ED334E0E $v|_{\overline{B'}\cap K}>v(x)-\epsilon $. By 1 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{\partial B}\leq v(x)-\epsilon $, hence by proposition 5.14.22 , $\gamma _ j|_ B\leq v(x)-\epsilon $. By 2 , we have $\gamma _ j|_{B\cap K}\leq v|_{B\cap K}$. On the other hand, $\gamma _ j|_{K\setminus B}=\eta _{j}|_{K\setminus B}\leq v|_{K\setminus B}$. Therefore, $\gamma _ j|_ K\leq v$. It follows again that $\gamma _ j\leq P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Therefore, we conclude as in the previous paragraph that $\gamma _ j
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)$. Thus, testing against non-negative continuous functions supported in $B$, we conclude that $	heta ^ n_{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}$ does not charge $B$ again by theorem 13.13.9 . Step 2 . We handle the general case. By corollary 18.28.17 , \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,X}[\varphi ]\left(P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight).  \] Now corollary 16.3.14 gives \[   egin{aligned}  	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) = P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)ight\} } 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n \  \leq &  \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K=P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)|_ K=vight\} }\, 	heta _{P_{	heta ,K}[V_{	heta }](v)}^ n, \end{aligned}  \] where in the second inequality we have used Step 1. Hence ( 18.28.23 ) follows, and a fortiori ( 18.28.22 ) follows as well. $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.27
text: Proposition 18.28.27 . 765C3766A729 Let $v,f \in C^0(K)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then $\mathbb {R}\ni t \mapsto \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf)$ is differentiable and 0B2DE1BB9170 18.28.28 \begin{equation}  \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tf) = \int _ K f\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)} \end{equation} for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$. Proof. We may assume that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-model by replacing $\varphi $ by $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$. Note that it suffices to prove ( 18.28.28 ) at $t=0$, which is equivalent to 94F4F91642C8 18.28.29 \begin{equation}  \lim _{t\to 0}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} It suffices to prove the right derivative at $0$ for an arbitrary $f$; applying the same argument to $-f$ then gives the left derivative. In other words, we need to prove that 8353FF09478E 18.28.30 \begin{equation}  \lim _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}=\int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}. \end{equation} We first reduce the proof of ( 18.28.30 ) to the case $f\leq 0$. Assume that this case is known. Choose $A\in \mathbb R$ such that $f-A\leq 0$ on $K$. Since for any $t>0$, \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}\Bigl ( v+t(f-A) \Bigr )= P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf)-tA,  \] then we have \[  \int _ K f\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}=\int _ K (f-A)\,  \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}+A\int _ X \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] By ( 16.5.13 ), for any $t>0$, \[  E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\Bigl (P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}\left(v+t(f-A)\right)\Bigr )=E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-tA\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n.  \] So the limit in ( 18.28.30 ) exists and is equal to the left-hand side of ( 18.28.30 ) with $f-A$ in place of $f$ plus $A\int _ X\theta _{\varphi }^ n$. So ( 18.28.30 ) for $f-A$ implies the desired formula for $f$ in view of 18.28.15 and the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 . Hence we may assume that $f\leq 0$. Fix $t>0$. Set \[  \eta _ t\coloneqq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v+tf),\quad \eta _0\coloneqq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v).  \] By the comparison principle ( 16.5.6 ) and proposition 16.5.30 , we find \[  \begin{aligned}  E_{\theta }^{\varphi }(\eta _ t)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }(\eta _0) ={}& \frac{1}{n+1}\sum _{i=0}^ n\int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\,  \theta _{\eta _ t}^ i\wedge \theta _{\eta _0}^{n-i}\\  \leq {}&  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] By 18.28.21 and corollary 18.28.14 , the measure $\theta _{\eta _0}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, and the measure $\theta _{\eta _ t}^ n$ is carried by $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $. On $K\cap \{ \eta _0=v\} $, we have $\eta _ t\leq v+tf=\eta _0+tf$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\leq tf.  \] On $K\cap \{ \eta _ t=v+tf\} $, we have $\eta _0\leq v$, hence \[  \eta _ t-\eta _0\geq tf.  \] It follows that \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n \leq t\int _ K f\, \theta _{\eta _0}^ n  \] and \[  \int _ X(\eta _ t-\eta _0)\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n \geq t\int _ K f\, \theta _{\eta _ t}^ n.  \] Thus, letting $t\to 0+$, we get the inequality \[  \varlimsup _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}\leq \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Similarly, for $t>0$, we have \[  \begin{aligned} & E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\\  \geq &  \int _ X \left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)-P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n\\  \geq &  t\int _ K f\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n. \end{aligned}  \] Letting $t\to 0+$, we find \[  \varliminf _{t\to 0+}\frac{E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)\right)-E_{\theta }^{\varphi }\left(P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)}{t}\geq \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}.  \] Here we used the following elementary continuity consequence: \[  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)-t\| f\| _{C^0(K)} \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) \leq P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)  \] for $t>0$, and hence $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf) \nearrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$ almost everywhere when $t\to 0+$. Next we claim that \[  \int _ K f\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}\leq \lim _{t\to 0+} \int _ K f\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v+tf)}^ n.  \] Choose a continuous extension $\tilde f\in C^0(X)$ of $f$. Since 18.28.21 , corollary 18.28.14 show that all the measures appearing here are carried by $K$, the integrals over $K$ against $f$ are the same as the integrals over $X$ against $\tilde f$. Thus corollary 13.13.12 applies. We conclude ( 18.28.29 ). $\square$
