title: Lemma 18.28.31
text:
Lemma 18.28.31 . D21332713DB8 Assume that $\{ 	heta \} $ represents a big cohomology class. Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ and a weighted subset $(K,v)$ of $X$. There exists a uniformly bounded increasing sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ and a uniformly bounded decreasing sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$, such that 32CDA8E3EB57 18.28.32  egin{equation}  \sup _ X |v_ j^-|\leq C,\quad \sup _ X |v_ j^+|\leq C \end{equation} for some constant $C$ depending only on $\| v\| _{C^0(K)}$, $X$, $K$ and $	heta +\omega $. Furthermore, for any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and any $\delta \in [0,1]$ we have the following: 9C89F797B0BF We have \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v_ j^+) \searrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v),  \] and \[  P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j) 
earrow P_{	heta +\delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)  \] almost everywhere. 4E87F51F9E7D Suppose in addition that $\varphi $ is $\mathcal{I}$-good, then \[  \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^-)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v),\quad \lim _{j	o \infty }\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,X}^{\varphi }(v_ j^+)=\mathcal{E}_{	heta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Step 1 . First we construct $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Let \[  C_{K,v} \coloneqq \sup \left\{ \sup _ X \eta : \eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\omega ), \eta |_ K \leq vight\} .  \] Since $K$ is non-pluripolar, we have $C_{K,v} \in \mathbb {R}$ by 5.17.4 . Set \[  M_{K,v}\coloneqq \max \{ C_{K,v}+1,\sup _ K v\} .  \] Now define $\widetilde v \colon X 	o \mathbb {R}$ as \[  \widetilde{v}(x)=\left\{   egin{aligned}  v(x),& \quad x\in K;\  M_{K,v},& \quad x\in X\setminus K. \end{aligned} ight.  \] Since $M_{K,v}\geq \sup _ K v$, the function $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous. Therefore there exists an increasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^-_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^-_ j 
earrow \widetilde v$ and \[  \| v_ j^-\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| 	ilde{v}\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] The right-hand side can clearly be bounded by a constant as in ( 18.28.32 ). Step 2 . We construct $(v_ j^+)_ j$. Since \[  h \coloneqq P_{	heta + \omega ,K}[V_{	heta +\omega }](v) \lor \left(\inf _ K v -1ight)  \] is usc, there exists a decreasing and uniformly bounded sequence $(v^+_ j)_ j$ in $C^\infty (X)$ such that $v^+_ j \searrow h$. We may guarantee that \[  \| v^+_ j\| _{C^0(X)}\leq \| h\| _{L^{\infty }(X)}+1.  \] Note that $\inf _ K v-1\leq h\leq C_{K,v} \lor (\inf _ K v-1)$. So ( 18.28.32 ) is satisfied. Step 3 . We finish the proof. Fix $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\delta \in [0,1]$. Note that 2 follows from corollary 18.28.14 , 18.28.15 , proposition 16.5.37 and 1 . Let us prove 1 . Step 3.1 . We prove 1 for $(v^-_ j)_ j$. Observe that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)$ is increasing in $j\geq 1$, and \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)\leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] We claim that A58ACF533BAE 18.28.33  egin{equation}  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight) 
earrow P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)\quad 	extup{a.e.}. \end{equation} Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )$ be a potential such that $\eta \preceq \varphi $ and $\eta |_ K\leq v$. Take some $\epsilon >0$. Then, since $\eta $ is upper semicontinuous, $\widetilde v$ is lower semicontinuous and $\eta < \epsilon +\widetilde v$, compactness gives $j_0>0$ such that $\eta < \epsilon + v^-_ j$ for $j \geq j_0$. Hence, \[  \eta \leq \epsilon +P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^-_ j)  \] for $j\geq j_0$. Therefore, \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight)+\epsilon .  \] Letting $\epsilon 	o 0+$, we find \[  \eta \leq \operatorname *{sup}_{j\geq 1}{}\! {}^{*} P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^-_ jight).  \] Since $\eta $ is arbitrary, ( 18.28.33 ) follows. Step 3.2 . We prove 1 for $(v^+_ j)_ j$. Note that $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v^+_ j)$ is decreasing in $j$, and 11BA40C76F9B 18.28.34  egin{equation}  \chi \coloneqq \lim _{j	o \infty } P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_ jight) \geq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} In particular, $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta +\delta \omega )_{>0}$, since $P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v)$ has the same singularity types as $P_{	heta + \delta \omega }[\varphi ]$ by 18.28.15 . Observe that \[  P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v_ j^+ight)\leq v_ j^+  \] for all $j\geq 1$, since $v_ j^+$ is continuous. Thus, $\chi \leq h$. On the other hand, $h|_ K\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. So in particular, $\chi |_{K}\leq v$ quasi-everywhere. On the other hand, \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,X}[\varphi ]\left(v^+_1ight)\sim _ P \varphi  \] by 18.28.15 . Hence, by corollary 18.28.13 , \[  \chi \leq P_{	heta + \delta \omega ,K}[\varphi ](v).  \] Therefore, ( 18.28.34 ) is an equality. $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.35
text:
Proposition 18.28.35 . 9724C0B32032 Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ be a sequence in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )_{>0}$. Then the following hold: BE5DB43FE077 If $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing, and $\varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $, then 1BDE5E6D4627 18.28.36  egin{equation}  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) \searrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} E712A3A2D87D If $\varphi _ j 
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere then \[  P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)	extup{ a.e.},\quad P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) 
earrow P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) 	extup{ a.e.}.  \] Proof. We only give the proof for the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelopes; the proof for the relative $P$-envelopes is identical, replacing $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]_{\mathcal{I}}$ by $P_{	heta }[ ullet ]$ and using corollary 18.28.13 for the final candidate condition. Set \[  \eta _ j\coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad \eta \coloneqq P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] By 18.28.15 , $d_ S(\eta _ j,P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ and $d_ S(\eta ,P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})=0$ for all $j$. Moreover, theorem 16.9.49 gives \[  P_{	heta }[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{	heta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}  \] in case 1 , and the same convergence holds in case 2 by corollary 16.9.12 and theorem 16.9.49 . Consequently, $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta $ in both cases. Assume first that $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ is decreasing. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is decreasing and $\eta _ j\geq \eta $. Let $\eta _\infty \coloneqq \inf _ j \eta _ j$. The Monge–Ampère masses of $\eta _ j$ converge to the mass of $\eta $, by the preceding $d_ S$-convergence and theorem 16.9.30 . Since $\eta _ j\geq \eta _\infty \geq \eta $, the monotonicity theorem theorem 13.13.11 gives \[  \int _ X	heta _{\eta _\infty }^ n=\int _ X	heta _\eta ^ n.  \] Hence $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}\eta _\infty $ by corollary 16.9.14 . The uniqueness of the $d_ S$-limit gives $d_ S(\eta _\infty ,\eta )=0$. Since $\eta _\infty \geq \eta $, proposition 16.9.6 implies $\eta _\infty \sim _ P \eta $. In particular, $\eta _\infty \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 16.8.14 . The condition $\eta _\infty \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere is inherited from the $\eta _ j$'s, so $\eta _\infty $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. Thus $\eta _\infty \leq \eta $, and the reverse inequality was already observed. This proves the $\mathcal{I}$-part of 1 . Assume next that $\varphi _ j
earrow \varphi $ almost everywhere. Then $(\eta _ j)_ j$ is increasing and $\eta _ j\leq \eta $. Put $	ilde\eta \coloneqq \operatorname *{sup}_{}{}\! {}^{*}_ j \eta _ j$. By corollary 18.28.11 and corollary 16.9.12 , we have $\eta _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}	ilde\eta $. The $d_ S$-convergence above therefore gives $d_ S(	ilde\eta ,\eta )=0$, hence $	ilde\eta \sim _ P \eta $ by proposition 16.9.6 . In particular, $	ilde\eta \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\varphi $ by corollary 16.8.14 . Also $	ilde\eta \leq v$ on $K$ quasi-everywhere by proposition 5.14.5 . Hence $	ilde\eta $ is a candidate for $P_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$, so $	ilde\eta \leq \eta $. Since $\eta _ j\leq \eta $ for all $j$, this proves $\eta _ j
earrow \eta $ almost everywhere. $\square$

text: 1BDE5E6D4627 18.28.36 \begin{equation}  P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v) \searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v),\quad P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j](v) \searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation}

title: 18.28.37 Quantization of partial equilibrium measures
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $L$ be a pseudo-effective line bundle on $X$, and let $h$ be a Hermitian metric on $L$. Set $\theta =c_1(L,h)$. Let $(T,h_ T)$ be a Hermitian line bundle on $X$.

title: 18.28.38 Bernstein–Markov measures
text: Let $K\subseteq X$ be a closed non-pluripolar subset, and $v\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be a measurable function. Definition 18.28.39 . E365D575C322 Let $\mu $ be a Borel probability measure on $K$. We introduce the following functions on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), with values possibly equal to $\infty $: 46ED22785DA5 18.28.40 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \coloneqq &  \left(\int _ K h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \mathrm{e}^{-kv} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2},\\  N^ k_{v,K}(s) \coloneqq &  \sup _{K\setminus \{ v=-\infty \} } \left( h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Observe that if $\mu $ puts no mass on $\{ v=-\infty \} $ then we always have F1111E54880E 18.28.41 \begin{equation}  N^ k_{v,\mu }(s)\leq N^ k_{v,K}(s). \end{equation} We start with the following elementary observation: Lemma 18.28.42 . E97173FEFAFD Let $v_1,v_2\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be two measurable functions such that 7AB5A208122C $v_1\leq v_2$; 60A51A0A77E1 $\{ v_1=-\infty \} =\{ v_2=-\infty \} $. Then for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), we have \[  N_{v_1,K}^ k(s)\geq N_{v_2,K}^ k(s).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from the definition ( 18.28.40 ). $\square$ Definition 18.28.43 . 48A0DBADBA86 Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. A Borel probability measure $\mu $ on $K$ is Bernstein–Markov with respect to $(K,v)$ if for each $\epsilon >0$, there is a constant $C_\epsilon >0$ such that FE92486453EB 18.28.44 \begin{equation}  N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k} N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \end{equation} for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ and any $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We write $\mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ for the set of Bernstein–Markov measures with respect to $(K,v)$. As pointed out in [ BBWN11 ] , any volume form on $X$ is Bernstein–Markov with respect to $(X,v)$, with $v \in C^\infty (X)$. Proposition 18.28.45 . A86573651304 Assume that $(K,v)$ is a weighted subset of $X$. Then A757D6ACA763 $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. 6EBD970292B6 For any $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. Proof. 1 As $v$ is bounded, $N^ k_{v,K}$ is clearly finite on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. In order to show that it is a norm, it suffices to show that for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$, $N^ k_{v,K}(s)=0$ implies that $s=0$. In fact, we have $s|_ K=0$, hence $s=0$ by the connectedness of $X$ and the assumption that $K$ is non-pluripolar. 2 As $v$ is bounded, clearly $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is finite and satisfies the triangle inequality. Non-degeneracy follows from the fact that $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm and ( 18.28.44 ). $\square$

We introduce the following functions on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), with values possibly equal to $\infty $: 46ED22785DA5 18.28.40 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \coloneqq &  \left(\int _ K h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \mathrm{e}^{-kv} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2},\\  N^ k_{v,K}(s) \coloneqq &  \sup _{K\setminus \{ v=-\infty \} } \left( h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

title: Equation 18.28.41

title: Lemma 18.28.42
text: Lemma 18.28.42 . E97173FEFAFD Let $v_1,v_2\colon K\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty )$ be two measurable functions such that 7AB5A208122C $v_1\leq v_2$; 60A51A0A77E1 $\{ v_1=-\infty \} =\{ v_2=-\infty \} $. Then for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$ ($k\geq 1$), we have \[  N_{v_1,K}^ k(s)\geq N_{v_2,K}^ k(s).  \] Proof. This follows immediately from the definition ( 18.28.40 ). $\square$

text: Definition 18.28.43 . 48A0DBADBA86 Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. A Borel probability measure $\mu $ on $K$ is Bernstein–Markov with respect to $(K,v)$ if for each $\epsilon >0$, there is a constant $C_\epsilon >0$ such that FE92486453EB 18.28.44 \begin{equation}  N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k} N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \end{equation} for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T)$ and any $k\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$. We write $\mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ for the set of Bernstein–Markov measures with respect to $(K,v)$.

title: Proposition 18.28.45
text: Proposition 18.28.45 . A86573651304 Assume that $(K,v)$ is a weighted subset of $X$. Then A757D6ACA763 $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. 6EBD970292B6 For any $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is a norm on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. Proof. 1 As $v$ is bounded, $N^ k_{v,K}$ is clearly finite on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$. In order to show that it is a norm, it suffices to show that for any $s\in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k\otimes T)$, $N^ k_{v,K}(s)=0$ implies that $s=0$. In fact, we have $s|_ K=0$, hence $s=0$ by the connectedness of $X$ and the assumption that $K$ is non-pluripolar. 2 As $v$ is bounded, clearly $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is finite and satisfies the triangle inequality. Non-degeneracy follows from the fact that $N^ k_{v,K}$ is a norm and ( 18.28.44 ). $\square$

title: Definition 18.28.46
text: Definition 18.28.46 . C3C647253911 For any $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$, we introduce the partial Bergman kernels of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) as follows: For any $k\geq 1$, we introduce 14.50 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }(x) \coloneqq \sup \left\{ h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv}(x):s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right),\right.\\  \left. N^ k_{v,\mu }(s) \leq 1 \right\} ,\quad x\in K. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We extend $B^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu }$ to the whole $X$ by setting it to be $0$ outside $K$. The partial Bergman measures of $\varphi $ (with respect to $(K,v)$) are defined as 14.53 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \coloneqq \frac{n!}{k^ n} B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \, \mathrm{d}\mu \end{equation} for each $k\geq 1$.

title: Remark 18.28.47
text: Remark 18.28.47 . 129D3B333F18 Recall that in the definition of $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$, the singular metric $\varphi $ only appears through the conditions $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The pointwise norm used to define $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$ and $N^ k_{v,\mu }$ is defined via $v$ not $\varphi $. This leads to the following seemingly paradoxical consequence, if $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ and $\varphi \preceq _{\mathcal{I}}\psi $, then \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }\leq \beta ^ k_{v,\psi ,\mu }\quad \forall \, k\geq 1.  \] We shall apply this consequence without further mention in the sequel.

title: Equation 18.28.48
text: 889A68CCEC83 18.28.48 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }=\operatorname{vol}\left(\theta _{\varphi }\right)=\int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \end{equation}

title: Theorem 18.28.49
text: Theorem 18.28.49 . EA3E101DCA5E Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )_{>0}$. Then A6F9F2DF4A0D 18.28.50 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof of theorem 18.28.49 . By 18.28.15 and proposition 16.6.11 , the three potentials below have the same multiplier ideals. Hence \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(kP_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}})\right)\\ & = \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I\left(kP_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\right)\right). \end{aligned}  \] This allows us to replace $\varphi $ with $P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)$. By 13.13.47 , there exists a sequence $(\varphi _ j)_ j$ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ such that $\varphi _ j\nearrow \varphi $ a.e. and $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for each $j\geq 1$. This gives \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu } \leq \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$. Then by proposition 18.28.74 , \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq \tau .  \] By proposition 18.28.35 and corollary 13.13.12 , we have \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n.  \] Hence, 8FD19D2B07C7 18.28.78 \begin{equation}  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K} [\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\leq \tau . \end{equation} A comparison of total masses using ( 18.28.48 ) gives that equality holds in ( 18.28.78 ). As $\tau $ is arbitrary, we obtain ( 18.28.50 ). $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.50
text: A6F9F2DF4A0D 18.28.50 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation}

title: Proposition 18.28.51
text: Proposition 18.28.51 . 4C368CFA09EB Assume here that $K=X$. Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. If $v \in C^\infty (X)$, then 4DF720497AC6 18.28.52 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=\theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof. The equality part in ( 18.28.52 ) follows from corollary 18.28.14 . It remains to prove the weak convergence. Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n})_ k$. In view of ( 18.28.48 ), it suffices to show that 14347C41585E 18.28.53 \begin{equation}  \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n. \end{equation} We can obtain an upper bound of $\tau $ via the observation: \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq \beta ^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n}.  \] After replacing $\varphi $ by $V_{\theta }$, the corresponding problem is handled by [ Theorem 1.2 , Ber11 ] , giving us \[  \beta ^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n} \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)}^ n=\mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n \quad \textup{as }k\to \infty ,  \] where the last identity is due to proposition 16.3.41 . We obtain that 1B7624ED3973 18.28.54 \begin{equation}  \tau \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ v = P_{\theta ,X}[V_{\theta }](v)\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n. \end{equation} Now observe that it suffices to show that C700200CB6BE 18.28.55 \begin{equation}  \tau \left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation} Assuming this, then ( 18.28.54 ) further gives \[  \tau \leq \mathds {1}_{\left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)= v\right\} }\, \theta _ v^ n= \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)}^ n,  \] where the equality follows from proposition 16.3.41 , and ( 18.28.53 ) follows. It now remains to argue ( 18.28.55 ). Fix a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$. Observe that \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) \sim \varphi  \] for all $\epsilon \geq 0$ by 18.28.15 and proposition 16.6.22 . The family $P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)$ is decreasing as $\epsilon \to 0+$. Let \[  \chi \coloneqq \inf _{\epsilon >0}P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Then $\chi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ since $\chi \geq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v)$. Moreover $\chi \leq v$ and $\chi \preceq \varphi $. Hence \[  \chi \leq P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] Thus, equality holds, and \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)\searrow P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v).  \] In other words, \[  \left\{ P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =\bigcup _{\epsilon \in \mathbb {Q}_{>0}}\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} .  \] So in order to show ( 18.28.55 ), we may fix $\epsilon >0$ and argue that CE5263973CB7 18.28.56 \begin{equation}  \tau \left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} =0. \end{equation} Let $k\geq 1$, and $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal I(k\varphi ))$ be a section such that $N^ k_{v,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1$. Then by [ Lemma 4.1 , Ber11 ] , there exists $C>0$ such that \[  h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s)\mathrm{e}^{-kv} \leq B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq B^ k_{v,V_{\theta },\omega ^ n} \leq k^ n C.  \] This implies that \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \leq v + \frac{\log C }{k} + n \frac{\log k}{ k }.  \] We define $\varphi _ k$ as in proposition 5.20.17 . Take $\alpha _ k\nearrow 1$ as in proposition 5.20.17 . After adding a constant to $\varphi $, we may assume that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $X$. After replacing $\alpha _ k$ by a subsequence, we also have $\alpha _ k\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon \omega )$ for all $k>0$, and $\alpha _ k\varphi \searrow \varphi $. Then \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)\preceq \varphi _ k\preceq \alpha _ k\varphi .  \] We notice that $\frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X, \theta + \epsilon \omega )$ for all $k \geq k_0(\epsilon )$. Indeed, \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k\otimes h_ T(s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}\left(X,\theta + k^{-1} c_1(T,h_ T)\right)  \] by proposition 5.20.4 . In particular, \[  \frac{1}{k}\log h^ k \otimes h_ T(s,s)-\frac{\log C}{k}-n\frac{\log k}{k}\leq P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v).  \] Now taking supremum over all candidates $s$, we obtain that 725395815923 18.28.57 \begin{equation}  B^ k_{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n} \leq C k^ n \mathrm{e}^{k \left(P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v)-v\right)},\quad k \geq k_0. \end{equation} Now we prove ( 18.28.56 ). First observe that $\alpha _ k\varphi \xrightarrow {d_ S}\varphi $ by 16.9.25 . Thus, by proposition 18.28.35 , \[  P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) \searrow P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v)  \] and we get that \[  \bigcup _{k=1}^{\infty }\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ k \varphi ](v) < v\right\} =\left\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\varphi ](v) < v\right\} .  \] It suffices to show that $\tau $ does not put mass on the set $\{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v\} $ for each fixed $m$. Fix a positive rational $\delta >0$, it suffices to show that $\tau $ puts no mass on $F\coloneqq \{ P_{\theta +\epsilon \omega ,X}[\alpha _ m \varphi ](v) < v-\delta \} $. Note that $F$ is open, and ( 18.28.57 ) gives $\beta ^\ell _{v,\varphi ,\omega ^ n}(F)\to 0$. Therefore, $\tau $ puts no mass on $F$ as well, proving ( 18.28.56 ). $\square$

title: Definition 18.28.58
text: Definition 18.28.58 . A0F71B40AAE1 Take $k\geq 1$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, let $\operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$ be the space of norms on the vector space $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi } \colon \operatorname{Norm}\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )) \to \mathbb R$ be the partial Donaldson functional : 14.62 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(H) = \frac{n!}{k^{n+1}} \log \frac{\operatorname{vol}\{ s \in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) : H(s) \leq 1\} }{\operatorname{vol}\left\{ s\in \mathrm{H}^0\left(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right) : N^ k_{0,\omega ^ n}(s) \leq 1\right\} }, \end{equation} where $\operatorname{vol}$ is a Lebesgue measure on $\mathrm{H}^0(X,L^ k \otimes T \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$. The normalization does not matter.

title: Proposition 18.28.59
text: Proposition 18.28.59 . F547344ACE10 Let $w,w' \in C^0(X)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then D29819040D75 18.28.60 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) \right)= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation} In particular, 04790CD84F49 18.28.61 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 18.28.45 , for any $k\geq 1$, $N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}$ and $N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 18.28.60 ) make sense. We first assume that $w,w'\in C^\infty (X)$. To start, we make the following observation: \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})& = \int _0^1 \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\omega ^ n})\, \mathrm{d}t\\ &  = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, \beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\,  \mathrm{d}t. \end{aligned}  \] The second equality follows from differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}$: \[  \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathcal L_{k,\varphi } \left(N^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\omega ^ n}\right)=\int _ X (w-w')\, \beta ^ k_{w'+t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}.  \] By proposition 18.28.51 , we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\int _ X (w-w') \, \beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}=\int _ X (w-w')\, \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n.  \] By theorem 18.1.46 , we have \[  \bigl |\int _ X (w-w')\beta ^ k_{w' + t(w-w'),\varphi ,\omega ^ n}\bigr | \leq C \sup _ X |w - w'|.  \] Hence, by the dominated convergence theorem we obtain that \[  \begin{aligned}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n})\right) & = \int _0^1 \int _ X (w-w') \, \theta _{P_{\theta ,X}[\varphi ](w' + t(w-w'))}^ n \, \mathrm{d}t\\ &  = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'), \end{aligned}  \] where in the last line we have used proposition 18.28.27 . This proves ( 18.28.60 ) for smooth weights. For general $w,w'\in C^0(X)$, choose smooth functions $w_ j,w'_ j$ converging uniformly to $w,w'$, respectively. If $\| w_ j-w\| _{C^0}\leq \delta _ j$, then \[  \mathrm{e}^{-k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}\leq N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n}\leq \mathrm{e}^{k\delta _ j/2}N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n},  \] and hence \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w_ j,\omega ^ n})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})\right| \leq \frac{n!}{k^ n}h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)\delta _ j.  \] The same estimate holds for $w'_ j$ and $w'$. Moreover, proposition 18.28.27 shows that the energy side is Lipschitz with respect to the uniform norm of the weight. Letting first $k\to \infty $ in the smooth case, and then $j\to \infty $, proves ( 18.28.60 ) for continuous weights. Equation ( 18.28.61 ) again follows by taking $w'=0$. $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.60
text: D29819040D75 18.28.60 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w',\omega ^ n}) \right)= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w'). \end{equation}

title: Equation 18.28.61
text: 04790CD84F49 18.28.61 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,\omega ^ n})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation}

title: Lemma 18.28.62
text: Lemma 18.28.62 . 922E6C36BCC8 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$. Let $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then C3210B1F6DE6 18.28.63 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\big ) = 0\, . \end{equation} Proof. By ( 18.28.41 ) and ( 18.28.44 ), for every $\epsilon >0$ and all $k\geq 1$, \[  N^ k_{v,\mu }\leq N^ k_{v,K}\leq C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}N^ k_{v,\mu }.  \] The corresponding unit balls therefore satisfy inclusions with radii differing by at most the factor $C_\epsilon \mathrm{e}^{\epsilon k}$. Taking logarithmic volumes and multiplying by $n!k^{-n-1}$ gives \[  \left|\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\right| \leq \frac{2n!}{k^{n+1}} h^0\left(X,L^ k\otimes T\otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )\right)(\log C_\epsilon +\epsilon k).  \] The right-hand side has limsup at most $2\epsilon \operatorname{vol}(\theta _\varphi )$ by theorem 18.1.46 . Letting $\epsilon \to 0+$ proves ( 18.28.63 ). $\square$

title: Equation 18.28.63
text: C3210B1F6DE6 18.28.63 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })\big ) = 0\, . \end{equation}

title: Corollary 18.28.64
text: Corollary 18.28.64 . 4CE59F3C4805 Let $w \in C^0(X)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _\varphi $ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w).  \] Proof. This follows from 18.28.62 and proposition 18.28.59 : indeed $\omega ^ n \in \mathrm{BM}(X,0)$, hence $\omega ^ n\in \mathrm{BM}(X,w)$ as $w$ is bounded. $\square$

title: Lemma 18.28.65
text:
Lemma 18.28.65 . 5C6401E18EB3 Let $v\in C^0(K)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, and $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$. Assume that $\eta \preceq \varphi $. Then 2DBAE7A20C99 18.28.66  egin{equation}  \sup _ K (\eta -v) = \sup _{\{ \eta 
eq -\infty \} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)=\sup _{\left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty ight\} } \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight). \end{equation} Proof. We prove the first equality first. We write $S=\{ \eta =-\infty \} $. By definition, $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)|_ K\leq v$, so \[  \left.\left(\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight)ight|_{K\setminus S}\geq \eta |_{K\setminus S}-v|_{K\setminus S}\, .  \] This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \leq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight).  \] Conversely, observe that $\sup _ K(\eta -v)>-\infty $ as $K$ is non-pluripolar. It follows that $\eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)$ is a candidate in the definition of $P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)$. Hence, 3504DA07F50F 18.28.67  egin{equation}  \eta -\sup _ K (\eta -v)\leq P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v). \end{equation} This implies that \[  \sup _ K (\eta -v) \geq \sup _{X\setminus S} \left(\eta - P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)ight),  \] finishing the proof of the first identity in ( 18.28.66 ). In order to prove the latter identity, observe that \[  \left\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v) =-\infty ight\}  \subseteq S  \] as a consequence of ( 18.28.67 ). On $\{ P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)
eq -\infty \} \cap S$, we have $\eta -P'_{	heta ,K}[\varphi ](v)=-\infty $. Hence the last equality of ( 18.28.66 ) also follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.68
text: Proposition 18.28.68 . F431300C59C4 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$, $(K',v')$ be two weighted subsets of $X$. Then FFF9581DFDD2 18.28.69 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v',K'}) \right) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v)-\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K'}^{\varphi }(v'). \end{equation} In particular, 5AAAC502B9E5 18.28.70 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty }\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})=\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v). \end{equation} Proof. First observe that by proposition 18.28.45 , for any $k>0$, $N^ k_{v,K}$ and $N^ k_{v',K'}$ are both norms, hence the expressions inside the limit in ( 18.28.69 ) make sense. Moreover, ( 18.28.70 ) is just a special case of ( 18.28.69 ) for $K'=X$ and $v'= 0$. To prove ( 18.28.69 ) it is enough to show that for any fixed $w \in C^\infty (X)$ we have AC1B69834497 18.28.71 \begin{equation}  \lim _{k\to \infty } \big ( \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K}) - \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X}) \big ) = \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)\, . \end{equation} For $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ small enough, $\theta _{(1-\epsilon )\varphi }$ is still a Kähler current. Let us fix such $\epsilon $, along with an arbitrary $\epsilon ' \in (0,1)$. Let $(v^-_{j})_ j$ and $(v^+_{j})_ j$ be the sequences of smooth functions constructed in 18.28.31 for the data $(K,v)$. By proposition 5.20.17 there exists $k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ') \in \mathbb N$ such that \[  \frac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \preceq (1-\epsilon )\varphi ,  \] and $\frac{1}{k} \log h^ k \otimes h_ T (s,s) \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta + \epsilon '\omega )$ for any $s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T\otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi ))$, as long as $k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ')$. In particular, 18.28.65 gives that \[  \begin{aligned}  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v,K}(s),\\  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s),\\  N^ k_{P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),X}(s)=&  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s). \end{aligned}  \] As \[  P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^-) \leq P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,K}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v) \leq P'_{\theta + \epsilon '\omega ,X}[(1-\epsilon )\varphi ](v_{j}^+),  \] where the second inequality follows from 18.28.31 and the fact that $P'=P$ for the global continuous obstacles $v_ j^\pm $. By 18.28.42 we have \[  N^ k_{v^+_{j},X}(s) \leq N^ k_{v,K}(s) \leq N^ k_{v_{j}^-,X}(s), \quad s \in \mathrm{H}^0(X,T \otimes L^ k \otimes \mathcal{I}(k\varphi )), k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] Composing with $\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }$ we arrive at \[  \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})\leq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})\, , \quad k \geq k_0(\epsilon ,\epsilon ').  \] For any $j>0$, by corollary 18.28.64 we get \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^-_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w)=&  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^-_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  \leq &  \lim _{k\to \infty } \left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v^+_{j},X})-\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\  =&  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(v^+_{j}) - \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{aligned}  \] Using 18.28.31 , we can let $j \to \infty $ to arrive at \[  \begin{split}  \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w) & \leq \varliminf _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\ & \leq \varlimsup _{k\to \infty }\left(\mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,K})- \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{w,X})\right)\\ &  \leq \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v) -\mathcal{E}_{\theta ,X}^{\varphi }(w). \end{split}  \] Hence, ( 18.28.71 ) follows. $\square$

title: Corollary 18.28.72
text: Corollary 18.28.72 . B1F17F151050 Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v,\mu })= \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v).  \] Proof. Our claim follows from proposition 18.28.68 and 18.28.62 . $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.73
text: Proposition 18.28.73 . AC691D964EDB Let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be a potential with analytic singularities such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Then \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi , \mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n=\theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n\quad \textup{as }k\to \infty .  \] Proof. For $w\in C^0(X)$, let $f_ k,g\colon \mathbb {R}\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ ($k\geq 1$) be defined as \[  f_ k(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{L}_{k,\varphi }(N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }),\quad g(t)\coloneqq \mathcal{E}_{\theta ,K}^{\varphi }(v+tw).  \] By corollary 18.28.72 , for all $t\in \mathbb {R}$, we have \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } f_ k(t)= g(t).  \] Here we use that $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v+tw)$ for all fixed $t$, which follows from $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$ and the boundedness of $tw$ on $K$. Note that $f_ k$ is concave by Hölder's inequality. For each $k$, the function $f_ k$ is differentiable and \[  f_ k'(0)=\int _ X w\, \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }.  \] This follows by differentiating the Gram matrix of the Hilbert norm $N^ k_{v+tw,\mu }$. The function $g$ is differentiable at $0$ by proposition 18.28.27 , with \[  g'(0)=\int _ K w\, \theta ^ n_{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal I}(v)}.  \] Applying 21.11.63 to the convex functions $-f_ k$ and $-g$ gives \[  \lim _{k\to \infty } f_ k'(0)=g'(0),  \] which is equivalent to $\beta ^ k_{v, \varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ](v)}^ n$, by proposition 18.28.27 . $\square$

title: Proposition 18.28.74
text: Proposition 18.28.74 . 0DFF36A22512 Suppose that $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ is such that $\theta _{\varphi }$ is a Kähler current. Let $(K,v)$ be a weighted subset of $X$ and $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$. Then 7EA15066EE63 18.28.75 \begin{equation}  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\quad \textup{as } k\to \infty . \end{equation} Proof. Let $\tau $ be the weak limit of a subsequence of $\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu }$. We claim that CBCF54FCD801 18.28.76 \begin{equation}  \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that this claim implies the conclusion. In fact, by theorem 18.1.46 , we have equality of the total masses, so equality holds in ( 18.28.76 ). As $\tau $ is an arbitrary cluster point of the sequence $(\beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu })_ k$, we get ( 18.28.75 ). It remains to prove ( 18.28.76 ). Let $(\varphi _ j)$ be a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. We may assume that $\theta _{\varphi _ j}$ is a Kähler current for all $j\geq 1$. By corollary 18.1.14 , we know that \[  \varphi _ j\xrightarrow {d_ S}P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}.  \] The quasi-equisingular approximation is decreasing, so applying the decreasing case of proposition 18.28.35 to the limit $P_{\theta }[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}$, and using the definition of the relative $\mathcal{I}$-envelope, we get \[  P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)\searrow P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v).  \] In particular, FD0D14628CD8 18.28.77 \begin{equation}  \lim _{j\to \infty } \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n= \int _ X \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n. \end{equation} Observe that \[  \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi ,\mu } \leq \beta ^ k_{v,\varphi _ j,\mu }  \] for any $k \geq 1$. As $\mu \in \mathrm{BM}(K,v)$, by proposition 18.28.73 , \[  \tau \leq \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi _ j]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n,  \] for any $j \geq 1$ fixed. By ( 18.28.77 ) and the semicontinuity theorem theorem 13.13.9 , we have \[  \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}\left[\varphi _ j\right]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n\rightharpoonup \theta _{P_{\theta ,K}[\varphi ]_{\mathcal{I}}(v)}^ n  \] as $j\to \infty $. Therefore, ( 18.28.76 ) follows. $\square$

title: Remark 18.28.79
text: Remark 18.28.79 . E9D132FDBF95 The results in this chapter can also be reformulated as the large deviation principle of a determinantal point process on $X$ using the Gärtner–Ellis theorem exactly as in [ Ber14 ] . We do not pursue this reformulation here.

title: 25.23.1 A brief history
text: Here we recall the origin of various results. section 5.7 . The notion of plurisubharmonic functions was introduced by Lelong [ Lel45 ] and Oka [ Oka42 ] , based on F. Riesz's theory of subharmonic functions [ Rie26 ] . See [ Bre72 ] for an excellent introduction to the early history of the subject. We refer to [ Bre65 ] for the foundations of potential theory and [ GZ17 ] for the pluripotential theory. The study of Josefson-type theorems was initiated by Josefson [ Jos78 ] , who proved theorem 5.13.19 . The global Josefson theorem theorem 5.13.20 was due to Vu [ Vu19 ] . In the projective setting, it was due to Dinh–Sibony [ DS06 ] and in the Kähler setting, it was established by Guedj–Zeriahi [ GZ05 ] . The extension theorem theorem 5.14.10 was proved in [ GR56 ] . In fact, they proved a more general version for complex spaces, see theorem 9.10.14 . For some related important extension theorems, see [ Shi72 , Wan22 , CGZ13 ] . proposition 5.14.15 was due to Kiselman [ Kis78 ] . The idea of fine topology was due to H. Cartan [ Car41 ] . The plurifine topology was introduced by Fuglede during the Séminaire d'analyse de Lelong–Dolbeault–Skoda of the year 1983/1984 [ Lel86 ] , but often wrongly attributed to Bedford–Taylor. The key result theorem 5.15.11 was claimed in Bedford–Taylor's work [ Theorem 2.3 , BT87 ] without proof. The first rigorous proof was given by El Marzguioui–Wiegerinck [ EMW06 ] . A weaker result was proved earlier in [ Theorem 4.8.7 , Kl91 ] . Results in 5.15.17 are certainly well-known and are already implicitly used in the literature. I could not find the proofs in the literature, so all details are presented. The semicontinuity theorem theorem 5.16.7 was due to Siu [ Siu74 ] . Multiplier ideal sheaves were introduced by Nadel [ Nad90 ] . The idea of theorem 5.16.18 first appeared in the ground-breaking work of Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson [ BFJ08 ] . The openness conjecture was formulated and studied by Demailly–Kollár [ DK01 ] and later proved by Berndtsson [ Bern13b ] . The strong openness theorem 5.16.21 was first established by Guan–Zhou [ GZ15 ] . 5.18.15 was due to [ Proposition 4.1.6 , Dem15 ] . The notions of positivity of currents definition 5.19.1 are due to Lelong [ Lel68 ] and Harvey–Knapp [ HK74 ] , although it is often mistakenly attributed to Demailly. The $L^2$ extension theorems such as theorem 5.16.26 were first studied by Ohsawa–Takegoshi [ OT87 ] . Since then, it has become a very active area. It is almost impossible to give a complete list of the various generalizations and improvements. section 13.1 The Monge–Ampère operators for bounded plurisubharmonic functions were introduced by Bedford–Taylor [ BT76 , BT82 ] . The non-pluripolar product was due to Bedford–Taylor [ BT87 ] , Guedj–Zeriahi [ GZ07 ] and Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi [ BEGZ10 ] . example 13.11.8 was claimed in [ BEGZ10 ] right after Definition 1.1 without proof. The first proof was essentially due to El Kadiri in [ EK24 ] . The semicontinuity theorem theorem 13.13.9 and the domination principle theorem 13.13.43 were due to [ DDNL18fullmass ] . The monotonicity theorem was due to [ WN19 , DDNL18mono ] . The key lemma 13.13.30 was proved in [ DDNLmetric ] . theorem 13.13.24 was due to [ DDNLsurv ] . section 16.1 16.3.3 was proved in [ Lemma 3.7 , DDNL18mono ] . The notion of the $P$-envelope is due to Ross–Witt Nyström [ RWN14 ] based on the ideas of Rashkovskii–Sigurdsson [ RS05 ] . theorem 16.3.12 is due to [ Theorem 3.8 , DDNL18mono ] . The diamond inequality theorem 16.3.35 and proposition 16.3.25 are due to [ Theorem 5.4 , DDNLmetric ] . Most results in 16.5 are simple generalizations of the corresponding results in [ DDNL18big , DDNL18fullmass ] . The study of finite energy potentials was initiated by Cegrell [ Ceg98 ] in the local setup; see also his general definition of the complex Monge–Ampère operator [ Ceg04 ] . The global setup was first studied by Guedj–Zeriahi [ GZ07 ] . The variational approach to degenerate complex Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes was developed by Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi [ BEGZ10 ] and Berman–Boucksom–Guedj–Zeriahi [ BBGZ13 ] . For the complex Monge–Ampère equation and pluripotential methods for weak solutions, see Kołodziej [ Kol98 , Kol05 ] and the references therein. The $\mathcal{I}$-envelope was introduced by Darvas–Xia [ DX22 ] , inspired by the works of Dano Kim [ Kim15 ] and Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson [ BFJ08 ] . The notion of $\mathcal{I}$-model singularities was first formulated in the explicit way in [ DX22 ] in 2020, although it was already essentially known in Boucksom–Jonsson's work. In fact, they correspond exactly to the homogeneous non-Archimedean potentials assuming that the relevant masses do not vanish. A less explicit equivalent formulation of $\mathcal{I}$-model potentials also appeared in [ Dem15 ] . A few months later, the same notion was rediscovered by Trusiani [ Tru22 ] . theorem 13.13.57 is due to [ DNT21 ] . section 17.10 The study of geodesics in the space of Kähler metrics was initiated by Mabuchi [ Mab87 ] , Semmes [ Sem92 ] and Donaldson [ Don99 ] . The existence of geodesics with smooth boundary data was established by Chen [ Chen00 ] . The metric geometry and Mabuchi completion of finite-energy classes in the Kähler case were developed by Darvas [ Dar15 , Dar17 ] . The notion of weak geodesics was studied in detail by Darvas [ Da17 ] in the Kähler case. The case of general big classes was partly handled in [ DDNL18fullmass ] , [ DDNL18big ] . However, the key fact that the geodesics between two full mass potentials have the correct limit at the end points does not seem to have been proved in any references. We give a proof in proposition 17.10.24 . We also extend the relevant results to the relative setting. In the special case $\phi =V_\theta $, proposition 17.10.65 was proved in [ Theorem 3.12 , DDNL18fullmass ] , while the sequential case of proposition 17.10.77 was proved in [ Proposition 3.3 , DDNL18fullmass ] . Previously, proposition 17.10.29 and proposition 17.10.39 were only known in the Kähler case. Most results in subsection 17.10.40 are simple extensions of [ DDNL18big ] . section 21.12 Classical toric Kähler geometry is rooted in the works of Atiyah [ Ati82 ] , Delzant [ Del88 ] , Guillemin [ Gui94 ] , Abreu [ Abr98 ] and Donaldson [ Don02 ] . The pluripotential-theoretic toric framework used here was first written down by Berman–Berndtsson [ BB13 ] and Coman–Guedj–Sahin–Zeriahi [ CGSZ19 ] . The beautiful theorem theorem 21.12.31 was first proved by Yi Yao, who did not publish the result. Later on, a new proof was found by Botero–Burgos Gil–Holmes–de Jong [ BBGHdJ21 ] . We chose to present the approach of Yao, which integrates naturally with our framework. Proposition 21.12.39 is an extension of [ Proposition 2.9 , BB13 ] . section 16.7 The notion of $P$-preorder is new, as well as most results in section 16.8 . The $d_ S$-pseudometric was introduced in [ DDNLmetric ] . The basic properties are proved in [ DDNLmetric ] and [ Xia21 ] . example 16.8.19 was due to Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson [ BBJ21 ] . theorem 16.9.45 can be viewed as a vast generalization of [ Cao15 ] , where a question raised by Demailly was confirmed. theorem 16.9.55 is proved in [ Xia22 ] . theorem 16.9.59 and theorem 16.9.57 appear to be new. These results appeared previously in the form of lecture notes. section 18.1 The notion of $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities was due to [ DX21 ] . The name $\mathcal{I}$-good was chosen in [ Xia22 ] . The key results theorem 18.1.2 and theorem 18.1.46 are due to [ DX21 , DX22 ] . Previously, Rashkovskii [ Ra13 ] also studied the local approximation problem with a different motivation. There are some further examples of $\mathcal{I}$-good singularities provided by [ BBGHdJ21 ] with applications in the theory of modular forms in [ BBGHdJ22 ] . section 20.2 The trace operator was introduced in [ DX24 ] . Here we present a different point of view. theorem 20.2.39 was proved in [ DX24 ] . The analytic Bertini theorem theorem 20.2.45 was proved in [ XiaBer ] , based on the works of Matsumura–Fujino [ FM21 ] and Fujino [ Fuj23 ] . A weaker result was established by Meng–Zhou [ MZ23 ] . section 17.11 The technique of test curves originates from [ RWN14 ] . It was generalized by Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu [ DDNL18big ] , [ DX21 ] , [ DZ22 ] and [ DXZ23 ] . We give the full details of the proofs. Test curves in definition 17.12.1 are called maximal test curves in the literature, a terminology which I do not like. I prefer to call the usual notion of test curves in the literature sub-test curves . proposition 17.13.35 was first proved by He–Testorf–Wang in [ HTW23 ] . proposition 17.13.38 was due to Hisamoto [ His16 ] . 17.14.15 was a folklore result. I am unaware of any written proof in the literature before our paper [ DX22 ] . Finski [ Fin22b ] also gave a different proof with different techniques later on. definition 17.14.7 was not the original definition of maximal geodesic rays of Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson in [ BBJ21 ] . One of the first major applications of our theory was this pluripotential-theoretical characterization of maximal geodesic rays, as proved in our very first paper [ DX22 ] . example 17.14.10 is essentially due to Ross–Witt Nyström [ RWN14 ] . The Phong–Sturm geodesics were first constructed in [ PS07 ] . For the related link between test configurations, filtrations and Okounkov bodies, see Boucksom–Chen [ BC11 ] and Witt Nyström [ WN12 ] . For filtrations and generalized test configurations in K-stability, see Székelyhidi [ Sze15 ] . Results in section 17.15 are easy generalizations of the results proved in [ Xia23Operations ] . section 19.1 The algebraic theory of partial Okounkov bodies was developed in [ Xia21 ] . The transcendental Okounkov body was first defined by Deng [ Deng17 ] as suggested by Demailly. The volume identity was proved in [ DRWNXZ ] . The transcendental theory of partial Okounkov bodies is new. section 20.1 The notion of b-divisors was introduced by Shokurov [ Sho93 ] in the context of minimal model programs. The applications of b-divisors in pluripotential theory began with [ BFJ09 ] . The intersection theory of nef b-divisors was introduced by Dang–Favre [ DF20 ] . The technique of singularity b-divisors was introduced in [ XiaPPT ] in 2020. The general form first appeared in [ Xia22 ] . One year later, a special case was rediscovered in [ BBGHdJ21 ] . The current chapter reproduces a large part of [ Xiabdiv ] . For further developments, we refer to [ Xiabdiv2 ] . example 20.1.9 is reproduced from [ Example 3.3 , DF20 ] . section 21.13 The whole chapter appears to be new. The study of toric pluripotential theory on big line bundles was made possible by the development of partial Okounkov bodies. The key result is theorem 21.13.45 . Most results in this chapter resulted from discussions with Yi Yao. section 22.1 Most results in this chapter come from [ Xia23Operations ] . Results from subsection 22.1.54 are new, although the main idea was already contained in [ Xia21 ] . The terminology of Duistermaat–Heckman measures goes back to the classical theorem of Duistermaat–Heckman [ DH82 ] ; see also their addendum [ DH83 ] . In the setting of Kähler geometry, the Duistermaat–Heckman measures were studied in detail by Boucksom–Hisamoto–Jonsson [ BHJ17 ] . Foundational non-Archimedean global pluripotential theory was developed by Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson [ BFJ16b ] and, over a trivially valued field, by Boucksom–Jonsson [ BJ22 ] . theorem 22.1.111 is due to [ DXZ23 ] . An alternative approach to the transcendental theory is due to Mesquita-Piccione [ MP24 ] . For further progress in this direction, we refer to [ MPWN25 , WN25 ] . Special cases of the results in this section have been applied to study K-stability, see [ XiaPPT ] , [ DZ22 ] , [ DXZ23 ] and [ DR22 ] . In [ DX22 ] , we established the bijective correspondence between a class of $\mathcal{I}$-model test curves and the maximal geodesic rays in the sense of [ BBJ21 ] . section 18.28 The study of asymptotic expansions of Bergman kernels in Kähler geometry was initiated by Tian [ Ti90 ] with later improvements due to Bouché [ Bou90 ] , Ruan [ Rua98 ] , Catlin [ Cat99 ] , Zelditch [ Zel98 ] , Lu [ Lu00 ] among many others. The special case of theorem 18.28.49 without the prescribed singularity $\varphi $ was due to Berman–Boucksom–Witt Nyström, see [ BB10 ] , [ BBWN11 ] . The general case is due to [ DX21 ] .

title: 25.23.2 Open problems
text:
We give a list of important open problems in this theory. We do not repeat the conjectures mentioned in the main text. Conjecture 25.23.3 . F96A00F2C17A Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold and $Y$ be a submanifold. Fix a Kähler class $\alpha $ on $X$. For each Kähler current $S\in \alpha |_ Y$, we can find a Kähler current $T\in \alpha $ such that \[  \operatorname{Tr}_ Y(T)\sim _{\mathcal{I}}S.  \] If we formally view $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y$ as an analogue of the trace operator in the theory of Sobolev spaces, then this conjecture corresponds exactly to the Dirichlet problem. Problem 25.23.4 . 6DBA7A1F707B Is it possible to extend the definition of the trace operator $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y$ to the case where the ambient variety is only unibranch? The difficulty lies in the lack of Demailly type regularization theorems. Problem 25.23.5 . 6BD8E77C1AAF Is there a natural definition of the transcendental Okounkov body of a closed positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ with $0$-mass so that its dimension is equal to the numerical dimension of $T$? See [ Cao14 ] for the definition of the numerical dimension of a current. 


The following two problems are proposed by Witt Nyström. Problem 25.23.6 . 0C91C5C2794A Consider a compact Kähler manifold $X$ and a connected submanifold $Y$. We have defined the trace operator $\operatorname{Tr}_ Y$ from a subset of $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)/\sim _\mathcal {I}$ to $\mathrm{QPSH}(Y)/\sim _\mathcal {I}$. Is it possible to refine this operator to one from a subset of $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)/\sim _ P$ to $\mathrm{QPSH}(Y)/\sim _ P$? Problem 25.23.7 . 7FAD0FAF17B7 Consider a connected compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$ and a smooth flag $Y_{\bullet }$ on $X$. Consider a closed smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ on $X$ representing a big cohomology class and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n>0$. Can one define a refined notion of partial Okounkov bodies $\Delta '_{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )$ contained in $\Delta _{Y_{\bullet }}(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi )$ with volume given by $\frac{1}{n!}\int _ X \theta _{\varphi }^ n$? Note that a satisfactory solution to the latter problem is not very likely, as can be easily seen from examples on $\mathbb {P}^1$. 


We also look for generalizations of our theory to more general settings. Problem 25.23.8 . 856DCCA91F34 To what extent can the results in the current book be generalized to the non-Kähler setting? The non-pluripolar products in the non-Kähler setting were recently studied by Boucksom–Guedj–Lu in [ BGL24 ] . See also the references therein. Problem 25.23.9 . 18561C2CB4F4 To what extent can the results in the current book about closed positive $(1,1)$-currents be generalized to closed positive currents of higher bidegree? A fundamental issue is the lack of a strong enough Demailly type approximation for general currents. The regularization theorem of Dinh–Sibony [ DS04 ] seems too weak for our purposes.

title: 21.11 Convex functions and convex bodies
text: Convex functions and convex bodies are studied through Legendre duality, recession functions, and real Monge–Ampère measures. Statements for convex functions apply to concave functions after changing the sign.

title: 21.11.1 The notion of convex functions
text:
Let $N$ be a real vector space of finite dimension. Definition 21.11.2 . 3B5FF6A6C162 Let $F\colon N\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ be a function. The epigraph of $F$ is defined as the following set \[  \operatorname{epi}F\coloneqq \left\{  (n,r)\in N\times \mathbb {R}: r\geq F(n) \right\} .  \] Definition 21.11.3 . 4FA12A948A00 A convex function on $N$ is a function $F\colon N\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$ such that the epigraph $\operatorname{epi}F$ is a convex subset of $N\times \mathbb {R}$. The effective domain of $F$ is the set \[  \operatorname{Dom}F\coloneqq \left\{  n\in N : F(n)<\infty \right\} .  \] A convex function $F$ on $N$ such that $\operatorname{Dom}F\neq \varnothing $ and $F(n)\neq -\infty $ for all $n\in N$ is said to be proper . The set of convex functions on $N$ is denoted by $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. The subset of proper convex functions is denoted by $\mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$. The following characterization of convex functions is well-known. Lemma 21.11.4 . 47309C75E6C1 Let $F\colon N\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$. Then $F$ is convex if and only if the following condition holds: suppose that $n,r\in N$ and $a,b\in \mathbb {R}$ such that $a>F(n)$, $b>F(r)$, then for any $t\in (0,1)$, we have \[  F(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b.  \] Proof. Assume first that the epigraph is convex. Given $a>F(n)$ and $b>F(r)$, choose finite $a'<a$ and $b'<b$ with $F(n)\leq a'$ and $F(r)\leq b'$. Convexity of the epigraph gives $F(tn+(1-t)r)\leq ta'+(1-t)b'<ta+(1-t)b$. Conversely, take $(n,a),(r,b)$ in the epigraph. For every $\varepsilon>0$ the assumed inequality applied to $a+\varepsilon,b+\varepsilon$ gives $F(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b+\varepsilon$. Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. The resulting weak inequality says that the convex combination of these two points belongs to the epigraph. Endpoints cause no difficulty. This proof also covers values $-\infty$; points with value $+\infty$ contribute no points to the epigraph. See [ Theorem 4.2 , Roc70 ] for the proof. Example 21.11.5 . 1532A37DD27F Let $A\subseteq N$ be a convex subset. Then the characteristic function $\chi _ A\colon N\rightarrow \{ 0,\infty \} $ of $A$ is defined by \[  \chi _ A(n)\coloneqq \left\{  \begin{aligned}  0,& \quad n\in A;\\  \infty ,& \quad n\not\in A. \end{aligned} \right.  \] The function $\chi _ A$ lies in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Example 21.11.6 . 8CBDC69B6C55 Let $M$ be the dual vector space of $N$ and $P\subseteq M$ be a convex subset. The support function $\operatorname{Supp}_ P\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ of $P$ is defined as follows: \[  \operatorname{Supp}_ P(n)\coloneqq \sup \{  \langle m,n \rangle : m\in P \} .  \] It is well-known that convexity is preserved by a number of natural operations. We recall a few to fix the notation. Definition 21.11.7 . 0ECB6CF7B06D Let $F_1,\ldots ,F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$ ($m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$). We define their infimal convolution $F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ as follows: \[  F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m(n)\coloneqq \inf \left\{  \sum _{i=1}^ m F_ i(n_ i):n_ i\in N, \sum _{i=1}^ m n_ i=n \right\} .  \] The fact $F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ is proved in [ Theorem 5.4 , Roc70 ] . One should note that $F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m$ is not always proper. Proposition 21.11.8 . 68114EF2F29C Let $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Then $\sup _{i\in I} F_ i\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Proof. For every $x\in N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$, the inequality $a\geq\sup_iF_i(x)$ holds exactly when $a\geq F_i(x)$ for every $i$. Consequently
\[\operatorname{epi}(\sup_iF_i)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{epi}F_i.\]
An intersection of convex sets is convex, so the supremum is convex. This also covers extended values and an empty epigraph. This follows from [ Theorem 5.5 , Roc70 ] . In particular, this allows us to introduce Definition 21.11.9 . 8F179BE28950 Let $f\colon N\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$. The lower convex envelope of $f$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{CE}f\coloneqq \sup \{ F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N): F\leq f \} .  \] It follows from proposition 21.11.8 that $\operatorname{CE}f\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Definition 21.11.10 . 6561D15F1216 Given a non-empty family $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$, we define \[  \bigwedge _{i\in I}F_ i\coloneqq \operatorname{CE}\left(\inf _{i\in I} F_ i\right).  \] When the family $I$ is finite, say $I=\{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $, we also write \[  F_1\land \cdots \land F_ m=\bigwedge _{i\in I}F_ i.  \] Definition 21.11.11 . 4D25259F16EC Given a non-empty family $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$, we define \[  \bigvee _{i\in I}F_ i\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I} F_ i.  \] When the family $I$ is finite, say $I=\{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $, we also write \[  F_1\lor \cdots \lor F_ m=\bigvee _{i\in I}F_ i.  \] Recall that $\bigvee _{i\in I}F_ i\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ by proposition 21.11.8 . Proposition 21.11.12 . B99B20CD6166 Let $F_1,\ldots ,F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$. Then \[  \begin{split}  F_1\land \cdots \land F_ m(x)=\inf \left\{ \sum _{i=1}^ m \lambda _ i F_ i(x_ i):x_ i\in \operatorname{Dom}(F_ i),\right.\\  \left.\lambda _ i\in [0,1],\sum _{i=1}^ m\lambda _ i=1, \sum _{i=1}^ m\lambda _ i x_ i=x \right\} . \end{split}  \] Proof. Let $H$ denote the infimum displayed in the statement, with the infimum of the empty set equal to $+\infty$. It is at most $F_i$ for every $i$: put weight $1$ on that index and weight $0$ on the others, choosing arbitrary points in their nonempty effective domains. To prove convexity, take admissible representations of $x$ and $y$, multiply their weights by $t$ and $1-t$, and combine them. For each index $i$ with combined weight $\gamma_i>0$, replace its two points by their weighted barycenter. Convexity of $F_i$ makes its new contribution no larger than the sum of the old contributions. If $\gamma_i=0$, choose any point of its domain. This produces a representation of $tx+(1-t)y$. Taking approximations to the infima proves the strict-height convexity criterion proved above , including when an infimum is $-\infty$. Finally, every convex function $G\leq F_i$ for all $i$ is at most the value of every admissible combination, by convexity applied to finite epigraph heights above the $F_i(x_i)$ and then taking their limits. Thus $G\leq H$. Therefore $H$ is the largest convex minorant of $\inf_iF_i$, which is precisely $F_1\land\cdots\land F_m$. See [ Theorem 5.6 , Roc70 ] for the more general result. Lemma 21.11.13 . 2F4F518BD56D Let $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Then $\inf _{i\in I} F_ i\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Proof. Write $F=\inf _{i\in I} F_ i$. We shall apply the characterization in 21.11.4 . Take $n,r\in N$, $a,b\in \mathbb {R}$ such that $a>F(n)$, $b>F(r)$ and $t\in (0,1)$. We need to show that 752978EE01F6 21.11.14 \begin{equation}  F(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b. \end{equation} By definition, there are $j_ n,j_ r\in I$ such that $a>F_ i(n)$ for $i\geq j_ n$ and $b>F_ i(r)$ for $i\geq j_ r$. Since $I$ is directed, we can find $j\in I$ dominating both $j_ n$ and $j_ r$, and then for any $i\geq j$, we have \[  a>F_ i(n),\quad b>F_ i(r).  \] It follows from 21.11.4 that \[  F_ i(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b  \] for any $i\geq j$. Since $F_ i$ is decreasing in $i$, we conclude ( 21.11.14 ). $\square$ Definition 21.11.15 . 61B746F5E884 Let $F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. The closure $\operatorname{cl}F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ of $F$ is defined as follows: If $F(n)=-\infty $ for some $n\in N$, then $\operatorname{cl}F\coloneqq -\infty $. Otherwise, we define $\operatorname{cl}F$ as the lower semicontinuity regularization of $F$. A convex function $F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ is closed if $F=\operatorname{cl}F$. In other words, $F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ is closed if one of the following conditions holds: 9B2264291DE3 $F\equiv -\infty $; 55523AC55CA5 $F\equiv \infty $; C1225E82131E $F$ is proper and lower semicontinuous. Proposition 21.11.16 . E013E1966E44 Let $F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ be a closed convex function. Then $F$ is the supremum of all affine functions lying below $F$. Proof. For a closed proper $F$, finite-dimensional Fenchel duality gives
\[F(x)=F^{**}(x)=\sup_p\{\langle p,x\rangle-F^*(p)\}.\]
For every $p$ with $F^*(p)<+\infty$, the expression in braces is an affine minorant of $F$, by the definition of conjugacy. Conversely, every affine minorant $\langle p,x\rangle+c$ satisfies $c\leq-F^*(p)$. Thus the supremum is exactly that of all affine minorants. If $F\equiv+\infty$, arbitrary constant minorants already have supremum $+\infty$. If $F\equiv-\infty$, there are no finite affine minorants and their supremum is $-\infty$. See [ Theorem 12.1 , Roc70 ] . Theorem 21.11.17 . 7E0B71CF3B0E Let $F\in \mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$. Then $\operatorname{cl}F$ is a closed proper convex function. Moreover, $\operatorname{cl}F$ agrees with $F$ except possibly on the relative boundary of $\operatorname{Dom}F$. Proof. Apply the closure theorem for proper convex functions . It proves that the lower semicontinuous regularization of $F$ is closed and proper and agrees with $F$ on the relative interior of its effective domain. Since $F$ is proper, this regularization is exactly the closure defined here. Outside the closure of $\operatorname{Dom}F$, both functions are $+\infty$: a neighborhood misses the effective domain, so the lower semicontinuous regularization is $+\infty$ there. Every remaining point outside the relative boundary belongs to the relative interior of the domain. Therefore disagreement is possible only on that relative boundary, as asserted. See [ Theorem 7.4 , Roc70 ] . Proposition 21.11.18 . B6B15657CD64 Let $F,F'\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ be closed convex functions. Assume that A4BAF58116DC $\operatorname{RelInt}\operatorname{Dom}F=\operatorname{RelInt}\operatorname{Dom}F'$, and FAD3EA2C74FA $F=F'$ on $\operatorname{RelInt}\operatorname{Dom}F$. Then $F=F'$. Proof. For proper closed functions this is the uniqueness assertion in the convex closure theorem . More explicitly, the closure of the epigraph over the relative interior of the effective domain is the whole epigraph: for a point of the epigraph, take convex combinations with a fixed epigraph point whose base is in that relative interior, and let the coefficient of the fixed point tend to zero. Thus identical values on the common relative interior give identical epigraphs and hence identical functions. The improper cases in the definition of closedness are also determined: empty effective domain means the function identically $+\infty$; if one function is identically $-\infty$, the common relative interior is $N$ and the value agreement makes the other identical to it. These cases complete the proof. This is a special case of [ Corollary 7.3.4 , Roc70 ] . Definition 21.11.19 . CC63E6A637E8 Given $F,F'\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$, we write $F\preceq F'$ if there is $C\in \mathbb {R}$ such that \[  F\leq F'+C.  \] We say $F\sim F'$ if $F\preceq F'$ and $F'\preceq F$ both hold. Theorem 21.11.20 . A7E9B5A114CA Let $C\subseteq N$ be an open subset. Let $(f_ i)_{i>0}$ be a sequence of real-valued convex functions on $C$. Suppose that the sequence converges on a dense subset of $C$ and the limit is finite. Then the limit \[  f(x)\coloneqq \lim _{i\to \infty } f_ i(x)  \] exists for all $x\in C$ and is convex on $C$. Moreover, the sequence $(f_ i)_ i$ converges uniformly to $f$ on each compact subset of $C$. Proof. On every open convex ball relatively compact in $C$, dense convergence for finite convex functions applies to the restriction of the given dense set and supplies a finite convex local limit with locally uniform convergence. Local limits agree on overlaps, because they are pointwise limits of the same sequence. They therefore define a finite function $f$ on $C$. Every compact subset of $C$ is covered by finitely many smaller such balls. Taking the maximum of the finitely many uniform error bounds proves uniform convergence on that compact set. Passing to the limit in each convexity inequality proves convexity wherever the corresponding segment lies in $C$; in the usual convention that the domain of a convex function is convex, this is convexity on $C$. In particular the limiting values at the original dense set determine $f$ uniquely. This is a special case of [ Theorem 10.8 , Roc70 ] .

title: Definition 21.11.7
text: Definition 21.11.7 . 0ECB6CF7B06D Let $F_1,\ldots ,F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$ ($m\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}$). We define their infimal convolution $F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$ as follows: \[  F_1 \square \cdots \square F_ m(n)\coloneqq \inf \left\{  \sum _{i=1}^ m F_ i(n_ i):n_ i\in N, \sum _{i=1}^ m n_ i=n \right\} .  \]

title: Proposition 21.11.8
text:
Proposition 21.11.8 . 68114EF2F29C Let $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ be a non-empty family in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Then $\sup _{i\in I} F_ i\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Proof. For every $x\in N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$, the inequality $a\geq\sup_iF_i(x)$ holds exactly when $a\geq F_i(x)$ for every $i$. Consequently
\[\operatorname{epi}(\sup_iF_i)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{epi}F_i.\]

title: Definition 21.11.9
text: Definition 21.11.9 . 8F179BE28950 Let $f\colon N\rightarrow [-\infty ,\infty ]$. The lower convex envelope of $f$ is defined as \[  \operatorname{CE}f\coloneqq \sup \{ F\in \mathrm{Conv}(N): F\leq f \} .  \] It follows from proposition 21.11.8 that $\operatorname{CE}f\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$.

title: Definition 21.11.10
text: Definition 21.11.10 . 6561D15F1216 Given a non-empty family $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$, we define \[  \bigwedge _{i\in I}F_ i\coloneqq \operatorname{CE}\left(\inf _{i\in I} F_ i\right).  \] When the family $I$ is finite, say $I=\{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $, we also write \[  F_1\land \cdots \land F_ m=\bigwedge _{i\in I}F_ i.  \]

title: Definition 21.11.11
text: Definition 21.11.11 . 4D25259F16EC Given a non-empty family $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$, we define \[  \bigvee _{i\in I}F_ i\coloneqq \sup _{i\in I} F_ i.  \] When the family $I$ is finite, say $I=\{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $, we also write \[  F_1\lor \cdots \lor F_ m=\bigvee _{i\in I}F_ i.  \]

title: Proposition 21.11.12
text: Proposition 21.11.12 . B99B20CD6166 Let $F_1,\ldots ,F_ m\in \mathrm{Conv}^{\mathrm{prop}}(N)$. Then \[  \begin{split}  F_1\land \cdots \land F_ m(x)=\inf \left\{ \sum _{i=1}^ m \lambda _ i F_ i(x_ i):x_ i\in \operatorname{Dom}(F_ i),\right.\\  \left.\lambda _ i\in [0,1],\sum _{i=1}^ m\lambda _ i=1, \sum _{i=1}^ m\lambda _ i x_ i=x \right\} . \end{split}  \] Proof. Let $H$ denote the infimum displayed in the statement, with the infimum of the empty set equal to $+\infty$. It is at most $F_i$ for every $i$: put weight $1$ on that index and weight $0$ on the others, choosing arbitrary points in their nonempty effective domains. To prove convexity, take admissible representations of $x$ and $y$, multiply their weights by $t$ and $1-t$, and combine them. For each index $i$ with combined weight $\gamma_i>0$, replace its two points by their weighted barycenter. Convexity of $F_i$ makes its new contribution no larger than the sum of the old contributions. If $\gamma_i=0$, choose any point of its domain. This produces a representation of $tx+(1-t)y$. Taking approximations to the infima proves the strict-height convexity criterion proved above , including when an infimum is $-\infty$. Finally, every convex function $G\leq F_i$ for all $i$ is at most the value of every admissible combination, by convexity applied to finite epigraph heights above the $F_i(x_i)$ and then taking their limits. Thus $G\leq H$. Therefore $H$ is the largest convex minorant of $\inf_iF_i$, which is precisely $F_1\land\cdots\land F_m$.

title: Lemma 21.11.13
text: Lemma 21.11.13 . 2F4F518BD56D Let $\{ F_ i\} _{i\in I}$ be a decreasing net in $\mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Then $\inf _{i\in I} F_ i\in \mathrm{Conv}(N)$. Proof. Write $F=\inf _{i\in I} F_ i$. We shall apply the characterization in 21.11.4 . Take $n,r\in N$, $a,b\in \mathbb {R}$ such that $a>F(n)$, $b>F(r)$ and $t\in (0,1)$. We need to show that 752978EE01F6 21.11.14 \begin{equation}  F(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b. \end{equation} By definition, there are $j_ n,j_ r\in I$ such that $a>F_ i(n)$ for $i\geq j_ n$ and $b>F_ i(r)$ for $i\geq j_ r$. Since $I$ is directed, we can find $j\in I$ dominating both $j_ n$ and $j_ r$, and then for any $i\geq j$, we have \[  a>F_ i(n),\quad b>F_ i(r).  \] It follows from 21.11.4 that \[  F_ i(tn+(1-t)r)<ta+(1-t)b  \] for any $i\geq j$. Since $F_ i$ is decreasing in $i$, we conclude ( 21.11.14 ). $\square$
