title: 5.27.27 Measure concentration under integrable convergence
text: Decreasing approximation controls Bedford–Taylor products, but convergence of the potentials in $L^1$ alone does not. If plurisubharmonic functions tend to zero in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and are locally uniformly bounded, the range estimate ( 5.27.3 ) shows that their Monge–Ampère measures tend to zero. Without a common bound, smooth bounded potentials that tend to zero, even in capacity, can have Monge–Ampère measures converging to a point mass. Lemma 5.27.28 . 55862640C106 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain. Suppose that $u_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ tend to zero in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ and satisfy $\sup _ j\| u_ j\| _{L^\infty (K)}<\infty $ for every compact set $K\subset \Omega $. Then $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n(K)\to 0$ for every such $K$. Proof. Fix concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset B_1\Subset \Omega $, and put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. If $\psi $ is a nonnegative smooth cutoff function supported in $B_1$ and equal to one near $\overline B$, integration by parts gives \[  0\leq \int _ B\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\wedge \beta ^{n-1} \leq \int _{B_1}u_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge \beta ^{n-1} \leq C\| u_ j\| _{L^1(B_1)}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Choose $M>0$ with $|u_ j|\leq M$ on $B$ for all $j$, and apply the first estimate in ( 5.27.3 ) to $u_ j+M$, whose values lie in $[0,2M]$. It bounds the top-degree mass of $B'$ by $C(2M)^{n-1}$ times the trace integral over $B$, which tends to zero; for $n=1$ the trace estimate itself suffices. Covering $K$ by finitely many such balls proves the lemma. $\square$ The construction uses a regularized maximum of a small multiple of a logarithm in one variable and a potential in the remaining variables. Its Monge–Ampère measure can be computed exactly by integration over circles in the first variable, and this will keep its top-degree mass fixed while the logarithmic coefficient tends to zero. Lemma 5.27.29 . E2307F7792A2 Let $n\geq 2$, let $U\subset \mathbb C^{n-1}$ be a domain, and let $v$ be a smooth plurisubharmonic function on $U$. Fix $\varepsilon ,R,\eta >0$ and $A\in \mathbb R$. Let $\chi _\eta $ be the convolution of $t\mapsto \max (t,0)$ with a smooth even probability density supported in $[-\eta ,\eta ]$, and put \[  \begin{split}  q(\zeta )& =\varepsilon \log (|\zeta |^2/R^2),\qquad T(\zeta ,z')=v(z')-A-q(\zeta ),\\  h(\zeta ,z')& =q(\zeta )+\chi _\eta (T(\zeta ,z')) \end{split}  \] for $\zeta \ne 0$. Then $h$ extends to a smooth plurisubharmonic function on $\mathbb C\times U$. Set \[  w_\eta (t)=n\chi _\eta '(t)^{n-1}\chi _\eta ''(t),\qquad r_ t(z')=R\exp \bigl ((v(z')-A-t)/(2\varepsilon )\bigr ).  \] The function $w_\eta $ is nonnegative, supported in $[-\eta ,\eta ]$, and has integral one. For every $f\in C_ c(\mathbb C\times U)$, 97724F2A7D19 5.27.30 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n =\varepsilon \int _ U\biggl [\int _{-\eta }^{\eta }w_\eta (t) \int _0^{2\pi }f(r_ t(z')\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\vartheta },z') \frac{\mathrm d\vartheta }{2\pi }\, \mathrm dt\biggr ] (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-1}. \end{split} \end{equation} Proof. By convexity, $0\leq \chi _\eta '\leq 1$ and $\chi _\eta ''\geq 0$. The function $\chi _\eta $ vanishes on $(-\infty ,-\eta ]$ and equals $t$ on $[\eta ,\infty )$. Since $T\to +\infty $ as $\zeta \to 0$, we have $h=v-A$ near each point with $\zeta =0$, which gives the smooth extension. Off the hyperplane $\{ \zeta =0\} $, the function $q$ is pluriharmonic and \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h=\chi _\eta '(T)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v +\chi _\eta ''(T)\, \mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T\geq 0.  \] The second summand has rank at most one, and the first has rank at most $n-1$. Hence \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n=n\chi _\eta '(T)^{n-1}\chi _\eta ''(T) \, \mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-1}.  \] The last factor has top degree in the variables $z'$, so the derivatives of $v$ in $\mathrm dT\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T$ contribute nothing. Write $s=\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$. In polar coordinates, $\mathrm dq=\varepsilon \, \mathrm ds$ and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q=\varepsilon \, \mathrm d\vartheta /(2\pi )$. At fixed $z'$, the change of variables from $s$ to $t=v-A-\varepsilon s$ gives ( 5.27.30 ). There is no contribution near $\zeta =0$, where $h=v-A$ and the form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ has rank at most $n-1$. Finally, $w_\eta $ is the derivative of $(\chi _\eta ')^ n$, whose values at $-\eta $ and $\eta $ are zero and one. $\square$ Proposition 5.27.31 . 026A64B7A5A2 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain and $a\in \Omega $. For every $c>0$, there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $ such that \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\longrightarrow 0\quad (1\leq p<\infty ), \qquad (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n\longrightarrow c\delta _ a \quad \text{vaguely}.  \] The same sequence tends to zero in local capacity. Here the norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure, and vague convergence means convergence against every compactly supported continuous test function. Proof. Translate $a$ to the origin and write $z=(\zeta ,z')\in \mathbb C\times \mathbb C^ m$, $m=n-1$. It suffices to construct measures of mass one and then multiply the potentials by $c^{1/n}$. For $\delta >0$, put $H_\delta (z')=\log (|z'|^2+\delta ^2)$. With $s=|z'|^2$, the complex Hessian of $H_\delta $ has the eigenvalue $(s+\delta ^2)^{-1}$ with multiplicity $m-1$ in the directions orthogonal to $z'$ and the eigenvalue $\delta ^2(s+\delta ^2)^{-2}$ in the radial direction. Taking the determinant and integrating in polar coordinates gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m= \frac{m!}{\pi ^ m}\frac{\delta ^2}{(|z'|^2+\delta ^2)^{m+1}} \, \mathrm d\lambda _{2m}, \qquad \int _{|z'|<b}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m =\left(\frac{b^2}{b^2+\delta ^2}\right)^ m,  \] where $\lambda _{2m}$ is Lebesgue measure. These probability measures tend to $\delta _0$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$, since their mass outside each ball about the origin tends to zero. Choose $R>\max (1,\sup _\Omega |\zeta |)$ and a ball $P\subset \mathbb C^ m$ containing the projection of $\Omega $ to the $z'$ variables. Set \[  \begin{gathered} \delta _ j=\varepsilon _ j=j^{-1},\qquad \eta _ j=j^{-2}, \qquad v_ j=\varepsilon _ j^{-1/m}H_{\delta _ j},\\ A_ j=\sup _ Pv_ j+2\varepsilon _ j\log (Rj). \end{gathered}  \] Apply lemma 5.27.29 on $\mathbb C\times \mathbb C^ m$ to these data, and let $u_ j=h_ j-\eta _ j$, where $h_ j$ is the resulting function. The convolution satisfies $0\leq \chi _{\eta _ j}(t)-\max (t,0)\leq \eta _ j$, and $q+\max (T,0)=\max (q,v_ j-A_ j)$. Both branches of this maximum are negative on $\Omega $, so \[  \varepsilon _ j\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)-\eta _ j \leq u_ j\leq 0.  \] Each $u_ j$ is smooth and bounded on $\Omega $, since the second branch $v_ j-A_ j$ is bounded below on the bounded set $P$. The logarithm has finite $L^ p(\Omega )$ norm for every finite $p$, by polar integration on a fixed polydisk containing $\Omega $. Hence $u_ j\to 0$ in all these norms. Let $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ be concentric balls, and let $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$. Since $|u_ j|\leq \varepsilon _ j|\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)|+\eta _ j$, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate applied to $\log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$, together with the range estimate ( 5.27.3 ) for the constant term, gives \[  \int _{B'}|u_ j|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n\leq C_ B(\varepsilon _ j+\eta _ j),  \] where $C_ B$ depends on the fixed balls and the logarithm but not on $j$ or $w$. Restricting the integral to $B'\cap \{ |u_ j|>t\} $, dividing by $t>0$ and taking the supremum over $w$ shows that the capacity of $B'\cap \{ |u_ j|>t\} $ relative to $B$ tends to zero. In ( 5.27.30 ), the factor $\varepsilon _ j(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ m$ equals $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m$. For $z'\in P$ and $|t|\leq \eta _ j$, the radii satisfy \[  r_ t(z')\leq j^{-1}\exp (\eta _ j/(2\varepsilon _ j)) \leq \mathrm e^{1/2}/j.  \] Extend $f\in C_ c(\Omega )$ by zero to $\mathbb C^ n$. Outside the projection of $\operatorname {supp}f$ to the $z'$ variables, both $f(r_ t\mathrm e^{\mathrm i\vartheta },z')$ and $f(0,z')$ vanish. On this projection, the uniform continuity of $f$ and the bound on the radii make their difference tend to zero uniformly. Since the weights $w_{\eta _ j}(t)\, \mathrm dt$ and $\mathrm d\vartheta /(2\pi )$ and the measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m$ all have total mass one, it follows that \[  \int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n -\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f(0,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_{\delta _ j})^ m \longrightarrow 0.  \] The second integral tends to $f(0)$, which proves the asserted vague limit. $\square$ Each approximating measure has a smooth density and charges no pluripolar set, whereas the limit is a point mass. By lemma 5.27.28 , the potentials therefore have no common lower bound on some compact set. Thus convergence in capacity is compatible with concentration of the Monge–Ampère measures once common local bounds are lost.

title: Lemma 5.27.28
text: Lemma 5.27.28 . 55862640C106 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain. Suppose that $u_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ tend to zero in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ and satisfy $\sup _ j\| u_ j\| _{L^\infty (K)}<\infty $ for every compact set $K\subset \Omega $. Then $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n(K)\to 0$ for every such $K$. Proof. Fix concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset B_1\Subset \Omega $, and put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Covering $K$ by finitely many such balls proves the lemma. $\square$

At fixed $z'$, the change of variables from $s$ to $t=v-A-\varepsilon s$ gives ( 5.27.30 ). Finally, $w_\eta $ is the derivative of $(\chi _\eta ')^ n$, whose values at $-\eta $ and $\eta $ are zero and one. $\square$

title: Equation 5.27.30

title: 5.27.32 Adding a prescribed local measure
text:
The concentration in proposition 5.27.31 can be produced on top of a given bounded potential $b$ and repeated, so as to add an arbitrary prescribed measure to $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Adding a perturbation $h$ to $b$ creates the mixed terms $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r$. A mixed Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate controls them, provided that the lower-degree currents of $h$ are kept small. Lemma 5.27.33 . 0EE345C93AFA Fix the data $n,U,v,\varepsilon ,R,\eta ,\chi _\eta $ of lemma 5.27.29 , and write $h_ A$ for the smooth plurisubharmonic function $h$ of that lemma, regarded as a function of $A$. Put $D=\{ 0\} 	imes U$, and write $[D]$ for the current of integration over this hypersurface. Then, for every $1\leq r\leq n$, \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\longrightarrow \varepsilon [D]\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1} \quad 	ext{as currents on }\mathbb C	imes U,\  A	o \infty .  \] The product on the right is integration of the restriction of the smooth form $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1}$ over $D$. Proof. Write $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$, $q=\varepsilon \log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$ and $T_ A=v-A-q$. The rank-one calculation in the proof of lemma 5.27.29 gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r=\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^ rS^ r +r\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(T_ A) \, \mathrm dT_ A\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T_ A\wedge S^{r-1}  \] off $D$; since $h_ A$ is smooth and $D$ has measure zero, this formula determines the current. Fix a smooth compactly supported test form. On the projection of its support to $U$, the function $v$ and its derivatives are bounded. Hence the support of $\chi _\eta '(T_ A)$ lies in $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $, where $s_ A=C\exp (-A/(2\varepsilon ))$ and $C$ depends only on this compact set and the fixed data. The coefficients involving $v$ and $\chi _\eta $ are bounded at the fixed parameters, so the first summand has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$. In the second summand, the term with two derivatives of $v$ also has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$, and the two cross terms have pairing $O(s_ A)$: the derivative of $q$ in the $\zeta $ direction has size $O(|\zeta |^{-1})$, and its area integral over the disk $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $ is $O(s_ A)$. It remains to integrate the term containing $\mathrm dq\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q$. The logarithmic change of the radial variable used for ( 5.27.30 ) leaves the factor $\varepsilon $ and the probability weight \[  r\chi _\eta '(t)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(t)\, \mathrm dt, \qquad -\eta \leq t\leq \eta .  \] Only the component of the test form in the $z'$ directions enters this term, and on the shrinking circles its coefficients tend uniformly to their values at $\zeta =0$. Integration in the angle therefore gives, in the limit, exactly the pairing with $\varepsilon [D]\wedge S^{r-1}$. This proves the convergence in every degree. $\square$ Lemma 5.27.34 . 0950BB9BC118 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, let $K$ and $L$ be compact subsets of $\Omega $ with $K$ contained in the interior $L^\circ $ of $L$, and put $ eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $, and let $T$ be a smooth positive closed $(r,r)$-form, $1\leq r<n$. Then \[  \int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge T \leq C_{K,L,n}(1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{n-r} \int _ L T\wedge  eta ^{n-r}.  \] Proof. Put $M=1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Cover $K$ by finitely many balls whose larger concentric balls have closures in $L^\circ $. Replacing $b$ by $b+M$, which has the same Hessian and takes values in $[0,2M]$ on $L$, we may assume $0\leq b\leq 2M$ there. For nested cutoff functions $\psi $, integration by parts against closed forms gives \[  \int \psi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge W =\int b\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge W \leq CM \int _{\operatorname {supp}\psi } eta \wedge W,  \] where $W$ is $T$ multiplied by the remaining positive closed factors. Apply this successively to the $n-r$ Hessians of $b$. For bounded $b$, the integrations by parts are justified by local decreasing regularization and theorem 5.27.1 , with one common bound on the range. Summing over the finite cover gives the asserted constant. $\square$ Proposition 5.27.35 . 6C1E4E8060FF Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain, let $b\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty (\Omega )$, $a\in \Omega $ and $c>0$. Given finitely many $f_ i\in C_ c(\Omega )$ and numbers $	au ,t>0$, there is a smooth bounded plurisubharmonic function $h\leq 0$ on $\Omega $ such that \[   egin{gathered} \| h\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}t\quad (1\leq p<\infty ),\ \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h))^ n-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n igr ) -cf_ i(a)ight|<	au \quad 	ext{for every }i. \end{gathered}  \] For concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ and every $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$, it also satisfies \[  \int _{B'}|h|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n\leq C_{B',B,\Omega }t.  \] These constants are independent of $b,a,c$, the test functions and the tolerances. Proof. We take for $h$ a function from lemma 5.27.29 whose top-degree measure approximates $c\delta _ a$ and whose lower-degree currents are small; lemma 5.27.34 then controls the mixed terms. Write $a=(a_1,a')$ and $m=n-1$, and fix $R=2\sup _\Omega |z_1|+2$. For $\delta >0$, put $H_\delta (z')=\log (|z'-a'|^2+\delta ^2)$. By the radial calculation in the proof of proposition 5.27.31 , $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m$ is a probability measure tending to $\delta _{a'}$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Extend every $f_ i$ by zero outside $\Omega $, and choose $\delta $ such that \[  \left|c\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f_ i(a_1,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m -cf_ i(a)ight|<	au /3\quad 	ext{for all }i.  \] Choose compact sets $K,L\subset \Omega $ with $K\subset L^\circ $ and $K$ containing the supports of all $f_ i$, and a nonnegative smooth cutoff function $\psi $ with compact support in $\Omega $, equal to one near $L$. Put $ eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Expanding the top power of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h)$, summing the bounds of lemma 5.27.34 with their binomial coefficients and the norms $\| f_ i\| _\infty $, we find $\gamma >0$ such that the mixed terms contribute less than $	au /3$ to every test integral whenever $h$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic and \[  \int _ L(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r\wedge  eta ^{n-r}<\gamma , \qquad 1\leq r<n.  \] Fix $0<\eta \leq t/2$. Apply lemma 5.27.29 on $\mathbb C	imes \mathbb C^ m$ with transverse variable $\zeta =z_1-a_1$ and $v=c^{1/m}\varepsilon ^{-1/m}H_\delta $. For $r<n$, lemma 5.27.33 gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\longrightarrow \varepsilon ^{(n-r)/(n-1)}c^{(r-1)/(n-1)} [\{ z_1=a_1\} ]\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^{r-1}  \] as $A	o \infty $. For the fixed $\delta $, the integrals of these limits against $\psi  eta ^{n-r}$ are finite, and their exponents of $\varepsilon $ are positive. Choose $0<\varepsilon \leq t/2$ so that each of them is less than $\gamma /2$. With these parameters fixed, choose $A$ so large that the integrals $\int _ L(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\wedge  eta ^{n-r}$ are less than $\gamma $, that $v-A\leq 0$ on the projection of $\Omega $ to the $z'$ variables, and that \[  \left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ n -c\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f_ i(a_1,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ might|<	au /3 \quad 	ext{for all }i.  \] The last choice follows directly from ( 5.27.30 ), because the circles there shrink uniformly over the projected supports of the tests and $\varepsilon (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ m=c(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m$. Set $h=h_ A-\eta $. As in the proof of proposition 5.27.31 , $h$ is smooth, bounded and nonpositive on $\Omega $, with \[  \varepsilon \log (|z_1-a_1|^2/R^2)-\eta \leq h\leq 0.  \] The logarithm has $L^ p(\Omega )$ norm bounded uniformly for $a_1$ in the projection of $\Omega $ to the first coordinate: after translation, its one-variable integral is bounded by polar integration on one fixed disk. This uniform bound, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate and the range estimate ( 5.27.3 ) give the asserted bound for the integrals over $B'$. Since $\varepsilon +\eta \leq t$, both estimates hold with constants depending only on $\Omega $, $p$, $B'$ and $B$. Finally, multilinearity of bounded products gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h))^ n=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n +\sum _{r=1}^{n-1} inom nr (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r.  \] The choice of $\delta $, the choice of $A$ for the top-degree term and the estimate of the mixed terms each contribute less than $	au /3$ to every test integral. This proves the required inequalities, with one choice of $h$ for all finite $p$. $\square$ Theorem 5.27.36 . u _ j-

title: Lemma 5.27.33
text: Lemma 5.27.33 . 0EE345C93AFA Fix the data $n,U,v,\varepsilon ,R,\eta ,\chi _\eta $ of lemma 5.27.29 , and write $h_ A$ for the smooth plurisubharmonic function $h$ of that lemma, regarded as a function of $A$. Put $D=\{ 0\} \times U$, and write $[D]$ for the current of integration over this hypersurface. Then, for every $1\leq r\leq n$, \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\longrightarrow \varepsilon [D]\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1} \quad \text{as currents on }\mathbb C\times U,\  A\to \infty .  \] The product on the right is integration of the restriction of the smooth form $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{r-1}$ over $D$. Proof. Write $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$, $q=\varepsilon \log (|\zeta |^2/R^2)$ and $T_ A=v-A-q$. The rank-one calculation in the proof of lemma 5.27.29 gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r=\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^ rS^ r +r\chi _\eta '(T_ A)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(T_ A) \, \mathrm dT_ A\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T_ A\wedge S^{r-1}  \] off $D$; since $h_ A$ is smooth and $D$ has measure zero, this formula determines the current. Fix a smooth compactly supported test form. On the projection of its support to $U$, the function $v$ and its derivatives are bounded. Hence the support of $\chi _\eta '(T_ A)$ lies in $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $, where $s_ A=C\exp (-A/(2\varepsilon ))$ and $C$ depends only on this compact set and the fixed data. The coefficients involving $v$ and $\chi _\eta $ are bounded at the fixed parameters, so the first summand has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$. In the second summand, the term with two derivatives of $v$ also has pairing $O(s_ A^2)$, and the two cross terms have pairing $O(s_ A)$: the derivative of $q$ in the $\zeta $ direction has size $O(|\zeta |^{-1})$, and its area integral over the disk $\{ |\zeta |\leq s_ A\} $ is $O(s_ A)$. It remains to integrate the term containing $\mathrm dq\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q$. The logarithmic change of the radial variable used for ( 5.27.30 ) leaves the factor $\varepsilon $ and the probability weight \[  r\chi _\eta '(t)^{r-1}\chi _\eta ''(t)\, \mathrm dt, \qquad -\eta \leq t\leq \eta .  \] Only the component of the test form in the $z'$ directions enters this term, and on the shrinking circles its coefficients tend uniformly to their values at $\zeta =0$. Integration in the angle therefore gives, in the limit, exactly the pairing with $\varepsilon [D]\wedge S^{r-1}$. This proves the convergence in every degree. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.27.34
text: Lemma 5.27.34 . 0950BB9BC118 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, let $K$ and $L$ be compact subsets of $\Omega $ with $K$ contained in the interior $L^\circ $ of $L$, and put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $, and let $T$ be a smooth positive closed $(r,r)$-form, $1\leq r<n$. Then \[  \int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge T \leq C_{K,L,n}(1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{n-r} \int _ L T\wedge \beta ^{n-r}.  \] Proof. Put $M=1+\| b\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Cover $K$ by finitely many balls whose larger concentric balls have closures in $L^\circ $. Replacing $b$ by $b+M$, which has the same Hessian and takes values in $[0,2M]$ on $L$, we may assume $0\leq b\leq 2M$ there. For nested cutoff functions $\psi $, integration by parts against closed forms gives \[  \int \psi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\wedge W =\int b\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi \wedge W \leq CM \int _{\operatorname {supp}\psi }\beta \wedge W,  \] where $W$ is $T$ multiplied by the remaining positive closed factors. Apply this successively to the $n-r$ Hessians of $b$. For bounded $b$, the integrations by parts are justified by local decreasing regularization and theorem 5.27.1 , with one common bound on the range. Summing over the finite cover gives the asserted constant. $\square$

title: Proposition 5.27.35
text: Proposition 5.27.35 . 6C1E4E8060FF Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain, let $b\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty (\Omega )$, $a\in \Omega $ and $c>0$. Given finitely many $f_ i\in C_ c(\Omega )$ and numbers $\tau ,t>0$, there is a smooth bounded plurisubharmonic function $h\leq 0$ on $\Omega $ such that \[  \begin{gathered} \| h\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}t\quad (1\leq p<\infty ),\\ \left|\int _\Omega f_ i\bigl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h))^ n-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n\bigr ) -cf_ i(a)\right|<\tau \quad \text{for every }i. \end{gathered}  \] For concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ and every $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$, it also satisfies \[  \int _{B'}|h|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n\leq C_{B',B,\Omega }t.  \] These constants are independent of $b,a,c$, the test functions and the tolerances. Proof. We take for $h$ a function from lemma 5.27.29 whose top-degree measure approximates $c\delta _ a$ and whose lower-degree currents are small; lemma 5.27.34 then controls the mixed terms. Write $a=(a_1,a')$ and $m=n-1$, and fix $R=2\sup _\Omega |z_1|+2$. For $\delta >0$, put $H_\delta (z')=\log (|z'-a'|^2+\delta ^2)$. By the radial calculation in the proof of proposition 5.27.31 , $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m$ is a probability measure tending to $\delta _{a'}$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Extend every $f_ i$ by zero outside $\Omega $, and choose $\delta $ such that \[  \left|c\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f_ i(a_1,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m -cf_ i(a)\right|<\tau /3\quad \text{for all }i.  \] Choose compact sets $K,L\subset \Omega $ with $K\subset L^\circ $ and $K$ containing the supports of all $f_ i$, and a nonnegative smooth cutoff function $\psi $ with compact support in $\Omega $, equal to one near $L$. Put $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Expanding the top power of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h)$, summing the bounds of lemma 5.27.34 with their binomial coefficients and the norms $\| f_ i\| _\infty $, we find $\gamma >0$ such that the mixed terms contribute less than $\tau /3$ to every test integral whenever $h$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic and \[  \int _ L(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r\wedge \beta ^{n-r}<\gamma , \qquad 1\leq r<n.  \] Fix $0<\eta \leq t/2$. Apply lemma 5.27.29 on $\mathbb C\times \mathbb C^ m$ with transverse variable $\zeta =z_1-a_1$ and $v=c^{1/m}\varepsilon ^{-1/m}H_\delta $. For $r<n$, lemma 5.27.33 gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\longrightarrow \varepsilon ^{(n-r)/(n-1)}c^{(r-1)/(n-1)} [\{ z_1=a_1\} ]\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^{r-1}  \] as $A\to \infty $. For the fixed $\delta $, the integrals of these limits against $\psi \beta ^{n-r}$ are finite, and their exponents of $\varepsilon $ are positive. Choose $0<\varepsilon \leq t/2$ so that each of them is less than $\gamma /2$. With these parameters fixed, choose $A$ so large that the integrals $\int _ L(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ r\wedge \beta ^{n-r}$ are less than $\gamma $, that $v-A\leq 0$ on the projection of $\Omega $ to the $z'$ variables, and that \[  \left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ A)^ n -c\int _{\mathbb C^ m}f_ i(a_1,z')(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m\right|<\tau /3 \quad \text{for all }i.  \] The last choice follows directly from ( 5.27.30 ), because the circles there shrink uniformly over the projected supports of the tests and $\varepsilon (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ m=c(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H_\delta )^ m$. Set $h=h_ A-\eta $. As in the proof of proposition 5.27.31 , $h$ is smooth, bounded and nonpositive on $\Omega $, with \[  \varepsilon \log (|z_1-a_1|^2/R^2)-\eta \leq h\leq 0.  \] The logarithm has $L^ p(\Omega )$ norm bounded uniformly for $a_1$ in the projection of $\Omega $ to the first coordinate: after translation, its one-variable integral is bounded by polar integration on one fixed disk. This uniform bound, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimate and the range estimate ( 5.27.3 ) give the asserted bound for the integrals over $B'$. Since $\varepsilon +\eta \leq t$, both estimates hold with constants depending only on $\Omega $, $p$, $B'$ and $B$. Finally, multilinearity of bounded products gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(b+h))^ n=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ n +\sum _{r=1}^{n-1}\binom nr (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^{n-r}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h)^ r.  \] The choice of $\delta $, the choice of $A$ for the top-degree term and the estimate of the mixed terms each contribute less than $\tau /3$ to every test integral. This proves the required inequalities, with one choice of $h$ for all finite $p$. $\square$

title: 5.27.37 Full cluster sets at the zero potential
search_title: Full cluster sets at the zero potential
text:
Theorem 5.27.36 prescribes one limit of the Monge–Ampère measures, but a single sequence of potentials can have many subsequential limits. In fact, every vaguely closed set of measures is the set of all subsequential limits for a suitable sequence of potentials tending to zero. For a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, write $\mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ for the set of positive Radon measures on $\Omega $, including zero and measures of infinite total mass, with the vague topology defined by integration against $C_ c(\Omega )$. Lemma 5.27.38 . 7F112BE621FD There are real functions $f_ i\in C_ c^\infty (\Omega )$ such that \[  d_ v(\alpha , eta )=\sum _{i\geq 1}2^{-i}  rac{\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha - eta )ight|}{1+\left|\int _\Omega f_ i(\alpha - eta )ight|}  \] is a metric inducing the vague topology on $\mathcal M_+(\Omega )$. This metric space is separable. Proof. Choose relatively compact open sets $U_\ell $ exhausting $\Omega $, with $\overline U_\ell \subset U_{\ell +1}$. For each $\ell $, choose a countable uniformly dense subset of $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ consisting of smooth compactly supported functions, extended by zero to $\Omega $; such families exist because $C_0(U_{\ell +1};\mathbb R)$ is separable and its elements can be approximated uniformly by smooth functions. Add a nonnegative smooth compactly supported cutoff function equal to one near $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and enumerate the union of all these functions as $(f_ i)$. Call the maps $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega f_ i\, \mathrm d\alpha $ the coordinates. If positive measures converge to a fixed measure in every coordinate, the cutoff coordinates give common mass bounds on each $\overline U_{\ell +1}$, and uniform approximation then gives convergence against every $g\in C_ c(\Omega )$. The same argument, applied near a fixed measure, shows that $\alpha \mapsto \int _\Omega g\, \mathrm d\alpha $ is continuous for the topology generated by the coordinates: bound the relevant cutoff coordinate on a neighborhood, choose one smooth test that is uniformly close to $g$, and shrink the neighborhood using the coordinate of that test. Thus the coordinates generate exactly the vague topology, and they separate measures. The function $s\mapsto s/(1+s)$ is increasing and subadditive on $[0,\infty )$. Applying it to the triangle inequalities for the coordinates gives the triangle inequality for $d_ v$, and $d_ v$ is positive on distinct measures because the coordinates separate them. Each coordinate is continuous for this metric, and the tails of the series are uniformly small, so the metric induces exactly the topology generated by the coordinates. Finally, the finite atomic measures with nonnegative rational weights at points of a fixed countable dense subset of $\Omega $ form a countable dense family. To approximate a measure in finitely many coordinates, partition a compact neighborhood of the supports of the corresponding tests into sets on which all these tests have small oscillation, place an atom in each set of nonzero mass, and then perturb its location and weight. Only the finite mass of that compact neighborhood is used, and the remaining tail of the metric is arbitrarily small. $\square$ The metric controls limits along corresponding subsequences: if $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ and one of the sequences converges vaguely to a fixed measure along a subsequence, then, by the triangle inequality, so does the other. Without common local mass bounds, however, $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ need not imply that $\int g(\alpha _ j- eta _ j)	o 0$ for every $g\in C_ c(\Omega )$. For example, fix $a\in \Omega $, a unit vector $e$, and numbers $r_ j\downarrow 0$ with $a+r_ je\in \Omega $, and put \[  \alpha _ j=r_ j^{-1/2}\delta _{a+r_ je},\qquad  eta _ j=r_ j^{-1/2}\delta _ a.  \] For every smooth compactly supported test, the difference of the two integrals is $O(r_ j^{1/2})$, so $d_ v(\alpha _ j, eta _ j)	o 0$ because the tails of the series are small. On the other hand, if $\chi \in C_ c^\infty (\Omega )$ equals one near $a$, the continuous test function $g(z)=\chi (z)|z-a|^{1/2}$ gives $\int g(\alpha _ j- eta _ j)=1$ for all large $j$. Theorem 5.27.39 . DCCBB28F9C78 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain. A set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ is vaguely closed if and only if there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $, tending to zero in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$: \[  F=\left\{ \mu \in \mathcal M_+(\Omega ):\  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j_ k})^ n\longrightarrow \mu 	ext{ vaguely for some }j_1<j_2<\cdots ight\} .  \] The empty set is allowed. Proof. In a metric space, the full cluster set of a sequence is the intersection of the closures of its tails: a point of this intersection can be approximated within $1/k$ at an index larger than the preceding one, successively for $k=1,2,\ldots $. The full cluster set is therefore closed, and lemma 5.27.38 proves necessity. For sufficiency, suppose first that $F$ is nonempty and closed. A subset of a separable metric space is separable, so we may choose a dense sequence $\mu _1,\mu _2,\ldots $ in $F$, repetitions allowed. Concatenating the finite lists $(\mu _1)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2,\mu _3)$, and so on, we obtain a sequence $(
u _ j)$ in which every $\mu _ k$ appears arbitrarily late. Hence every point of $F$ is the limit of a subsequence, and since $F$ is closed, no other subsequential limit occurs. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 5.27.38 , and perform the finite atomic construction from the proof of theorem 5.27.36 separately for each $j$, with background zero, target $
u _ j$ and tests $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$. Thus we approximate $
u _ j$ in these coordinates by a finite atomic measure with error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, apply proposition 5.27.35 successively with $t=	au =(jN_ j)^{-1}$; if it has none, take $u_ j=0$. The resulting smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ satisfy \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] On every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the bounds of that proposition for test measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$, with $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ and $0\leq w\leq 1$, also sum to $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$. Dividing by a positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. These estimates require neither convergence of the targets $
u _ j$ nor a common local mass bound for them. Splitting the series defining the metric after its first $j$ terms gives \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Consequently, the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences, and hence the same full cluster set $F$. $\square$ For subharmonic functions on a planar domain, by contrast, $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ convergence to zero forces $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j	o 0$ in the sense of distributions, and positivity, tested against compactly supported cutoff functions, then gives vague convergence to zero. The freedom in the theorem therefore begins in dimension two.

title: Theorem 5.27.39
text:
Theorem 5.27.39 . DCCBB28F9C78 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 2$, be a bounded domain. A set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$ is vaguely closed if and only if there are smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ on $\Omega $, tending to zero in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$: \[  F=\left\{ \mu \in \mathcal M_+(\Omega ):\  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j_ k})^ n\longrightarrow \mu 	ext{ vaguely for some }j_1<j_2<\cdots ight\} .  \] The empty set is allowed. Proof. In a metric space, the full cluster set of a sequence is the intersection of the closures of its tails: a point of this intersection can be approximated within $1/k$ at an index larger than the preceding one, successively for $k=1,2,\ldots $. The full cluster set is therefore closed, and lemma 5.27.38 proves necessity. For sufficiency, suppose first that $F$ is nonempty and closed. A subset of a separable metric space is separable, so we may choose a dense sequence $\mu _1,\mu _2,\ldots $ in $F$, repetitions allowed. Concatenating the finite lists $(\mu _1)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2)$, $(\mu _1,\mu _2,\mu _3)$, and so on, we obtain a sequence $(
u _ j)$ in which every $\mu _ k$ appears arbitrarily late. Hence every point of $F$ is the limit of a subsequence, and since $F$ is closed, no other subsequential limit occurs. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 5.27.38 , and perform the finite atomic construction from the proof of theorem 5.27.36 separately for each $j$, with background zero, target $
u _ j$ and tests $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$. Thus we approximate $
u _ j$ in these coordinates by a finite atomic measure with error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, apply proposition 5.27.35 successively with $t=	au =(jN_ j)^{-1}$; if it has none, take $u_ j=0$. The resulting smooth bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq 0$ satisfy \[  \| u_ j\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] On every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the bounds of that proposition for test measures $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$, with $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ and $0\leq w\leq 1$, also sum to $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$. Dividing by a positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. These estimates require neither convergence of the targets $
u _ j$ nor a common local mass bound for them. Splitting the series defining the metric after its first $j$ terms gives \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Consequently, the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences, and hence the same full cluster set $F$. $\square$

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a domain, $n\geq 1$, and let $b$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $\Omega $. If potentials approach $b$ from below in local capacity, every limit of their Monge–Ampère measures must dominate $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Truncation at a fixed distance below $b$ provides a common bound, and plurifine locality keeps the measure outside the small set where the truncation changes the potential. Lemma 5.27.41 . CD407359DDEA Let $b,u_ j$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $ with $u_ j\leq b$ and $u_ j	o b$ in local capacity. Then, for every nonnegative $f\in C_ c(\Omega )$, \[  \liminf _{j	o \infty }\int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n \geq \int _\Omega f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n.  \] In particular, every vague subsequential limit of $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n$ dominates $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$. Proof. First suppose that $f$ is supported in $B'$, where $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $ are concentric balls. Put $v_ j=\max (u_ j,b-1)$ and $E_ j=\{ u_ j\leq b-1\} $. The functions $v_ j$ lie between $b-1$ and $b$ and tend to $b$ in local capacity. Because of their common bounds, the continuity of bounded products recalled in section 5.27 gives $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n	o (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ vaguely on $B$. With $R=\sup _ B b-\inf _ B b+1$, the capacity bound for bounded potentials gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f) \leq R^ n\operatorname {cap}(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f,B) \longrightarrow 0,  \] where the limit holds because $E_ j\subset \{ |u_ j-b|>1/2\} $. On the plurifine open Borel set $\{ u_ j>b-1\} $ we have $v_ j=u_ j$, so theorem 5.27.1 shows that the two measures agree there. By positivity, \[  \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n \geq \int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n -\| f\| _\infty (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^ n(E_ j\cap \operatorname {supp}f).  \] Taking the lower limit proves the assertion for such $f$. For a general $f$, use a finite nonnegative partition of unity subordinate to a cover of its support by such balls. Applying the inequality along a vaguely convergent subsequence proves the final assertion. $\square$ Theorem 5.27.42 . 745A94C03209 Assume that $\Omega $ is bounded, $n\geq 2$, and $b\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )\cap L^\infty (\Omega )$. For a set $F\subset \mathcal M_+(\Omega )$, the following are equivalent: $F$ is vaguely closed and every $\mu \in F$ satisfies $\mu \geq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$; there are bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_ j\leq b$ on $\Omega $, converging to $b$ in $L^ p(\Omega )$ for every $1\leq p<\infty $ and in local capacity, whose full vague cluster set is $F$. The empty set is allowed. If $b$ is smooth, every $u_ j$ in the second condition can be chosen smooth. Proof. If the second condition holds, lemma 5.27.41 gives the measure inequality, and the full cluster set is closed in the metrizable vague topology by the argument at the beginning of the proof of theorem 5.27.39 . Conversely, assume the first condition. If $F$ is nonempty, the concatenation of a dense sequence used in the proof of theorem 5.27.39 gives measures $
u _ j\in F$ whose full vague cluster set is $F$. If $F$ is empty, take $
u _ j=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+j\delta _ a$ for a fixed $a\in \Omega $. A nonnegative compactly supported test function equal to one at $a$ has integral at least $j$ against $
u _ j$, so this sequence has no vaguely convergent subsequence. In either case, $
u _ j-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ is a positive Radon measure. Let $(f_ i)$ and $d_ v$ be as in lemma 5.27.38 . For each $j$, approximate the excess $
u _ j-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n$ against $f_1,\ldots ,f_ j$ by a positive finite atomic measure, with each error less than $1/j$. If this measure has $N_ j>0$ atoms, perform the construction from the proof of theorem 5.27.36 , starting at $b$ and using $	au =t=(jN_ j)^{-1}$ for each atom; if it has none, take $u_ j=b$. Summing the estimates of proposition 5.27.35 gives \[  \| u_ j-b\| _{L^ p(\Omega )}\leq C_{\Omega ,p}/j, \qquad \left|\int _\Omega f_ i igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n-
u _ j igr )ight| <2/j\quad (i\leq j).  \] For every fixed pair of concentric balls $B'\Subset B\Subset \Omega $, the same construction bounds the integral of $|u_ j-b|$ over $B'$ against $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ n$ by $C_{B',B,\Omega }/j$, for every $w\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $0\leq w\leq 1$. Dividing by a fixed positive threshold and taking the supremum over $w$ gives convergence in local capacity. Each $u_ j$ is bounded and lies below $b$, and it is smooth when $b$ is smooth. One sequence serves all finite $p$, and no common local mass bound on the $
u _ j$ is needed. The error in the first $j$ coordinates and the tail of the series yield \[  d_ v igl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j)^ n,
u _ j igr )\leq 2/j+2^{-j}\longrightarrow 0.  \] By the remark following lemma 5.27.38 , the two sequences of measures have the same limits along corresponding subsequences. Hence their full vague cluster sets coincide. $\square$ For example, on the unit ball the function $b=|z|^2-1$ has nonzero Monge–Ampère measure. For every point $a$ of the ball, the theorem allows the cluster sets $\{ (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n\} $, $\{ (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b)^ n+\delta _ a\} $ and the empty set, but it excludes $\{ 0\} $; this exclusion relies on the convergence in local capacity. In dimension one, $L^1$ convergence alone forces $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j	o \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b$ vaguely, so the full cluster set is always $\{ \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\} $.

title: 5.28 Products with smooth backgrounds
text:
The Bedford–Taylor construction also defines products of currents of the form $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ with $u$ locally bounded: one expands them into Hessians of plurisubharmonic functions and smooth forms. Since the result does not depend on the local correction, these products are defined globally. Their positivity is not visible term by term; it follows from the lower curvature bound by freezing the coefficients of the background. For a smooth real $(1,1)$-form $\theta $ and a function $v$, we write $\theta _ v=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$, and similarly $\omega _ v=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ for other backgrounds. Fix $1\leq k\leq n$. Let $u$ be locally bounded and $\theta $-plurisubharmonic. On a relatively compact coordinate ball with coordinates $z$, choose $A>0$ such that $p=u+q$ is plurisubharmonic, where $q=A|z|^2$. Set $\beta =\theta -\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q$ and define C87F0ACE9C76 5.28.1 \begin{equation}  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ k :=\sum _{j=0}^ k\binom {k}{j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ j\wedge \beta ^{k-j}. \end{equation} Each summand is a product from theorem 5.27.1 multiplied by a smooth form. The individual terms of this expansion need not be positive. Proposition 5.28.2 . 3EDAB69A7289 The construction ( 5.28.1 ) and its mixed version are independent of the local correction $q$ and of the decomposition of each current into a smooth form and the Hessian of a potential. They define global products of currents with locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic potentials. These products are symmetric, multilinear and plurifinely local, and they do not charge pluripolar sets. If every factor is positive, their mixed product is positive. Proof. On the intersection of two coordinate balls, the two corrected potentials differ by a smooth function. The rule $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(p+f)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$, for bounded $p$ and smooth $f$ in bounded local products, follows by smooth approximation; together with the binomial formula, it shows that the two expansions agree. The same argument handles a smooth change in the decomposition of a current. Moreover, any two decompositions of the same $(1,1)$-current differ by a smooth function: the difference of the potentials has a smooth Hessian, and taking its local Euclidean trace and applying elliptic regularity shows that it is smooth. Symmetry, multilinearity and locality then follow term by term. Bounded Bedford–Taylor products wedged with smooth forms have locally finite variation and do not charge pluripolar sets, so these properties pass to the finite expansion as well. It remains to prove positivity, which does not follow from the signs of the summands. Write the factors as $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, $1\leq i\leq k$, where each $\theta _ i$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and each $u_ i$ is locally bounded and quasi-plurisubharmonic, and assume $T_ i\geq 0$. Fix $\varepsilon >0$, a point of the coordinate ball and a positive constant form $\kappa $. On a sufficiently small neighborhood of the point, each $\theta _ i$ is close to a constant, hence closed, form $\theta _ i'$: \[  -\varepsilon \kappa \leq \theta _ i-\theta _ i' \leq \varepsilon \kappa .  \] Then $S_ i=\theta _ i'+\varepsilon \kappa +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i\geq T_ i$ is a positive closed current there, with a bounded local plurisubharmonic potential, and \[  T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa =S_ i+(\theta _ i-\theta _ i'+\varepsilon \kappa ),  \] where the last term is a smooth semipositive form. Expanding the product of the currents $T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa $ therefore gives a sum of positive currents, so this product is positive near the chosen point. Such neighborhoods, although they depend on $\varepsilon $, cover the coordinate ball, so the product of the $T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa $ is positive on the whole ball. By multilinearity, it converges weakly to the product of the $T_ i$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, which proves positivity. $\square$ The local expansion also gives continuity along decreasing sequences of uniformly locally bounded potentials: apply theorem 5.27.1 to the corrected potentials and sum the finitely many terms. Since $X$ is compact, every bounded top-degree product has finite total mass. For bounded $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ we write $\mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=(\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n$. Decreasing maxima compare the products of two ordered potentials on the set where they are equal. The comparison also holds in the presence of fixed positive factors, which will be useful in integration by parts. Lemma 5.28.3 . 5087175B2C39 Let $a\leq b$ be locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on an $n$-dimensional complex manifold, and let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form such that $\theta _ a,\theta _ b\geq 0$. For $1\leq k\leq n$, let $W$ be a product of $n-k$ positive currents with smooth backgrounds and locally bounded potentials, with $W=1$ when $k=n$. Then \[  \mathbf1_{\{ a=b\} }\theta _ a^ k\wedge W \leq \mathbf1_{\{ a=b\} }\theta _ b^ k\wedge W.  \] Proof. The functions $m_\delta =\max (a+\delta ,b)$ satisfy $b\leq m_\delta \leq b+\delta $ and decrease to $b$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$. By lemma 5.24.1 and proposition 5.28.2 , the products $\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W$ are positive, and by bounded decreasing continuity they converge weakly to $\theta _ b^ k\wedge W$. On the plurifine open set $\{ a+\delta >b\} $, which contains $\{ a=b\} $, we have $m_\delta =a+\delta $, so plurifine locality identifies the restriction of $\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W$ to this set with that of $\theta _ a^ k\wedge W$. Hence, for every compact set $K\subset \{ a=b\} $ in a coordinate chart, the upper semicontinuity of the mass of compact sets under weak convergence gives \[  \int _ K\theta _ a^ k\wedge W =\lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}\int _ K\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W \leq \int _ K\theta _ b^ k\wedge W.  \] Since the measures are locally finite, inner regularity extends this inequality to all Borel subsets of the contact set, and a countable cover by charts proves the assertion. $\square$ The products commute with pullback by holomorphic submersions. Here the pullback of a current is defined in local product coordinates by pulling back its distributional coefficients. Lemma 5.28.4 . 636D22C6199B Let $\pi :Z\to Y$ be a holomorphic submersion of complex manifolds. For $1\leq r\leq \dim Z$, let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ r$ be locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $Y$, and let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ r$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $Y$. Then \[  \bigwedge _{i=1}^ r\bigl (\pi ^*\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i\circ \pi )\bigr ) =\pi ^*\! \left(\bigwedge _{i=1}^ r(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i)\right).  \] For $r>\dim Y$, the product on the left vanishes, and the right-hand side is interpreted as zero. Proof. Work in product coordinates in which $\pi $ is a coordinate projection. On a smaller chart of $Y$, choose smooth quadratic functions $q_ i$ such that $p_ i=u_ i+q_ i$ is plurisubharmonic, and approximate each $p_ i$ by a decreasing sequence of smooth plurisubharmonic functions. Their pullbacks have the same properties on the product chart, and for smooth forms pullback commutes with wedge products. Applying bounded decreasing continuity to the local expansions ( 5.28.1 ) on both charts gives the asserted identity, because pullback of currents by the projection is weakly continuous: pairing the pullback with a compactly supported test form amounts to pairing the original current with the integral of the test form over the fiber variables. If $r>\dim Y$, every smooth approximating product vanishes for degree reasons, and so does its limit. $\square$ For $C^{1,1}$ potentials, these products of currents agree with the products of their measurable Hessian coefficients. Proposition 5.28.5 . 6CBD4E4A94B6 Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ k$ be locally $C^{1,1}$ quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, and let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ k$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms. Then the bounded product \[  (\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ k+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)  \] is the form with locally bounded measurable coefficients obtained by taking the wedge product of the factors pointwise almost everywhere. Proof. On a smaller coordinate ball, add a common smooth quadratic function $q$ such that each $u_ i+q$ is plurisubharmonic, and convolve with a smooth radial probability kernel. The Hessians of the convolutions are uniformly locally bounded and converge to the weak Hessians in every $L^ s$ space with $s<\infty $, so their finite products converge in $L^1$ on smaller balls. Since the potentials converge uniformly, the continuity of bounded Bedford–Taylor products identifies this limit with the pluripotential product. Expanding with respect to the smooth correction, as in ( 5.28.1 ), proves the assertion for the original factors. $\square$ When the Hessian coefficients are bounded, a positive lower bound for the top-degree product gives a lower bound for the current itself. Proposition 5.28.6 . 2A843EB4B4AE Let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form, let $h$ be a Hermitian form on $X$, and let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cap C^{1,1}(X)$. If \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n\geq a h^ n  \] for a constant $a>0$, then $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq \delta h$ as a current for some $\delta >0$. Proof. Put $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Its measurable coefficients are bounded on the compact manifold $X$, so there is $K>0$ such that, almost everywhere, the eigenvalues of $T$ relative to $h$ lie in $[0,K]$. By proposition 5.28.5 , their product is the density of $T^ n$ with respect to $h^ n$, and hence it is at least $a$. Each eigenvalue is therefore at least $a/K^{n-1}$ almost everywhere. This inequality of matrices almost everywhere gives the asserted inequality of currents with $\delta =a/K^{n-1}$. $\square$ The mixed Monge–Ampère inequality of theorem 5.27.5 also holds after a smooth background is added. In the following three lemmas, $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ is an open set and $\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$. Lemma 5.28.7 . 6C81352D9EE7 Let $T_ i=\vartheta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i\geq 0$, $i=1,2$, where the $\vartheta _ i$ are smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $U$ and the $u_ i$ are locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $U$. If \[  T_ i^ n\geq F_ i\beta ^ n, \qquad F_ i\geq 0\text{ measurable},  \] then, for every integer $0\leq k\leq n$, C06268DF902D 5.28.8 \begin{equation}  T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k} \geq F_1^{k/n}F_2^{(n-k)/n}\beta ^ n. \end{equation} Consequently, for $a,b\geq 0$, 4547B4E0976D 5.28.9 \begin{equation}  (aT_1+bT_2)^ n \geq \bigl (aF_1^{1/n}+bF_2^{1/n}\bigr )^ n\beta ^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $W\Subset U$. Since the forms $\vartheta _ i$ are smooth, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every $x\in W$ and every small ball $B_ r(x)$, the constant forms \[  A_ i=\vartheta _ i(x)+Cr\beta  \] satisfy $0\leq S_ i\leq 2Cr\beta $ on $B_ r(x)$, where $S_ i=A_ i-\vartheta _ i$. If $q_ i$ is a quadratic potential for $A_ i$, then $u_ i+q_ i$ is plurisubharmonic on $B_ r(x)$ and \[  \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+q_ i)\bigr )^ n=(T_ i+S_ i)^ n\geq F_ i\beta ^ n.  \] Apply theorem 5.27.5 to these two closed Hessians. After expansion, every term other than $T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k}$ contains some $S_ i$ and is therefore bounded by $C'r\mu $, where \[  \mu =\sum _{\ell +m\leq n-1}T_1^\ell \wedge T_2^ m\wedge \beta ^{n-\ell -m}  \] is a locally finite measure. A finite cover and a partition of unity give, on $W$, \[  T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k} \geq F_1^{k/n}F_2^{(n-k)/n}\beta ^ n-C'r\mu .  \] Letting $r\downarrow 0$ proves ( 5.28.8 ), and the binomial expansion then gives ( 5.28.9 ). $\square$ Lemma 5.28.10 . C5B4B944142C Let $\vartheta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $U$. Suppose that $u$ is continuous, $T=\vartheta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq 0$, and $T^ n\geq g^ n\beta ^ n$ with $g\geq 0$ continuous. For a nonnegative convolution kernel $\chi _\delta $ of mass one, D12EFD5440D2 5.28.11 \begin{equation}  (T*\chi _\delta )^ n\geq (g*\chi _\delta )^ n\beta ^ n \end{equation} on every smaller domain on which the convolution is defined. Proof. Approximate the convolution by finite convex combinations of translates, and apply ( 5.28.9 ), extended by induction to finitely many terms. Along these approximations, the background forms converge smoothly and the potentials converge uniformly on compact sets. To pass to the limit, add a common quadratic function and write the difference of two $n$-th powers as a telescoping sum. After pairing with a test form, integration by parts bounds each term by the uniform distance between the potentials times the mass of a mixed current, and successive integration against nested cutoff functions bounds these masses uniformly. Thus the products of the bounded potentials converge, and ( 5.28.11 ) follows. $\square$ For a positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $U$, write $T_{\mathrm{ac}}$ for the measurable $(1,1)$-form whose coefficients are the absolutely continuous parts of the coefficients of $T$, and define $\det _\beta T_{\mathrm{ac}}$ by $(T_{\mathrm{ac}})^ n=(\det _\beta T_{\mathrm{ac}})\beta ^ n$. When the top-degree product has a continuous density, the convolution estimate identifies this determinant. Lemma 5.28.12 . 00AB47766404 Let $u$ be continuous and $T=\vartheta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq 0$, with $\vartheta $ a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $U$. If $T^ n=F\beta ^ n$ for a continuous function $F\geq 0$, then \[  \det _\beta T_{\mathrm{ac}}=F\qquad \text{almost everywhere}.  \] Proof. Take a nonnegative smooth radial mollifier $\chi _\delta $ supported in the ball of radius $\delta $. Then $T*\chi _\delta \to T_{\mathrm{ac}}$ almost everywhere. Indeed, the convolutions of the absolutely continuous parts converge at Lebesgue points of their densities, while the convolution of the singular part $\lambda _ s$ of a coefficient measure is bounded by $C\delta ^{-2n}|\lambda _ s|(B_\delta )$, which tends to zero almost everywhere by the differentiation theorem for measures. Applying lemma 5.28.10 with $g=F^{1/n}$ and letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ gives $\det _\beta T_{\mathrm{ac}}\geq F$. For the reverse inequality, write the convolved current as the Hessian of a decreasing regularization of a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function plus a convergent smooth correction. The continuity of bounded products gives $(T*\chi _\delta )^ n\rightharpoonup T^ n$. Fatou's lemma, applied against a nonnegative compactly supported test function, then gives $\det _\beta T_{\mathrm{ac}}\, \beta ^ n\leq T^ n=F\beta ^ n$. $\square$ Lemma 5.28.13 . D263A93C1D69 Let $h\leq a$ be locally bounded $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions, and let $\chi $ be a smooth function on a neighborhood of $(-\infty ,0]$ with $0\leq \chi '\leq 1$ and $\chi ''\geq 0$. Then $w=a+\chi (h-a)$ is $\theta $-plurisubharmonic and \[  \theta _ w=(1-\chi '(h-a))\theta _ a+\chi '(h-a)\theta _ h +\chi ''(h-a)\, \mathrm{d}(h-a)\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}(h-a).  \] In particular, $\theta _ w^ n\geq \chi '(h-a)^ n\theta _ h^ n$. The positivity of $\theta _ w$ and this inequality also hold for convex functions $\chi $ of class $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals with $0\leq \chi '\leq 1$. Proof. The function $G(x,y)=x+\chi (y-x)$, for $y\leq x$, is convex and nondecreasing in each variable: its first derivatives are $1-\chi '$ and $\chi '$, and its Hessian is \[  \chi ''\begin{pmatrix} 1

& -1

\\ -1

& 1

\end{pmatrix}\geq 0.  \] For smooth potentials, the chain rule gives the identity. For bounded potentials, add a common quadratic correction and convolve. Convolution preserves the order of the potentials, and since $G(x+r,y+r)=r+G(x,y)$, adding the same correction to both arguments adds it to $G$. The bounded chain rule ( 5.27.9 ) and its products with the gradient term give the identity in the limit. Freezing the smooth background as in the proof of proposition 5.28.2 preserves the exact lower bound. Every term on the right is positive, and the positivity of bounded mixed products gives the last assertion. For a convex weight of class $C^{1,1}$, extend it convexly across zero with derivative in $[0,1]$, and smooth it in one variable. The smooth convex weights and their first derivatives converge uniformly on compact intervals, and the derivatives stay in $[0,1]$. On each smaller coordinate ball, the corresponding potentials converge uniformly to $w$. The continuity of bounded products gives convergence of their top powers, while the weights on the right-hand side converge uniformly against the fixed measure $\theta _ h^ n$. Passing to the limit proves the positivity and the product inequality with the original smooth background. $\square$

title: Proposition 5.28.2
text: Proposition 5.28.2 . 3EDAB69A7289 The construction ( 5.28.1 ) and its mixed version are independent of the local correction $q$ and of the decomposition of each current into a smooth form and the Hessian of a potential. They define global products of currents with locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic potentials. These products are symmetric, multilinear and plurifinely local, and they do not charge pluripolar sets. If every factor is positive, their mixed product is positive. Proof. On the intersection of two coordinate balls, the two corrected potentials differ by a smooth function. The rule $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(p+f)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$, for bounded $p$ and smooth $f$ in bounded local products, follows by smooth approximation; together with the binomial formula, it shows that the two expansions agree. The same argument handles a smooth change in the decomposition of a current. Moreover, any two decompositions of the same $(1,1)$-current differ by a smooth function: the difference of the potentials has a smooth Hessian, and taking its local Euclidean trace and applying elliptic regularity shows that it is smooth. Symmetry, multilinearity and locality then follow term by term. Bounded Bedford–Taylor products wedged with smooth forms have locally finite variation and do not charge pluripolar sets, so these properties pass to the finite expansion as well. It remains to prove positivity, which does not follow from the signs of the summands. Write the factors as $T_ i=\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, $1\leq i\leq k$, where each $\theta _ i$ is a smooth real $(1,1)$-form and each $u_ i$ is locally bounded and quasi-plurisubharmonic, and assume $T_ i\geq 0$. Fix $\varepsilon >0$, a point of the coordinate ball and a positive constant form $\kappa $. On a sufficiently small neighborhood of the point, each $\theta _ i$ is close to a constant, hence closed, form $\theta _ i'$: \[  -\varepsilon \kappa \leq \theta _ i-\theta _ i' \leq \varepsilon \kappa .  \] Then $S_ i=\theta _ i'+\varepsilon \kappa +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i\geq T_ i$ is a positive closed current there, with a bounded local plurisubharmonic potential, and \[  T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa =S_ i+(\theta _ i-\theta _ i'+\varepsilon \kappa ),  \] where the last term is a smooth semipositive form. Expanding the product of the currents $T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa $ therefore gives a sum of positive currents, so this product is positive near the chosen point. Such neighborhoods, although they depend on $\varepsilon $, cover the coordinate ball, so the product of the $T_ i+2\varepsilon \kappa $ is positive on the whole ball. By multilinearity, it converges weakly to the product of the $T_ i$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, which proves positivity. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.28.3
text: Lemma 5.28.3 . 5087175B2C39 Let $a\leq b$ be locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on an $n$-dimensional complex manifold, and let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form such that $\theta _ a,\theta _ b\geq 0$. For $1\leq k\leq n$, let $W$ be a product of $n-k$ positive currents with smooth backgrounds and locally bounded potentials, with $W=1$ when $k=n$. Then \[  \mathbf1_{\{ a=b\} }\theta _ a^ k\wedge W \leq \mathbf1_{\{ a=b\} }\theta _ b^ k\wedge W.  \] Proof. The functions $m_\delta =\max (a+\delta ,b)$ satisfy $b\leq m_\delta \leq b+\delta $ and decrease to $b$ as $\delta \downarrow 0$. By lemma 5.24.1 and proposition 5.28.2 , the products $\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W$ are positive, and by bounded decreasing continuity they converge weakly to $\theta _ b^ k\wedge W$. On the plurifine open set $\{ a+\delta >b\} $, which contains $\{ a=b\} $, we have $m_\delta =a+\delta $, so plurifine locality identifies the restriction of $\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W$ to this set with that of $\theta _ a^ k\wedge W$. Hence, for every compact set $K\subset \{ a=b\} $ in a coordinate chart, the upper semicontinuity of the mass of compact sets under weak convergence gives \[  \int _ K\theta _ a^ k\wedge W =\lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}\int _ K\theta _{m_\delta }^ k\wedge W \leq \int _ K\theta _ b^ k\wedge W.  \] Since the measures are locally finite, inner regularity extends this inequality to all Borel subsets of the contact set, and a countable cover by charts proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.28.4
text: Lemma 5.28.4 . 636D22C6199B Let $\pi :Z\to Y$ be a holomorphic submersion of complex manifolds. For $1\leq r\leq \dim Z$, let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ r$ be locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $Y$, and let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ r$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $Y$. Then \[  \bigwedge _{i=1}^ r\bigl (\pi ^*\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i\circ \pi )\bigr ) =\pi ^*\! \left(\bigwedge _{i=1}^ r(\theta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i)\right).  \] For $r>\dim Y$, the product on the left vanishes, and the right-hand side is interpreted as zero. Proof. Work in product coordinates in which $\pi $ is a coordinate projection. On a smaller chart of $Y$, choose smooth quadratic functions $q_ i$ such that $p_ i=u_ i+q_ i$ is plurisubharmonic, and approximate each $p_ i$ by a decreasing sequence of smooth plurisubharmonic functions. Their pullbacks have the same properties on the product chart, and for smooth forms pullback commutes with wedge products. Applying bounded decreasing continuity to the local expansions ( 5.28.1 ) on both charts gives the asserted identity, because pullback of currents by the projection is weakly continuous: pairing the pullback with a compactly supported test form amounts to pairing the original current with the integral of the test form over the fiber variables. If $r>\dim Y$, every smooth approximating product vanishes for degree reasons, and so does its limit. $\square$

title: Proposition 5.28.5
text: Proposition 5.28.5 . 6CBD4E4A94B6 Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ k$ be locally $C^{1,1}$ quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, and let $\theta _1,\ldots ,\theta _ k$ be smooth real $(1,1)$-forms. Then the bounded product \[  (\theta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (\theta _ k+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)  \] is the form with locally bounded measurable coefficients obtained by taking the wedge product of the factors pointwise almost everywhere. Proof. On a smaller coordinate ball, add a common smooth quadratic function $q$ such that each $u_ i+q$ is plurisubharmonic, and convolve with a smooth radial probability kernel. The Hessians of the convolutions are uniformly locally bounded and converge to the weak Hessians in every $L^ s$ space with $s<\infty $, so their finite products converge in $L^1$ on smaller balls. Since the potentials converge uniformly, the continuity of bounded Bedford–Taylor products identifies this limit with the pluripotential product. Expanding with respect to the smooth correction, as in ( 5.28.1 ), proves the assertion for the original factors. $\square$

title: Proposition 5.28.6
text: Proposition 5.28.6 . 2A843EB4B4AE Let $\theta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form, let $h$ be a Hermitian form on $X$, and let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\cap C^{1,1}(X)$. If \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n\geq a h^ n  \] for a constant $a>0$, then $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq \delta h$ as a current for some $\delta >0$. Proof. Put $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Its measurable coefficients are bounded on the compact manifold $X$, so there is $K>0$ such that, almost everywhere, the eigenvalues of $T$ relative to $h$ lie in $[0,K]$. By proposition 5.28.5 , their product is the density of $T^ n$ with respect to $h^ n$, and hence it is at least $a$. Each eigenvalue is therefore at least $a/K^{n-1}$ almost everywhere. This inequality of matrices almost everywhere gives the asserted inequality of currents with $\delta =a/K^{n-1}$. $\square$

title: Lemma 5.28.7
text: Lemma 5.28.7 . 6C81352D9EE7 Let $T_ i=\vartheta _ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i\geq 0$, $i=1,2$, where the $\vartheta _ i$ are smooth real $(1,1)$-forms on $U$ and the $u_ i$ are locally bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $U$. If \[  T_ i^ n\geq F_ i\beta ^ n, \qquad F_ i\geq 0\text{ measurable},  \] then, for every integer $0\leq k\leq n$, C06268DF902D 5.28.8 \begin{equation}  T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k} \geq F_1^{k/n}F_2^{(n-k)/n}\beta ^ n. \end{equation} Consequently, for $a,b\geq 0$, 4547B4E0976D 5.28.9 \begin{equation}  (aT_1+bT_2)^ n \geq \bigl (aF_1^{1/n}+bF_2^{1/n}\bigr )^ n\beta ^ n. \end{equation} Proof. Fix $W\Subset U$. Since the forms $\vartheta _ i$ are smooth, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every $x\in W$ and every small ball $B_ r(x)$, the constant forms \[  A_ i=\vartheta _ i(x)+Cr\beta  \] satisfy $0\leq S_ i\leq 2Cr\beta $ on $B_ r(x)$, where $S_ i=A_ i-\vartheta _ i$. If $q_ i$ is a quadratic potential for $A_ i$, then $u_ i+q_ i$ is plurisubharmonic on $B_ r(x)$ and \[  \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+q_ i)\bigr )^ n=(T_ i+S_ i)^ n\geq F_ i\beta ^ n.  \] Apply theorem 5.27.5 to these two closed Hessians. After expansion, every term other than $T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k}$ contains some $S_ i$ and is therefore bounded by $C'r\mu $, where \[  \mu =\sum _{\ell +m\leq n-1}T_1^\ell \wedge T_2^ m\wedge \beta ^{n-\ell -m}  \] is a locally finite measure. A finite cover and a partition of unity give, on $W$, \[  T_1^ k\wedge T_2^{n-k} \geq F_1^{k/n}F_2^{(n-k)/n}\beta ^ n-C'r\mu .  \] Letting $r\downarrow 0$ proves ( 5.28.8 ), and the binomial expansion then gives ( 5.28.9 ). $\square$

title: Equation 5.28.8

title: Lemma 5.28.10
text: Lemma 5.28.10 . C5B4B944142C Let $\vartheta $ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $U$. Suppose that $u$ is continuous, $T=\vartheta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\geq 0$, and $T^ n\geq g^ n\beta ^ n$ with $g\geq 0$ continuous. For a nonnegative convolution kernel $\chi _\delta $ of mass one, D12EFD5440D2 5.28.11 \begin{equation}  (T*\chi _\delta )^ n\geq (g*\chi _\delta )^ n\beta ^ n \end{equation} on every smaller domain on which the convolution is defined. Proof. Approximate the convolution by finite convex combinations of translates, and apply ( 5.28.9 ), extended by induction to finitely many terms. Along these approximations, the background forms converge smoothly and the potentials converge uniformly on compact sets. Thus the products of the bounded potentials converge, and ( 5.28.11 ) follows. $\square$

title: 5.29 Hermitian capacity
text: After a fixed rescaling, a local capacity test can be glued to a constant function and so becomes a global potential on $X$. This compares the local Bedford–Taylor capacity with a capacity defined by global potentials, and it transfers to $X$ both the volume–capacity estimate and an estimate for the sublevel sets of normalized potentials. For a Borel set $E\subset X$, the Hermitian capacity of $E$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_\omega (E) =\sup _{v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega ),\  0\leq v\leq 1} \int _ E(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n,  \] where the products are those of proposition 5.28.2 . Their local expansion and ( 5.27.3 ) show that $\operatorname {Cap}_\omega (X)<+\infty $. On relatively compact coordinate balls, a fixed smooth correction bounds the measures of global tests by a constant times the corresponding local capacity. Conversely, the gluing construction in the proof of lemma 5.29.2 below bounds local capacity by global capacity. Consequently, the quasi-continuity of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions and the characterization of sets of capacity zero recalled in section 5.27 hold for $\operatorname {Cap}_\omega $. A sequence $u_ j$ converges to $u$ in capacity if \[  \operatorname {Cap}_\omega (\{ |u_ j-u|>\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{for every }\delta >0,  \] where pole sets may be omitted. To compare with another Hermitian form $\omega '$, choose $C\geq 1$ with $\omega '\leq C\omega $. Every test $0\leq v\leq 1$ for $\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega '}$ gives a test $v/C$ for $\operatorname {Cap}_\omega $, and the positivity of mixed products gives \[  (\omega '+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\leq C^ n(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v/C))^ n.  \] Thus $\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega '}\leq C^ n\operatorname {Cap}_\omega $. Interchanging the two forms shows that the capacities are equivalent up to fixed multiplicative constants, so convergence in capacity does not depend on the choice of $\omega $. Finally, the continuity statements for bounded products in section 5.27 pass to the products with smooth backgrounds, by their local expansion and a finite cover.

title: 5.29.1 Capacity estimates
text: In this subsection we abbreviate $\operatorname {Cap}=\operatorname {Cap}_\omega $, and, as before, $\omega _ v=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$. Lemma 5.29.2 . 5CEF121C5391 There are constants $a,C>0$ such that 87E51BAEC1C0 5.29.3 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Vol}(E)\leq C\exp \bigl (-a\operatorname {Cap}(E)^{-1/n}\bigr ) \end{equation} for every Borel set $E\subset X$. Moreover, for every $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with $\sup _ Xu=0$ and every $t>1$, 3EF8F920CDD3 5.29.4 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Cap}(\{ u<-t\} )\leq C/t. \end{equation} Proof. Cover $X$ by finitely many coordinate balls $B'_ j$, with larger concentric balls $B_ j$, $B'_ j\Subset B_ j$. A local capacity test $0\leq v\leq 1$ on $B_ j$ can be turned into a global test as follows. Choose a smooth function $\chi _ j$ with $-2\leq \chi _ j\leq 0$, equal to zero near $\overline{B'_ j}$ and to $-2$ near $\partial B_ j$. Choose $\delta >0$ so small that \[  \omega +\delta \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j\geq 0,\qquad 3\delta /2\leq 1.  \] The function \[  V=\max \{ \delta (v+\chi _ j),-\delta /2\} +\delta /2 \quad \hbox{on }B_ j, \qquad V=0\quad \hbox{outside }B_ j,  \] is $\omega $-plurisubharmonic on $X$, because near $\partial B_ j$ the constant branch is the larger one, and it takes values between zero and one. On $B'_ j$ we have $\omega _ V\geq \delta \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$. By the positivity of bounded products, \[  \operatorname {cap}(E\cap B'_ j,B_ j) \leq \delta ^{-n}\operatorname {Cap}(E).  \] The local volume–capacity estimate, summed over the finite cover, proves ( 5.29.3 ). For the second estimate, choose on each $B_ j$ a smooth negative quadratic function $r_ j$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}r_ j\geq \omega $. For every global test $0\leq v\leq 1$, the functions $u+r_ j\leq 0$ and $v+r_ j$ are plurisubharmonic on $B_ j$. Thus \[  \begin{split}  \int _{\{ u<-t\} }\omega _ v^ n & \leq t^{-1}\int _ X(-u)\omega _ v^ n\\ & \leq t^{-1}\sum _ j\int _{B'_ j}(-u-r_ j) \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+r_ j)\bigr )^ n\\ & \leq \frac Ct\left(1+\int _ X|u|\, \mathrm{d}V\right). \end{split}  \] Here the second inequality uses $\omega _ v\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+r_ j)$, and the third is the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg inequality, applied to local test functions with a common bound. The $L^1$ bound for normalized potentials in theorem 5.25.2 completes the proof after taking the supremum over $v$. $\square$ Corollary 5.29.5 . EACB00126847 Fix $p>1$. There is a constant $C_ p$ such that every nonnegative $F\in L^ p(X,\mathrm{d}V)$ satisfies \[  \int _ E F\, \mathrm{d}V\leq C_ p\| F\| _ p\operatorname {Cap}(E)^2  \] for every Borel set $E\subset X$. Proof. By Hölder's inequality and ( 5.29.3 ), the integral is at most \[  C\| F\| _ p\exp (-a\operatorname {Cap}(E)^{-1/n}/p'), \qquad p'=p/(p-1).  \] The function $x\mapsto x^{-2}\exp (-ax^{-1/n}/p')$ is bounded on $0<x\leq \operatorname {Cap}(X)<\infty $, and sets of capacity zero have zero volume. $\square$ The same proof bounds the integral of an $L^ p$ density by any fixed positive power of the capacity. The exponent two will be convenient for the iteration over sublevel sets in lemma 14.19.16 .

title: Lemma 5.29.2
text: Lemma 5.29.2 . 5CEF121C5391 There are constants $a,C>0$ such that 87E51BAEC1C0 5.29.3 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Vol}(E)\leq C\exp \bigl (-a\operatorname {Cap}(E)^{-1/n}\bigr ) \end{equation} for every Borel set $E\subset X$. Moreover, for every $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with $\sup _ Xu=0$ and every $t>1$, 3EF8F920CDD3 5.29.4 \begin{equation}  \operatorname {Cap}(\{ u<-t\} )\leq C/t. \end{equation} Proof. Choose $\delta >0$ so small that \[  \omega +\delta \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j\geq 0,\qquad 3\delta /2\leq 1.  \] The function \[  V=\max \{ \delta (v+\chi _ j),-\delta /2\} +\delta /2 \quad \hbox{on }B_ j, \qquad V=0\quad \hbox{outside }B_ j,  \] is $\omega $-plurisubharmonic on $X$, because near $\partial B_ j$ the constant branch is the larger one, and it takes values between zero and one. On $B'_ j$ we have $\omega _ V\geq \delta \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$. By the positivity of bounded products, \[  \operatorname {cap}(E\cap B'_ j,B_ j) \leq \delta ^{-n}\operatorname {Cap}(E).  \] The local volume–capacity estimate, summed over the finite cover, proves ( 5.29.3 ). For the second estimate, choose on each $B_ j$ a smooth negative quadratic function $r_ j$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}r_ j\geq \omega $. For every global test $0\leq v\leq 1$, the functions $u+r_ j\leq 0$ and $v+r_ j$ are plurisubharmonic on $B_ j$. Thus \[  \begin{split}  \int _{\{ u<-t\} }\omega _ v^ n & \leq t^{-1}\int _ X(-u)\omega _ v^ n\\ & \leq t^{-1}\sum _ j\int _{B'_ j}(-u-r_ j) \bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+r_ j)\bigr )^ n\\ & \leq \frac Ct\left(1+\int _ X|u|\, \mathrm{d}V\right). \end{split}  \] Here the second inequality uses $\omega _ v\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+r_ j)$, and the third is the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg inequality, applied to local test functions with a common bound.
