title: Corollary 5.29.5
text: Corollary 5.29.5 . EACB00126847 Fix $p>1$. There is a constant $C_ p$ such that every nonnegative $F\in L^ p(X,\mathrm{d}V)$ satisfies \[  \int _ E F\, \mathrm{d}V\leq C_ p\| F\| _ p\operatorname {Cap}(E)^2  \] for every Borel set $E\subset X$. Proof. By Hölder's inequality and ( 5.29.3 ), the integral is at most \[  C\| F\| _ p\exp (-a\operatorname {Cap}(E)^{-1/n}/p'), \qquad p'=p/(p-1).  \] The function $x\mapsto x^{-2}\exp (-ax^{-1/n}/p')$ is bounded on $0<x\leq \operatorname {Cap}(X)<\infty $, and sets of capacity zero have zero volume. $\square$

title: 5.29.6 Integration against a Hölder reference
text: A Hölder modulus for a bounded potential gives a modulus for integration against its Monge–Ampère measure. The proof uses a smooth approximation of the reference, with integration by parts controlling the change in its measure. Lemma 5.29.7 . D9AF18430F97 Let $B'\Subset B$ be concentric balls in $\mathbb C^ n$, and let $0<\alpha \leq 1$. Suppose $p\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)\cap C^{0,\alpha }(B)$ has $C^{0,\alpha }$ norm at most $N$. For every $M\geq 1$ there is a constant $C_ M$ such that bounded $a,b\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)$ with $|a|,|b|\leq M$ satisfy \[  \int _{B'}|a-b|(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n \leq C_ M\| a-b\| _{L^1(B)}^{\alpha /(\alpha +2n)}.  \] The constants are uniform for references with the stated bound $N$. Proof. Choose intermediate concentric balls and a smooth cutoff $0\leq \chi \leq 1$ supported in the innermost of them and equal to one on $B'$. All integrations below take place away from $\partial B$. Let $p_\varepsilon $ be a nonnegative radial convolution of $p$ on a larger intermediate ball. It is plurisubharmonic, and, for small $\varepsilon >0$, \[  \| p-p_\varepsilon \| _\infty \leq C\varepsilon ^\alpha , \qquad 0\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_\varepsilon \leq C\varepsilon ^{-2}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2.  \] Both references have a common bounded range. Set $f=|a-b|=2\max (a,b)-a-b$, and put \[  T=\sum _{j=0}^{n-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ j\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_\varepsilon )^{n-1-j}.  \] This is a closed positive current. Factorization and integration by parts give \[  \int \chi f\bigl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n-(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p_\varepsilon )^ n\bigr ) =\int (p-p_\varepsilon )\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi f)\wedge T.  \] We check that the last signed measure has variation at most $C(1+M)^2$, uniformly in $\varepsilon $. The term $\chi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f\wedge T$ is a linear combination of the positive measures formed with $\max (a,b),a,b$, whose masses are at most $CM$ by local Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimates. The term $f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge T$ has variation at most $CM$. For the two terms involving $\mathrm df$, use a cutoff $\eta $ equal to one near $\operatorname {supp}\chi $. If $q$ is any of $a,b,\max (a,b)$, translate it so that $0\leq q\leq 2M$. The bounded chain rule and closedness of $T$ give \[  \int \eta \, \mathrm dq\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}q\wedge T =\frac12\int q^2\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\eta \wedge T -\int \eta q\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\wedge T\leq CM^2.  \] The last term is nonnegative before subtraction, and the first is bounded using the local mass of $T$. Since $f=2\max (a,b)-a-b$, its gradient energy is also bounded by $CM^2$. Cauchy–Schwarz against the positive current $T$ now bounds the variation of $\mathrm d\chi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge T$ and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi \wedge \mathrm df\wedge T$ by $CM$. These are all the terms of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi f)\wedge T$. The bounded formulas follow first for local smooth regularizations. To pass to bounded potentials, regularize $a,b,p$ decreasingly on the intermediate balls, write $f$ as the displayed linear combination, and apply lemma 5.27.2 to the expanded identities. The energy bounds are uniform; thus the integration by parts and its estimate survive this limit. Writing $L=\| a-b\| _{L^1(B)}$, we have proved 16B648CFC04A 5.29.8 \begin{equation}  \int \chi f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n \leq C(1+M)^2\varepsilon ^\alpha +C\varepsilon ^{-2n}L. \end{equation} For small positive $L$, take $\varepsilon =L^{1/(\alpha +2n)}$. A fixed admissible radius and the bounded local mass handle the remaining $L$. For $L=0$, let $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ in the same inequality. $\square$ Corollary 5.29.9 . F701C1999BDC Let $(X,\omega )$ be compact Hermitian, and let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )\cap C^{0,\alpha }(X)$, $0<\alpha \leq 1$. If uniformly bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions $a,b$ have a fixed common smooth lower curvature bound, then \[  \int _ X|a-b|\, \omega _ u^ n \leq C\| a-b\| _{L^1(\mathrm dV)}^{\alpha /(\alpha +2n)}.  \] The constant depends on the bounds for $a,b$, their lower curvature bound and the $C^{0,\alpha }$ norm of $u$. Proof. On each of finitely many coordinate balls, choose a fixed smooth strictly plurisubharmonic quadratic $Q$ such that $a+Q,b+Q,u+Q$ are plurisubharmonic and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}Q\geq \omega $. There $0\leq \omega _ u\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+Q)$, so positivity of bounded products gives $\omega _ u^ n\leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+Q))^ n$. Apply lemma 5.29.7 on smaller balls covering $X$. The quadratic cancels in the difference, and the local volumes are equivalent to $\mathrm dV$. Summing proves the assertion. $\square$ The estimate before optimization also controls the tails of unbounded potentials. We need the following local form with a compact ambient space, so that the exponential bound for smooth volume is uniform. Lemma 5.29.10 . EF54C7C9A0A8 Let $(Y,\Omega )$ be compact Hermitian, let $B'\Subset B\subset Y$ be coordinate balls, and let $p\in \mathrm{PSH}(B)\cap C^{0,\alpha }(B)$ have norm at most $N$, with $0<\alpha \leq 1$. There are $c,C>0$, uniform for these references, such that \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n\bigl (B'\cap \{ v<-t\} \bigr )\leq C\mathrm e^{-ct} \quad (t\geq 0)  \] for every $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(Y,\Omega )$ with $\sup _ Yv=0$. Proof. Choose a smooth quadratic $Q$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}Q\geq \Omega $ on $B$ and a fixed constant $D$ such that $w=v+Q-D\leq 0$. By lemma 5.26.2 on $(Y,\Omega )$ and the bounded correction $Q-D$, \[  \| f_ m\| _{L^1(B)}\leq C\mathrm e^{-am}  \] for a fixed $a>0$. Taking $\varepsilon =\mathrm e^{-am/(\alpha +2n)}$ gives \[  \int \chi f_ m(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n \leq C(1+m)^2\exp \left(-\frac{a\alpha m}{\alpha +2n}\right) \leq C\mathrm e^{-cm}  \] for some $c>0$. Large $m$ ensure that the convolution radius is admissible; the common local mass handles the other integers. The bounded difference between $w$ and $v$, and then choosing an integer just below the given height, prove the estimate for every real $t\geq 0$. $\square$

title: 5.29.11 Capacity bounds for Hölder references
text: To pass from the exponential tail estimate to a capacity estimate, we use a closed background on an auxiliary projective space. The local capacity comparison then returns the result to the original Hermitian manifold. For the Fubini–Study form $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$ on $\mathbb P^ n$, normalized by $\int \omega _{\mathrm{FS}}^ n=1$, define for a compact set $K$ \[  T(K)=\inf _{v\in \mathrm{PSH}(\mathbb P^ n,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}),\  \sup v=0} \exp (\sup _ Kv).  \] We recall the classical global extremal-function theorem in this closed setting [ GZ17 ] . If $K$ is non-pluripolar, the upper semicontinuous regularization of \[  V_ K=\sup \{ v\in \mathrm{PSH}(\mathbb P^ n,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}):v|_ K\leq 0\}   \] is bounded, nonnegative and $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$-plurisubharmonic. Its Monge–Ampère probability is supported on $K$. If $K$ is pluripolar, $\sup V_ K=+\infty $ and $T(K)=0$. Lemma 5.29.12 . 1017EA20E8D8 For every compact $K\subset \mathbb P^ n$, \[  T(K)\leq \mathrm e\exp \bigl (-\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K)^{-1/n}\bigr ).  \] The right-hand side is zero for capacity zero. Proof. The pluripolar case follows from the recalled theorem and the characterization of capacity-zero sets. Otherwise let $M=\sup V_ K^*<\infty $. Subtracting $\sup _ Kv$ from a normalized competitor, and conversely normalizing competitors for $V_ K$, shows directly that $T(K)=\mathrm e^{-M}$. If $M\geq 1$, the function $q=V_ K^*/M$ satisfies $0\leq q\leq 1$ and is an admissible capacity test. Since the background is closed, \[  1=\int _ K\omega _{V_ K^*}^ n \leq M^ n\int _ K\omega _ q^ n \leq M^ n\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K).  \] Here $\omega _{V_ K^*}\leq M\omega _ q$ follows from $M\geq 1$. Thus $M\geq \operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K)^{-1/n}$. If $M<1$, $V_ K^*$ itself is a capacity test, so the same supported probability gives $\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K)=1$. Since $T(K)\leq 1$, the stated factor $\mathrm e$ covers this case. $\square$ Proposition 5.29.13 . D00B685B1791 Let $(X,\omega )$ be compact Hermitian. Fix $0<\alpha \leq 1$ and $N>0$. There are $a,C>0$ such that every $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )\cap C^{0,\alpha }(X)$ with $\| u\| _{C^{0,\alpha }}\leq N$ satisfies \[  \omega _ u^ n(E)\leq C\exp \bigl (-a\operatorname {Cap}_\omega (E)^{-1/n}\bigr ) \quad (E\subset X\text{ Borel}).  \] Consequently, for each $s>0$ there is a uniform $C_ s$ with $\omega _ u^ n(E)\leq C_ s\operatorname {Cap}_\omega (E)^ s$. Proof. Fix nested coordinate balls $B'\Subset B$ and a smooth quadratic $Q$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}Q\geq \omega $ on $B$. The function $p=u+Q$ is plurisubharmonic with a common Hölder bound, and $\omega _ u^ n\leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n$ there. Regard $B$ as a ball in the affine chart $\mathbb C^ n\subset \mathbb P^ n$ and restrict this local measure to $B'$, extending it by zero. By lemma 5.29.10 on $(\mathbb P^ n,\omega _{\mathrm{FS}})$, it has a uniform exponential tail on every normalized global Fubini–Study potential. Its total mass is uniformly bounded by local Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimates. For a non-pluripolar compact $K\subset B'$, choose a normalized potential $v$ with $\sup _ Kv\leq \log T(K)+1$. For small $T(K)$ the tail estimate gives \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p)^ n(K)\leq C T(K)^ c \leq C\exp \bigl (-c\operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K)^{-1/n}\bigr ).  \] The common mass bound handles the remaining $T(K)$, and pluripolar sets have zero local product mass. A bounded local potential for $\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}$ turns every global test $0\leq v\leq 1$ into a plurisubharmonic function of a fixed bounded range on $B$. Hence \[  \operatorname {Cap}_{\omega _{\mathrm{FS}}}(K) \leq C_1\operatorname {cap}(K,B) \leq C_2\operatorname {Cap}_\omega (K),  \] where the last inequality is the gluing construction of lemma 5.29.2 on the original manifold. These inequalities have the required direction after taking negative inverse powers. Inner regularity of the finite local product extends the bound from compact to Borel subsets of $B'$. Summing over a fixed finite cover proves the first assertion. The second follows by bounding $x^{-s}\exp (-ax^{-1/n})$ on $0<x\leq \operatorname {Cap}_\omega (X)$. $\square$
